THE PSYCHOPATHOLOGY OF EVERYDAY LIFE

日常生活中的心理病理学

SIGMUND FREUD was born in 1856 in Moravia; between the ages of four and eighty-two his home was Vienna: in 1938 Hitlers invasion of Austria forced him to seek asylum in London, where he died in the following year. His career began with several years of brilliant work on the anatomy and physiology of the nervous system. He was almost thirty when, after a period of study under Charcot in Paris, his interests first turned to psychology; and after ten years of clinical work in Vienna (at first in collaboration with Breuer, an older colleage) he invented what was to become psychoanalysis. This began simply as a method of treating neurotic patients through talking, but it quickly grew into an accumulation of knowledge about the workings of the mind in general. Freud was thus able to demonstrate the development of the sexual instinct in childhood, and largely on the basis of an examination of dreams, arrived at this fundamental discovery of the unconscious forces that influence our everyday thoughts and actions. Freud’s life was uneventful, but his ideas have shaped not only many specialist disciplines, but also the whole intellectual climate of the twentieth century.

西格蒙德·弗洛伊德于1856年出生于摩拉维亚；从四岁到八十二岁，他一直居住在维也纳。1938年，希特勒入侵奥地利，迫使他前往伦敦寻求庇护，并于次年逝世于此。他的职业生涯始于数年对神经系统解剖学和生理学的卓越研究。在巴黎跟随夏尔科学习一段时间后，他近三十岁时开始对心理学产生兴趣；在维也纳进行了十年的临床工作（最初与年长的同事布鲁尔合作）后，他创立了后来被称为精神分析的理论。精神分析最初只是通过谈话治疗神经症患者的方法，但很快发展成为对心理运作机制的全面研究。弗洛伊德由此得以证明性本能的儿童期发展，并主要基于对梦境的研究，最终发现了影响我们日常思想和行为的无意识力量这一根本性发现。弗洛伊德的一生平淡无奇，但他的思想不仅塑造了许多专业学科，而且塑造了二十世纪的整个知识氛围。

ANTHEA BELL was born in Suffolk and educated at Somerville College, Oxford. She has worked as a translator for many years, primarily from German and French. Her translations include works of nonfiction (biology, politics, social history, musicology and art history), literary and popular fiction, and books for young people including classic German works by the Grimm brothers, Clemens Brentano, Wilhelm Hauff and Christian Morgenstern. Recent translations include E. T. A. Hoffmann’s The Life and Opinions of the Tomcat Murr (1999), Lilian Faschinger’s Vienna Passion (2000) and W. G. Sebald’s Austerliz (2001). Anthea Bell has also served on the committee of the Translator’s Association and the jury panel of the Schlegel-Tieck German translation prize in the UK, and has received a number of translation prizes and awards, including the 1987 Schlegel-Tieck award for Hans Bemmann’s The Stone and the Flute. She lives in Cambridge and has two adult sons.

安西娅·贝尔出生于萨福克郡，毕业于牛津大学萨默维尔学院。她从事翻译工作多年，主要翻译德语和法语作品。她的译作涵盖非虚构类作品（生物学、政治学、社会史、音乐学和艺术史）、文学和通俗小说，以及青少年读物，其中包括格林兄弟、克莱门斯·布伦塔诺、威廉·豪夫和克里斯蒂安·摩根施特恩等德国经典作家的作品。近期译作包括E·T·A·霍夫曼的《雄猫穆尔的生活与见解》（1999年）、莉莲·法辛格的《维也纳激情》（2000年）和W·G·塞巴尔德的《奥斯特利兹》（2001年）。安西娅·贝尔曾任英国翻译协会委员会委员和施莱格尔-蒂克德语翻译奖评委，并荣获多项翻译奖项，其中包括1987年凭借汉斯·贝曼的《石头与笛子》获得的施莱格尔-蒂克奖。她现居剑桥，育有两子，均已成年。

PAUL KEEGAN was formerly editor of Penguin Classics, and is now Poetry Editor at Faber & Faber. He is the editor of The New Penguin Book of English Verse (2000).

保罗·基根曾任企鹅经典文库编辑，现任费伯出版社诗歌编辑。他是《新企鹅英语诗歌选集》（2000年）的编辑。

ADAM PHILLIPS was formerly Principal Child Psychotherapist at Charing Cross Hospital in London. He is the author of several books on psychoanalysis including On Kissing, Tickling and Being Bored, Darwin’s Worms, Promises, Promises and Houdini’s Box.

亚当·菲利普斯曾任伦敦查令十字医院首席儿童心理治疗师。他著有多部关于精神分析的书籍，包括《论接吻、挠痒和无聊》、《达尔文的蠕虫》、《承诺，承诺》和《胡迪尼的盒子》。

Introduction

介绍

‘There is a house where twice every day for six years, at regular hours, I used to wait to be let in outside a door on the second floor…’

“有一座房子，六年来，我每天两次，在固定的时间，都会在二楼的一扇门外等着被人开门……”

While doing things, or in the interstices between doing things, we do other, less obvious things. The Psychopathology of Everyday Life is the inventory of what goes on when nothing much is going on, or of what we do when we think we know what we are doing. Its concern is ordinary life, using as its optic the not-so-ordinary life of the bourgeoisie at the century’s turn, in Vienna and other Hapsburg capitals and resorts. The stage is largely given over to what Veblen termed ‘the performance of leisure’. Doing nothing much, circa 1900, is all-consuming: we sit in coffee houses, wait in rooms, stand in trams; we visit each other, and effect introductions; we return from honeymoon, compose letters, consult watches and timetables; we take holidays, stay at pensione, in sanatoria, at health resorts and spas; we stroll zoos, walk mountains, wander museums. We are in thrall to travel, or to the rituals of displacement — as if places are more important than where they are. And wherever we are we repeat ourselves: we window-shop, stare at statues, scrutinize business plates, study menus. We are addicted to signs of every description, describing anything.

在做事的同时，或者在做事的间隙，我们还会做其他一些不太明显的事情。《日常生活心理病理学》一书记录了在看似平静无事之时，或者在我们自以为清楚自己在做什么的时候，人们都在做些什么。它关注的是日常生活，并以世纪之交维也纳和其他哈布斯堡王朝的首都和度假胜地中资产阶级的非凡生活为视角。舞台很大程度上被凡勃伦所说的“休闲表演”所占据。大约在1900年，无所事事占据了人们的全部精力：我们坐在咖啡馆里，在房间里等候，站在电车里；我们互相拜访，互相介绍；我们蜜月归来，写信，查看手表和时刻表；我们度假，住在旅馆、疗养院、温泉疗养地；我们漫步动物园，徒步登山，徜徉博物馆。我们沉迷于旅行，或者说沉迷于漂泊的仪式——仿佛地点比实际位置更重要。无论身处何地，我们都在重复着同样的行为：逛橱窗，凝视雕像，仔细查看商家的招牌，研究菜单。我们对各种各样的符号都上了瘾，这些符号描述了万物。

Above all (and Karl Kraus ridicules us for it) we read magazines and newspapers, by the avalanche. We drown in print. By the 1920s in Germany more than a thousand magazines were being founded annually. Added to which the streets are aswarm with advertisements, hoardings, billboards, displays. The metropolis of Everyday Life is as much a lexical as a visual field. And print is the omnipresent occasion for misprints, for wandering meanings. Suddenly the field of nonsense seems to have been exponentially enlarged. (Item: ‘Our readers will be well aware that we have always promoted the common good in the most [un]self-interested manner.’) This extends to the non sequiturs we ourselves generate. We seem to misread much of what comes our way: we even misread misprints. In fact, given how little we do, we get a lot of it wrong, much of the time, without paying any attention to the fact. Freud’s book is all attention, and one way of reading it is as a parody, a work of pseudo-prescription, a critique of scientific method. Its starting-point is that, on the evidence all around us, we can never be as scientific, as empirical, as we might wish.

最重要的是（卡尔·克劳斯为此嘲笑我们），我们如雪崩般阅读杂志和报纸。我们被印刷品淹没。到了20世纪20年代，德国每年创刊的杂志超过一千种。此外，街头巷尾充斥着广告、围挡、广告牌和各种展示。日常生活的大都市既是一个词汇场，也是一个视觉场。而印刷品无处不在，错误印刷和含义游移不定的现象层出不穷。突然间，荒谬的领域似乎呈指数级增长。（例如：“我们的读者非常清楚，我们始终以最[不]自私的方式促进公共利益。”）这甚至延伸到我们自己产生的不合逻辑的论证。我们似乎误解了大部分接收到的信息：我们甚至误解了印刷错误。事实上，鉴于我们所做的如此之少，我们常常犯错，而且往往毫不在意。弗洛伊德的著作处处体现着专注，一种解读方式是将其视为一部戏仿之作、一部伪处方之作、一部对科学方法的批判之作。它的出发点是，根据我们周围的一切证据，我们永远无法像我们希望的那样科学、那样经验主义。

Doing nothing much is one thing; getting it wrong, suggests Freud, is something more interesting. Ordinary acts bristle with redundancy — with stumbling, slipping, falling; with dropping things, knocking things over, losing things, pouring things over ourselves; with forgetting each other’s names, addressing each other by the wrong names, mislaying the names of our husbands, of our cities; with forgetting what we intend to do, omitting to carry out tasks, mixing up dates. Our days are full of farcical detour and unscripted subplots. We cannot trust ourselves to post our letters, we make mistakes in the writing, we wrongly address them to those for whose eyes their contents are specifically not intended. We put calls through to the wrong people. We take the wrong trains, we register our children with the wrong names, we forget to sign cheques. No sooner do we receive presents than we mislay them. We are inept at dodging each other in the street, and we cannot be relied on to cross an empty thoroughfare without getting run over. More generally, we produce a constant unspecified static: we fiddle with our clothes and our hair, we scribble things, we jingle coins, we hum tunes ‘thoughtlessly’, like Sterne’s Uncle Toby; we make meaningless gestures and movements; we are obscurely ‘impelled’ to perform odd acts, acts which are not quite actions. We are the landing strips for all these minor furies. And through it all we say — or rather we come out with — the wrong things, with hybrid utterance, with things concealed but struggling for appearance.

无所事事是一回事；弗洛伊德认为，犯错则更有趣。日常行为中充满了重复——跌跌撞撞、滑倒、摔跤；掉东西、碰倒东西、丢失东西、把东西洒在自己身上；忘记彼此的名字、叫错名字、弄丢丈夫的名字、弄丢所在城市的名字；忘记自己打算做什么、疏忽任务、搞错日期。我们的日子充满了滑稽的插曲和即兴的支线剧情。我们无法相信自己能把信寄出去，我们会写错字，我们会把信寄错收件人，而收件人显然不是信的内容。我们会把电话拨错人。我们会坐错火车，我们会用错误的名字给孩子登记，我们会忘记在支票上签名。我们刚收到礼物，就又会弄丢它们。我们笨拙地在街上躲避彼此，也无法指望我们能平安穿过空旷的马路。更普遍地说，我们制造出一种持续不断的、难以名状的噪音：我们摆弄衣服和头发，我们涂涂画画，我们叮当作响地摇晃硬币，我们像斯特恩笔下的托比叔叔那样“漫不经心”地哼着小调；我们做出毫无意义的手势和动作；我们被一种莫名的“驱使”去做一些奇怪的事情，一些根本算不上行动的事情。我们就像所有这些微小怒火的着陆带。在这一切之中，我们说着——或者更确切地说，我们脱口而出——不恰当的话，说着杂乱无章的话语，说着那些隐藏却又挣扎着想要显露出来的东西。

The ‘parapraxis’ — a collective noun for all slips and errors 1 — is also a paradox: a cancelled action, so to speak. And Freud is the first observed to be philosophically struck, not by our failure rate, but by how unintrigued we are by the fact — how feckless, how innocent. In his essay ‘A Plea for Excuses’, discriminating the niceties of everyday usage in the matter of disclaimers, J. L. Austin wondered: ‘I do not know how many of you keep a list of the kinds of fool you make of yourselves.’ Freud says: I have made a list of the kinds of fool we make of ourselves. Everyday Life is a pattern book of examples — or of digressions, since parapraxes are detours inside the ordinary. The book is a revolving door of entrances and exits, with a largely nameless cast of hundreds. If The Interpretation of Dreams (Freud’s previous book, published two years earlier) is structured as a journey, the Ithaca of whose discoveries comes clearly into view only near its end, Everyday Life is more radically peripatetic, a makeshift city comedy whose sets change so rapidly as to be superimposed rather than sequential: a café theatrical about our improvisations, the contingencies by which we live.

“口误”（parapraxis）——一个指代所有失误和错误的集合名词——本身也是一个悖论：可以说，它是一种被取消的行为。弗洛伊德是第一个在哲学层面上对此感到震惊的人，他关注的并非我们的失败率，而是我们对这一事实的漠不关心——我们是多么的无能，多么的天真。在《为借口辩护》一文中，J·L·奥斯汀在探讨日常用语中免责声明的细微差别时，不禁问道：“我不知道你们当中有多少人会记录自己犯过的各种愚蠢错误。”弗洛伊德则说：“我列了一张我们犯过的各种愚蠢错误的清单。”《日常生活》是一本例证的模式书——或者说是一本离题的模式书，因为口误是日常生活中的迂回曲折。这本书就像一个旋转门，进出不穷，其中穿插着数百个大多不知名的角色。如果说《梦的解析》（弗洛伊德两年前出版的前一本书）的结构是一段旅程，其发现的伊萨卡岛直到接近尾声才清晰可见，那么《日常生活》则更具漫游性，是一部临时搭建的城市喜剧，其场景变化如此之快，以至于是叠加的而不是顺序的：一部关于我们即兴发挥、我们赖以生存的偶然性的咖啡馆戏剧。

To maintain the focus on ordinary actions, Freud finds it necessary to admit the infra-ordinaiy — the micro-neurotic, the zero degree of behaviour — to focus on the unfocused, on what he calls ‘occurrences which drop out of the concatenation of events’ ( Introductory Lectures , 1919). On the one hand, his concern is with the satin lining of time passing, rather than the hair shirt of obligation, and this gives the book its air of dawdle, its serpentine line of aimlessness. On the other hand, Freud is tactically committed to conveying the sense of business as usual for the psyche’s functionings, given that he expected strong resistance — from empiricist and sociological accounts of the self-evidence of ordinary life — to his claims for the slipping self. He must therefore avoid the suspicion of offering an exceptionalist account. As he explained retrospectively in the Introductory Lectures , this meant eschewing ‘the much richer material offered by my neurotic patients’ so as to avoid incurring the charge that parapraxes apply to pathological states rather than to normal mental functioning. Parapraxes are not divagations from the norm, they are its measure. As if it were normal to be unable to be normal.

为了保持对日常行为的关注，弗洛伊德认为有必要承认“低于寻常”的存在——即微神经症、零度行为——从而聚焦于那些未被关注的事物，即他所谓的“从事件串联中脱离出来的事件”（《导论讲稿》，1919）。一方面，他关注的是时间流逝的丝滑质感，而非义务的苦行，这使得本书呈现出一种拖沓的氛围，一种漫无目的的蜿蜒曲折。另一方面，鉴于弗洛伊德预料到，他关于“自我滑落”的主张会遭到强烈的抵制——来自经验主义和社会学对日常生活自明性的论述——因此，他策略性地致力于传达心理运作一切如常的理念。他必须避免被怀疑提供了一种例外主义的解释。正如他在导论讲座中回顾性地解释的那样，这意味着要避开“我的神经症患者提供的更为丰富的素材”，以免被指责为语无伦次只适用于病理状态而非正常的心理功能。语无伦次并非偏离常态，而是常态的衡量标准。仿佛无法正常行事才是常态。

*

No wishes for today, except

今天没有愿望，除了

To play it out, and not become the fool.

认真对待这件事，别让自己沦为笑柄。

(Hugo Williams, ‘Early Morning’)

（雨果·威廉姆斯，《清晨》）

Freud offers himself up as the primary witness: in the crucible of Everyday Life he is his own experiment. ‘I am usually obliged to take those examples of the psychic disturbance of functioning in everyday life that I am collecting in this work from my self-observations.’ His own experience is the Plimsoll line, and the vessel of normality must be seen to ‘steer clear of’ (Freud’s image) the ship of fools steaming in the other direction. In other words, Freud recruited normal life for an account of universal deviancy from the norm (‘we are all slightly neurotic’), and Everyday Life is in this sense a satire, an encyclopédie de la bêtise. If W. H. Auden apostrophized normality as ‘goddess of bossy underlings’ (misprinted in a recent edition as goddess of bossy ‘underthings’), this was to imply its reign of terror over the entire building of the self. Freud reveals the internalization of norms as something rather less successful, or threatening, or total: as a secret reign of error. Normality — the protocols of the day — is a failed regime, and Freud’s cast of personae (in both senses: not-quite characters, but also: splintery versions of Freud) have something of the ungovernable yet self-governing oddity of Dickens’s minor creations.

弗洛伊德将自己作为主要见证人：在《日常生活》的熔炉中，他成为了自己的实验对象。“我通常不得不从自我观察中汲取我在这部作品中收集的关于日常生活中心理功能紊乱的例子。”他自身的经验就是普林索尔线，而正常状态的船只必须“避开”（弗洛伊德的意象）驶向相反方向的愚人船。换句话说，弗洛伊德利用正常生活来解释普遍存在的偏离常态的行为（“我们都有些神经质”），《日常生活》从这个意义上说是一部讽刺作品，一部“怪癖百科全书”。如果W·H·奥登将正常状态称为“专横下属的女神”（在最近的版本中被误印为专横“下属”的女神），这暗示了它对整个自我构建的恐怖统治。弗洛伊德揭示了规范的内化并非一种成功、威胁或彻底的制度：而是一种隐秘的错误统治。常态——即当时的准则——是一种失败的制度，而弗洛伊德笔下的人物（既非完全意义上的角色，也是弗洛伊德自身的碎片化版本）带有狄更斯笔下那些次要人物身上那种难以驾驭却又自我约束的怪诞特质。

The rehearsal of everyday life in these pages is piled high with small (that big Freudian word) specimens. What results is a collage or palimpsest, extrapolated through recension after recension, over two decades — from its first periodical publication in 1901, and book appearance in 1904, to progressively enlarged editions in 1907, 1910, 1912, 1917, 1919, 1920 and 1924. It is Freud’s Thousand and One Days , whose vertiginous extensios evinces a fear of closure, as if to finish would be to fail to have convinced the reader. ( Everyday Life, The Interpretation of Dreams and the three essays on sexuality were Freud’s most revised books: he was unable to say or have the last word on sex, or slips, or dreams.) But it is a mistake to think of these examples as redundant. In a sense, they are all there is, along with their explanations, which are often as provisional and performative — or as interminable — as what they describe.

这些篇章中对日常生活的描绘堆砌着大量的小例子（弗洛伊德式的“小例子”）。最终呈现的是一幅拼贴画或重写本，经过二十多年的反复修订——从1901年首次在期刊上发表，1904年出版成书，到1907年、1910年、1912年、1917年、1919年、1920年和1924年不断扩充的版本。这是弗洛伊德的《一千零一天》，其令人眩晕的延伸性体现出一种对完结的恐惧，仿佛完成就意味着未能说服读者。（《日常生活》、《梦的解析》和三篇关于性的文章是弗洛伊德修改次数最多的著作：他无法就性、口误或梦境等问题给出最终的定论。）但认为这些例子是多余的，那就错了。从某种意义上说，它们就是一切，连同它们的解释，这些解释往往和它们所描述的事物一样，都是暂时的、表演性的，或者没完没了的。

In Freud’s comedy of errors, the individual scene is the isolated slip, a piece of ‘incompletely suppressed psychic material which, although displaced from the conscious mind, is not, however, deprived of all ability to express itself. The repressed returns, but this time as farce. If the Oedipus complex represents our lives as consolingly tragic, then the parapraxis presents everyday life — the placeless place where we live, flickeringly, partially — as disconsolately comic. The social comedy of Everyday Life is both more nuanced and more slapstick than that of The Joke and Its Relation to the Unconscious , which appeared four years later. Here is a symptomatic vignette (inserted in 1907) of the woman who mistook her husband for an Other:

在弗洛伊德的错误喜剧中，个体场景是孤立的口误，是一段“未被完全压抑的心理素材，虽然它已脱离意识，但并未丧失表达自身的能力”。被压抑的情感回归，但这次是以闹剧的形式出现。如果说俄狄浦斯情结将我们的生活描绘成一种令人慰藉的悲剧，那么口误则将日常生活——我们栖居的、闪烁不定、片面的、无处安身的场所——呈现为一种令人沮丧的喜剧。《日常生活》的社会喜剧比四年后出版的《玩笑及其与无意识的关系》更加微妙，也更加滑稽。以下是一个典型的例子（插入于1907年），讲述了一位女士将丈夫误认为“他者”的故事：

I was once visiting a young married couple and heard the young wife, laughing, tell the tale of a recent experience of hers: the day after she came home from a journey, she had visited her unmarried sister, as she habitually did, to go shopping while her husband went out to work. She had suddenly seen a gentleman on the other side of the street, nudged her sister, and said: ‘Oh, look, there’s Herr L.’ She had forgotten that Herr L. had actually been her husband for some weeks.

我曾拜访一对年轻夫妇，听到年轻的妻子笑着讲述她最近的一次经历：她旅行回来后的第二天，像往常一样去她未婚的妹妹家逛街，趁着丈夫上班的时候去购物。她突然看到街对面有个男人，便碰了碰妹妹，说：“哦，你看，那是L先生。”她这才想起，L先生其实是她结婚几周的丈夫。

Or an example of slipped penmanship (added in 1920):

或者举个字迹潦草的例子（1920年添加）：

An American staying in Europe, who had parted with his wife on bad terms, thought perhaps they could now make the quarrel up and asked her to cross the Atlantic and meet him on a certain date. ‘It would be a good idea if you sailed on the Mauretania ,’ he wrote. However, he did not venture to send the sheet of paper on which he had written this sentence, preferring to rewrite the whole letter in case she noticed the correction he had been obliged to make to the name of the ship. He had originally written Lusitania.

一位旅居欧洲的美国人，与妻子不欢而散，心想或许现在他们可以和好如初，于是邀请妻子横渡大西洋，在某个特定的日子与他相会。“如果你乘坐‘毛里塔尼亚号’就更好了，”他写道。然而，他不敢寄出写着这句话的那张纸，而是选择重写整封信，以免妻子发现他不得不修改船名。他最初写的是“卢西塔尼亚号”。

Freud remarks that the best slips have the ‘explosiveness’ of jokes. ‘A lady once advanced the following opinion at a social gathering — and the words show that they were uttered with fervour and under the pressure of a host of secret impulses: “Oh yes, a woman must be pretty if she is to please men. It’s much easier for a man: so long as he has his fünf geraden Glieder [five straight limbs] that’s all he needs!”’ (added in 1910). But whereas in the Joke book the self is a consumer, a net importer of jokes, in the Mistakes book the self becomes a producer. For if jokes are what we hear on their way elsewhere, ostensibly directed at others, then mistakes are jokes that the unconscious makes up, on the spot, against the self. With jokes we confine humour safely to quarters (‘We can only laugh when a joke has come to our help’), whereas mistakes set it loose to roam the day.

弗洛伊德指出，最好的口误具有笑话般的“爆发力”。“一位女士曾在一次社交聚会上发表了如下观点——从字里行间可以看出，她是在各种隐秘冲动的驱使下，满怀热情地说出这句话：‘哦，是的，女人要想取悦男人，就必须漂亮。男人就容易多了：只要他有五条笔直的四肢，就足够了！’”（1910年添加）。然而，在“笑话书”中，自我是一个消费者，一个笑话的净进口者；而在“错误书”中，自我则变成了一个生产者。因为如果说笑话是我们无意中听到的、表面上是针对他人的笑话，那么错误就是无意识即兴创作的、针对自我的笑话。笑话让我们把幽默安全地限制在某个区域（“只有当笑话帮到我们时，我们才能笑”），而错误则让它自由地在一天中游荡。

A man walking in a strange city at around the time when, because of a course of medical treatment, he needed to open his bowels read the word Klosetthaus [lavatory] on a large sign over the first floor of a tall department store, although his pleasure at seeing it was mingled with some surprise at the unusual situation of this convenient place. Next moment he was less pleased to see that the signboard really read: Korsetthaus [corset-makers].

一个男人在陌生的城市里行走，正值因治疗需要排便之际，他看到一家高大百货商店一楼上方的一块大招牌上写着“Klosetthaus”（厕所），他看到这几个字时，既感到高兴，又有些惊讶于这地方如此方便。然而，下一刻，当他发现招牌上写的其实是“Korsetthaus”（束身衣店）时，高兴之情便荡然无存了。

Parapraxes occur where our unconscious gangs up with circumstance, and gets to ridicule us merely for getting up in the morning and agreeing to appear on the stage of the day (there needs no unbuttoned fly, dear colleague, come from your bedsit to tell us this). As if our days arrive already filled with the reverse of achievement.

当我们的潜意识与环境沆瀣一气，仅仅因为我们早上起床、同意出现在一天的舞台上，就嘲笑我们（亲爱的同事，无需你从你的单身公寓里跑出来告诉我们这一点，即使裤子拉链没扣好）。仿佛我们的每一天都注定与成功背道而驰。

*

‘At dinner in the sanatorium one day I used a particularly attentive phrase to my neighbour at table during a conversation which did not much interest me, and was very conventional in tenor…’

“有一天在疗养院吃晚饭时，我跟邻桌聊着天，谈话内容我并不感兴趣，而且也很老套……”

Freud offers a dressing-down of belle époque life, and in such epitomized forms that he often seems to be riding that distinctly Viennese observation car, the aphorism: ‘Girls who are proud of their beautiful hair arrange their combs and hairpins so skilfully that their hair is bound to come down in the middle of a conversation’; ‘I once treated a patient whose morbid fear of reading newspapers turned out to be a reaction against his morbid ambition to see himself mentioned in print’; ‘aristocrats are particularly apt to distort the names of the doctors they have consulted’; women (who are forever forgetting to pay their analysts) ‘pay, as it were, with their looks’. Freud breaks intellectual rank by noticing what lies below the threshold of attention, and he breaks social rank by noticing cracks in the smooth glass of ritual. 2

弗洛伊德对美好年代的生活进行了辛辣的讽刺，他以极其精炼的方式，仿佛乘坐着维也纳特有的观光车厢，抛出了这样一句格言：“那些为自己美丽的秀发感到自豪的女孩，会巧妙地梳理梳子和发夹，以至于她们的头发总会在谈话中途散落下来”；“我曾治疗过一位病人，他对阅读报纸的病态恐惧，最终被证实是对他渴望在报纸上看到自己名字的病态野心的一种反抗”；“贵族们尤其容易歪曲他们咨询过的医生的名字”；而那些总是忘记支付分析师费用的女人们，“仿佛是用她们的容貌来支付”。弗洛伊德通过注意到那些隐藏在注意力阈值之下的东西，打破了知识分子的等级制度；他通过注意到仪式光鲜外表下的裂痕，打破了社会等级制度。

At the same time he builds up a picture of fin-de-siècle Vienna in full dress, and Everyday Life is the exploded Baedeker of its rites of passage, its ordeals of civility. Think of the complexity of codes of dress or forms of address, of what it meant to be incorrectly addressed or announced, of the vertiginous decorum of family life, of the rules that govern entering (‘falling’) into conversation with a stranger. There is no stumbling without thresholds — the more rituals, the more trespass.

与此同时，他描绘了一幅世纪末维也纳盛装打扮的景象，《日常生活》就像是一部浓缩版的维也纳礼仪指南，展现了当时的种种礼节和礼仪考验。想想看，当时的着装规范和称呼方式有多么复杂，被错误称呼或宣读信息意味着什么，家庭生活中令人眼花缭乱的礼仪，以及与陌生人交谈时必须遵守的种种规则。没有门槛，就不会有磕磕绊绊——仪式越多，越容易越过界限。

‘One lady said or intended to say admiringly to another: “I expect you trimmed that pretty new hat yourself?” but instead of aufgeputzt [trimmed] said aufgepatzt [echoing the word Patzerei , a clumsy job].’

一位女士对另一位女士说（或本想说）赞赏的话：“我想这顶漂亮的新帽子应该是你自己修剪的吧？”但她没有说 aufgeputzt（修剪），而是说了 aufgepatzt（与 Patzerei 一词重复，意为笨拙的工作）。

(inserted in 1907). Or the niece who, when asked how her uncle is, says: ‘I don’t know; these days I see him only in flagranti [for en passant]’; or the uncle who, when his nieces leave after paying him a long overdue visit, says with much feeling: ‘Well, from now on I hope to see you still more seldom than before’; or this, entranced specimen, of a bungled or ‘mishandled’ ( vergreift ) action, supplied by Freud’s colleague Stekel (also added in 1907):

（1907年插入）。又如，侄女被问及叔叔近况时说：“我不知道；这些天我只在路上见过他。”；又如，叔叔在侄女们久别重逢后离开时，满怀深情地说：“好吧，从今以后，我希望比以前更少见到你们。”；又如，弗洛伊德的同事斯特克尔提供的这个令人着迷的例子，一个笨拙或“处理不当”（vergreift）的行为（同样于1907年添加）：

I entered someone’s home, and gave the lady of the house my right hand. Oddly enough, in the process I untied the bow holding her loose morning dress together. I was not aware of any dishonourable intentions, yet I had performed this unskilful movement with a conjuror’s sleight of hand.

我走进一户人家，向女主人伸出了右手。奇怪的是，在这个过程中，我竟然解开了她宽松晨礼服上的蝴蝶结。我当时并没有任何不轨之举，却用魔术师般的手法完成了这个笨拙的动作。

The shame-culture of fin-d’empire Vienna is selectively but mordantly on view throughout Everyday Life , as is the contemporary passion for self-betrayal, in other words, for new forms of self-display. As Stefan Zweig remarked in his memoir, Those Were The Days (1942): ‘our entire generation was inhibited in its freedom of speech by the pressure of the times’. Contemporary Austria-Hungary was monarchical, clerical, militarist, socially and politically restrictive in respect of minorities. More significant for the culture of the parapraxis, the bourgeoisie was itself constituted as an outside caste, forever seeking assimilation with the aristocracy, and the strong assimilationist Jewish element within the Viennese bour-geoise redoubled or exemplified these emphases. The parapraxis thrives along fault-lines, and Hapsburg Vienna is the home of the slip because it is here that bourgeois rectitude encounters a highly developed critical spirit — mixing psychologism, experiment and what Zweig in his memoirs evoked as ‘an atmosphere of dangerous erotic infection’. 3 In polite life a host of taboos had to be negotiated — or scrambled in the dyslexicon of the verbal slip: sex, politics, money, the Jewish question, authority, relations with colleagues, professional self-esteem. Some of these, it has been argued — such as class relations and the fear of revolution — were so censored as to be conspicuously absent even from Freud’s array of examples. 4 Freud diagnoses slips of the tongue as exposing ‘an inner insincerity’; but they are also forms of authenticity: sharp sayings, acts of ventriloquial outspokenness where we momentarily disown society — instead of ourselves — for teaching us manners. (Lacan: ‘through slips of the tongue we discover our own voice’.)

在《日常生活》中，帝国末期维也纳的羞耻文化被选择性地、却又尖锐地展现出来，当代人对自我背叛的热情，换言之，对新型自我展示方式的追求，也同样如此。正如斯蒂芬·茨威格在其回忆录《那些日子》（1942）中所述：“我们这一代人都因时代的压力而丧失了言论自由。”当时的奥匈帝国是一个君主制、教权主义、军国主义盛行的国家，在社会和政治上对少数群体都采取了严格的限制。更重要的是，对于这种矫揉造作的文化而言，资产阶级本身就被视为一个外来阶级，始终寻求与贵族阶层同化，而维也纳资产阶级中强烈的犹太同化倾向则强化或体现了这种倾向。口误沿着断层线滋生，而哈布斯堡王朝统治下的维也纳正是口误的发源地，因为正是在这里，资产阶级的正直与高度发展的批判精神相遇——融合了心理学、实验以及茨威格在其回忆录中所描述的“一种危险的情欲感染的氛围”。在文明社会中，一系列禁忌必须被协商——或者说，在口误的语言障碍中被打乱：性、政治、金钱、犹太人问题、权威、与同事的关系、职业自尊。有人认为，其中一些——例如阶级关系和对革命的恐惧——受到如此严苛的审查，以至于即使在弗洛伊德的一系列例子中也明显缺失。弗洛伊德将口误诊断为暴露了“内在的虚伪”；但它们也是真实性的体现：犀利的言辞，如同腹语般直言不讳的行为，让我们暂时与社会——而非我们自己——决裂，因为社会教会了我们礼仪。（拉康：“通过口误，我们发现了自己的声音。”）

It was often remarked, at the time, that the good citizens of Vienna flocked to the theatre so as to learn how to be Viennese. The architectural façade-ism of Vienna was the backdrop. Freud takes for granted the innate theatricality of everyday life, and focuses upon its gestic aspect, its surfaces. (‘Where are the depths concealed?’ asked Hugo von Hoffmansthal, and answered: ‘On the surface.’) Put differently, there can be no difference between watching an actorimitate a parapraxis on stage and seeing an acquaintance commit a parapraxis in real life. In both cases the spectacle is the same: the faultless performance of a fault. The parapraxis has something in common with the improvisings of Sartrean mauvaise foi. Like Sartre’s waiter (the superbia of whose every gesture proclaims: ‘I am a waiter in the function of being what I am not’), the parapraxis makes no mistakes. Sartre invented situations to illustrate bad faith playing out its daily script. Were we suddenly to discover that Freud’s examples were all inventions — some of them undoubtedly are inventions, and some of Freud’s collaborators, notably Stekel, were far from reliable as sources — it is not clear how this would compromise their validity.

当时人们常说，维也纳的市民们蜂拥至剧院，学习如何成为维也纳人。维也纳的建筑立面主义便是这幕布。弗洛伊德认为日常生活本身就具有戏剧性，并着重关注其姿态层面和表面现象。（“深层隐藏在哪里？”雨果·冯·霍夫曼斯塔尔问道，并回答说：“就在表面。”）换句话说，观看演员在舞台上模仿口误，与观看熟人在现实生活中犯口误并无本质区别。在这两种情况下，奇观都是一样的：完美地演绎错误。口误与萨特笔下“坏的自恋”（mauvaise foi）的即兴发挥有某种共通之处。就像萨特的侍者（他的每一个动作都体现着一种傲慢：“我是一个侍者，但我扮演的却是我不是的人”），口误本身不会出错。萨特虚构了一些情境来阐释不诚信的日常运作。如果我们突然发现弗洛伊德的例子都是虚构的——其中一些无疑是虚构的，而且弗洛伊德的一些合作者，特别是斯特克尔，作为信息来源也远非可靠——我们并不清楚这会如何影响这些例子的有效性。

There is a generalized Proustian comedy of the surface in Everyday Life , reminiscent of an item from Proust’s own correspondence, which suggests how all slips enact the belatedness of all self-knowledge:

《日常生活》中存在一种普遍的普鲁斯特式的表面喜剧，让人想起普鲁斯特自己信件中的一段话，暗示所有的失误都体现了所有自我认知的迟延性：

My dear Madam, I just noticed that I forgot my cane at your house yesterday; please be good enough to give it to the bearer of this letter. P.S. Kindly pardon me for disturbing you; I have just found my cane.

亲爱的夫人，我昨天才发现把拐杖忘在您家了；请您好心把它交给送信人。附：打扰您了，请您谅解；我刚刚找到了我的拐杖。

From this compound example of a forgetting accompanied by a social gesture so recondite as to be nameless, the elite could be said to have incorporated the slip into its charades, its own needy endgame ceremonies, rather than ceremony being simply exposed or compromised by the slip. 5 And Freud’s text can seem like a contemporary reader’s guide to A la recherche du temps perdu , which was appearing in instalments during the same two decades as the recensions of Everyday Life. In both ventures, minor arcana to do with the social presentation of the self were subject to a critique of unprecedented acuity, and rendered suddenly intelligible to themselves. The pathos of both texts consists in their intimation that, for the society they describe, this knowledge is too late, is a form of esprit d’escalier , more autopsy than diagnosis.

从这个遗忘与一种晦涩难懂、难以名状的社会姿态相结合的复合例子中，可以说精英阶层将这种失言融入了他们的伪装，融入了他们自身那需要被认可的最终仪式，而不是仪式本身仅仅因为失言而暴露或受损。 5 弗洛伊德的文本似乎可以看作是当代读者对《追忆似水年华》（A la recherche du temps perdu）的指南，后者与《日常生活》（Everyday Life）的修订版在同一时期以连载形式出版。在这两部作品中，与自我社会呈现相关的细微之处都受到了前所未有的敏锐批判，并突然变得易于理解。两部作品的悲怆之处在于，它们暗示，对于它们所描述的社会而言，这种认知为时已晚，是一种“爬楼梯”式的精神，与其说是诊断，不如说是尸检。

*

‘I was sitting in a café, turning over the pages of the Leipziger Illustrierte…’

“我坐在一家咖啡馆里，翻着《莱比锡画报》……”

Since the 1860s, urban life at large had been described along primarily sociological lines — criticized or praised for having eroded the partitions of class. In a state of uncertainty, when the categories have become equivocal, the need to find under-described but solving mechanisms in ordinary life became pressing. Freud’s is not the first systematic attempt, but the first anti-sociological attempt to find a new code for interpreting social display. The city-dweller gives nothing away, except what is given away for free, and which cannot be used. Parapraxes say everything about the need to give things away, by accident, in ways that can only be paraphrased. Freud laid down rules for the investigation of these accidents. The parapraxis must be ‘within the range of normality’; it must be motiveless (‘if we notice the slip at all, we must not recognize any motivation for it in ourselves; instead, we must be tempted to put it down to “carelessness” or “chance”’); and it must be ‘a brief and temporary disturbance’ (‘If someone else corrects our slip, we must immediately acknowledge the justice of the correction’). Noticeable here is that Freud makes the agent of discovery the final arbiter of intentions.

自19世纪60年代以来，城市生活主要以社会学的视角进行描述——人们或批评或赞扬它削弱了阶级界限。在不确定状态下，当各种范畴变得模糊不清时，在日常生活中寻找那些鲜为人知但却能解决问题的机制变得迫切起来。弗洛伊德并非首次进行系统性的尝试，但却是首次反社会学地尝试寻找一套新的社会行为解读准则。城市居民不会轻易付出任何东西，除非是免费赠送的、无法使用的物品。言语失用症（parapraxis）以一种只能被转述的方式，无形地揭示了人们想要付出东西的需要。弗洛伊德为研究这些意外事件制定了规则。言语失用症必须“在正常范围内”；它必须是无动机的（“如果我们注意到这种失误，我们不能从自身的角度去思考它；相反，我们必须倾向于将其归因于‘粗心’或‘偶然’”）。而且这必须是“短暂的干扰”（“如果有人纠正了我们的错误，我们必须立即承认这种纠正的合理性”）。值得注意的是，弗洛伊德将发现者视为意图的最终仲裁者。

At the same time, parapraxes allow us knowledge of other minds only as passers-by. They are part of the timing of the self. Freud’s individuals are mobile, in transit, caught between inside and outside. On stage so briefly, they perform actions that are incomplete, their stories are unfinished, amenable only because stalled momentarily along the via negativa of the mistake. The parapraxis re-imagines what William James called ‘the continuous flow of the mental stream’ as a stopping clock, as if these are the terms for knowing a subject who cannot be interpreted at leisure. Kafka pondered ‘the picture of dissatisfaction presented by a street, where everyone is perpetually lifting his feet to escape from the place on which he stands’. Mistakes are glimpses, registered in einem zug , whose idiomatic sense is ‘in one go’, but whose literal meaning is ‘on a train’. (In a recent academic misreading, we are told that Kafka’s story ‘The Judgement’ was written on a train — rather than, as Kafka confided to his diary, ‘at one sitting’ — a case of an error or a slip?) Hanns Sachs, repository of Freud’s many examples of the parapraxis in time of war, offered the following in 1917:

与此同时，语误让我们只能以过客的身份了解他人的思想。它们是自我时间流逝的一部分。弗洛伊德笔下的个体是流动的，处于过渡状态，徘徊于内外之间。他们在舞台上短暂出现，他们的行为是不完整的，他们的故事未完待续，之所以能够被理解，仅仅是因为他们在错误的否定之路上暂时停滞。语误将威廉·詹姆斯所说的“精神之流的持续流动”重新想象成一个停止运转的时钟，仿佛这就是理解一个无法被悠闲解读的主体的方式。卡夫卡思考着“一条街道所呈现的不满景象，每个人都在不停地抬起脚，试图逃离自己所站的地方”。错误是惊鸿一瞥，记录在“一趟”（einem zug）之中，其习语含义是“一气呵成”，但其字面含义是“在火车上”。 （最近学术界出现了一种误读，有人说卡夫卡的小说《审判》是在火车上写成的，而不是像卡夫卡在日记中透露的那样“一气呵成”——这究竟是笔误还是失误？）汉斯·萨克斯，这位收集了弗洛伊德在战争时期诸多口误案例的学者，在1917年提出了以下观点：

Sitting in the tram, I was thinking that many of the friends of my youth, who had always been considered delicate and frail, now seemed able to stand up to the harshest of conditions which would certainly have a shattering effect on me. In the middle of this unwelcome train of thought, as we were passing a firm’s signboard, I was only half aware of registering, as we passed, a word in big black letters saying Eisenkonstitution [iron constitution]. A moment later it struck me that this was not really right for a business sign, and turning back quickly I caught another glimpse of the inscription, and saw that it really read Eisenkonstruktion [Iron Construction].

坐在电车里，我心想，我年轻时的许多朋友，他们一直被认为体弱多病，如今却似乎能承受最严酷的考验，而这些考验对我来说肯定会是毁灭性的。正当我沉浸在这种不愉快的思绪中时，我们经过一家公司的招牌，我隐约看到上面用黑色大字写着“Eisenkonstitution”（钢铁结构）。片刻之后，我意识到这不太像商业招牌上的字，于是赶紧回头又看了一眼，发现上面写的其实是“Eisenkonstruktion”（钢铁结构）。

Everything in Everyday Life — including trains of thought — may be imagined as taking place on a train. (The railway was the most visible sign of Austria-Hungary’s belated industrialization: 3,000 km of track in 1860, 20,000 km in 1910.) Or there is the moving escalator of the street — ‘It was true that I had passed the display-window countless times’; ‘I had gone down every other street in the area, avoiding only this single one as if it were forbidden’ — which contributes to the atmospherics of the text, in thrall to the circularities and symptoms it diagnoses. There is often a dreamlike mutuality between slip and explanation, as with the patient of Freud’s who

日常生活中的一切——包括思维的流动——都可以被想象成发生在火车上。（铁路是奥匈帝国姗姗来迟的工业化最显著的标志：1860年铁路里程为3000公里，1910年达到20000公里。）或者，街道上就像自动扶梯一样——“我确实无数次经过那个橱窗”；“我走遍了这片区域的每一条街道，唯独避开了这条，仿佛它是禁区”——这些都为文本营造了一种氛围，一种对循环往复和所诊断的症状的沉迷。在口误和解释之间，常常存在一种梦幻般的相互依存，就像弗洛伊德的病人那样……

‘…thought that recently he had seen a work on Agoraphobia in the display window of a bookshop, and tried to get hold of it by consulting all the publishers’ catalogues. I was then able to explain why his efforts were bound to be unsuccessful: the work on agorapobia existed only in his imagination as an unconscious intention, because he was planning to write such a book himself.’

“……他最近在一家书店的橱窗里看到了一本关于广场恐惧症的书，于是查阅了所有出版社的目录，想找到这本书。这时我才明白为什么他的努力注定徒劳：那本关于广场恐惧症的书只存在于他的想象中，是一种无意识的意图，因为他正计划自己写一本这样的书。”

Thus do we go prospecting with our errors.

于是，我们带着错误去探索未来。

These repetitions without variation anticipate Freud’s definitive account of being parapractically lost while walking the streets — in his paper on ‘The Uncanny’ (1919) — with its insidious intent and its overwhelming question:

这些没有变化的重复预示了弗洛伊德在其论文《论怪诞》（1919 年）中对在街上行走时迷路这一现象的权威描述——其中蕴含着阴险的意图和令人震惊的问题：

Strolling one hot summer afternoon through the empty and to me unfamiliar streets of a small Italian town, I found myself in a district about whose character I could not long remain in doubt. Only heavily made-up women were to be seen at the windows of the little houses, and I hastily left the narrow street at the next turning. However, after wandering about for some time without asking the way, I suddenly found myself back in the same street, where my presence began to attract attention. Once more I hurried away, only to return there again by a different route. I was now seized by a feeling that I can only describe as uncanny…

在一个炎热的夏日午后，我漫步在意大利一座小镇空旷而陌生的街道上。不知不觉间，我走进了一个街区，对这里的氛围很快就有了疑虑。街边小房子的窗户里，只有浓妆艳抹的女人在晃悠。我赶紧在下一个拐角处离开了这条狭窄的街道。然而，我漫无目的地闲逛了一会儿，也没问路，却突然发现自己又回到了同一条街上。这时，我又换了一条路，再次回到了那里。一种难以言喻的怪异感觉涌上心头……

The ‘uncanny’ ( Unheimlich ) exists in rich because apparent opposition to the heimlich (the ‘homely’, the ‘familiar’ — the ‘concealed’). In Everyday Life Freud praises Strindberg for the ‘uncanny faithfulness’ of his depiction of the ‘secret nature’ of minor symptomatic acts and parapraxes, for example in his novel The Gothic Booms. Home is the heart of the matter, because everything uncanny entails an act of recognition, and the power of E. T. A. Hoffmann’s story ‘The Sand Man’ (the text at the heart of Freud’s essay) is that he invades the home. As Baudelaire put the matter in a memo to himself: ‘Study of The Great Malady: horror of Home’. The parapraxis is an unhoused action, and it wires the outdoors for gothic recognitions. Many of Freud’s examples casually fix upon this aspect of a situation, as with the woman who gets run over in the street, in the chapter on bungled actions: That morning there were almost no vehicles about, since the trams, omnibuses, etc., were on strike — there was almost absolute calm at the time.’

“怪诞”（Unheimlich）之所以丰富，是因为它与“家常”（heimlich，即“熟悉的”、“熟悉的”、“隐秘的”）形成明显的对立。在《日常生活》中，弗洛伊德赞扬斯特林堡对轻微症状行为和口误的“隐秘本质”的描绘具有“怪诞的忠实性”，例如在他的小说《哥特式繁荣》中。家是问题的核心，因为一切怪诞都包含一种认知行为，而E.T.A.霍夫曼的小说《睡魔》（弗洛伊德论文的核心文本）的力量在于它入侵了家庭。正如波德莱尔在一份备忘录中写道：“对大病的研究：家庭的恐惧”。口误是一种无处可寻的行为，它将户外空间与哥特式的认知联系起来。弗洛伊德的许多例子都随意地聚焦于这种情况的这一方面，例如在关于笨拙行为的章节中提到的在街上被车撞倒的女人：那天早上几乎没有车辆，因为电车、公共汽车等都在罢工——当时几乎一片绝对平静。

*

Here men walk alone

这里的男人独自行走

For most of their lives,

在他们生命的大部分时间里，

What with hydrants for dogs,

给狗狗用的消防栓，

And windows for wives.

还有给妻子的窗户。

(Ogden Nash, ‘City’)

（奥格登·纳什，《城市》）

Everyday Life is a plein-air forum of individual acts both joined and isolated inside collective life, as of a turning away from privacy and its reticences towards improvised forms: streets, cafes, resorts. Always a model of the unconscious, for Freud, the agora joins sleeping with waking and walking, since the structure of the dream has its equivalent in ordinary waking life, and the city is the topographical and psychic, mnemonic and syntactical form that the day takes. It is a marketplace, but for the exchange of what? — if not mistakes. Freud’s focus upon citizens recalls Marx’s dictum that the bourgeoisie can never arrive at a perfectly clear awareness of itself. As if parapraxes and their acknowledgement are the attempt of a certain historical type to pinch himself awake before it is too late. Freud focuses a general nomadism, the picaresque of selves caught off-balance, giving themselves away, prey to ‘momentary and temporary disturbance’. And this is of a piece with the untethered drift of examples. The text contains a flotsam of decorously displaced persons (‘An American staying in Europe…), who could be said to stand in for or are themselves displacements of an untidier reality: behind the scenes of Everyday Life. Vienna was filling up with an influx of settlers and luftmenschen , becoming a laboratory of social anomie, an old world full of new arrivals. And in later editions, when history eerily catches up with Everyday Life , the universal displacement of the First World War provokes a haemorrhage of new examples of error and slippage. Embedded in Freud’s text — at fairytale depth — are the only real homes, the homes away from home (pensione, spas, sanatoria), a parallel world of witness and gossip beyond the everyday.

日常生活是一个露天的论坛，个人的行为既融入集体生活又彼此孤立，仿佛是从私密及其缄默转向即兴形式：街道、咖啡馆、度假胜地。对于弗洛伊德而言，广场始终是无意识的典范，它将睡眠与清醒和行走连接起来，因为梦的结构在日常清醒生活中有着对应的体现，而城市则是白天的地形、心理、记忆和句法形式。它是一个市场，但交换的是什么呢？——如果不是错误的话。弗洛伊德对公民的关注让人想起马克思的格言：资产阶级永远无法完全清晰地认识自己。仿佛口误及其承认是某种历史类型在为时已晚之前试图让自己清醒过来的一种尝试。弗洛伊德关注的是一种普遍的游牧性，一种失衡的自我的流浪生活，他们袒露心扉，成为“短暂的干扰”的牺牲品。这与那些不受约束的例证如出一辙。文本中充斥着形形色色的流离失所者（“一个待在欧洲的美国人……”），他们或许代表着，或者本身就是某种更为混乱的现实的流离失所者：日常生活幕后的真相。维也纳涌入了大量的移民和“空中飞人”，成为社会失范的实验室，一个充满新来者的旧世界。在后来的版本中，当历史诡异地追上《日常生活》时，第一次世界大战造成的普遍流离失所引发了大量新的错误和偏差例证。在弗洛伊德的文本中——如同童话般深邃——隐藏着唯一真正的家，远离家乡的家（旅馆、温泉疗养院、疗养院），一个超越日常生活的、充满见证和流言蜚语的平行世界。

One of the locales of the parapraxis is commodity — error whose nexus is things seen, displayed, purchased, places visited and thereby colonized. Everyday life condenses into spectacle. ‘When I am on holiday and walking down the street in a foreign town…I read every shop sign that suggests the word in any way at all as Antiques. This must be an expression of my interests as a collector’. Many of the examples concern things desired, hesitated over, mislaid, misconstrued. There is a constant va-et-vient between physical and psychic realms; to mislay something is a kind of forgetting, to forget something is a kind of mislaying (‘just before the accident she had seen a pretty picture in a shop on the opposite side of the street’; ‘I like to use good blotting paper, and on my afternoon walk into the inner city I meant to buy some’; ‘When I saw the book…in the shop window I did not at first intend to buy it. However, a few days later I decided that I would, but by then the book was not in the window.’) Props of potentially farcical materiality abound: rings, fountain pens, watches, keys, pipes, stairs, letters, telephones, books. More generally, the Freudian metropolis is a collapsing empire of signs, a scene of miscognition. Or of coincidence. In a renunciatory embrace, Everyday Life denies chance actions — which it sees everywhere, and from which Surrealism was to take its cues — in favour of examples and explanations which are themselves coincidences.

误用行为的场所之一是商品——错误的根源在于所见、所展示、所购买的物品，以及所到之处，进而被其所“殖民”。日常生活被浓缩成奇观。“当我在异国他乡度假，走在街上……我把所有带有‘古董’字样的商店招牌都解读成‘古董’。这一定是出于我作为收藏家的兴趣。”许多例子都与渴望之物、犹豫之物、遗失之物、误解之物有关。物质世界和精神世界之间存在着一种持续的虚幻性；遗失某物是一种遗忘，遗忘某物也是一种遗失（“就在事故发生前，她在街对面的一家商店里看到了一幅漂亮的画”；“我喜欢用吸墨纸，那天下午我去市中心散步时打算买一些”；“当我看到那本书……在商店橱窗里时，我起初并没有打算买。然而，几天后我决定要买，但那时那本书已经不在橱窗里了。”）各种可能带有滑稽色彩的物质道具比比皆是：戒指、钢笔、手表、钥匙、烟斗、楼梯、信件、电话、书籍。更广泛地说，弗洛伊德式的都市是一个正在崩塌的符号帝国，一个认知错误或巧合的场景。《日常生活》以一种弃绝的态度，否定了偶然行为——它认为偶然行为无处不在，而超现实主义正是从中汲取灵感——转而支持那些本身就是巧合的例子和解释。

*

To see is to forget the names of the things one sees.

看见之后，就会忘记所见之物的名称。

(Paul Valéry)

（保罗·瓦雷里）

‘[T]emporarily forgetting names is one of the most frequent observed of all slips of the mind,’ says Freud, and one of the forms of hide-and-seek played out in Everyday Life concerns naming and not-naming. A Herr Lederer, on honeymoon in Venice, runs across an acquaintance whom he reluctantly introduces to his new wife. Since he has forgotten the man’s name he gets by with ‘murmuring something indistinct’. When they meet again (‘as was bound to happen in Venice’) he draws him aside and asks him for help: “‘I can easily believe that you didn’t remember my name,” says the prescient other, “— it’s Lederer , like yours!”’ Or there is the timid but ambitious young doctor who parapractically introduces himself to the celebrated pathologist Dr Virchow as — ‘Dr Virchow’. Or the young father who presents himself before the registrar of births to give notice of the birth of his second daughter. ‘When asked the child’s name he replied: “Hanna”. “But you already have a child called Hanna,” the registrar told him.’ This stealthy convergence of names occurs because your name — whatever it is — calls up my personal associations; in a sense, we all have the same name, because any name will do the job. Karl Kraus described Austria-Hungary as ‘this pseudonymous civilization’, and one of the poles of his satire is to regard all names as duplicitous — Germanized Jewish names above all. The pages of Die Faekel , the journal that Kraus edited from 1899 (and in which Freud’s name often appeared) read like a telephone directory. Kraus names multitudes of names, but mockingly claims to be making them all up: in each instance the accused coincidentally bears the name of an actual person.

弗洛伊德说：“暂时忘记名字是所有记忆失误中最常见的一种。”《日常生活》中上演的捉迷藏游戏之一就与命名和不命名有关。莱德勒先生在威尼斯度蜜月时，偶遇一位熟人，他很不情愿地将他介绍给新婚妻子。由于他忘记了对方的名字，便含糊其辞地嘟囔了几句。当他们再次相遇时（“在威尼斯，这几乎是必然的”），他把对方拉到一边，请他帮忙：“‘我完全相信你记不起我的名字，’这位先见之明的人说道，‘——我的名字是莱德勒，和你一样！’” 还有一位胆怯却雄心勃勃的年轻医生，他几乎是脱口而出地向著名的病理学家维尔肖博士介绍自己时，说自己是——“维尔肖博士”。或者，一位年轻的父亲来到出生登记处，登记他第二个女儿的出生。“当被问及孩子的名字时，他回答说：‘汉娜’。“但你已经有一个孩子叫汉娜了，”登记员告诉他。这种名字的巧妙重合，是因为你的名字——无论是什么——都会唤起我个人的联想；从某种意义上说，我们都拥有同一个名字，因为任何名字都能起到同样的作用。卡尔·克劳斯将奥匈帝国描述为“一个伪名化的文明”，他讽刺的重点之一就是将所有名字都视为双重的——尤其是那些德意志化的犹太名字。克劳斯从1899年开始编辑的期刊《Die Faekel》（弗洛伊德的名字也经常出现在其中）的内容读起来就像一本电话簿。克劳斯列举了无数个名字，却又嘲讽地声称这些都是他编造的：在每个例子中，被指控的人都恰好与某个真实存在的人同名。

Freud unaccountably forgets the first name of a young man, the brother of one of his patients, who appears in his consulting room, whom he has seen countless times, and whose name is by no means unusual. ‘I went out into the street to read the signboards over the business premises, and recognized the name as soon as I encountered it.’ He ponders the reasons for this forgetting, in terms of the family story (what are brothers for?), but his symptomatic solution to the quandary of forgetting goes unremarked. That the privacy of a name (‘the name is an integral part of the personality’ we are told elsewhere) is to be found posted in the street is part of the book’s uninvestigated suspensions. On the one hand, the argument of Everyday Life is legitimated by names (streets, shops, literary characters, historical figures, titles of books, authorities, colleagues, contributors of examples) — by the belief that objects, including slips, can be named and thereby located. On the other hand, it is a book in which no one is named. The individuals whose short stories are its concern remain unindividuated (‘A certain Herr Y. fell in love with a lady who did not return his affection, and soon afterwards married another man, Herr X.’), like the hubbub of backs and faces which is our sight of each other amid the surrounding overspecification. In Freud’s text, precisions as to place always ensure anonymity of persons. And when the same examples from Everyday Life are reproduced much later in the Introductory Lectures , the peripheral focus often sharpens. ‘One day in the Dolomites I met two ladies in walking dress’ becomes ‘I once met two Viennese ladies in the lovely Dolomites…’ The more precision, the more anonymity, rather in the manner of the Sherlock Holmes stories to which Freud was addicted.

弗洛伊德莫名其妙地忘记了一个年轻人的名字，此人是他一位病人的弟弟，曾无数次出现在他的诊室里，而且名字也并不罕见。“我走到街上去看商店的招牌，一眼就认出了他的名字。”他从家族故事的角度思考自己为何会忘记（兄弟不就是用来干这个的吗？），但他对遗忘困境的症状性解释却无人提及。书中未加探究的名字隐私（我们在其他地方被告知“名字是人格不可分割的一部分”）竟然出现在街头，这本身就是书中未加探究的悬置之一。一方面，《日常生活》的论点以名字（街道、商店、文学人物、历史人物、书名、权威人士、同事、例证提供者）为依据——基于这样一种信念：事物，包括笔误，都可以被命名，从而被定位。另一方面，这本书里却没有任何人被提及名字。短篇小说中涉及的人物始终保持着模糊不清的形象（“某位Y先生爱上了一位不爱他的女士，不久后便嫁给了另一位男士，X先生。”），如同我们身处过度描述之中，彼此之间如同嘈杂的背影和面孔。在弗洛伊德的文本中，对地点的精确描述总是确保了人物的匿名性。而当《日常生活》中的相同例子在之后的《导论讲义》中再次出现时，这种边缘化的关注点往往会更加清晰。“有一天在多洛米蒂山脉，我遇到了两位身着休闲装的女士”变成了“我曾在美丽的多洛米蒂山脉遇到两位维也纳女士……”越是精确，匿名性就越强，这与弗洛伊德痴迷的福尔摩斯探案故事颇为相似。

This is dramatized in an allusion to the Fragment of an Analysis of a Case History (‘ Dora ’), which he was writing up in the first months of 1901, interrupting Everyday Life to do so. ‘When I was preparing the case history of a woman patient of mine for publication, I wondered what first name to give her.’ There would naturally appear to be an unlimited choice of available names. ‘Instead, only a single name came into my mind: — the name Dora. ’ Freud asks himself why — who else was there called Dora?

这一点在弗洛伊德1901年初撰写的《病例分析片段》（“朵拉”）中得到了戏剧化的体现，当时他甚至中断了《日常生活》的写作。“当我准备发表一位女病人的病例时，我在想该给她取什么名字。” 显然，可供选择的名字数不胜数。“然而，我脑海中却只浮现出一个名字：——朵拉。” 弗洛伊德不禁自问：为什么？除了她，还有谁叫朵拉呢？

I felt like rejecting the next idea to occur to me as incredible, for it told me that the nanny who looked after my sister’s children was called Dora, but I had enough self-discipline, or enough experience of analysis, to follow that idea and take it further. I immediately thought of a small incident the previous evening, which brought me the association determining the name I was seeking. I saw a letter addressed to ‘Fräulein Rosa W.’ lying on the table in my sister’s dining room. In surprise, I asked who that was, and learned that the nanny Dora was really called Rosa, but had been obliged to change her name on entering the household because my sister is a Rosa too and could have taken the name to mean herself. I said, sympathetically: Poor servants, they can’t even keep their own names! And now that I came to think of it, I said no more for a moment, but began meditating on various serious subjects. My thoughts trailed vaguely away, but I could now easily recall them to my conscious mind. So when next day I was looking for a name for someone who could not he allowed to keep her own , only Dora sprang to mind.

我感觉接下来冒出的一个想法简直不可思议，因为它告诉我，照顾我姐姐孩子的保姆名叫朵拉。但我自律性够强，或许分析能力也足够，所以决定顺着这个想法继续往下思考。我立刻想起前一天晚上发生的一件小事，正是这件事让我联想到了我一直在寻找的名字。我看到姐姐餐厅的桌子上放着一封写着“罗莎·W小姐”的信。我惊讶地问她是谁，才知道保姆朵拉其实就叫罗莎，但她来我家后不得不改名，因为我姐姐也叫罗莎，可能会误以为这个名字指的是她自己。我同情地说：可怜的佣人，连自己的名字都不能保留！想到这里，我沉默了一会儿，开始思考一些严肃的问题。我的思绪飘忽不定，但现在我很容易就能把它们记下来。所以第二天，当我为一个不能保留自己名字的人寻找名字时，脑海中只浮现出朵拉这个名字。

The Dora of Everyday Life is a shadow, one of the recessive governesses and servants who hover at the edges of the text, dropping fragile articles, mutely hostile to objets d’art. They constitute a doubling of ourselves, too close for comfort (for we too drop things), a stock from which contemporaries such as Walser and Kafka were to recruit heroes without qualities.

《日常生活中的朵拉》中的朵拉是一个影子，是文本边缘徘徊的那些隐匿的家庭教师和仆人之一，她们会丢掉易碎物品，对艺术品怀有无声的敌意。她们构成了我们自身的镜像，过于接近，令人不安（因为我们也会丢东西），她们是瓦尔泽和卡夫卡等同时代作家用来塑造缺乏特质的英雄的素材库。

*

‘It reached me in a somewhat roundabout way, but comes from a reliable source…’

“我收到这个消息的方式有点绕，但消息来源可靠……”

The other Dora belongs to another world: however ‘fragmentary’ in construction, the case history offers a heroine, a plot, and the display of a selfhood without precedent. The this-world of the parapraxis offers only fugitive scenarios of the possible, and Everyday Life is a host of walk-ons: here conies everybody. With rare exceptions, Freud’s book is a study of errors rather than selves, of individual parapraxes rather than individual histories. His explanations largely refer to the recent past, to the experiences of adult life, rather than back to childhood. Which makes us wonder what children’s slips would be like, and whether parapraxes are not a developmental, phase-specific achievement. One of the more buried suggestions of Everyday Life — considered as a collection of biographemes — is that not all memories are stories, and not all remembering is storytelling. The cumulative effect of Freud’s anecdotes, far from interrupting his argument, is to replicate the mechanism of the slip as being, above all else, an interruption. As a unit of meaning, the parapraxis interrupts the narrative of our days, and as a unit of narrative it interrupts their meaning.

另一个朵拉属于另一个世界：尽管其结构“零散”，但这个案例却塑造了一个女主角、一个情节，以及一种前所未有的自我。而口误的现实世界只展现了转瞬即逝的可能性，《日常生活》则充斥着形形色色的人物：在这里，每个人都可能犯错。除了极少数例外，弗洛伊德的著作研究的是错误而非自我，研究的是个体的口误而非个体的历史。他的解释大多指向近期的过去，指向成年后的经历，而非童年时期。这让我们不禁思考，儿童的口误会是什么样子，口误是否是一种发展过程中的、特定阶段的成就。《日常生活》——如果将其视为一系列传记式文本——所蕴含的一个较为隐晦的观点是：并非所有的记忆都是故事，也并非所有的回忆都是在讲述故事。弗洛伊德的轶事累积起来，非但没有打断他的论证，反而强化了口误机制的本质——首先，它是一种中断。作为意义单位，口误打断了我们日常生活的叙事；作为叙事单位，口误打断了我们日常生活的意义。

Moreover, knowledge of slips can be acquired unproblematically at second- or third-hand, by hearsay and anecdote. ‘A good and easily explained example…is provided by the self-observation of one Herr J. G. while he was in a sanatorium’ — a circular moment, and part of the oddity with which the text stages its evidence. It makes the debate over the unfalsifiability of Freud’s explanations seem irrelevant: so unprivileged is the information from which they take their cue. The text has as many intermediaries — friends, colleagues, contributors — as characters. Moreover, it is a function of the ‘thinness’ of the slip — of its inauthenticity, even — that ‘some other slip could have functioned just as well’. The specific form that error takes is not determined by the concealed idea that it has disturbed — just as a slip of the tongue is determined not by the near identity of sounds themselves, but by thoughts that lie outside the intended speech-act. A parapraxis marks the spot, locates the fact but not the direction of deviation, and Everyday Life is concerned less with selves than with situations. Hence its low-wattage intensities, its shavings from the table of selfhood, its status as a study in residua. These moments have fallen out of a novel, and Everyday Life contains the opening sentences of innumerable unwritten novels (‘A young man staying in a mixed boarding house met an English woman…’; ‘By a coincidence, there was a guest from Paris in her lodgings at present…’). These remain unintegrated, like specimen sentences, utterances for a manual or etiquette book. As if our parapraxes, far from belonging to us, serve to undifferentiate us as subjects.

此外，关于口误的知识很容易通过二手甚至三手渠道、道听途说和轶事获得。“一个很好的、易于解释的例子……来自J.G.先生在疗养院期间的自我观察”——这是一个循环论证，也是文本呈现证据方式的怪异之处之一。这使得关于弗洛伊德解释是否不可证伪的争论显得无关紧要：因为他们所依据的信息如此缺乏权威性。文本中涉及的中间人——朋友、同事、撰稿人——与文本中的人物一样多。而且，正是由于口误的“薄弱性”——甚至是其不真实性——才使得“其他一些口误也能起到同样的作用”。错误的具体形式并非由它所扰乱的隐藏想法决定——正如口误并非由声音本身的近似性决定，而是由意图之外的想法决定一样。口误标记了地点，定位了事实，却无法指出偏差的方向。《日常生活》关注的与其说是自我，不如说是情境。因此，它的强度很低，它只是从自我意识的餐桌上刨下的碎屑，它更像是对残余的研究。这些瞬间仿佛是从小说中掉落出来的，《日常生活》包含了无数未完成小说的开头几句（“一个住在男女混住的寄宿公寓的年轻人遇到了一位英国女士……”；“碰巧，她住的地方现在正好有一位来自巴黎的客人……”）。这些句子保持着未整合的状态，如同示例句，如同手册或礼仪书中的语句。仿佛我们的口误非但不属于我们，反而使我们作为主体变得模糊不清。

Just as the slip is and is not an action, it is only partially interpretable. As an occurrence of doubtful status — did you say what I just heard you say? — its natural medium is the anecdote (‘a married woman, who liked a good story…’), or the higher gossip (‘A lady told me that when she last saw a common acquaintance…’). Freud notes our fascinated resistance when we are shown to have committed or are caught committing a parapraxis — ‘it is worth noting that no one likes admitting to a slip of the tongue’ — the slip is hearsay about ourselves, news from a foreign country. This might seem to distinguish slips from other forms of psychoanalytic knowing, but as Freud tells his audience in the Introductory Lectures : ‘You cannot be present at a psychoanalytic treatment. You can only be told about it; and, in the strictest sense of the word, it is only by hearsay that you will get to know psychoanalysis’ — as if theories are themselves anecdotes at one remove. Freud analysed Schreber on the basis of Schreber’s published Memoirs , which ‘took the place of’ personal acquaintance. There is always mediation, and in the extroversions of Everyday Life it is as if Freud’s brief lives become folkloric with accretion. (‘I am afraid that all the examples above have been rather commonplace…since my intention is solely to collect everyday material.’) Everyday life is a bush telegraph, and Everyday Life is an organon of the urban bungle. Experience is continuous — we all worry about the same things, we all make mistakes, our slips are interchangeable. Freud’s inclusion of misprints as ‘writing mistakes’ on the compositor’s part, or of telegram errors as writing mistakes on the telegraphist’s part, are yet ghostlier demarcations, ever further from a constituted human subject. At another remove, and this has an oddly complicating effect upon our sense of what kind of book it is that we are reading, one of the witnesses most frequently called upon in this pages is that form of hearsay known as literature, considered as a store of copia or convenient examples from Shakespeare to Strindberg. ‘We can only repeat what they said long ago,’ remarks Freud — or on occasion anticipate what they have yet to say.

正如口误既是行为又是行为一样，它也只能部分地被解读。作为一种性质存疑的事件——你刚才说的是我听到的吗？——它自然而然地以轶事（“一位喜欢听故事的已婚妇女……”）或更高级的闲言碎语（“一位女士告诉我，她上次见到一位共同认识的人时……”）的形式出现。弗洛伊德注意到，当我们被发现犯了口误或被抓到犯了口误时，我们会产生一种既着迷又抗拒的心理——“值得注意的是，没有人喜欢承认自己口误”——口误就像是关于我们自身的传闻，来自异国他乡的消息。这似乎将口误与其他形式的精神分析认知区分开来，但正如弗洛伊德在导论讲座中告诉他的听众：“你无法亲身参与精神分析治疗。你只能被告知治疗过程；而且，严格来说，你只能通过传闻来了解精神分析”——仿佛理论本身在某种程度上也是一种轶事。弗洛伊德根据施雷伯已出版的回忆录分析了他，这些回忆录“取代”了与施雷伯的私人交往。其中总存在着中介，在《日常生活》的外向叙述中，弗洛伊德短暂的人生经历仿佛随着积累而变得具有了民间传说的色彩。（“恐怕以上所有例子都相当平庸……因为我的目的仅仅是收集日常素材。”）日常生活就像一条简易的电报机，《日常生活》则是都市笨拙的象征。经验是连续的——我们都为同样的事情担忧，我们都会犯错，我们的失误可以互换。弗洛伊德将印刷错误归咎于排字工的“书写错误”，将电报错误归咎于电报员的书写错误，这些划分更加模糊不清，与构成完整的人类主体渐行渐远。换个角度来看——这会对我们理解所读书籍的类型产生一种奇特的复杂影响——本书中最常引用的证人之一，便是被称为“文学”的那种道听途说，它被视为从莎士比亚到斯特林堡等各种典故或例证的宝库。“我们只能重复他们很久以前说过的话，”弗洛伊德说道——或者偶尔预测他们尚未说过的话。

*

He happened to be putting some fresh water in the vase…

他当时正好在往花瓶里倒清水……

Although it takes the form of a treatise, Everyday Life has continuities with literary texts in which the modern was clarified as that which can be brought into view only by a process of blurring. The prestige of ‘accident’ is implied here, and Freud’s belief in the importance of the accidental — from lapsus linguae to quotidian routine — is part of a more general breach in the recalcitrance of the ordinary. How to make ordinary life visible is a central problem of aesthetics from Flaubert onwards: in other words, that area of experience which disqualifies itself as vestigial or discrepant, and which Freud qualified as the central concern of psychoanalysis: ‘the dregs of the world of appearances’ ( Introductory Lectures).

尽管《日常生活》以论著的形式呈现，但它与文学文本有着一脉相承之处，在这些文本中，现代性被阐释为唯有通过模糊的过程才能显现之物。“偶然性”的威望在此显露无疑，弗洛伊德对偶然性重要性的信念——从语言失误到日常惯例——正是对平凡事物顽固性的更普遍突破的一部分。如何使日常生活可见，自福楼拜以来便是美学的核心问题：换言之，即那些因被视为残余或矛盾而丧失自身价值的经验领域，弗洛伊德将其定义为精神分析的核心关注点：“表象世界的残渣”（《导论》）。

This common enterprise has its synchronicities. Between the appearance of The Psychopathology of Everyday Life in periodical form in 1901 and in book form in 1904, for example, Joyce was collecting fragments of overheard dialogue or found speech, which he hoarded in a notebook and later transposed for fiction. When he began collecting these ‘epiphanies’ he regarded them, in the words of his brother, Stanislaus, as little errors and gestures — mere straws in the wind, by which people betrayed the very things they were most careful to conceal’. 6 Joyce’s interest in psychology was intermittent, and he was more interested in the insignificant than the significant slip — in the freight of consciousness rather than in signs of psychic repression — but both Joyce and Freud were committed to the epic temporalities of the single day.

这种共同的事业自有其同步性。例如，在《日常生活心理病理学》于1901年以期刊形式发表，1904年以书籍形式出版之间，乔伊斯一直在收集偶然听到的对话片段或拾得的言语，他将这些片段记录在一个笔记本中，后来又将其改编用于小说创作。当他开始收集这些“顿悟”时，用他哥哥斯坦尼斯劳斯的话来说，他把它们视为“微小的错误和姿态——如同风中的稻草，人们通过这些稻草暴露了他们最小心隐藏的东西”。乔伊斯对心理学的兴趣时断时续，他更关注的是微不足道的失误而非意义重大的失误——关注的是意识的承载而非心理压抑的迹象——但乔伊斯和弗洛伊德都致力于展现一日之内宏大的时间性。

Freud’s epiphanies are the audition of a language going on inside language, a rhyme which he began hearing all around him — or as Kraus remarked: ‘I hear noises which others don’t hear,’ referring to his own apocalyptic audition of sinister meanings in the unexamined usages of ordinary life. Freud’s moment of clear hearing is documented in a letter to Fliess (26 August 1898): ‘I have at last grasped a little thing that I had long suspected.’ Not the perception of nonsense — since ‘what results from a slip of the tongue has a sense of its own’, or as Wittgenstein said, you must pay attention to your nonsense — so much as the sound of sense without the sense, akin to Robert Frost’s discovery (in his letter to John Bartlett, July 1913) that ‘the best place to get the abstract sound of sense is from voices behind a door that cuts off the words’. In the same year Kafka noted in his diary: ‘Yesterday’s observation. The most appropriate situation for me: to listen to a conversation between two people who are discussing a matter that concerns them closely while I have only a very remote interest in it which is in addition completely selfless.’ The free-floating attentiveness of psychoanalysis is close to the care with which these early listeners felt impelled to record motiveless moments, to conduct fieldwork amid the disjecta of the day. As if that which does not concern you, which has nothing to do with you, is of the greatest personal significance (which is what Freud meant by the unconscious). That Kafka repeatedly castigates himself in the Diaries for the poverty of his ‘miserable observations’ merely confirms their necessity to a nocturnal art constructed out of the refuse of the day.

弗洛伊德的顿悟，是对语言内部语言的聆听，是他开始在周遭听到的韵律——或者正如克劳斯所说：“我听到了别人听不到的声音”，指的是他自己对日常生活中未经审视的用法中蕴含的险恶含义的末世般的聆听。弗洛伊德清晰聆听的时刻记录在一封写给弗利斯的信中（1898年8月26日）：“我终于领悟了我长期以来一直怀疑的一件事。”这并非是对无意义的感知——因为“口误的结果本身就具有意义”，或者正如维特根斯坦所说，你必须注意你的无意义——而是对无意义之声的感知，类似于罗伯特·弗罗斯特（在1913年7月写给约翰·巴特利特的信中）的发现：“获得抽象意义之声的最佳途径，是聆听隔着一扇门、阻断了言语的声音。”同年，卡夫卡在日记中写道：“昨日的观察。对我来说，最合适的情境莫过于聆听两个人讨论一件与他们息息相关的事情，而我对此却只有微弱的兴趣，而且这种兴趣完全是无私的。”精神分析中那种自由漂浮的专注，与早期聆听者们记录无动机瞬间、在日常琐碎中开展田野调查的细致入微颇为相似。仿佛那些与你无关、与你毫无关联的事物，反而具有最重要的个人意义（这正是弗洛伊德所说的无意识）。卡夫卡在日记中反复自责自己“可怜的观察”的贫乏，这恰恰印证了这些观察对于一种由白日残渣构建而成的夜间艺术而言的必要性。

One of the premises of psychoanalysis is that a clear-cut distinction between sleeping and waking has no meaning, from which Henri Bergson concluded that ‘it is the awake-state, rather than the dream-state, which requires explanation’. 7 Everyday Life explains the awake-state as a state of analogy:

精神分析的前提之一是，睡眠和清醒之间泾渭分明的界限毫无意义，亨利·柏格森由此得出结论：“需要解释的是清醒状态，而不是梦境状态。”《日常生活》将清醒状态解释为一种类比状态：

The inconsistencies, absurdities and mistakes of the content of dreams, which have largely prevented them from being recognized as the product of psychic processes, arise in the same way, although admittedly with freer use of the means available, as do the common slips in our everyday life.

梦境内容的矛盾、荒谬和错误，在很大程度上阻碍了人们认识到梦境是心理过程的产物，这些矛盾、荒谬和错误与我们日常生活中的常见失误的产生方式相同，尽管不可否认的是，梦境的产生方式是基于对可用手段更自由的运用。

The two are linked by more than this, however, since what has claimed our attention by day is recycled by night. More important, for present purposes, what does not claim our attention by day also shapes the dream. What Freud in The Interpretation of Dreams calls ‘the remains’ of the day — ‘worthless fragments of daily life’ (IV) — are the façade for what the dream wishes to conceal: they encode its latent content. In Everyday Life this unsuspected franchise of the banal is further extended, as if in flashback (most of Everyday Life concerns the tenses of adulthood) to the material of childhood memories, since these too preserve what is indifferent, as screens for other repressed memories. Like parapraxes, they owe their preservation not to their own content but to an associative relation between their content and another memory. The Interpretation of Dreams sets the scene for the investigation of Everyday Life , as if the latter were framed inside the former — as if our days are dignified by the discovery that they are in the service of our nights.

然而，两者之间的联系远不止于此，因为白天吸引我们注意力的事物会在夜晚被重新利用。更重要的是，就目前而言，白天不吸引我们注意力的事物也会塑造梦境。弗洛伊德在《梦的解析》中称之为“白日残余”——“日常生活中毫无价值的碎片”（第四章）——是梦境想要隐藏之物的伪装：它们编码了梦境的潜在内容。在《日常生活》中，这种不为人知的平庸之物被进一步延伸，仿佛通过闪回（《日常生活》的大部分内容都与成年期有关）的方式，延伸到童年记忆的素材，因为这些记忆也保存着无关紧要之物，作为其他被压抑记忆的屏障。如同口误一样，它们的保存并非源于自身内容，而是源于其内容与其他记忆之间的关联。《梦的解析》为对日常生活的探究奠定了基础，仿佛后者被置于前者之中——仿佛我们的白昼因发现它们服务于我们的夜晚而变得庄严起来。

*

What I tell you three times is true.

我跟你说三遍的话都是真的。

(Lewis Carroll, The Hunting of the Snark )

（刘易斯·卡罗尔，《猎杀巨鲨》）

The notion of the dream’s dependence on the disregarded lumber of the day is shocking, because this material had seemed so incapable — or so unworthy — of being editorialized. Even diaries defer to a remembered present. Freud’s time-exposures (the parapraxis is a frozen moment) revealed psychic mechanisms rather as photography had amazed the day, asleep in the conviction of its own unregisterability. ‘Whereas it is a commonplace that we have some idea of what is involved in the act of walking, we have no idea what happens during the fraction of a second when a person steps out . 8 The parapraxis shows the self as it steps out, or steps out of line. Photography revealed what Walter Benjamin called the optical unconscious. In early photographs, the human subject is caught and caught out, discomposed, error-stricken. Which is why, the more innocent the image, the more it struck the viewer as documenting a transgression. Cinema likewise made all habitual and familiar action seem as if somehow in the wrong. Whence its comedy: in keeping with Freud’s account of the Joke, the first audiences did not know what they were laughing at. Cinema projected the inadvertence of our presence as witnesses (observing the unseeable) as an inadvertence in the realm of the seen — again, a mechanism outlined in The Joke and Its Relation to the Unconscious.

梦境依赖于白天被忽视的素材这一概念令人震惊，因为这些素材似乎如此难以——或者说如此不值得——被编辑。即使是日记也依赖于对当下的回忆。弗洛伊德的延时摄影（口误是凝固的瞬间）揭示了心理机制，正如摄影曾令沉睡在自身不可记录性的信念中的白天感到惊叹一样。“我们通常知道行走行为包含哪些内容，但我们却不知道一个人迈出第一步的瞬间究竟发生了什么。”口误展现了自我迈出一步，或者说越界的那一刻。摄影揭示了瓦尔特·本雅明所说的“视觉无意识”。在早期的照片中，人物被捕捉到，被暴露出来，显得混乱，充满错误。正因如此，图像越是纯真无邪，就越会让观者觉得它记录了一种越轨行为。同样，电影也让所有习以为常的熟悉行为看起来都像是出了错。喜剧的根源在于：正如弗洛伊德对玩笑的解释，最初的观众并不知道自己在笑什么。电影将我们作为见证者（观察不可见之物）的无意之举，投射为可见领域的无意之举——这同样是《玩笑及其与潜意识的关系》一书中阐述的机制。

In silent cinema, the discontinuity of the action and the continuo of the music offer a convenient image of the parapraxis and what it conceals. The early cinemas were places where the public gathered to witness mistakes in motion, in real time, showing what the flow of the day ordinarily conceals from view. Writing in 1936, Walter Benjamin made the connections explicit:

在无声电影中，动作的断续性和音乐的持续低音，为口误及其所掩盖的内容提供了一种便捷的意象。早期的电影院是公众聚集在一起，实时观看动态错误的地方，展现了日常生活中通常被掩盖的事物。瓦尔特·本雅明在1936年撰文明确阐述了这些联系：

Film has enriched our field of perception with methods which can be illustrated by those of Freudian theory. Fifty years ago, a slip of the tongue passed more or less unnoticed. Only exceptionally may such a slip have revealed dimensions or depth in a conversation which had seemed to be taking its course on the surface. Since The Psychopathology of Everyday Life things have changed. This book isolated and made analysable things which had heretofore floated along unnoticed on the broad stream of perception. For the entire spectrum of optical, and now also acoustic perception, film has brought about a similar deepening of appercepion…By close-ups of the things around us film extends our comprehension of the necessities that rule our lives, and manages to assure us of an immense and unsuspected field of action. Evidently a different nature opens itself to the camera than opens to the naked eye — if only because an unconsciously penetrated space is substituted for a space consciously explored. 9

电影以弗洛伊德理论可以阐释的方法丰富了我们的感知领域。五十年前，口误几乎不会引起注意。只有在极少数情况下，这样的口误才会揭示出原本看似平淡无奇的对话中隐藏的维度或深度。自从《日常生活心理病理学》出版以来，情况发生了变化。这本书将此前在广阔的感知洪流中不为人知的事物分离出来，并使其变得可分析。电影对整个视觉感知领域，以及现在的听觉感知领域，都带来了类似的感知深化……通过对我们周围事物的特写镜头，电影扩展了我们对支配我们生活的必需品的理解，并成功地向我们展现了一个巨大而意想不到的行动领域。显然，镜头所展现的自然与肉眼所看到的自然截然不同——这仅仅是因为无意识地渗透的空间取代了有意识地探索的空间。

One of cinema’s discoveries was that everyday life is repetition — as if our actions are constantly trying to remember something — and it turned this to account in the figure of the accident-prone hero. Mayakovsky noted that Chaplin characteristically repeats a gag three times, and he called these passages ‘analytical sequences’. The parapraxis is a gag, the combined parapraxis is a serial gag whose spacing is the bearer of meaning, and in this it resembles the syntax of the dream. 10 In the Introductory Lectures Freud refers to combined slips (a symptomatic act combined with a case of mislaying, for example) as ‘the finest flower of their kind’. A pedantically precise man forgets his watch at home; he has to go on from work to an evening engagement, so he borrows the watch of a ladyfriend; the following day he goes to return the borrowed watch, and finds he has left it at home, although this time he has his own watch with him; he goes home to recover the lady’s watch, returns it to her, and finds he has now left his watch at home (‘as if his conscious mind were saying “I can’t get this business out of my head”’). The heroic waifs and strays of the silent screen are innocents who see themselves — in Adorno’s version of the city-dweller in general — ‘solely as objects of opaque processes, who, torn between sudden shock and sudden forgetfulness, are no longer capable of a sense of temporal continuity’. 11

电影的一项发现是，日常生活就是重复——仿佛我们的行为总是在试图记住某些东西——而电影正是通过塑造容易出糗的英雄形象来体现这一点。马雅可夫斯基注意到，卓别林的典型特征是重复一个笑料三次，他称这些段落为“分析序列”。口误是一种笑料，组合口误则是一种连续的笑料，其间隔承载着意义，在这方面，它类似于梦的句法。在《导论》中，弗洛伊德将组合口误（例如，症状性行为与遗失情况相结合）称为“同类中最美的花朵”。一个一丝不苟的人把手表忘在家里；他下班后要去赴晚宴，于是借了一位女士的手表；第二天他去还借的手表时，发现自己把它落在家里了，尽管这次他带了自己的手表；他回家取回女士的手表，还给她后，却发现自己的手表也落在家里了（“仿佛他的意识在说‘这件事一直萦绕在我心头’”）。无声银幕上那些英勇的孤儿和流浪者，都是天真无邪的个体，他们——在阿多诺笔下，是典型的都市居民——“仅仅把自己视为晦涩过程的客体，在突如其来的震惊和瞬间的遗忘之间摇摆不定，丧失了对时间连续性的感知”。

*

This cannot possibly be an individual peculiarity of my own…

这绝不可能是我个人的特殊情况……

Freud rejected the operating idea that below a certain level whatever we do is inadvertent, and he confronts our investment in contingency — our superstitious tenderness towards the throwaway, the gamble, the happy minute, the feat — with a concealed symptomatic order. Everyday Life enlarged the number of things we do which must be thought of as actions, by finding new ways of explaining them as actions. This of course breaks with all our ordinary convictions of behaving freely — automatically — in regard to unimportant things. Instead,

弗洛伊德否定了那种认为低于某个程度我们所做的一切都是无意的运作观念，他直面我们对偶然性的执着——我们对那些无关紧要之事、赌博、短暂的快乐、壮举的迷信式的偏爱——并揭示了一种隐蔽的症状秩序。《日常生活》一书通过寻找新的解释方式，扩大了我们必须将其视为行动的行为范围。这当然打破了我们所有关于在无关紧要的事情上自由——自动——行事的日常信念。相反，

’Any change of one’s usual appearance, any small act of negligence — for instance a button left undone — every exposure means something which the person wearing that clothing does not want to say directly, indeed generally does not intend to say at all.’

“一个人日常装束的任何改变，任何小小的疏忽——例如没扣上纽扣——每一次暴露都意味着穿着这身衣服的人不想直接表达，实际上通常根本不打算表达的东西。”

Never such innocence again. We accept this enlargement of meaning largely under the aegis of comedy, since if we could not make parapraxes interesting and amusing we would be oppressed and horrified by them, by the new inescapability.

这样的纯真再也不会出现了。我们之所以接受这种意义的扩展，很大程度上是因为喜剧的缘故，因为如果我们不能让口误变得有趣好笑，我们就会感到压抑和恐惧，感到这种新的不可避免的现象带来的困扰。

Indeed, it is just when we are being required to envisage a world in which we must take such injunctions seriously, that the unsettling and ambivalent figure of the paranoiac enters Freud’s story of ordinary life. At the outset, Freud explains our forgettings as the power of the repressed in making hidden connections:

的确，正当我们被要求设想一个必须认真对待此类诫命的世界时，令人不安且矛盾的偏执狂形象便出现在弗洛伊德的日常生活叙事中。一开始，弗洛伊德将我们的遗忘解释为被压抑之物建立隐秘联系的力量：

There is thus a constant stream of ‘self-referentiality’ going through my mind. I am not usually aware of it, but it betrays itself when I forget names in this way. It is as if I were obliged to relate everything I hear about other people to myself: as if my personal complexes were aroused by my perception of others. This cannot possibly be a quality peculiar to myself alone; instead, it must contain some indication of the way in which we perceive ‘otherness’.

因此，我的脑海中始终萦绕着一股“自我指涉”的思绪。我通常意识不到这一点，但当我以这种方式忘记名字时，它便会显露出来。仿佛我必须将听到的关于他人的一切都与自己联系起来：仿佛我对他人的感知会唤起我的个人情结。这绝不可能是我独有的特质；相反，它必然包含着我们感知“他者”方式的某种暗示。

So far so normal. However, paranoiacs likewise ‘draw conclusions from the trivial signs they observe in other people’. Everything the paranoiac observes in others is rich with disclosure. He notes how passers-by laugh to themselves, flourish their sticks, even spit on the ground as they go by’ 12 — in other words, how they commit endless symptomatic acts. His hubris is to refer it all to himself: ‘When his train was moving out of the station, everyone makes a particular gesture with one hand…Or he notes the way people walk in the street, how they flourish their sticks and so on.’ The paranoiac takes signs for wonders, such as to render his knowledge ‘useless’. 13 He orchestrates the world into what Freud, in his Psychoanalytic Remarks on an Autobiographically Described Case of Paranoia , calls ‘the plot against Schreber’.

到目前为止一切正常。然而，妄想症患者同样会“从他们观察到的他人身上的琐碎迹象中得出结论”。妄想症患者观察到的他人的一切迹象都蕴含着丰富的信息。他会注意到路人如何自言自语地笑，如何挥舞拐杖，甚至边走边往地上吐痰——换句话说，他们会做出无数的症状性行为。他的狂妄之处在于将这一切都与自己联系起来：“当他的火车驶出车站时，每个人都会用一只手做出一个特定的手势……或者他会注意到人们在街上走路的方式，他们如何挥舞拐杖等等。”妄想症患者将这些迹象视为奇迹，以至于他的知识“毫无用处”。他将整个世界编织成弗洛伊德在其《关于一个自传体妄想症案例的精神分析评论》中所说的“针对施雷伯的阴谋”。

In a sense, the paranoiac cannot commit parapraxes, because he is destined to observe them — is perhaps their ideal observer. He sees life as it strikes a contemporary, and it all means too much. By the same token, perhaps, our parapraxes — our acts of unknowing, our refusals to notice — prevent us from becoming paranoiac. We habitually posit a zone of involuntary mental life in ourselves and those around us. Not to notice things is to fall over them, but parapraxes have a certain redemptive grace: they allow for what Beckett chastised Proustian voluntary memory as refusing to allow for: ‘the mysterious element of inattention that colours our most commonplace experiences’. 14 Psychoanalysis in one mode suggests that we cannot know ourselves but that we can have knowledge of others. In another mode, that ‘The way to carry out the famous injunction to know thyself is through studying our apparently accidental actions and omissions’. The paranoiac attempts to conflate these claims. Which is why he comes to grief (but never quite to mourning). He is none the less Freud’s semblable , the only other proper character in Everyday Life — and the only sort of clairvoyant whom Freud could ever take seriously.

从某种意义上说，妄想症患者无法犯下无意识的错误行为，因为他注定要观察这些行为——或许正是这些行为的理想观察者。他以当代人的视角看待生活，而这一切对他而言意义非凡。同样地，或许正是我们的无意识错误行为——我们无知的行为，我们拒绝注意的行为——阻止了我们变成妄想症患者。我们习惯性地在自身和周围的人身上设定一个非自主的心理活动区域。不注意事物就如同跌倒在它们面前，但无意识错误行为却具有某种救赎的恩典：它们允许贝克特批判普鲁斯特式的自愿记忆所拒绝允许的那种东西存在，即“我们最平凡的经历中那神秘的、漫不经心的元素”。精神分析的一种模式认为，我们无法了解自己，但我们可以了解他人。另一种模式则认为，“践行‘认识你自己’这一著名训诫的方法，是通过研究我们看似偶然的行为和疏忽”。这个偏执狂试图混淆这些说法。这就是他最终遭遇不幸（但从未真正陷入悲痛）的原因。尽管如此，他仍然是弗洛伊德的化身，是《日常生活》中唯一一个真正意义上的角色——也是弗洛伊德唯一能够认真对待的预言家。

*

We had fallen into conversation…

我们聊了起来……

There runs through Everyday Life a ‘strong current’ of autobiographical reference, ranging from affectively charged moments from Freud’s early adulthood (‘When I was a young man living alone in a foreign city, I often enough heard my name suddenly called by a beloved and unmistakable voice’), to laconic glimpses into the later home life of the Freuds: ‘Recently there was a time, when unusual quantities of glass and china were broken in my household.’ One of the latter scenes involves the throwing of a slipper:

《日常生活》一书中贯穿着一股强烈的自传性指涉，从弗洛伊德青年时期充满情感的片段（“当我年轻时独自生活在异国他乡，我常常听到一个我深爱的、无可置疑的声音突然呼唤我的名字”）到对弗洛伊德夫妇后期家庭生活的简洁描绘：“最近有一段时间，我家摔碎了数量异常多的玻璃和瓷器。”其中一个场景就涉及扔拖鞋：

For instance, one morning as I was walking through a room in my dressing gown, wearing straw slippers, I obeyed a sudden impulse and kicked one slipper off my foot and against the wall, where it brought down a pretty little marble Venus from her bracket.

例如，一天早上，我穿着睡袍，脚蹬草鞋，走过一个房间，突然一时冲动，踢掉了一只草鞋，草鞋撞到了墙上，把墙上一个漂亮的小大理石维纳斯雕像从支架上碰了下来。

The impulse, and his calm acceptance of its consequences, are explained in terms of the sudden realization that his eldest daughter was showing signs of recovery from a grave illness: the breakage is an unconscious act of ‘sacrificial’ gratitude. The example and its explanation are closely fitting and fitted, self-sufficient. There is, however, a more occluded autobiographical strain in Everyday Life — having to do with the reluctant notion of the parapraxis as, of necessity, a conversation: as if the faux pas is always a pas de deux.

这种冲动，以及他对后果的平静接受，可以用他突然意识到大女儿正从重病中康复的迹象来解释：这种失言是一种无意识的“牺牲式”感恩行为。例子及其解释严谨贴切，自成一体。然而，《日常生活》中还蕴含着更为隐晦的自传性倾向——这与他勉强接受的“口误必然是一种对话”的概念有关：仿佛失言总是一场双人舞。

At the very outset of Everyday Life , Freud offers one of his major examples. It is cast in the form of a Socratic dialogue — because it means to persuade us of the general validity of his methods, and pave the way for easier examples to come. 15 He describes being on holiday the previous summer, and passing time with a young Austrian Jew who complains of the position in which Jews are currently held in Austria-Hungary — unable to develop their talents and doomed to atrophy. The young man ends his speech by quoting the passionate injunction that Virgil puts into the mouth of Dido, abandoned by Aeneas and on the point of suicide: ‘ Exoriar(e) aliquis nostris ex ossibus ultor! [May someone rise, an avenger, from my bones!]’. But his memory of the line is at fault, and all he manages to recall is Exoriar(e) ex nostris ossibus ultor! He omits aliquis [someone] and he inverts the word-order.

在《日常生活》的开篇，弗洛伊德就举了一个重要的例证。这个例证以苏格拉底式对话的形式呈现——因为其目的是为了说服我们相信他的方法具有普遍的有效性，并为接下来更容易理解的例证铺平道路。 15 他描述了前一年夏天度假时与一位年轻的奥地利犹太人的交往。这位犹太人抱怨犹太人在奥匈帝国的处境——他们无法发展自己的才能，注定要萎缩。年轻人在演讲的最后引用了维吉尔笔下狄多被埃涅阿斯抛弃、濒临自杀时所作的充满激情的祈祷：“Exoriar(e) aliquis nostris ex ossibus ultor! [愿有人从我的骸骨中复活，成为复仇者！]”。然而，他对这句诗的记忆出现了偏差，他所能回忆起的只有“Exoriar(e) ex nostris ossibus ultor!”他省略了 aliquis（某人），并且颠倒了词序。

But why forget the innocent aliquis ? Challenged by the young man — who is familiar with Freud’s publications — and in the hope of adding a new specimen to his collection, Freud accepts. He asks his companion to call up any associations that the forgotten word might hold. With Freud’s assistance as souffleur , the process leads with dazzling rapidity, via a-liquis and ‘fluid’ connotations, to the young man’s fears that a certain lady of his acquaintance, whose periods have stopped, may now be pregnant. Having expressed a desire for descendants (a new avenging generation), he has had a contrary thought — descendants, yes, but not on these terms — and the collision of contrary impulses ignites the parapraxis, a case of strategic forgetting.

但为何要忘记无辜的“aliquis”呢？这位年轻人熟悉弗洛伊德的著作，为了给弗洛伊德的收藏增添新的例证，弗洛伊德接受了挑战。他请同伴回忆一下这个被遗忘的词可能蕴含的任何联想。在弗洛伊德的引导下，这个过程以惊人的速度展开，通过“a-liquis”（非液体）和“流动”的含义，最终指向了年轻人对一位熟识的女士的担忧——这位女士已经停经，她可能怀孕了。他曾表达过想要子孙后代（一个复仇的新一代）的愿望，但随后又产生了相反的想法——子孙后代，没错，但并非以这种方式——这两种矛盾的冲动碰撞引发了口误，这是一种策略性遗忘。

However, there are not one but two encounters with Virgil’s text here: there is the young man’s failure to recall correctly, but there is also Freud’s perfect and immediate recall: “‘There’s something the matter with that line. How does the whole thing really go?” “I’ll be happy to tell you,” — I replied, and quoted the line as it really runs.’ What is elided by this suave moment, and what goes unremarked in commentaries on the aliquis example (as if remembering, unlike forgetting, is self-evident), is that Freud might have his own reasons for recalling the line. For Dido’s cry is a prophetic augury of the coming of Hannibal — the future avenger whom Virgil, writing in retrospect, had in mind, and whom contemporary commentators called to mind — and whom Freud must also call to mind, having since childhood identified with Hannibal as the Carthaginian (‘Semitic’) general who defeated the Romans yet failed to take Rome.

然而，这里并非只有一次，而是两次与维吉尔文本的接触：一次是年轻人未能正确回忆，另一次是弗洛伊德完美而迅速地回忆起来：“‘这句诗有点问题。整句诗到底是怎么说的？’‘我很乐意告诉你，’我回答道，并把这句诗原原本本背了下来。” 这段优雅的对话所掩盖的，也是在对“aliquis”（反义词）例子的评注中被忽略的（仿佛记住与遗忘不同，是理所当然的），是弗洛伊德回忆起这句诗可能有他自己的理由。因为狄多的呼喊预示着汉尼拔的到来——这位未来的复仇者是维吉尔在回顾写作时所设想的，也是当时的评论家们所提及的——弗洛伊德也必然会想起他，因为他从小就将汉尼拔视为击败罗马人却未能攻克罗马的迦太基（“闪米特”）将军。

In The Interpretation of Dreams , published the previous year, Freud dwells on a series of dreams which have their basis in his as yet unfulfilled longing to see Rome. He recalls that, as an adolescent, ‘ Hannibal and Rome symbolized to me the opposition between the tenacity of Jewry and the organization of the Catholic Church. The significance which the anti-Semitic movement has since acquired for our emotional life later helped to fix the thoughts and feelings of that earlier period.’ Rome comes to stand for the Viennese medical establishment and the Hapsburg political regime at large. Freud offers a studio portrait of himself as a Hannibal who might storm the citadel of his chosen profession but still be denied the ultimate prize: a professorship and recognition. ‘Like Hannibal, I had been fated not to see Rome’ (V.B.).

在前一年出版的《梦的解析》中，弗洛伊德着重分析了一系列梦境，这些梦境源于他尚未实现的对罗马的渴望。他回忆道，少年时期，“汉尼拔和罗马对我来说象征着犹太人的顽强与天主教会的严密组织之间的对立。反犹运动后来对我们情感生活的影响，也强化了我早年的一些想法和感受。”罗马则代表了维也纳的医学界和整个哈布斯堡王朝的政治体制。弗洛伊德将自己比作汉尼拔，他或许能够攻克自己所选择的职业堡垒，却仍然无法获得最终的奖赏：教授职位和认可。“就像汉尼拔一样，我注定无法见到罗马”（V.B.）。

The narrative doors of The Interpretation of Dreams open in sequence, and the Hannibal comparison leads to the sudden recovery of the childhood scene that inaugurated Freud’s Rome obsession. He recalls his father explaining, when he was ten or twelve years old, how the triumph of mid-century liberalism had ushered in a better world in which to be a Jew, and how formerly he himself had once been humiliated by a passer-by (‘Jew!
