Get off the pavement!’) At which the child’s filial curiosity is aroused — ‘What did you do?’ — and he is disappointed to learn that his father submitted unheroically to the insult: ‘I compared this episode, by which ‘I was not impressed, with another more suited to my feelings: the scene (in Livy) where Hannibal’s father makes his son swear before the household altar to take vengeance on the Romans. From that time on, Hannibal had a place in my fantasies.’

《梦的解析》的叙事之门按顺序打开，汉尼拔的比喻引出了弗洛伊德童年记忆中开启他对罗马迷恋的场景。他回忆起十岁或十二岁时，父亲向他解释，世纪中叶自由主义的胜利如何为犹太人带来了一个更美好的世界，以及他自己曾经如何被路人羞辱（“犹太人！滚下人行道！”）。这激起了孩子的好奇心——“你做了什么？”——但他失望地得知，父亲并没有以英雄的方式忍受这种侮辱：“我把这件事——我并不觉得它有什么特别之处——与另一件事做了比较，那件事更能引起我的共鸣：李维笔下汉尼拔的父亲让儿子在家里的祭坛前发誓要向罗马人复仇。从那时起，汉尼拔就占据了我幻想中的位置。”

In adulthood, for Freud to take vengeance on the Romans means to affirm the liberal ideals that his father had momentarily failed to defend decades earlier, to resist the present crisis of liberalism — and the resurgence of institutional anti-Semitism in the 1890s — which threaten to destroy those principles. Freud travelled repeatedly to Italy during this decade, but each time failed to reach — found reasons for not reaching — Rome. But he succeeded in 1901, the year in which Everyday Life was published (five years after his father’s death) — and he succeeded symbolically in the following year, when the long-awaited professorship was secured.

成年后的弗洛伊德向罗马人复仇，意味着重申他父亲几十年前未能捍卫的自由主义理想，抵制当时自由主义的危机——以及19世纪90年代制度性反犹主义的复兴——这些危机威胁着这些原则的存亡。在这十年间，弗洛伊德多次前往意大利，但每次都未能抵达罗马——或者说，他总能找到各种理由拒绝前往。然而，在1901年，也就是《日常生活》出版的那一年（在他父亲去世五年后），他终于成功了。次年，他获得了期盼已久的教授职位，这在象征意义上也标志着他的成功。

Freud often quoted Goethe on Lichtenberg: ‘When he makes a joke, a problem lies concealed.’ The light-heartedness of the aliquis example — told with a brio verging on triumphalism — is its autobiographical trace element. What is being played out, in diaologue form, is the retrospect of a struggle which Freud is aware of having all but come through. He looks forward to reaching Rome while looking back at his travelling companion, as at his own younger self. Two actors, one story. The young Austrian Jew appropriates Dido’s cry and the older responds qua Hannibal, most particularly so since the latter goes unmentioned, or no longer needs to be mentioned. It has been suggested — the aliquis example attracts sceptical commentary — that the encounter with the young Austrian never occurred, that it was one of the fictions (true stories of a hidden self) which Freud smuggled in among his exhibits. At the least there is a symbolic working-through in this and other passages of Everyday Life , comparable to the way in which The Interpretation of Dreams contains a running frieze of personal history. One could say that in Everyday Life , as with an equally composite text like Dora , Freud ‘provides us with the materials for understanding some things that have escaped his own understanding’. 16 A parapraxis might, after all, describe the arc of a life as well as a momentary episode.

弗洛伊德经常引用歌德对利希滕贝格的评价：“当他开玩笑时，问题就隐藏在背后。” 这段对话式的例子轻松诙谐，带着近乎凯旋的活力，正是其自传式的痕迹。对话中展现的是弗洛伊德意识到自己几乎已经克服的一场斗争的回顾。他一边期待着抵达罗马，一边回望着他的旅伴，就像回望年轻时的自己。两个演员，一个故事。年轻的奥地利犹太人借用了狄多的呼喊，而年长的弗洛伊德则以汉尼拔的口吻回应，尤其因为汉尼拔没有被提及，或者说不再需要被提及。有人认为——这段对话式的例子也招致了一些质疑——与这位年轻奥地利人的相遇从未发生过，这只是弗洛伊德偷偷塞进他作品中的虚构故事（隐藏自我的真实故事）之一。至少在《日常生活》的这一段落和其他段落中，存在着一种象征性的梳理，这与《梦的解析》中包含的贯穿始终的个人历史片段类似。可以说，在《日常生活》中，就像在同样结构复杂的文本《朵拉》中一样，弗洛伊德“为我们提供了理解某些他自己都未能理解的事物的素材”。 16 毕竟，口误既可以描述人生的轨迹，也可以描述某个瞬间的插曲。

*

‘Oh, look, there’s Herr L.’

“哦，看，那是L先生。”

A slip is, among other things, an act of pointing, a communication. It says: ‘I want you to know that I am hiding something from myself,’ as if it takes two to make a mistake. What makes the Freudian slipper example unconvincing is the lack of witness, the silence surrounding it, the absence of comedy, the atypical self-completion (no one enters the room just as the slipper is being thrown). A slip, like a crime, usually has witnesses: relatives, intimates, colleagues; the perpetrator is known to the victim. But, as we have seen, the message is a confused one, opaque to both parties. The slip resembles a seduction, neither more nor less real, factitious rather than fictitious. A slip is always a cancellation slip, a denial. As if to take one’s keys with one is to have performed an act, but to forget them is to have not acted. The parapraxis opens a door into the unacted life of wishes fulfilled: I forget my keys, and the day acquires a subplot (‘One’s real life is so often the life one does not lead,’ said Wilde).

失言，除其他含义外，也是一种指认行为，一种交流。它仿佛在说：“我想让你知道，我对自己有所隐瞒”，仿佛犯错需要两个人共同努力。弗洛伊德的拖鞋例子之所以缺乏说服力，是因为缺乏目击者，周围一片寂静，缺乏喜剧元素，以及非典型的自我完成（拖鞋被扔出去时，没有人正好走进房间）。失言，如同犯罪，通常都有目击者：亲戚、密友、同事；施害者是受害者认识的人。但是，正如我们所见，信息是混乱的，对双方都晦涩难懂。失言类似于一种诱惑，既不真实也不虚假，是人为的而非虚构的。失言总是一张取消单，一种否认。仿佛带走钥匙就意味着完成了一项行为，而忘记带钥匙则意味着没有完成一项行为。口误打开了一扇通往未实现愿望的生活的大门：我忘记了钥匙，这一天就有了副情节（王尔德说：“一个人的真实生活往往是他没有过的生活。”）。

The witness to a parapraxis could be pictured as an involved bystander. Whence the uncertainty of the proffered (but also the withdrawn) error. Freud makes us behold the everyday, whose self-absorption was formerly taken for granted, as something rescripted daily in front of others, whose presence modifies what occurs. Freud’s absorption of the beholder into the mechanisms of the parapraxis (such as Manet made inescapable in art: Le Déjeuner sur l’herbe is the painting of a parapraxis) is so thoroughgoing as to go unmentioned. Just as one of the witnesses required is an internal other, because only a split subject can be described, by himself, as having made an error. One of Freud’s specimens crystallizes this figure — ‘the addressee necessarily implied by every articulation of the unconscious’ 17 — in the person of an eavesdropping husband:

目睹口误的人可以被想象成一个卷入其中的旁观者。因此，所提出的（以及被撤回的）错误都存在不确定性。弗洛伊德让我们看到，那些曾经被视为理所当然的日常自我沉溺，如今却在他人面前每日被重新书写，而他人的存在改变了事件的发生。弗洛伊德将旁观者纳入口误机制之中（例如马奈在艺术中使其无法回避：《草地上的午餐》就是一幅描绘口误的画作），这种做法如此彻底，以至于人们往往避而不谈。正如所需的证人之一是内在的他者，因为只有分裂的主体才能自我描述为犯了错误。弗洛伊德的一个例子将这种形象——“无意识的每一次表达都必然隐含的受众”——凝练为一个偷听的丈夫：

I was to read a certain lady a stern lecture at the request of her husband, who was listening on the other side of the door. At the end of my sermon, which obviously made an impression, I said, ‘Well, goodbye then, gnädiger Herr [instead of gnädige Fran ]!

应某位女士丈夫的要求，我要对她进行一番严厉的训诫，她丈夫当时正在门外偷听。我的训诫显然给她留下了深刻的印象，训诫结束后，我说：“好吧，再见，先生（而不是先生）！”

The parapraxis in all its forms could also be said to take this form.

可以说，各种形式的口误也可以采取这种形式。

Coda

结尾

Freud avoids systematic reflection upon the language he employs. Or he worries at languge as a way of worrying about language. The Psychopathology of Everyday Life is saturated in everyday usage — ‘the insights that reflect our common experience’ — and as a text it cuts its cloth from the same materials. It defers to ordinary language as its guide 18 so as to conduct a critique, a prising away of utterance from its uses in the world, and a giving back of new meanings to what has become occluded by habit — which hides everything under our noses — and by those actions (slips, dreams, jokes) that say what they have to say, but ‘in other words’. Because the explanations are events in language, acts of translation, the focus is instructively sharpened, rather than diffused, by a consideration of how to find just equivalents in English. The question of how to translate Freud’s text becomes as good a question as any to be asked of that text.

弗洛伊德避免系统地反思他所使用的语言。或者说，他担忧语言本身就是一种对语言的担忧。《日常生活心理病理学》充满了日常用法——“反映我们共同经验的洞见”——而作为一部文本，它也从同样的素材中汲取养分。它以日常语言为指导，进行批判，将话语从其在世界中的用途中剥离出来，并赋予那些被习惯所掩盖的事物以新的意义——习惯掩盖了我们眼皮底下的一切——以及那些以“换句话说”表达其含义的行为（口误、梦境、玩笑）。由于这些解释是语言事件，是翻译行为，因此，思考如何在英语中找到恰当的对应词，反而能有效地聚焦而非分散焦点。如何翻译弗洛伊德的文本，本身就成了一个值得探讨的问题。

Ernest Jones’s protective view was that Freud ‘forged’ his own terminology. One could equally say that he uses the same word in many different ways and contexts, so as to build up a ‘picture’ of its uses, and that it is by such means that his terms become instantiated. The standard English terminology was instantiated by James Strachey more by fiat , if only because Strachey’s is the Standard Edition , and remains the only authorized translation to date. Revision is underway to accommodate the accumulated suggestion that Strachey and colleagues Englished at least some of Freud’s German in doctrinaire, or retrospective, or over-systematic, or abstract, or Latinate, or unduly scientistic ways.

欧内斯特·琼斯的辩护观点是，弗洛伊德“创造”了自己的术语。同样可以说，他以多种不同的方式和语境使用同一个词，从而构建出该词用法的“图景”，而正是通过这种方式，他的术语才得以具体化。詹姆斯·斯特雷奇确立了标准的英语术语，这更多是出于权威性，即便仅仅是因为斯特雷奇的译本是标准版，并且至今仍是唯一获得授权的译本。目前正在进行修订，以回应越来越多的批评意见，即斯特雷奇及其同事在翻译弗洛伊德的部分德语时，采用了教条主义、回顾性、过于系统化、抽象化、拉丁化或过于科学化的方式。

Freud unites the main topics of Everday Life by choosing terms that share the same prefix, following the natural lead of the German language where the ‘same word formation, with the prefix ver -[roughly, English ‘mis-’], gives a linguistic indication of tie internal similiary of most of these phenomena’. Thus versprechen (‘to misspeak’; Strachey: ‘slips of the tongue’), vergreifen (‘to mishandle’; Strachey: ‘bungled actions’) and vergessen (‘to forget). Cognate examples reinforce the decisions of language in respect of minor error: verschreiben (‘to miswrite’: Strachey: ‘slips of the pen’), verlesen (‘to misread’; Strachey: ‘slips of reading’), verlegen’ (‘to mislay’), verlieren (‘to misplace’, ‘to lose’). Some of these are reflexive verbs ( sich verhoren, ‘ to mishear’, sich versprechen ’, ‘to misspeak’, sich vergreifen , ‘to mishandle’), and in German many of Freud’s uses hover on the verges of the vernacular, in and out of the lexically transparent — slightly stiffened uses of the usual, which create an air of alertness around themselves.

弗洛伊德通过选择具有相同前缀的词语，将日常生活的主要主题联系起来，这遵循了德语的自然规律，即“相同的词形，加上前缀ver-（大致相当于英语的‘mis-’），就能从语言学的角度表明大多数此类现象之间存在内在的相似性”。例如，versprechen（“说错话”；斯特雷奇解释为“口误”）、vergreifen（“处理不当”；斯特雷奇解释为“笨拙的行为”）和vergessen（“忘记”）。同源词的例子也强化了语言在处理细微错误方面的决定：verschreiben（“写错字”；斯特雷奇解释为“笔误”）、verlesen（“读错字”；斯特雷奇解释为“阅读失误”）、verlegen（“放错地方”）、verlieren（“放错位置”、“丢失”）。其中一些是反身动词（sich verhoren，“听错”，sich versprechen，“说错”，sich vergreifen，“处理不当”），在德语中，弗洛伊德的许多用法徘徊在白话的边缘，时而进入词汇透明的范畴，时而又脱离——略微僵硬的常用用法，营造出一种警觉的氛围。

In addition to ver -, there is a complementary and overlapping cluster of German compounds for things going awry, which lead with the prefix fehl - (‘wrong’, ‘false’). Thus fehlen (‘to err’, ‘fail’, ‘mistake’), Fehlgriff (‘a mistake’) from Griff (‘a grip’, ‘a handle’) and greifen (‘to grasp’, ‘to handle’) — which leads in a circle back to Freud’s ver-greifen (‘to misgrasp’, ‘to mishandle’). There is even a verb ver/fehlen (‘to miss’ [a train], ‘to choose wrongly’ [a career]). When it came to finding a word to subsume all local strayings of the self in daily life, rather than employ existing usage Freud coined a new term from fehl -, namely Fehl-leistung. Leistung means ‘act’, ‘performance’, ‘achievement’: hence ‘faulty performance’.

除了 ver- 之外，德语中还有一组与之互补且相互重叠的复合词，用来表示事情出错，这些复合词都以 fehl- 前缀（意为“错误的”、“虚假的”）开头。例如 fehlen（意为“犯错”、“失败”、“失误”），Fehlgriff（意为“错误”，源自 Griff，意为“抓握”、“把手”），以及 greifen（意为“抓住”、“处理”）——这又循环回到了弗洛伊德的 ver-greifen（意为“错抓”、“处理不当”）。甚至还有一个动词 ver/fehlen（意为“错过火车”、“错误地选择职业”）。当弗洛伊德需要找到一个词来概括日常生活中所有局部性的自我偏差时，他并没有沿用现有的用法，而是从 fehl- 中创造了一个新词，即 Fehl-leistung。 Leistung 的意思是“行为”、“表现”、“成就”，因此是“表现不佳”。

Strachey chose to render Fehlleistung as ‘parapraxis’, and in the Standard Edition the strange term appears for the first time in the editor’s Introduction to The Psychopathology of Everyday Life , footnoted thus:

斯特雷奇选择将 Fehlleistung 译为“parapraxis”，在标准版中，这个奇怪的术语首次出现在编辑为《日常生活心理病理学》所作的导言中，脚注如下：

In German Fehlleistung , ‘faulty function’. It is a curious fact that before Freud wrote this book the general concept seems not to have existed in psychology, and in English a new word had to be invented to cover it.

德语中的“Fehlleistung”意为“功能缺陷”。有趣的是，在弗洛伊德撰写此书之前，心理学中似乎并不存在这个概念，英语中不得不创造一个新词来涵盖它。

Neither of these assertons is quite valid (and faulty ‘function’ is already a running away with the bone). Freud’s Fehlleistung may have been a new word, but its composite parts are thoroughly vernacular. Moreover, his employment of it in Everyday Life is not technical in the sense of proprietory or rigorously apodictic. Fehlleistung alludes to and is used by Freud alongside other extant terms — notably Fehlhandlung — as in Fehl-und Zufallshandlungen , for example, Englished by the Standard edition as ‘parapraxes and chance actions’. Handlung means ‘action’, and Fehlhandlung — ‘erroneous action’ — has been in currency since Goethe. 19

这两个断言都不太成立（而“功能缺陷”本身就有点跑题了）。弗洛伊德的“Fehlleistung”（错误）或许是个新词，但它的组成成分却非常通俗易懂。此外，他在《日常生活》中使用该词并非出于专有或绝对的权威性。“Fehlleistung”一词与弗洛伊德已有的其他术语——尤其是“Fehlhandlung”（错误行为）——并被他并列使用，例如在《Fehl-und Zufallshandlungen》（错误行为和偶然行为）中，标准版将其译为“parapraxes and chance actions”（语境不明，意为“语境错误和偶然行为”）。“Handlung”意为“行为”，而“Fehlhandlung”（错误行为）一词自歌德时代起就已存在。

‘Parapraxis’ on the other hand is not English coin — it has the odd distinction of describing something we all do, while ensuring that none of us know what it means (in vain will you look up the word in the Concise Oxford Dictionary ). It has held until now as the accepted translation, 20 but has found enemies along the way. Bruno Bettelheim pointed out that Freud’s Fehlleistung simultaneously suggests achievement or accomplishment ( Leistung ) and failure, errance ( fehl -):.

另一方面，“Parapraxis”并非英语词汇——它奇特地描述了一种我们都会做的事情，却又确保我们谁也不知道它的含义（即使你在《简明牛津词典》中查找这个词也无济于事）。它一直被认为是公认的译法，但在此过程中也遇到了一些反对者。布鲁诺·贝特尔海姆指出，弗洛伊德的“Fehlleistung”同时暗示着成就或功绩（Leistung）和失败、错误（fehl-）。

When we think of a mistake we feel that something has gone wrong, and when we refer to an accomplishment we approve of it. In Fehlleistung , the two responses become somehow merged: we both approve and disapprove. Fehlleistung is much more than an abstract concept: it’s a term that gives German readers an immediate, intuitive feeling of admiration for the cleverness and ingenuity of the unconscious processes, without the reader’s losing sight of the fact that the end result of those processes is a mistake. For example, when we make an error in talking we frequently feel that what is said is right, though we also somehow know it is wrong. When we forget an appointment, we know that forgetting it was an error, but also feel that somehow we probably wanted to avoid keeping the appointment. Perhaps the best rendering of Fehlleistung would be ‘faulty achievement’. 21

当我们想到一个错误时，我们会觉得出了问题；当我们提到一项成就时，我们会表示赞赏。在德语中，“Fehlleistung”（错误）一词将这两种反应融合在一起：我们既赞赏又不赞赏。Fehlleistung 远不止是一个抽象概念：它能让德国读者立刻产生一种直觉式的赞叹，欣赏无意识过程的巧妙和独创性，同时又不会忽略这些过程的最终结果是错误这一事实。例如，当我们说话出错时，我们常常感觉自己说的是对的，尽管我们内心深处也知道它是错的。当我们忘记约会时，我们知道忘记约会是个错误，但同时也觉得我们可能本来就想逃避约会。或许 Fehlleistung 的最佳译法是“有缺陷的成就”。

‘Faulty achievement’ is not ideal, but it is alert to the problem, in translating Freud’s words, of conveying their undertow of individual agency. Another example is vergreifen , literally ‘mishandle’. This is not quite the same as Strachey’s ‘bungle’, which suggests nonperformance, or some such extenuation. The present translation prefers ‘inadvertent actions’ — since Freud’s examples have often little to do with bungling per se (rather the dress unfastened ‘with a conjuror’s sleight of hand’, the slipper aimed ‘so well’ at the statue, and so on). ‘Bungled’ suggests an action feebly intended and clumsily executed; Bettelheim suggests that in Freud’s examples an action is not so much intended as carried out, and with perfect aplomb. But, in fact, a parapraxis is the site of a compromise (in Freud’s words, ‘a half-success and a half-failure for each of two intentions’). It is the chance meeting, on the operating table of the day, of a deflected and a deflecting intention — the former often the mere occasion for the latter. And the load-bearer of Freud’s explanations is always the latter, the intervening counter-intention. The danger with the English terms is that the two become equals. As a result, the Freudian slip gets understood as occasioned by something very like a banana peel in the self’s path.

“有缺陷的成就”并非理想之选，但它敏锐地指出了翻译弗洛伊德的话语时，如何传达其中蕴含的个人能动性这一难题。另一个例子是 vergreifen，字面意思是“误操作”。这与斯特雷奇的“笨拙”（bungle）略有不同，后者暗示着未完成或类似的轻描淡写。本文的译法更倾向于“无意的行为”——因为弗洛伊德的例子往往与笨拙本身关系不大（而是像魔术师的障眼法般解开裙子，或者“精准地”将拖鞋踢向雕像等等）。“笨拙地”暗示着意图不明确、执行笨拙的行为；贝特尔海姆则认为，在弗洛伊德的例子中，行为与其说是意图，不如说是执行，而且执行得非常得体。但事实上，口误是一种妥协（用弗洛伊德的话来说，就是“两种意图各有一半成功和一半失败”）。它是在日常的“手术台”上，一种被偏离的意图和一种试图偏离的意图偶然相遇——前者往往只是后者的诱因。而弗洛伊德解释的核心始终是后者，即介入的反意图。英语术语的危险之处在于，它们将二者等同起来。结果，弗洛伊德式的口误被理解为某种非常类似于自我道路上的香蕉皮之类的东西造成的。

‘Parapraxis’ is usually decanted into plain English as [Freudian] ‘slip’, and this is the vernacular solution that has been adopted in the present translation. There are interesting difficulties with ‘slip’, its modern uses having elided precisely the earlier and germane associations of transgression, of error in conduct ( OED : ‘Adam’s fatal slip’, etc., from 1601 onwards). The modern sense of sheer ‘inadvertence’ or accident — merely a slip — suggests a cancelling passivity: it replaces the neutral clarity of agency with a warm muddle of intentionality. To adopt Austin’s austerities, a ‘slip’ implies either justification (‘I accept that it happened, but deny that it means anything’) or excuse (‘I accept that it means something, but deny that I meant it to happen’). From being something which merely occurred, there is a short exculpatory step to its becoming something which happened to me: the perpetrator as the victim of circumstance. At least ‘parapraxis’ suggests, albeit with decent obscurity, that the perpetration of an act is at issue. Freud’s words weigh such feathers in their scales. 22

“Parapraxis”通常被简化为[弗洛伊德式的]“slip”（口误），这也是本文译文所采用的通俗表达方式。“slip”一词本身存在一些有趣的难题，其现代用法恰恰抹去了早期与越轨、行为错误相关的恰当含义（例如，《牛津英语词典》中“亚当的致命失误”等，始于1601年）。现代意义上的“无意”或意外——仅仅是一个口误——暗示了一种否定性的被动性：它用一种模糊不清的意图取代了主体性的中立清晰。借用奥斯汀的简洁论证，“口误”要么意味着辩解（“我承认它发生了，但我否认它意味着什么”），要么意味着借口（“我承认它意味着什么，但我否认我故意让它发生”）。从仅仅发生的事情，到发生在我身上的事情，中间有一个简短的开脱步骤：作恶者变成了环境的受害者。至少“失言”（parapraxis）一词，尽管含义晦涩，暗示着问题的关键在于是否实施了某种行为。弗洛伊德的论述也关注着这类问题。

‘Slip’ by now carries an inevitable [Freudian] cargo, which means that it is culturally too late to suggest a viable alternative (Bettelheim proposed ‘lapse’). But by the same token it is impossible for ‘a [Freudian] slip’ to function non-tautologically within a translation of Freud’s text. (The common German expression eine [Freudsche] Fehlleistung at least uses Freud’s own word.) Likewise we need a notional term for both the generality of slips and the concept of ‘slip’ — since ‘slip’ clearly cannot serve as the class of which it is also a member.

如今，“口误”一词不可避免地带有弗洛伊德式的色彩，这意味着在文化上提出一个可行的替代方案（贝特尔海姆曾提出“失误”）为时已晚。但同样地，在弗洛伊德文本的翻译中，“弗洛伊德式的口误”也无法不产生同义反复的效果。（德语常用表达“eine [Freudsche] Fehlleistung”至少使用了弗洛伊德自己的词汇。）同样，我们需要一个概念术语来同时指代口误的普遍性和“口误”的概念本身——因为“口误”显然不能作为它自身所属的类别。

Freud supplements ordinary usage — applies words in conflict with their uses — and sometimes supplants it with the unusual and therefore exact word. German meets this need halfway because it allows the coining of technical terms within a strong vernacular habitat, and neologism is not unilaterally inhibiting of common speech, whereas in English it is a case of either/or. In the present Introduction, however, ‘parapraxis’ has been retained to subsume the generality of slips, and to suggest something of the abstraction (if not the concretion) of Fehlleistung. ‘Slip’ has also been used, to refer to speech acts and suchlike, but inconsistently so, in that — as Freud might be the first to allow, given his profoundly rhetorical procedures — it must find its own level of sound and sense inside the accident of a sentence.

弗洛伊德对日常用法进行了补充——运用了与其用法相悖的词语——有时甚至用不寻常的、因而也更精确的词语取而代之。德语在某种程度上满足了这种需求，因为它允许在强大的日常用语环境中创造专业术语，而且新词的出现并不会单方面抑制日常用语，而英语则不然，二者只能二选一。然而，在本导论中，我们保留了“口误”（parapraxis）一词，以涵盖口误的普遍性，并暗示某种程度上与错误（Fehlleistung）的抽象性（即便不是具体化）相关。我们也使用“口误”（slip）一词来指代言语行为等等，但这种用法并不一致，因为——鉴于弗洛伊德深奥的修辞手法，他或许会首先承认——口误必须在句子的偶然性中找到其自身的音韵和意义层次。

Paul Keegan, 2002

保罗·基根，2002年

As we reached the Karlsplatz, I realized to my dismay that my right stocking was falling down. I walked on as far as the tram shelters. There, stammering helplessly, I stopped. He gloated at my predicament.

走到卡尔广场时，我惊恐地发现右脚的袜子快要掉下来了。我继续往前走，直到走到电车候车亭。在那里，我结结巴巴地停了下来，不知所措。他幸灾乐祸地看着我的窘境。

Can’t you keep walking while we’re talking?

我们说话的时候，你不能继续走吗？

I can’t.

我不能。

After making a series of stupid remarks, such as ‘If you weren’t so young’, etc., I told him that my stocking was torn. Meanwhile the stocking had worked its way down into my shoe. I rushed off to the ladies’ room. I re-emerged, blushing for shame. He said:

说了一堆蠢话，比如“如果你不是这么年轻”等等之后，我告诉他我的丝袜破了。这时丝袜已经滑进了我的鞋子里。我赶紧跑到洗手间。出来的时候，我羞愧得满脸通红。他说：

Why so petty, Fräulein? It can happen to anyone.

小姐，何必这么斤斤计较呢？这种事谁都可能遇到。

15 . In Introductory Lectures Freud was to reverse the procedure: beginning with easy examples and leading on to more complex cases, or at least more complex explanations.

15. 在导论讲座中，弗洛伊德反其道而行之：从简单的例子入手，逐步深入到更复杂的案例，或者至少是更复杂的解释。

16 . Stephen Marcus, Freud and the Culture of Psychoanalysis (London, 1984), p. 78.

18 . In contrast to William James, for example, who considered the reliance of the language of psychology upon everyday speech to be parasitical, and one of its greatest sources of error, and whose call for a distinct discipline of psychology was a call for a distinct language. By which was meant not only a recourse to neologism but also an epic reinvigoration of the existing descriptive registers of language so as to capture nuances of consciousness. Thus his celebrated description of ‘forgetting a name’, Principles of Psychology (1890).

18. 例如，威廉·詹姆斯就持相反观点。他认为心理学语言对日常用语的依赖是一种寄生现象，也是其最大的谬误来源之一。他呼吁建立一门独立的心理学学科，实际上就是呼吁建立一种独立的语言。这不仅意味着要创造新词，更意味着要彻底革新现有的语言描述体系，以便捕捉意识的细微差别。例如，他在《心理学原理》（1890）中对“忘记名字”这一现象的著名描述。

19. 杰里米·阿德勒指出，歌德在《亲和力》（1807-9）的结尾创造了“Fehlhandlung”一词，用来定义奥蒂莉“无意中”淹死婴儿的行为——小说中的这一幕，弗洛伊德作为歌德的忠实读者，一定会非常关注。

20 . Its coinage predates Strachey, and predates even A. A. Brill’s 1914 translation of The Psychopathology of Everyday Life. ( OED: parapraxia , ‘a condition in which there is a defective performance of certain purposive acts’, 1912.) Brill preferred to render Fehlleistungen as ‘faulty actions’.

20. 这个词的出现早于斯特雷奇，甚至早于A. A. 布里尔1914年翻译的《日常生活心理病理学》。（牛津英语词典：parapraxia，“一种在某些有目的的行为中存在缺陷的状况”，1912年。）布里尔更倾向于将Fehlleistungen译为“错误的行为”。

21 . Bruno Bettelheim, Freud and Man’s Soul (London, 1983), pp. 85ff.

L. Austin, ‘A Plea for Excuses’ in Philosophical Papers (Oxford, 1961).

# ↩

Translators Preface

译者序

Translators are always trying to get inside the minds of the authors on whom they are working. When the author in question is Sigmund Freud, the task is rather daunting, but fascinating. The experience of translating The Psychopathology of Everyday Life has left me with a great admiration for the man, a closer knowledge of his time, and a sense of finding him far more approachable than I did before.

译者总是试图深入了解他们所翻译的作者的思想。当翻译的作者是西格蒙德·弗洛伊德时，这项任务既艰巨又充满魅力。翻译《日常生活心理病理学》的经历让我对弗洛伊德这位哲学家更加敬佩，对他的时代有了更深入的了解，也让我感觉他比以前更容易接近。

Translation is an interpretative craft, often compared to acting, except that the translator of prose does not have the freedom of an actor or director to produce a startlingly individual version (poetry is a different matter, for very considerable freedom can produce what amounts to a new poem in its own right; Ted Hughes translating Ovid is a case in point). But in general the translator has a double duty: to the author, whose work is to be rendered as faithfully as possible, with the proviso that it may be more important to preserve the spirit than the letter of the original; and to the reader, who in my view should be able to read the text as easily as if it had been written in the language of translation in the first place. Today there is an interesting discussion among translators, some of whom believe that the foreignness of the original text ought to be preserved. I have seen them described as ‘visible translators’, while others attempt to be ‘invisible translators’. There is a strong case to be made out for the first camp, but my own instinctive preferences place me in the second, among those who hope, ideally, to achieve invisibility.

翻译是一门诠释性的技艺，常被比作表演，但散文译者不像演员或导演那样拥有创作出惊世骇俗的个性化版本（诗歌则不同，因为相当大的自由度可以催生出堪称全新诗篇的作品；泰德·休斯翻译奥维德的作品便是一个例证）。但总的来说，译者肩负着双重责任：一是要对作者尽心尽力，尽可能忠实地传达其作品，但前提是保留原文的精神可能比字面意义更为重要；二是要对读者尽心尽力，在我看来，读者应该能够像阅读原文一样轻松地理解译文。如今，译者之间就此展开了一场有趣的讨论，一些译者认为应该保留原文的异域性。我见过有人称他们为“可见译者”，而另一些人则力图成为“隐形译者”。第一种观点有其充分的理由，但我本能的偏好使我倾向于第二种观点，即希望理想情况下能够隐身。

In the case of Freud one could claim that there is a strongly ‘foreign’ element present anyway, first because of our distance from the period when he wrote his early tides. Working through The Psychopathology of Everyday Life (several times, as one does in the course of translation), I have felt as if I were walking the streets of Vienna a century ago, or visiting those holiday resorts favoured by Freud, his patients, friends, colleagues and correspondents. It was a world where well-to-do ladies seldom worked for a living; where one gets the general impression that they were bent on marriage, while their suitors or lovers would rather avoid it. Second, certain attitudes taken for granted in that world have become foreign to us. Although some of Freud’s subjects, as he recounts in this book, may have betrayed a reluctance to pay their medical bills through an inadvertent slip of word or deed, these were prosperous people used to employing domestic staff (who often figure in the anecdotal material of this title). Our ideas have undergone considerable change since Freud claimed that the servant classes were unable to appreciate art unless they could identify with it, in a proprietorial manner, out of loyalty to their employers, or (in a footnote) that a woman who is raped must really have wanted it in part of her mind, or she would have put up more resistance. Here one simply has to adjust one’s ideas to those of upper middle-class society in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. Freud wins the modern reader’s strong sympathy, however, for his awareness of the latent anti-Semitism just below the surface of his world, and he was right to fear it, for it would eventually drive him into exile in London when he was old and approaching death. All the little case histories in this book — some of them only a few lines long — build up into a social history of their time and place.

就弗洛伊德而言，可以说他的作品中本身就存在着强烈的“异域”元素，首先是因为我们与他早期著作的写作年代相距甚远。在研读《日常生活心理病理学》（如同翻译过程中那样，我反复阅读了好几遍）的过程中，我仿佛置身于一个世纪前的维也纳街头，或是造访弗洛伊德、他的病人、朋友、同事和通信者们钟爱的度假胜地。在那个时代，富裕的女士们很少工作谋生；人们普遍认为她们一心想结婚，而她们的追求者或情人则避之不及。其次，在那个时代被视为理所当然的某些观念，如今对我们来说已变得陌生。尽管弗洛伊德在书中叙述，他的一些研究对象可能因无意间的言语或行为而流露出不愿支付医疗费用的情绪，但这些人都是富裕阶层，习惯于雇佣家政人员（这些家政人员经常出现在本书的轶事素材中）。自弗洛伊德声称仆人阶级只有出于对雇主的忠诚，才能以占有的方式认同艺术，从而无法欣赏艺术，或者（在脚注中）认为被强奸的女性内心深处一定有某种渴望，否则她会进行更强烈的反抗以来，我们的观念已经发生了相当大的变化。在这里，我们只需调整一下自己的观念，使其与十九世纪末二十世纪初中上层阶级的观念相符即可。然而，弗洛伊德对潜藏于他所处世界表面之下的反犹主义的敏锐洞察力赢得了现代读者的强烈同情，而他的担忧不无道理，因为最终，这种反犹主义迫使他在年老体衰、濒临死亡之际流亡伦敦。本书中所有的小案例——有些甚至只有寥寥数行——共同构建了一部反映其所处时代和地域的社会史。

The Psychopathology of Everyday Life is famous in the English-speaking world for giving the language the phrase ‘Freudian slip’. From the layman’s point of view, it is one of the more cheerful of Freud’s works, since it is about the slips of speech, writing, reading, remembering and acting that normal people make, although he often uncovers disturbing motives behind these little incidents. He was scrupulously conscientious in trying to illustrate them not from the case histories of his neurotic patients, but from examples he had noted in himself, or instances contributed from their own experience by his medical colleagues. And indeed we all frequently make such slips, and it is entertaining to work out why; I kept catching myself out in them during my work on this title, and trying rather more consciously than usual to discover how they had arisen. One almost wanted to pick up the telephone and ring back to the year 1901, offering another specimen for the collection.

《日常生活心理病理学》在英语世界因创造了“弗洛伊德式口误”这一术语而闻名。从普通读者的角度来看，这算是弗洛伊德著作中比较轻松愉快的一部，因为它探讨的是正常人在言语、写作、阅读、记忆和行为中都会出现的口误，尽管弗洛伊德常常揭示这些小插曲背后令人不安的动机。他一丝不苟地用自己亲身经历的例子，或是医学同行提供的自身经验来阐释这些口误，而不是引用神经症患者的病例。的确，我们都经常犯这样的错误，探究其原因也颇为有趣；我在撰写本书的过程中，也常常发现自己犯了这样的错误，并比以往更加有意识地去探究它们是如何产生的。我甚至几乎想拿起电话拨回1901年，再提供一个例子加入到这个“口误收集”中。

But although ‘Freudian slip’ has entered the English language to mean, broadly speaking, something said or done that betrays the existence of a subtext or a subliminal motive, of course it is not a term which could be used in the translation of this book. The terminology of the new science of Freudian psychoanalysis was, obviously, coined in Freud’s native tongue of German, a good language for the purpose with its ability to alter the connotations of a word by the addition of a small prefix such as ver - or zer -. All of us working on the New Penguin Freud translations will have had our special problems, and we were not required to draw up a list of standard translations of Freudian terminology and stick to it. A set of specialist terms in English does exist, but on the whole they are not in plain English, but in a coinage either producing terms for use in the sphere of psychoanalysis alone (‘unpleasure’, ‘affect’ as a noun), or derived from ancient Greek (‘cathexis’, ‘parapraxis’, both dated in the Shorter Oxford Dictionary as first found in the early twentieth century, in fact specifically to render Freud’s German terms).

尽管“弗洛伊德式口误”一词已进入英语，大致意思是说，言语或行为中流露出某种潜台词或潜在动机，但当然，它并不适用于本书的翻译。弗洛伊德精神分析这门新兴学科的术语显然是用弗洛伊德的母语德语创造的，德语非常适合这种翻译，因为它可以通过添加诸如“ver-”或“zer-”之类的前缀来改变词义。我们所有参与企鹅出版社弗洛伊德著作翻译的译者都会遇到各自的难题，我们也没有被要求制定一份弗洛伊德术语的标准译法清单并严格遵守。英语中确实存在一套专业术语，但总的来说，它们不是用普通的英语表达的，而是人为创造的，要么是专门用于精神分析领域的术语（例如名词“不快感”、“情感”），要么是源自古希腊语的术语（例如“投注”、“失言”，这两个词在《简明牛津词典》中被标注为最早出现于二十世纪初，实际上专门用来翻译弗洛伊德的德语术语）。

In a work of this nature it is inevitable that many of the slips of the tongue or pen recounted by Freud himself or his informants must be given in German, and then translated and/or explained in English. My translations/explanations are contained in square brackets. I have also added, in square brackets, translations of those passages from French that Freud gave in the original text only. Parentheses in round brackets are of course Freud’s own (as are the footnotes from the Fischer Psychologie edition I have used, itself from the Gesammelte Werke edition and therefore later than the very first publication of this title in 1901; the reader will find several comments by Freud referring back to that first publication and indicating that he made later additions to the material). But the necessary presence of so many quotations in German made me particularly anxious to avoid placing a heavy weight of specialist terminology on the rest of the book, in the passages that can go straight into plain English.

在这样一部作品中，不可避免地会引用弗洛伊德本人或其线人所记录的许多口误或笔误，这些口误必须以德语呈现，然后再翻译和/或解释成英语。我的翻译/解释用方括号括起来。我还用方括号添加了弗洛伊德仅在原文中引用的法语段落的译文。圆括号内的括号当然是弗洛伊德本人的（我使用的费舍尔心理学版中的脚注也是如此，该版本本身来自《弗洛伊德全集》，因此晚于该书1901年的首次出版；读者会发现弗洛伊德的一些评论回顾了该书的首次出版，并指出他后来对材料进行了补充）。但是，由于必须引用如此多的德语原文，我特别注意避免在本书的其他部分，尤其是在那些可以直接用浅显易懂的英语表达的段落中，使用过多的专业术语。

My own special problem has naturally been the translation of the word Fehlleistung , the Freudian slip itself, in German denoting a failure to achieve or embody some intended purpose. The specialist English term that has been coined for it is ‘parapraxis’. I decided from the first not to use it if I could possibly avoid doing so; these new translations are for people like me who have no psychoanalytical training and do not find ‘parapraxis’ an instantly familiar term. Depending on context, I have therefore translated Fehlleistung sometimes as plain ‘slip’, sometimes as ‘slip of the memory’, ‘slip of the mind’, ‘slip of the tongue’, ‘slip of the pen’. Unlust occurs only very occasionally in this particular title, and the literal English ‘unpleasure’ is, as the Penguin Dictionary of Psychoanalysis concedes, a clumsy word but useful as the antithesis of ‘pleasure’. I might have had to use it if it had occurred more frequently in my text; as it was, in those contexts where the word was used in German I felt I could employ ‘aversion’ or ‘sense of aversion’ instead. Most of the time I have avoided ‘affect’ as a noun, for one thing because, as I found several times in going back over an earlier draft of the translation, it makes it difficult to use the verb ‘to affect [something or someone]’ in the usual way in English. I did use it as a noun, however, in the account of Professor N.’s lecture delivered in Switzerland in section V, where the whole point of the story depends on slang or jargon terms, and in that context it seemed appropriate.

我遇到的特殊问题自然是德语单词“Fehlleistung”（弗洛伊德式口误）的翻译，它指的是未能达到或体现某种预期目的。英语中专门用来描述这种情况的术语是“parapraxis”（语无伦次）。我从一开始就决定尽可能避免使用它；这些新的译文是为像我一样没有接受过精神分析训练、对“parapraxis”这个术语不太熟悉的人准备的。因此，根据上下文，我有时将“Fehlleistung”翻译成简单的“slip”（口误），有时翻译成“slip of the memory”（记忆失误）、“slip of the mind”（思维失误）、“slip of the tongue”（口误）、“slip of the pen”（笔误）。“Unlust”（不愉悦）一词在本书中出现频率很低，而正如《企鹅精神分析词典》所承认的，它的英文直译“unpleasure”（不愉悦）是一个笨拙的词，但作为“pleasure”（愉悦）的反义词却很有用。如果它在我的文本中出现得更频繁，我或许不得不使用它；事实上，在德语中出现该词的那些语境下，我觉得可以用“厌恶”或“厌恶感”来代替。大多数情况下，我都避免将“affect”用作名词，原因之一是，正如我在多次修改早期译稿时发现的那样，它使得动词“影响[某事或某人]”在英语中难以按常规用法使用。然而，在第五部分对N教授在瑞士的演讲的描述中，我确实将其用作了名词，因为该部分故事的重点完全依赖于俚语或行话，在这种情况下，使用“affect”似乎比较合适。

Even more difficult than the Fehlleistung , however, was the problem of English terminology for the various actions that Freud describes mainly in sections VIII and IX of this book, as well as the final section. He sometimes speaks of such an action in general as a Fehlhandlung — an action which goes wrong in one way or another. But he then further divides them up into Das Vergreifen (the subject of section VIII), and Symptom- und Zufallshandlungen (the subject of section IX). The latter section heading translates easily enough, as Symptomatic and Fortuitous Actions , and when Freud comes to consider these he concludes that they are really one and the same thing. My major difficulty was with Das Vergreifen. None of the dictionary definitions of this word (from the verb vergreifen , here used as a verbal noun) will quite do in this Freudian context. I tried ‘inappropriate/unsuitable actions’, but did not want to import any suggestion, however slight, of sexual misconduct, although as the reader will find there is certainly a sexual undercurrent to some of the actions Freud describes in these chapters. I tried ‘erroneous/mistaken/failed actions’, and did not really care for them. ‘Blunders’ is perhaps closer to the sense of the German than any of those terms, but seemed to me too general. Since one of the chief meanings of the verb vergreifen is musical, ‘to strike the wrong note’, I tried ‘off-key’ or ‘out-of-key’ actions. I thought back to what Freud was actually talking about, and came up with ‘actions that miss their mark’: descriptive but clumsy. I contemplated using the phrase in conjunction with an occasional ‘off-key’, but ultimately felt it would be better to employ a single term throughout. In the end I settled upon ‘inadvertent actions’. I then wondered whether the phrase was too close to the ‘fortuitous actions’ of Freud’s second category, but since the English dictionary definition of ‘inadvertent’ in the context of an action is ‘unintentional’, I took comfort from Freud’s own remarks in the opening paragraphs of section VIII: ‘I have drawn up two groups of cases here: those in which the essential factor seems to be the effect of failure itself — the departure from an intention [Intention in German] — I have described as “inadvertent actions” [ Vergreifen ], and those in which, by contrast, the entire action appears inappropriate I call “symptomatic and fortuitous actions”. However,’ adds Freud, sensibly, ‘no clear-cut distinction can be drawn; one has to acknowledge that all the categories mentioned in this work have only a descriptive significance.’

然而，比“错误”（Fehlleistung）更棘手的是，弗洛伊德在本书第八章、第九章以及最后一章中描述的各种行为的英文术语问题。他有时将这类行为统称为“Fehlhandlung”，意指以某种方式出错的行为。但他随后又将其进一步细分为“Das Vergreifen”（第八章的主题）和“Symptom- und Zufallshandlungen”（第九章的主题）。后一章节的标题很容易翻译，即“症状性行为和偶然行为”，而弗洛伊德在探讨这些行为时得出结论，它们实际上是一回事。我遇到的主要困难在于“Das Vergreifen”这个词。在弗洛伊德的语境中，任何词典中对这个词的定义（源自动词vergreifen，此处用作动名词）都无法完全适用。我尝试用“不恰当/不合适的行为”，但不想暗示任何性行为不端的意味，哪怕是轻微的。尽管读者会发现，弗洛伊德在这些章节中描述的某些行为确实带有性暗示。我又尝试用“错误的/失误的/失败的行为”，但不太满意。“失误”或许比这些词更接近德语原文的意思，但我觉得它太笼统了。由于动词vergreifen的主要含义之一是音乐上的，即“弹错音符”，我尝试用“走调”或“不协调”的行为。我回想了一下弗洛伊德实际在谈论的内容，想到了“未能击中目标的行为”：描述准确，但略显笨拙。我考虑过偶尔使用“走调”这个词组，但最终觉得最好还是通篇使用一个词。最后，我决定用“无意的行为”。我随即想到，这个短语是否与弗洛伊德第二类中的“偶然行为”过于接近。但由于英语词典中“inadvertent”在行为语境下的定义是“无意的”，我从弗洛伊德在第八部分开篇段落中的论述中得到了安慰：“我在此列出了两类情况：一类是本质因素似乎是失败本身的结果——即偏离意图——我称之为‘无意行为’；另一类则相反，整个行为本身似乎都不恰当，我称之为‘症状性偶然行为’。然而，”弗洛伊德明智地补充道，“两者之间无法做出明确的区分；我们必须承认，本书中提到的所有类别都只有描述性的意义。”

The translator’s task often consists of such thinking around words in two languages like this, and in the end something has to go down on the printed page, even if one can never be sure of having found the best solution. But the experience, if sometimes tortuous, is always enjoyable. Translators generally would rather not read translations; they are so hungry to get at the words in the original that they inadvertently qualify themselves to be translators. Perhaps just because I had therefore never read Freud in anything but German, I have found the attempt to supply an English version of one of his works particularly fascinating.

译者的工作往往就是围绕两种语言的词语进行这样的思考，最终总要把一些东西呈现在纸上，即便永远无法确定是否找到了最佳方案。但这个过程，即便有时曲折，也总是令人愉悦的。译者通常不愿阅读译文；他们如此渴望理解原文的文字，以至于无意中就具备了译者的资格。或许正因为我之前从未读过弗洛伊德的德语译本，我才觉得尝试翻译他的一部作品格外引人入胜。

Anthea Bell, 2001

安西娅·贝尔，2001年

# ↩

I

我

Forgetting Proper Names

忘记专有名词

In the Monatschrift für Psychiatrie und Neurologie for 1898, I published a brief article entitled ‘On the Psychic Mechanism of Forgetfulness’, and I will summarize its content here as my point of departure for further discussion of the subject. In that article, I subjected the frequent occurrence of temporary inability to remember proper names to psychological analysis, using a telling example drawn from my own self-observation, and I came to the conclusion that this common, and in practice not very significant, case of the failure of a psychic function — the function of memory — casts light on matters going far beyond evaluation of the phenomenon itself.

我在1898年的《精神病学与神经病学月刊》（Monatschrift für Psychiatrie und Neurologie）上发表了一篇题为《论遗忘的心理机制》的短文，本文将概述其内容，以此为出发点，进一步探讨该主题。在那篇文章中，我运用心理分析方法，分析了人们经常出现的暂时性记不住人名的现象，并以我自身的观察为例，得出了这样的结论：这种常见且在实践中并不十分重要的心理功能（即记忆功能）的失效，却揭示了远超现象本身评估的诸多问题。

Unless I am much mistaken a psychologist, asked to explain why we so often fail to remember names which we think we know, would content himself with saying that it is easier to forget proper names than the rest of what our memory contains. He would give plausible reasons explaining the special position occupied by proper names, but he would not suspect that the process had any wider relevance.

除非我理解有误，否则一位心理学家如果被问及为何我们常常记不住自认为熟悉的名字，大概只会说，人名比记忆中的其他内容更容易被遗忘。他会给出一些看似合理的理由来解释人名为何如此容易被遗忘，但他不会想到这个过程还有更广泛的意义。

My own observation of certain details, which may not be present in all cases but can be clearly identified in some, led me to make a thorough study of the phenomenon of the temporary forgetting of names. In such cases the person concerned does not merely forget , but also remembers incorrectly. As he tries to remember the names that elude him other names — substitute names — come into his mind, and although they are immediately recognized as incorrect they persist in forcing themselves upon him. The process that ought to lead to the correct reproduction of the name he is looking for has, so to speak, become displaced , thus leading to the incorrect substitute. The basis of my argument is that in psychological terms this displacement is not merely arbitrary, but follows regular and predictable paths. In other words, I assume that the substitute name or names will relate to the name sought in a way that can be traced, and I hope that if I can succeed in proving this relationship I shall also cast some light on the process which makes us forget names.

我观察到的一些细节（这些细节或许并非所有案例都存在，但在某些情况下却清晰可见）促使我对暂时性遗忘姓名的现象进行了深入研究。在这种情况下，当事人不仅会遗忘，而且还会记错。当他试图回忆起那些一时想不起来的名字时，其他名字——替代名字——会浮现在脑海中。尽管他立刻意识到这些名字是错误的，但它们却会不断地强行出现在他的脑海中。原本应该引导他正确回忆起所寻找名字的过程，可以说发生了偏移，从而导致了错误的替代名字的出现。我的论点是，从心理学角度来看，这种偏移并非完全随机，而是遵循着规律且可预测的路径。换句话说，我假设替代名字与所寻找的名字之间存在某种可追溯的关联。我希望，如果我能够成功证明这种关联，我也能为解释我们遗忘姓名的过程提供一些线索。

In the example that I chose to analyse in 1898, I was trying in vain to remember the name of the Old Master who painted the magnificent frescos of the ‘Four Last Things’ in Orvieto Cathedral. Instead of the name I wanted — Signorelli — the names of two other painters, Botticelli and Boltraffio , sprang to mind, and were immediately and firmly rejected by my judgement as wrong. When I learned the correct name from another source I recognized it instantly and without any hesitation. My study of the influences and associations that had displaced my ability to reproduce the name in this way — taking me from Signorelli to Botticelli and Boltraffio — led me to the following conclusions:

在我选择分析的1898年的例子中，我徒劳地试图回忆起为奥尔维耶托大教堂绘制宏伟壁画《四终》的古典大师的名字。我想要的名字是西尼奥雷利，但脑海中却浮现出另外两位画家的名字：波提切利和博尔特拉菲奥。我立刻断然否定了这两个名字，认为它们是错误的。当我从其他渠道得知正确的名字时，我毫不犹豫地立刻认了出来。我研究了导致我错误地回忆起这个名字的各种影响和联想——从西尼奥雷利到波提切利再到博尔特拉菲奥——最终得出以下结论：

a) The reason for my forgetting the name Signorelli is not to be sought in any special feature of the name itself, or in the psychological nature of the context in which it occurred. The name I had forgotten was just as familiar to me as one of the substitute names — Botticelli — and far more familiar than the other substitute name, Boltraffio, since I could have said hardly anything about the man who bore it except that he belonged to the Milanese school of painting. As for the circumstances in which I forgot the name, they appear to me innocuous, and cast no further light on the matter: I was travelling by carriage from Ragusa in Dalmatia, with a stranger, to a destination in Herzegovina, on the way we began talking about visits we had paid to Italy, and I asked my travelling companion whether he had ever been to Orvieto and seen the famous frescos by ٭٭٭ there.

a) 我忘记西尼奥雷利这个名字的原因并非在于这个名字本身有什么特殊之处，也不是它出现时的心理语境。我忘记的这个名字对我来说和另一个替代名字——波提切利——一样熟悉，而且比另一个替代名字博尔特拉菲奥要熟悉得多，因为我对这个名字的主人几乎一无所知，只知道他属于米兰画派。至于我忘记这个名字的情况，在我看来并无恶意，也无法提供任何线索：当时我和一位陌生人乘马车从达尔马提亚的拉古萨前往黑塞哥维那，途中我们聊起了各自去过的意大利，我问我的旅伴是否去过奥尔维耶托，是否看过那里著名的壁画。

b) My forgetting the name is explained only when I remember the subject we were discussing immediately before I put this question, and it may be seen as a case of disturbance of the new subject by its predecessor. Just before I asked my travelling companion whether he had ever been to Orvieto, we had been speaking of the customs of the Turks who live in Bosnia and Herzegovina. I had told him something I had heard from a colleague who practised medicine among these people, and who said that they usually show both complete confidence in their doctors and a total resignation to fate. If you have to tell them that nothing can be done for a sick patient, they will reply: ‘ Herr [Sir], what can I say? I know that if he could have lived, then you would have saved him!’ And in these remarks the place-names Bosnia and Herzegovina and the word Herr occurred, setting off a series of associations between Signorelli and Botticelli or Boltraffio.

b) 我之所以忘记这个名字，只有当我记起在提出这个问题之前我们正在讨论的话题时，才能解释得通。这或许可以看作是新话题被前一个话题干扰了。就在我问我的旅伴是否去过奥尔维耶托之前，我们正在谈论居住在波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那的土耳其人的习俗。我告诉他，我从一位在当地行医的同事那里听说，他们通常对医生既充满信心，又完全听天由命。如果你不得不告诉他们病人已经无药可救，他们会回答：“先生，我还能说什么呢？我知道如果他能活下来，您一定会救他的！” 在这些话中，出现了波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那这两个地名，以及“先生”这个词，引发了一系列将西尼奥雷利与波提切利或博尔特拉菲奥联系起来的联想。

c) I assume that the train of thought leading from the customs of the Bosnian Turks and so forth could disturb my next idea because before that train of thought reached its end, I had withdrawn my attention from it. I remember that I had been about to tell a second story closely associated in my mind with the first. These Bosnian Turks set a very high value on sexual pleasure, and if anything impairs their sexual faculties they fall into despair, a despair which is in curious contrast to their resignation in the face of death. One of my colleague’s patients once said to him: ‘Well, you know, Herr , without all that, life’s not worth living.’ But I refrained from mentioning this characteristic of the Turks because it was not a subject I thought suitable for a conversation with a stranger. And I did more: I also distracted my attention from continuing my train of thought along those lines, lines that could have led to the subject of ‘death and sexuality’ in my mind. At the time I was feeling the after-effect of some news I had heard a few weeks earlier, during a brief visit to Trafoi : a patient over whom I had taken a great deal of trouble had committed suicide because of an incurable sexual disorder. I am perfectly sure that I did not consciously remember this sad event or anything connected with it on that journey to Herzegovina. But the similarity of the names Trafoi and Boltraffio obliges me to assume that at the time, and although I was intentionally distracting my attention from it, this memory was activated in my mind.

c) 我猜想，从波斯尼亚土耳其人的习俗等等引出的思路可能会干扰我接下来的想法，因为在思路结束之前，我已经转移了注意力。我记得我当时正准备讲述第二个故事，这个故事在我脑海中与第一个故事紧密相连。这些波斯尼亚土耳其人非常重视性快感，如果有什么损害了他们的性能力，他们就会陷入绝望，这种绝望与他们面对死亡时的坦然接受形成了奇特的对比。我的一位同事的病人曾经对他说：“先生，您知道，如果没有这些，人生就失去了意义。”但我没有提及土耳其人的这个特点，因为我觉得这不适合与陌生人谈论。而且，我做的还不止这些：我还转移了自己的注意力，没有继续沿着这些思路思考，因为这些思路可能会引出我脑海中关于“死亡与性”的主题。当时，我正沉浸在几周前短暂探访特拉福伊时听到的一则消息的余波中：一位我曾倾注大量心血的病人，因患有不治之症的性功能障碍而自杀。我完全确定，在那次前往黑塞哥维那的旅途中，我并没有有意识地想起这件悲伤的事，也没有想起任何与之相关的事情。但特拉福伊和博尔特拉菲奥这两个地名如此相似，让我不得不推测，尽管我当时刻意转移注意力，但这段记忆还是在我的脑海中浮现了。

d) I can no longer regard the fact that I forgot the name of Signorelli as mere chance. I have to recognize the influence of a motive in the procedure. I had motives for interrupting myself as I was about to impart my ideas (about the customs of the Turks and so forth) to my companion, and those motives also caused me to block the ideas connected with them, which would have led on to the news I heard in Trafoi, out of my conscious mind. I therefore wanted to forget something; I had repressed something. What I wanted to forget was not in fact the name of the painter of the masterpiece in Orvieto, but the other subject, the one I did want to forget, contrived to associate itself with his name, so that my act of volition failed to find its target, and I unintentionally forgot one idea while I intentionally meant to forget the other. My aversion for remembering was directed against the content of one idea; my inability to remember emerged in another context. Obviously this case would have been simpler if the contexts of my aversion and my inability to remember had been the same. But the substitute names no longer seem to me so entirely unjustified as they were before the context was elucidated; in the manner of a compromise, they remind me of both what I wanted to forget and what I wanted to remember, showing that my intentional forgetfulness was neither wholly successful nor entirely unsuccessful.

d) 我不能再把忘记西尼奥雷利的名字仅仅看作是偶然。我必须承认，这其中存在某种动机。我当时正要向同伴讲述我的想法（关于土耳其人的习俗等等），却突然中断了谈话，而这些动机也导致我刻意压抑了与这些想法相关的念头，这些念头原本会引出我在特拉福伊听到的消息。因此，我想要忘记某些东西；我压抑了某些东西。事实上，我想要忘记的并非奥尔维耶托那幅杰作的画家的名字，而是另一个我真正想要忘记的主题，它巧妙地与他的名字联系在一起，以至于我的意志未能触及目标，我无意中忘记了一个想法，而我原本是想忘记另一个想法。我对记忆的厌恶针对的是某个想法的内容；而我的记忆障碍则出现在另一个情境中。显然，如果我厌恶和无法记住的缘由相同，这件事就会简单得多。但如今，在弄清背景之后，我觉得这些替代名称不再像之前那样完全不合理了；它们像是一种折衷方案，既提醒我曾经想要忘记的，也提醒我曾经想要记住的，这表明我刻意遗忘的努力既非完全成功，也非完全失败。

e) The way in which I made a connection between the name I sought and the subject I had repressed (death and sexuality, etc., with mention of the names of Bosnia, Herzegovina and Trafoi) is very striking. The diagram I give here, taken from my 1898 article, attempts to illustrate this connection.

e) 我将我所寻求的名字与我压抑的主题（死亡、性等等，并提及波斯尼亚、黑塞哥维那和特拉福伊）联系起来的方式非常引人注目。我在此提供的图表（摘自我1898年的文章）试图阐明这种联系。

The name Signorelli has been divided into two. One pair of syllables ( elli ) also occurs unchanged in the substitute name; the other, if we translate Signor into Herr , has a number of different connections with the names belonging to the repressed subject, but because of those connections it eludes reproduction. The substitution occurred as if there had been a displacement of meaning through the linked names of ‘Herzegovina and Bosnia’, but disregarding the sense and the acoustic demarcation of the syllables. In the process, therefore, the names have been treated like the written characters of a sentence that is to be turned into a rebus or pictorial puzzle. No understanding entered my conscious mind of the way in which the substitute names replaced the name of Signorelli. At first it seems impossible to trace any connection — deriving from the recurrence of the same syllables (or rather sets of characters) — between the subject in which the name of Signorelli occurred and the subject that I had repressed just before broaching it.

西尼奥雷利（Signorelli）这个名字被拆分成了两部分。其中一对音节（elli）在替代名称中也保持不变；另一对音节，如果我们把Signor翻译成Herr，则与被压抑主体的名字有着诸多不同的关联，但正因为这些关联，它才无法被复制。这种替换仿佛是通过“黑塞哥维那和波斯尼亚”这两个关联名称转移了意义，却忽略了音节本身的意义和语音界限。因此，在这个过程中，这些名字被当作句子中的文字，准备转换成一个谜语或图画谜题。我完全没有意识到这些替代名称是如何取代西尼奥雷利这个名字的。起初，似乎不可能在西尼奥雷利这个名字出现的主体和我之前压抑的主体之间找到任何联系——这种联系源于相同音节（或者更确切地说是字符集）的重复出现。

It may not be superfluous to point out that the conditions assumed by psychologists to affect correct reproduction and forgetfulness, which we should seek in certain relationships and predispositions, are not invalidated by the explanation I have given above. Only in some cases can a motive be added to the recognized factors that may lead to our forgetting a name, thus also explaining the mechanism of false memory. In the case we are studying here, these predispositions are essential to allow the repressed element to associate itself with the name being sought, and then to repress that name too. The same thing might not have happened with another name, in conditions more favourable to its reproduction. In fact it is likely that a suppressed element is always trying to make itself felt somewhere else, but will succeed in doing so only where it finds suitable conditions. On other occasions, suppression may occur without any disturbance of the functions or, as we might accurately say, without showing any symptoms.

或许有必要指出，心理学家假设的、影响正确记忆和遗忘的条件——即我们应该在某些关系和倾向中寻求的条件——并不会因为我上面给出的解释而失效。只有在某些情况下，我们才能在已知的导致我们忘记名字的因素之外，再添加一个动机，从而解释虚假记忆的机制。在我们研究的案例中，这些倾向至关重要，它们使得被压抑的成分能够与我们正在寻找的名字联系起来，进而也压抑住这个名字。在更有利于记忆的条件下，同样的情况可能不会发生在另一个名字上。事实上，被压抑的成分很可能总是试图在其他地方找到自己的存在，但只有在合适的条件下才能成功。在其他情况下，压抑可能发生在没有任何功能干扰的情况下，或者更准确地说，不会表现出任何症状。

To sum up the conditions for forgetting a name and remembering it incorrectly, therefore, they comprise: 1) a certain predisposition to forget that name, 2) a process of suppression which has taken place shortly before, 3) the possibility of establishing an external association between the name concerned and the recently suppressed element. The last-named condition need not necessarily be considered very important, since the establishment of some association or other is so easy that it would probably be possible to find one in most cases. However, another question, and one that goes deeper, is whether such an external association can really be sufficient to make the repressed element prevent reproduction of the name being sought, or whether there must not necessarily be some closer connection between the two subjects. At first sight one would be inclined to reject this last requirement and say that the temporal proximity of a subject with an entirely different content is enough. On closer examination, however, it becomes increasingly frequent to find that the two elements (the repressed element and the new one), while linked by an external association, also have some connection of content, and such a connection can indeed be shown to exist in my example of Signorelli.

综上所述，遗忘姓名和错误记忆的条件包括：1）某种遗忘该姓名的倾向；2）不久前发生的压制过程；3）在相关姓名和最近被压制的因素之间建立外部关联的可能性。最后一个条件未必十分重要，因为建立某种关联非常容易，在大多数情况下几乎都能找到。然而，另一个更深层次的问题是：这种外部关联是否真的足以使被压制的因素阻止人们回忆起正在查找的姓名？或者说，两者之间是否必须存在某种更紧密的联系？乍一看，人们似乎倾向于否定最后一个要求，认为时间上接近一个内容完全不同的对象就足以导致遗忘。然而，仔细观察就会发现，这两个元素（被压抑的元素和新的元素）虽然通过外部关联联系在一起，但也存在某种内容上的联系，而这种联系确实可以在我的 Signorelli 例子中得到证明。

The value of the insight acquired through analysis of the Signorelli example of course depends on whether one wants to explain the case as typical or as an isolated instance. I can only say that it is extremely usual for a name to be forgotten and incorrectly remembered in the same way as in the Signorelli case which I have set out here. Almost every time I have observed the phenomenon in myself, I have also been able to explain it as being motivated by repression in the way described above. I must also state another point supporting the likelihood that this analysis was typical. I believe that in principle there are no grounds for drawing a distinction between cases in which names are forgotten and incorrectly remembered, and those in which no incorrect substitute names come to mind. Such substitute names occur spontaneously in a number of cases; in certain other cases, where they do not occur spontaneously, they can be made to do so by intense concentration, and they will then show the same connections between the repressed element and the name being sought as they would if they actually had been spontaneous. There seem to be two main factors in the emergence of a substitute name into the conscious mind: first, the effort of concentration, and second, an internal context associated with the psychic material. I might trace the latter to the comparative ease or difficulty of establishing the necessary external association between the two elements. A good many of the cases in which a name is forgotten but no false name is remembered may thus be classed with those cases in which substitute names are produced, as described in the mechanism of the Signorelli example. I will not, however, be so bold as to claim that all cases of forgetting proper names can be classified under this heading. There are undoubtedly cases where names are forgotten for much simpler reasons, We shall probably have defined the facts cautiously enough if we say that while proper names are sometimes forgotten for simple reasons, they are also sometimes forgotten for reasons motivated by repression.

当然，通过分析西尼奥雷利案例所获得的洞见的价值，取决于我们想把这个案例解释为典型案例还是孤立案例。我只能说，像我在此阐述的西尼奥雷利案例那样，名字被遗忘并错误记忆的情况极其普遍。几乎每次我观察到自己出现这种现象时，我都能将其解释为由上述的压抑机制所驱动。我还必须指出另一点，以支持这种分析具有典型性的可能性。我认为，原则上，没有理由区分名字被遗忘并错误记忆的情况和没有想到任何错误替代名字的情况。在许多情况下，这些替代名字会自发出现；在某些其他情况下，即使它们并非自发出现，也可以通过高度集中注意力来诱发，并且它们会展现出与自发出现时相同的压抑因素与所寻找的名字之间的联系。替代名称进入意识层面似乎主要有两个因素：首先是集中注意力，其次是与心理素材相关的内在语境。后者可能与建立两者之间必要的外部联系的难易程度有关。因此，许多忘记名字却记不起假名的情况，可以归类为产生替代名称的情况，正如西尼奥雷利例子中所描述的机制。然而，我不敢断言所有忘记专有名词的情况都可以归入此类。毫无疑问，有些名字的遗忘原因要简单得多。如果我们说，虽然专有名词有时因简单原因而被遗忘，但有时也因压抑而遗忘，那么我们或许已经足够谨慎地界定了事实。

# ↩

II

二

Forgetting Foreign Words

忘记外语

The familiar vocabulary of one’s native language, within the range of normal functioning, seems to be proof against being forgotten. As we all know, it is not the same with words in a foreign tongue. There is a predisposition to forget all parts of speech in another language, and the first degree of functional disturbance appears in the irregularity with which foreign words are available to us, depending on our state of health in general and how tired we happen to be. In a number of cases this kind of forgetfulness operates by the same mechanism as we found in the example of the name Signorelli. As evidence, I will cite a single analysis, but one which is notable for demonstrating some valuable features, and which concerns the forgetting of a word — not in this case a noun — in a Latin quotation. I hope I may be allowed to describe this little incident clearly and at some length.

在正常认知范围内，母语中熟悉的词汇似乎不易遗忘。但我们都知道，外语词汇却并非如此。人们似乎有一种倾向，会忘记另一种语言的所有词性，而这种倾向最先体现在我们对外国词汇的记忆力会受到影响，这取决于我们的整体健康状况和疲劳程度。在许多情况下，这种遗忘的机制与我们在“Signorelli”这个名字的例子中发现的机制相同。作为证据，我将引用一个分析案例，该案例因揭示了一些有价值的特征而引人注目，它涉及对拉丁语引文中某个词（在本例中并非名词）的遗忘。我希望能够清晰而详细地描述这个小事件。

Last summer — again while I was away on holiday — I renewed my acquaintance with a young man who had an academic education and, as I soon realized, was familiar with several of my psychological publications. I no longer remember how we broached the subject, but we were talking about the social standing of the race to which we both belong, and he, being an ambitious man, was deploring the fact that his generation, as he put it, was condemned to waste away unable to develop its talents or satisfy its needs. He concluded his passionately felt remarks with that famous line of Virgil in which the unfortunate Dido urges posterity to avenge her on Aeneas: Exoriare …or rather that was how he meant to conclude, for he could not finish the quotation, and sought to conceal an obvious gap in his memory by rearranging the words: Exoriar(e) ex nostris ossibus ultor! At last he said, in some annoyance: ‘Please don’t smile in that ironic way as if you were relishing my difficulty — you might help me instead. There’s something the matter with that line. How does the whole thing really go?’

去年夏天——又是在我外出度假的时候——我又一次和一位受过高等教育的年轻人重逢。我很快发现，他似乎很熟悉我的几篇心理学著作。我已经记不清我们是如何开启这个话题的了，但我们当时正在谈论我们各自所属种族的社会地位。他是个雄心勃勃的人，他哀叹自己这一代人，正如他所说，注定要虚度光阴，既无法发挥才能，也无法满足自身的需求。他最后引用了维吉尔那句著名的诗句来结束他充满激情的发言。诗中，不幸的狄多恳求后人为她向埃涅阿斯复仇：“Exoriare…”（或者说，他原本想这样结尾，但他没能完整地引用完，于是试图用重新排列的句子来掩盖记忆上的明显缺失：“Exoriar(e) ex nostris ossibus ultor!”（让我们的后裔为她复仇！）他最后有些恼火地说：“请不要用那种讽刺的笑容，好像你很享受我的窘境似的——你或许可以帮帮我。这句台词有点问题。整句话到底是怎么写的？”

‘I’ll be happy to tell you,’ I replied, and quoted the line as it really runs: Exoriar(e) aliquis nostris ex ossibus ultor! [May someone rise, an avenger, from my bones!]

“我很乐意告诉你，”我回答道，并引用了这句诗的原文：Exoriar(e) aliquis nostris ex ossibus ultor! [愿有人从我的骸骨中崛起，成为复仇者！]

‘How stupid of me to forget a word like that. But you’re always saying that people don’t forget things for no reason at all. Can you tell me how I came to forget the impersonal pronoun aliquis ?’

“我居然忘了这么个词，真是太蠢了。但你总是说人不会无缘无故地忘记事情。你能告诉我我怎么会忘记非人称代词aliquis吗？”

I readily accepted this challenge, hoping for a contribution to my collection, so I said, ‘We can get to the root of it at once if you’ll tell me everything that occurs to you when you concentrate on the word you forgot, without any definite intention in mind but honestly and exercising no critical judgement .’ 1

我欣然接受了这个挑战，希望能为我的收藏增添一些内容，所以我说：“如果你能把你在集中注意力思考你忘记的那个词时想到的一切都告诉我，我们就能立刻找到问题的根源。不要有任何预设的目的，只要诚实地、不带任何批判性地思考就行。”

‘All right, I think of the ridiculous idea of dividing the word into two parts, like this: a and liquis .’

“好吧，我想到一个荒谬的想法，就是把这个词分成两部分，像这样：a 和 liquis。”

‘What does that suggest to you?’ ‘I’ve no idea.’ ‘So what else occurs to you?’ ‘Well, it goes on like this: relics — liquidation — liquidity — fluid [German: Reliquien — Liquidation — Flüssigkeit — Fluid ]. Does that tell you any more?’

“这让你想到什么？”“我不知道。”“那你还能想到什么？”“嗯，它就这样一直延续下去：遗物——清算——流动性——流体[德语：Reliquien——清算——Flüssigkeit——流体]。这能告诉你更多吗？”

‘No, not by a long way. But go on.’

“不，差得远呢。不过，你继续吧。”

‘Well,’ he continued with a sarcastic laugh, ‘I think of Simone of Trento , whose relics I saw a couple of years ago in a church in that city. I think of the accusations of ritual sacrifice once again being levelled against the Jews these days, and I think of the work by Kleinpaul , who sees all the alleged victims as incarnations of the Saviour, new editions of him, so to speak.’

“嗯，”他带着讽刺的笑声继续说道，“我想到了特伦托的西蒙，几年前我在那座城市的一座教堂里看到了他的遗物。我想到了如今犹太人再次被指控进行祭祀仪式，我还想到了克莱因保尔的作品，他把所有所谓的受害者都视为救世主的化身，可以说是救世主的全新版本。”

‘That idea isn’t entirely unconnected with the subject we were discussing before you forgot the Latin word.’

“这个想法与我们之前讨论的话题并非完全无关，只是你忘了那个拉丁词而已。”

‘You’re right. And then I think of a piece I read recently in an Italian newspaper. I think the headline was: The Opinions of Saint Augustine on Women. What do you make of that?’

“你说得对。然后我想起了最近在意大利报纸上读到的一篇文章。我记得标题是：《圣奥古斯丁对女性的看法》。你对此有何看法？”

‘I’m still waiting to see.’

“我还在等待结果。”

‘Well, now I come to something that quite certainly has no connection with our subject.’

“嗯，现在我要说的这件事，肯定和我们今天的主题没有任何关系。”

‘I did ask you to abstain from any critical judgement —’

“我确实要求你不要妄加评判——”

‘All right, I know. Well, I remember a fine-looking old gentleman whom I met on my travels last week. A real original [German: ein wahres Original ] who looks like a great bird of prey. His name is Benedikt , in case that’s of any interest.’

“好吧，我知道了。嗯，我记得上周旅行时遇到一位相貌英俊的老先生。他真是个特立独行的人，长得像一只威猛的猛禽。他叫贝内迪克特，如果你感兴趣的话。”

‘At least we now have a whole series of saints and church fathers: St Simon , St Augustine , St Benedict. And I believe one of the church fathers was called Origen. What’s more, three of those names are first names, like Paul , part of the surname Kleinpaul.’

“至少我们现在有了一系列圣人和教父：圣西蒙、圣奥古斯丁、圣本笃。而且我相信其中一位教父名叫奥利金。更重要的是，这三个名字中有三个是名字，比如保罗，它是克莱因保罗这个姓氏的一部分。”

‘Next I think of St Januarius and the miracle of his blood — but I imagine all this is just mechanical association.’

“接下来我想到了圣雅努阿里乌斯和他宝血的奇迹——但我认为这一切都只是机械的联想。”

‘Never mind that; St Januarius and St Augustine are both connected with the calendar. Can you remind me of the miracle of the saint’s blood?’

“别管那些了；圣雅努阿里乌斯和圣奥古斯丁都与历法有关。你能提醒我一下圣人宝血的神迹吗？”

‘Oh, surely you know that! There’s a phial of the blood of St Januarius which is kept in a Neapolitan church and miraculously liquefies on a certain feast-day. The people think highly of this miracle and get very upset if it is late to occur, as it once was under French occupation. At the time the commanding general — or am I wrong there? Was it Garibaldi? — well, he took the priest aside and let him know, indicating the soldiers posted outside in a very meaningful manner, that he very much hoped the miracle would soon take place. And sure enough, so it did…’

“哦，你肯定知道！那不勒斯的一座教堂里保存着一瓶圣雅努阿里乌斯的血，据说在某个节日会奇迹般地液化。人们对这个奇迹非常敬重，如果奇迹迟迟不发生，他们就会非常难过，就像法国占领时期那样。当时的指挥官——我记错了吗？是加里波第吗？——他把神父叫到一边，意味深长地指了指教堂外的士兵，告诉他，他非常希望奇迹能尽快发生。果不其然，奇迹真的发生了……”

‘Well, go on. Why do you hesitate?’

“那就说吧。你为什么犹豫呢？”

‘I’ve just thought of something…but it’s too private to tell you…anyway, I can’t see any connection, so there’s no need to mention it.’

“我刚刚想到一件事……但这太私人了，不方便告诉你……反正我觉得这之间没什么联系，所以没必要提。”

‘Leave me to make the connections. I can’t force you to tell me something if you’d rather not, but in that case you can’t ask me to tell you how you came to forget the word aliquis either.’

“让我来理清头绪。如果你不想说，我不能强迫你，但既然如此，你也不能问我你是怎么忘记‘aliquis’这个词的。”

‘Really? You think not? Very well, I suddenly thought of a lady who might soon be giving me news that would be very unwelcome to both of us.’

“真的吗？你觉得不会？好吧，我突然想到一位女士，她可能很快就会告诉我一些我们俩都不愿听到的消息。”

‘You mean she’s missed her period?’

“你是说她月经没来吗？”

‘How on earth did you guess that?’

“你是怎么猜到的？”

‘It’s not so difficult. You gave me plenty of background information. Remember the calendar saints, the liquefaction of the blood on a certain day, the agitation when it failed to occur, the overt threat to the effect that the miracle must happen, or else …The fact is that you reworked the miracle of St Januarius to make it an ingenious reference to the lady’s period.’

“这并不难。你给了我很多背景信息。记住日历上的圣人，记得某一天血液会液化，记得当奇迹没有发生时人们的焦虑，记得那种必须发生奇迹否则就会有后果的公开威胁……事实上，你重新诠释了圣雅努阿里乌斯的奇迹，巧妙地将其与那位女士的月经联系起来。”

‘I had no idea. Do you really think I couldn’t come up with that little word aliquis just because I’m waiting anxiously for news?’

“我完全不知道。你真以为我只是焦急地等待消息，就想不出‘aliquis’这个词吗？”

‘I’m sure of it. Remember the way you separated it into a-liquis , and then the associations with relics, liquidation, fluid. And need I point out how St Simon the child martyr, of whom the relics reminded you, fits into this context?’

“我确信这一点。还记得你是如何把它分解成‘a-liquis’（液体）的吗？还有，你联想到的圣物、清算、液体这些概念。我还需要指出，圣物让你想起的殉道圣西蒙，是如何融入到这个语境中的吗？”

‘I’d rather you didn’t. I hope you won’t take these ideas of mine seriously — that is, if I ever really had them. In return I’ll confess that the lady is Italian, and I went to Naples with her. But couldn’t it all be coincidence?’

“我倒希望你别这么想。我希望你不要把我的这些想法当真——如果我真的有过这些想法的话。作为交换，我会承认那位女士是意大利人，我和她一起去了那不勒斯。但这会不会只是巧合呢？”

‘I must leave it to your own judgement to decide whether you can explain away all these connections by assuming coincidence. But I can tell you that any similar case, if you care to offer it for analysis, will lead you to equally remarkable “coincidences”.’ 2

“至于你是否能用巧合来解释所有这些联系，我必须交由你自己判断。但我可以告诉你，任何类似的案例，如果你愿意进行分析，都会发现同样令人惊奇的‘巧合’。”

I have several reasons to value this little analysis, and I owe my travelling companion of that time thanks for providing it. First, because in this case I was able to draw on a source not commonly available to me. I am usually obliged to take those examples of the psychic disturbance of functioning in everyday life that I am collecting in this work from my self-observations. I try to avoid the far greater wealth of material offered by my neurotic patients because I have to face the potential objection that the phenomena in question are the outcome and expression of neurosis. Consequently it is particularly valuable for my purposes when someone else, a person in good mental health, presents himself as the subject of such an investigation. This analysis is also valuable to me in another way, because it casts light on a case of forgetting a word without the substitution of another word by the memory, confirming my statement above that the emergence of incorrect substitute memories, or their failure to emerge, does not constitute grounds for any essential distinction. 3

我之所以珍视这份简短的分析，有几个原因，我非常感谢当时的旅伴提供这份分析。首先，因为在这种情况下，我能够利用一个我通常无法获得的资料来源。通常情况下，我不得不从自身的观察中收集日常生活中精神功能障碍的案例。我尽量避免使用神经症患者提供的更为丰富的素材，因为我不得不面对这样的潜在质疑：这些现象是神经症的结果和表现。因此，当一位心理健康的人主动提出作为此类研究的对象时，对我来说就显得尤为珍贵。这份分析对我来说还有另一个价值，因为它阐明了一个遗忘某个词语却没有用其他词语替代的案例，这证实了我之前的观点：错误的替代记忆的出现，或者它们的缺失，并不构成任何本质区别的理由。

The main value of the aliquis example, however, lies in another of its differences from the Signorelli case. In that example, the reproduction of the name was impaired by the influence of a train of thought on which I had just embarked, then breaking it off, but the content of which stood in no clear relation to the new subject containing the name of Signorelli. Only a connection of temporal contiguity existed between the repressed subject and the forgotten name, but that was enough for me to connect the two by external association. 4 In the aliquis example, on the other hand, there is no trace of any such independent repressed subject occupying my acquaintance’s conscious mind just before the incident and making itself felt as disturbance. The disturbed reproduction of the line of verse here arose from the subject on which it touched, producing unconscious opposition to the wishful thinking expressed in the quotation. One must reconstruct the process thus: the speaker was lamenting the fact that the rights of the present generation of his people are restricted; a new generation, he foretells, like Dido, will be avenged on its oppressors. So he has expressed a wish for offspring. At the same moment a contradictory idea enters his mind. ‘Do you really want children so much? Surely not. It would be very difficult for you to receive news at this point that you may in fact expect to have offspring by a certain person of your acquaintance. No, you do not want offspring — however useful they might be in the matter of revenge.’ This contradiction makes itself felt by creating an external association between one of its conceptual elements, and an element in the wish that was rejected, and this time it does so very forcefully, through what appears to be an artificial and circuitous associative route. A second significant similarity to the Signorelli example derives from the fact that the contradiction arises from repressed sources and sets out from ideas which would divert the attention. — So much, then, for the difference and the internal relationship between these two paradigmatic examples of forgetting a name. We have become acquainted with a second mechanism for forgetting something: the disturbance of an idea by an inner contradiction arising from something repressed. This process strikes me as the more easily comprehensible, and we shall come across it again several times in the course of this work.

然而，这个别名例子的主要价值在于它与西尼奥雷利案例的另一个不同之处。在西尼奥雷利的例子中，我之所以无法准确地复述名字，是因为我刚刚开始思考，然后又中断了思考，而思考的内容与包含西尼奥雷利名字的新主题之间并没有明显的关联。被压抑的主题和被遗忘的名字之间只存在时间上的邻近关系，但这足以让我通过外部联想将两者联系起来。 4 而在别名例子中，没有任何迹象表明，在事件发生之前，我的熟人有任何独立的、被压抑的主题占据了他的意识，并让他感到不安。这里，诗句复述的混乱源于它所触及的主题，从而产生了对引文中所表达的愿望的无意识反对。我们必须这样重构这个过程：说话者在哀叹他这一代人的权利受到了限制；他预言，新一代人将像狄多一样，向压迫者复仇。因此，他表达了想要子嗣的愿望。与此同时，一个矛盾的想法涌上心头。“你真的那么想要孩子吗？肯定不是。此时此刻，你很难接受自己可能与某个熟人育有子女的消息。不，你不想要孩子——无论他们在复仇中多么有用。”这种矛盾通过在自身概念的某个要素与被否决的愿望的某个要素之间建立外部联系而显现出来，这一次，它通过看似人为且迂回的联想路径，以一种非常强烈的方式呈现出来。与西尼奥雷利的例子相比，第二个显著的相似之处在于，这种矛盾源于被压抑的根源，并始于那些会转移注意力的想法。——以上便是这两个遗忘名字的典型例子之间的差异和内在联系。我们已经了解了第二种遗忘机制：某种观念因被压抑的内在矛盾而受到干扰。在我看来，这个过程更容易理解，而且在接下来的论述中，我们还会多次遇到它。

Notes

笔记

1 . This is the usual way of bringing concealed ideas into the conscious mind. Cf. my Interpretation of Dreams [II] ( Gesammelte Werke , 8th edition, p. 71).

1. 这是将隐藏的想法带入意识的常用方法。参见我的《梦的解析》[II]（Gesammelte Werke，第 8 版，第 71 页）。

2 . This little analysis has aroused much attention in the professional literature on the subject, giving rise to lively discussion. E. Bleuler has tried to record the credence to be placed on psychoanalytical interpretation in mathematical terms by using this very example, and has concluded that such interpretation has a greater degree of probability than thousands of undisputed ‘medical findings’, occupying its present anomalous position only because we are not yet used to reckoning on psychological probabilities in science. ( Das autistisch-undisziplinierte Denken in der Medizin und seine Überwindung [ Autistically Undisciplined Thinking in Medicine and Overcoming It ], Berlin 1919.)

2. 这篇简短的分析在相关专业文献中引起了广泛关注，并引发了热烈的讨论。E. Bleuler 试图用数学术语来记录精神分析解释的可信度，并以这个例子为例得出结论：这种解释比成千上万无可争议的“医学发现”具有更高的概率，它目前之所以处于这种特殊的地位，仅仅是因为我们尚未习惯在科学中运用心理学概率。（《医学中的自闭症式思维及其克服》，柏林，1919 年。）

3 . Further observation tends to moderate the difference between the substitute memories in the Signorelli analysis and the aliquis case, for in both the forgetting seems to have been accompanied by a substitute formation. When I asked my interlocutor later whether some substitute had not occurred to him in his efforts to remember the missing word, he told me that initially he had been tempted to add an ab to the line: nostris ab ossibus (perhaps derived from the disconnected part of a-liquis ), and that then the word exoriare had forced its way into his mind with particular clarity and persistence. Taking the sceptical approach, he added that this was obviously because it was the first word of the line. But when I asked him to think about the associations of exoriare , he gave me the word ‘exorcism’. I can well imagine that the emphasis on exoriare in his recital of the line represented the force of such a substitute formation. It would have come about through the association of exorcism with the names of the saints. However, these are details upon which one need not dwell too much. (On the other hand P. Wilson, ‘The Imperceptible Obvious’, Bevista de Psiquitria , Lima, January 1922, insists that the emphasis added to exoriare is very enlightening, since exorcism would have been the best symbolical substitute for the repressed idea of an abortion to get rid of the unwanted child. I am happy to accept this correction, which does not invalidate the force of the analysis.) It does, however, seem possible that the appearance of some kind of substitute memory is a constant, if perhaps only a characteristic and revealing, feature of tendentious forgetfulness motivated by repression. This substitute formation may also occur where no incorrect substitute names have emerged, by emphasizing an element closely related to the forgotten subject. In the Signorelli case, for instance, while the name of the painter eluded me, my visual memory of the cycle of frescos and his self-portrait in the corner of one of the pictures was extremely clear , or at least far more intense than my traces of visual memory usually are. In another case, also mentioned in my article of 1898, I had entirely forgotten the street name in an address in a strange town which I did not much want to visit, but as if to mock me the house number came into my mind with the utmost clarity, although I usually have the greatest difficulty in remembering numbers.

3. 进一步的观察似乎缓和了西尼奥雷利分析和aliquis案例中替代记忆之间的差异，因为在这两种情况下，遗忘似乎都伴随着替代结构的形成。后来我问我的对话者，在他努力回忆缺失的词语时，是否曾想过某种替代词，他告诉我，起初他曾想在诗句中添加一个ab：nostris ab ossibus（或许源自a-liquis的断续部分），然后exoriare这个词以格外清晰和持久的方式闯入了他的脑海。他以怀疑的态度补充说，这显然是因为它是诗句的第一个词。但当我让他思考exoriare的联想时，他告诉我的是“驱魔”。我完全可以想象，他在背诵这句诗时对exoriare的强调，正是这种替代结构的力量。这可能是由于驱魔与圣徒的名字联系起来而产生的。然而，这些细节无需过多赘述。（另一方面，P. Wilson 在《不可察觉的显而易见》（载于《精神病学杂志》，利马，1922年1月）中坚持认为，对 exoriare 的强调非常具有启发性，因为驱魔是象征性地替代被压抑的堕胎观念（即为了摆脱不想要的孩子而堕胎）的最佳方式。我乐于接受这一修正，这并不影响分析的有效性。）然而，某种替代记忆的出现似乎是压抑驱动的倾向性遗忘的一个恒定特征，即便它或许只是这种遗忘的一个典型特征。即使没有出现错误的替代名称，这种替代记忆的形成也可能通过强调与被遗忘的主题密切相关的元素而发生。例如，在西尼奥雷利（Signorelli）的例子中，虽然我记不起画家的名字，但我对那组壁画以及其中一幅画角落里的自画像却记忆犹新，或者至少比我通常的视觉记忆要清晰得多。另一个例子也出现在我1898年的文章中，我完全忘记了一个陌生小镇的街道名称，而我并不想去那里。但仿佛是为了嘲弄我，门牌号却无比清晰地浮现在我的脑海中，要知道我通常最不擅长记数字。

4 . I would not like to say I am fully convinced that there was no internal connection at all between the two trains of thought in the Signorelli case. Careful study of my repressed thoughts on the subject of death and sexuality does produce an idea that comes close to the subject of the Orvieto frescos.

4. 我并不想说我完全确信西尼奥雷利案中的两种思路之间没有任何内在联系。仔细研究我压抑的关于死亡和性欲的想法，确实会产生一个与奥尔维耶托壁画主题接近的想法。

# ↩

III

三

Forgetting Names and Sequences of Words

忘记人名和词序

Experiences like the one just described, accounting for the way in which a sequence of words from a quotation in a foreign language can be forgotten, make one curious to know whether forgetting sequences of words in the speaker’s mother tongue requires some fundamentally different explanation. People are not usually surprised to find that, after a certain lapse of time, they can reproduce a form of words or a poem learnt by heart only inaccurately, making changes and leaving gaps. However, as this forgetfulness is not uniform in the way it affects something learnt in a coherent context, but once again seems to dislodge only parts of it from the mind, it may be worth bringing analytical investigation to bear on some examples of this kind of inaccurate reproduction.

刚才描述的经历解释了为什么人们会忘记外语引文中的某些词语，这不禁让人好奇，忘记母语中的某些词语是否需要某种截然不同的解释。人们通常不会惊讶地发现，经过一段时间后，他们只能不准确地复述一些曾经背诵过的词语或诗歌，常常会做出改动或留下空白。然而，这种遗忘并非总是如出一辙，它对在连贯语境中学习的内容的影响也并非完全一致，而似乎只会将部分内容从脑海中抹去。因此，或许值得对这类不准确复述的例子进行一些分析研究。

In conversation with me, a younger colleague said he thought that forgetting poems in one’s mother tongue could well be motivated in the same way as forgetting parts of a sequence of words in a foreign language, and offered himself as a subject for study. I asked him to say what poem he would like as the test piece, and he chose Goethe’s ballad ‘Die Braut von Korinth’ [‘The Bride of Corinth’], a poem of which he said he was very fond, and he thought that he knew it by heart, or at least several verses of it. As he began reciting it he had a moment of really striking uncertainty. ‘Does it go: “From Corinth to Athens there came”, or: “To Corinth from Athens there came”?’ he asked. I hesitated for some time myself, but then pointed out, with a smile, that the tide of the poem, ‘The Bride of Corinth’, left us in no doubt of which way the youth was going. His recitation of the first verse then went smoothly, or at least without any notable inaccuracy. After the first line of the second verse, my colleague seemed to be searching for words, but he soon continued, and recited:

一位年轻的同事和我聊天时说，他认为忘记母语诗歌的原因可能和忘记外语单词序列的原因类似，并主动提出以自己为研究对象。我问他想用哪首诗来做测试，他选择了歌德的叙事诗《科林斯的新娘》。他说他很喜欢这首诗，而且自认为能背诵，至少能背诵其中的几句。当他开始背诵时，突然出现了一个明显的犹豫。“是‘从科林斯到雅典’，还是‘从雅典到科林斯’？”他问道。我也犹豫了一会儿，然后笑着指出，《科林斯的新娘》这首诗的韵律已经很清楚地告诉我们这位年轻人要背诵的是哪一句。他背诵第一节诗句的过程很顺利，至少没有出现任何明显的错误。背完第二节诗句的第一句后，我的同事似乎在斟酌用词，但他很快又继续背诵了下去：

Aber wird er auch willkommen scheinen,

但他会受到大家的欢迎吗？

Jetzt, wo jeder Tag was neues bringt?

现在每天都有新鲜事发生了？

Denn er ist noch Heide mit den Seinen

因为他和他的人民仍然是异教徒。

Und sie sind Christen und — getauft.

他们是基督徒，而且已经受洗。

[But will he still be welcome now that every day brings something new? For he and his kin are heathen, and they are Christians and — baptized.]

但如今每天都有新情况发生，他还会受到欢迎吗？因为他和他的亲属是异教徒，而他们却是基督徒，而且——受过洗礼。

I had already been listening with a sense that something had gone wrong, and after the end of the second line we both agreed that there had been some distortion. As we could not think just what it was, however, we hurried off to the library to look up Goethe’s poem, and found to our surprise that the wording of the second line of this verse was nothing like what my colleague had quoted, but had been, so to speak, rejected by his memory and replaced by something quite different. The lines really ran:

我当时就觉得哪里不对劲，听完第二行后，我们俩都觉得有些地方出了问题。但我们一时想不出究竟哪里不对，于是赶紧跑到图书馆查阅歌德的诗，结果惊讶地发现，这首诗第二行的措辞和我同事引用的完全不一样，仿佛是被他的记忆抛弃了，取而代之的是完全不同的内容。原文是这样的：

Aber wird er auch willkommen scheinen,

但他会受到大家的欢迎吗？

Wenn er teuer nicht die Gunst erkauft ?

如果他不用昂贵的手段收买人心呢？

[But will he still be welcome if he does not buy favours dear?]

但如果他不花钱买人情，还会受欢迎吗？

Getauft [baptized] rhymed with erkauft [buys], and I thought it odd that the combined ideas of ‘heathen’, ‘Christian’ and ‘baptized’ had not been more helpful to him in his reproduction of the text.

Getauft（受洗）与 erkauft（购买）押韵，我觉得很奇怪，“异教徒”、“基督徒”和“受洗”这几个概念的组合并没有对他复述文本起到更大的帮助。

‘Can you explain,’ I asked my colleague, ‘how you came to forget a whole line in a poem that you say you know very well, and do you have any idea where you found what you substituted for it?’

“你能解释一下吗？”我问我的同事，“你明明说你很熟悉一首诗，怎么会忘记其中的一整行呢？你知道你从哪里找到替代它的诗句了吗？”

He was in fact able to offer an explanation, although he obviously did not like doing so. ‘The line about “every day bringing something new” strikes me as familiar; I must have used those words recently in connection with my practice for, as you know, I’m very pleased with its flourishing state at the moment. But how did that sentence get into the poem? In fact I believe I can think of a connection. The reason why I obviously didn’t care for the line about “buying favours dear” is to do with a lady to whom I recently proposed marriage. She turned me down, but now, in view of the great improvement in my financial situation, I am thinking of proposing again. I can’t tell you any more, but of course if I am accepted this time, it won’t be pleasant for me to remember that a certain amount of calculation was involved on both occasions.’

事实上，他确实能够给出解释，尽管他显然并不愿意这样做。“‘每天都有新事物’这句诗让我感到似曾相识；我最近肯定在谈论我的实践时用过这些词，因为，你知道，我对它目前的蓬勃发展状态非常满意。但这句话怎么会出现在诗里呢？事实上，我想我能想到一个联系。我之所以不喜欢‘花钱买人情’这句诗，是因为最近我向一位女士求婚了。她拒绝了我，但现在，鉴于我的经济状况有了很大的改善，我正在考虑再次求婚。我不能透露更多，但当然，如果这次她答应了，我会很不愉快地想起，两次求婚都包含着某种算计。”

This seemed to me plausible enough without my needing to know the circumstances in any more detail. However, I went on to ask: ‘But how did you come to insert yourself and your private relationships into the text of “The Bride of Corinth”? Are there perhaps differences of religious faith involved in your own case — differences of the kind that become significant in the poem?’

我觉得这解释得挺有道理，无需了解更多细节。不过，我还是继续问道：“你是如何将自己和你的私人关系融入到《科林斯的新娘》这首诗的文本中的呢？你的情况是否涉及宗教信仰上的差异——那种在诗中显得重要的差异？”

Keimt ein Glaube neu ,

当一种新的信仰萌芽时，

Wird oft Lieb’ und Treu

往往是爱与忠诚

Wie ein böses Unkraut ausgerauft.

像拔除讨厌的杂草一样把它拔掉。

[When a new faith begins to burgeon, love and constancy are often rooted out like weeds.]

[当一种新的信仰开始萌芽时，爱与忠诚往往会像杂草一样被连根拔起。]

As it happened, I had not guessed right, but it was remarkable to see how this one penetrating question suddenly enlightened my colleague, enabling him to give me an answer which I am sure he had not known himself until that moment. He looked at me with a rather troubled and reluctant expression, and murmured a later quotation from the poem under his breath:

结果，我猜错了，但令人惊讶的是，我这一个直击要害的问题竟让我的同事茅塞顿开，让他给出了一个他自己此前也未曾想到的答案。他带着几分困惑和不情愿的神情看着我，低声吟诵了诗中的一段：

Sieh sie an genau!

仔细看看它们！

Morgen ist sie grau , 1

明天将是灰色的， 1

[Look closely at her! For tomorrow she’ll be grey,]

仔细看看她！因为明天她的头发就会变灰了。
