adding briefly, ‘The lady is a little older than me.’ Here I broke off our investigation to spare him any more embarrassment. The explanation seemed to me adequate, although it was undoubtedly surprising to find that an attempt to trace a harmless slip of the memory back to its origins touched on such intimate and painful feelings in the subject I was studying, distant as they were from the poem.

我简短地补充道：“这位女士比我年纪稍长一些。”说完，我便结束了我们的调查，以免他更加尴尬。我觉得这个解释已经足够了，尽管的确令人惊讶：试图追溯一段看似无害的记忆偏差，竟然触及了我研究对象内心深处如此私密而痛苦的情感，而这些情感与诗歌本身却相去甚远。

Here, in the author’s own words, I will quote from C. G. Jung, 2 who gives another example of a case in which words from a well-known poem were forgotten.

在这里，我将引用作者自己的话语，引用荣格的话，他举了另一个例子，说明一首著名诗歌中的词语是如何被遗忘的。

‘A man was about to recite Heine’s familiar poem “Ein Fichtenbaum steht einsam” [‘A spruce tree stands alone’]. In the line that says Ihn schläfert [It drowses] he became hopelessly stuck, having entirely forgotten the next words, mit weißer Decke [with a white covering]. It seemed to me odd for anyone to forget such a famous line, and I asked him to tell me what he thought of in connection with the phrase mit weißer Decke. He produced the following train of thought: “Well, a white covering suggests a shroud — the linen cloth covering a corpse — (pause) — and that makes me think of a close friend — a friend whose brother recently died quite suddenly — apparently it was a heart attack — and he was a very stout man — my friend is stout too, and it has occurred to me that he might go the same way — he probably doesn’t take enough exercise — and when I heard of the death I suddenly feared the same thing might happen to me too, since our family is inclined to obesity anyway, and my grandfather died of a heart attack; I’m afraid I am overweight myself, so I have recently gone on a diet.”

“一位男士正要朗诵海涅那首著名的诗《一棵云杉树孤零零地立着》（Ein Fichtenbaum steht einsam）。在念到‘它打盹’（Ihn schläfert）这句时，他却突然卡住了，完全忘记了接下来的‘披着白布’（mit weißer Decke）。我觉得很奇怪，竟然有人会忘记这样一句名句，于是我问他，‘披着白布’（mit weißer Decke）这个词组让他想到了什么。”他接着说道：“嗯，白色的覆盖物让人联想到裹尸布——覆盖尸体的亚麻布——（停顿）——这让我想起一位挚友——他哥哥最近突然去世了——显然是心脏病发作——他是个非常壮硕的人——我的朋友也很壮硕，我突然想到他可能也会遭遇同样的命运——他可能缺乏锻炼——当我听到他去世的消息时，我突然担心同样的事情也会发生在我身上，因为我们家本来就容易肥胖，而且我的祖父就是死于心脏病；恐怕我自己也超重了，所以我最近开始节食了。”

‘Unconsciously, therefore, this gentleman identified with the spruce tree wrapped in its white shroud,’ comments Jung.

“因此，这位先生在不知不觉中认同了那棵被白色裹尸布包裹的云杉树，”荣格评论道。

The following example of forgetting a series of words, which I owe to my friend S. Ferenczi of Budapest, differs from those mentioned above in referring to something said in ordinary conversation, not a quotation from a poet. It will also illustrate the rather unusual kind of case in which we forget something for our own good, because our common sense threatens to be overcome by some passing fancy. The slip of the mind thus has a useful function. Once we are in a more sober mood again, we concur with those ideas that could previously express themselves only in failure — forgetting something, psychic impotence.

以下这个忘记一系列词语的例子，要感谢我的朋友，布达佩斯的S. Ferenczi，它与前面提到的例子不同，因为它指的是日常对话中的一些话语，而不是诗人的引语。它还将说明一种相当特殊的情况：我们忘记某些事情反而对我们有益，因为我们的常识有可能被一时兴起的想法所蒙蔽。因此，这种记忆失误具有一定的实用价值。一旦我们恢复清醒，我们就会认同那些之前只能以失败告终的想法——遗忘，精神上的无能为力。

‘At a party someone quoted the saying: Tout comprendre c’est tout pardonner [To understand all is to forgive all]. I said that the first part of the sentence was enough on its own; to speak of “pardoning” was arrogant, since forgiveness is best left to God and men of the cloth. Another man present thought this remark of mine very good, and I was emboldened — probably to heighten my kindly critic’s good opinion of me — to say that I had recently thought of something better. But when I was about to repeat it, it refused to come back to my mind. I immediately withdrew and wrote down the ideas that had screened it out. First was the name of a friend of mine in Budapest and the street where he lives, which was where the idea I was trying to retrieve had come to me; then the name of another friend, Max , known to us as Maxi. This in turn led me to the word maxim , and I remembered that on that occasion (as in the case mentioned above) I was thinking about an alteration to a familiar maxim. Oddly enough, I then came up not with a maxim, but with the phrase God created man in his own image , and its reverse: Man created God in his. Thereupon the memory of what I was looking for immediately surfaced: that day in Andrássy Street my friend had said: Nothing human is alien to me , whereupon I — referring to psychoanalytical findings — said: You should go further than that, you ought to confess that nothing animal is alien to you.

在一次聚会上，有人引用了一句谚语：“Tout comprendre c’est tout pardonner”（理解一切即宽恕一切）。我说，这句话的前半部分就足够了；谈论“宽恕”未免太过傲慢，因为宽恕最好还是留给上帝和神职人员。在场的另一位男士觉得我这番话很有道理，我便更加大胆——大概是为了博得这位和蔼批评者的好感——说我最近想到了一个更好的主意。但当我正要重复一遍时，却怎么也想不起来了。我立刻停了下来，把那些让我忘记它的想法都写了下来。首先是我在布达佩斯的一位朋友的名字和他住的街道，我试图找回的灵感正是在那里产生的；然后是另一位朋友的名字，Max，我们都叫他Maxi。这让我联想到了“格言”这个词，我记起当时（就像上面提到的情况一样），我正在思考如何修改一句耳熟能详的格言。奇怪的是，我当时想到的不是格言，而是“上帝按照自己的形象创造了人”，以及它的反义词：“人按照自己的形象创造了上帝”。这时，我一直在寻找的东西立刻浮现在我的脑海中：那天在安德拉什大街，我的朋友说：“对我来说，没有什么是陌生的。”于是我——引用精神分析的研究成果——说：“你应该更进一步，你应该承认，对我来说，没有什么是陌生的。”

‘However, when I had finally remembered what I was trying to recall, I could not tell my story in the company where I happened to find myself. The party included the young wife of the friend to whom I had commented on the animal nature of the unconscious mind, and I was aware that she would not like such a distasteful notion. My forgetting the story had spared me a number of awkward questions from her and a discussion leading nowhere, and that must have been the reason for my “temporary amnesia”.

“然而，当我终于想起自己努力回忆的事情时，却无法在当时的场合讲述这件事。聚会上还有我之前评论过潜意识动物本性的那位朋友的年轻妻子，我知道她不会喜欢这种令人不快的想法。我忘记这件事让我免于被她问一些尴尬的问题，也避免了一场毫无意义的讨论，这大概就是我‘暂时失忆’的原因吧。”

‘It is interesting that the substitute idea which occurred to me was a saying in which the deity is downgraded to the status of a human invention, while the comment I was really looking for referred to the animal element in human nature. What both sayings had in common was a capitis diminutio , the idea of demotion. The whole thing was obviously just the continuation of the train of thought about understanding and pardoning set off by our conversation.

“有趣的是，我脑海中浮现的替代想法是一句将神降格为人类发明之物的谚语，而我真正想表达的却是关于人性中动物性成分的评论。这两句谚语的共同之处在于它们都带有贬低的意味，即‘capitis diminutio’（降级）。显然，这一切都只是我们谈话中关于理解和宽恕的思考的延续。”

‘The fact that in this case I found what I was looking for so quickly may also owe something to the fact that I immediately withdrew from the party where I felt I could not tell such a story, and went into an empty room.’

“这次我能这么快找到我想要的东西，可能也跟我立即离开我觉得无法讲述这个故事的聚会，走进一个空房间这件事有关。”

Since then I have analysed many other cases of forgetting a phrase, or reproducing it inaccurately, and the general consensus of my findings in these studies makes me inclined to think that the mechanism of forgetting, as demonstrated in the aliquis and ‘Bride of Corinth’ examples, is almost universally valid. It is usually rather awkward to describe such analyses, since like those mentioned above they always lead to intimate subjects that are painful to the person who is the subject of analysis, so I will add no more such examples. Something in common to all these cases, regardless of their material, is that whatever has been forgotten or distorted is linked by association, in some way or other, with unconscious ideas which manifest themselves as forgetfulness.

此后，我分析了许多其他遗忘或错误复述短语的案例，这些研究结果的普遍共识使我倾向于认为，正如在“阿利奎斯”和“科林斯的新娘”案例中所展示的那样，遗忘机制几乎是普遍适用的。描述这类分析通常相当棘手，因为就像上述案例一样，它们总是会触及被分析者难以启齿的私密话题，所以我不再赘述此类例子。所有这些案例的共同之处在于，无论其具体内容如何，被遗忘或扭曲的内容都以某种方式与潜意识观念相关联，而这些潜意识观念最终表现为遗忘。

I will now go back to the subject of forgetting names, since we have not yet thoroughly investigated either how or why such cases occur. Since this is a kind of slip that, on occasion, I am particularly apt to observe in myself, I am not at a loss for examples here. The slight migraines from which I still suffer usually announce themselves hours in advance by my inability to remember names, and when they are at their worst, although they do not force me to stop work, I often forget all proper names entirely. Now, cases like mine could raise an objection in principle to our analytical work. Should we not conclude from such observations that the reasons for forgetfulness, more particularly the forgetting of names, reside in circulatory and general functional disturbances of the cerebrum, and spare ourselves the attempt to find psychological explanations of these phenomena? I would not agree at all: that would mean confusing the mechanism of a process which is the same in every case with features encouraging it, which vary and are not necessarily present. Rather than engaging in a dispute, however, I will counter any such objection with a parable.

现在，我将回到忘记名字这个话题，因为我们尚未彻底探究此类情况发生的原因和方式。由于我有时也容易出现这种记忆力衰退的情况，因此我有很多例子可以说明问题。我仍然会受到轻微偏头痛的困扰，这种症状通常会在发作前几个小时出现，表现为我记不住名字。偏头痛最严重的时候，虽然不会让我停止工作，但我常常会完全忘记所有人的名字。像我这样的情况可能会从根本上质疑我们的分析工作。我们是否应该从这些观察中得出结论：遗忘，尤其是忘记名字，其原因在于大脑循环和整体功能紊乱，从而放弃寻找这些现象的心理学解释呢？我完全不同意这种观点：这相当于将一个在所有情况下都相同的机制，与那些因人而异且并非必然存在的促成因素混淆起来。然而，与其争论，我更愿意用一个寓言来反驳这种反对意见。

Let us suppose I have been incautious enough to go walking at night in a part of a city where there are few people around. I am attacked, and my watch and purse are stolen. I report the theft at the nearest police station, saying: I was in such and such a street, where isolation and darkness robbed me of my watch and purse. Although this account would not have been inaccurate, such a way of putting it would risk making the police think me not quite right in the head. I could describe the facts of the matter correctly only by saying that, aided by the isolation of the place and under cover of darkness, unknown criminals had stolen my valuables. The situation in which we forget names need not be different; encouraged by weariness, circulatory disturbance or intoxication, an unknown psychic power deprives me of access to the proper names in my memory, whereas in other cases the same power can cause the same failure of memory in someone enjoying his full health and strength.

假设我粗心大意，晚上独自一人在人烟稀少的城市街区散步。结果遭到袭击，手表和钱包被盗。我到最近的警察局报案，说：“我当时在某某街，因为周围人烟稀少，加上夜色昏暗，手表和钱包被偷了。”虽然这样的描述并非不实，但这种说法可能会让警察觉得我精神不太正常。我只有这样才能如实描述事情经过：由于地点偏僻，夜色昏暗，一些身份不明的罪犯偷走了我的贵重物品。我们忘记名字的情况也类似；疲劳、血液循环紊乱或醉酒等因素，会让我不知不觉地忘记别人的名字；而同样的原因，即使是身体健康、精力充沛的人，也可能出现记忆力衰退的情况。

When I analyse those instances of forgetting names that I observe in myself, I almost always find that the name which eludes me is related to some subject closely affecting my own person, and able to cause me strong and often painful feelings. According to the felicitous phraseology of the Zurich school (Bleuler, Jung and Riklin), which I recommend, the phenomenon can be expressed thus: the name eluding me has touched on some ‘personal complex’ of mine. The relation of the name to my person is unexpected and is usually conveyed by superficial association (double meanings, similarities of sound); in general, it can be described as a tangential relationship. A few simple examples are the best way to clarify its nature:

当我分析自己偶尔出现的忘记名字的情况时，我几乎总是发现，那个我记不起来的名字与我自身密切相关的某些事物有关，并且能够引发我强烈而往往痛苦的情感。根据苏黎世学派（布鲁勒、荣格和里克林）精辟的表述（我推荐这种表述），这种现象可以这样表达：我记不起来的名字触及了我自身的某些“个人情结”。这个名字与我的关联是出乎意料的，通常是通过表面上的联想（双关语、发音相似）来传达的；总的来说，它可以被描述为一种间接的关联。以下几个简单的例子最能阐明其本质：

1) A patient asked me to recommend him a spa resort on the Riviera. I knew of such a place very near Genoa, I recollected the name of my German colleague who practises there, but although I believed I knew the place itself very well I could not remember its name. I had to ask my patient to wait while I went off in a hurry to consult the female members of my family. ‘What’s the name of that place near Genoa where Dr N. has his little clinic, the one where Frau so-and-so had treatment for so long?’ ‘Well, fancy you of all people forgetting the name! It’s called Nervi. ’ And as a neurologist I do indeed have a great deal to do with nerves.

1）一位病人让我推荐里维埃拉的一个温泉度假村。我知道热那亚附近有个这样的地方，也想起了我一位在那里执业的德国同事的名字，但我虽然自认为对那个地方很熟悉，却怎么也想不起它的名字。我只好让病人稍等片刻，匆匆忙忙地去咨询一下家里的女性成员。“热那亚附近那个地方叫什么名字来着？就是N医生开诊所的那个，某某女士在那里接受了很久的治疗。”“哎呀，你居然忘了名字！它叫内尔维。”作为一名神经科医生，我的确经常和神经打交道。

2) Another patient mentioned a nearby holiday resort, saying that it has not only two well-known inns but also a third, one which he remembered very well for a certain reason; give him a moment, he said, and he would tell me its name. I queried the existence of this third inn, pointing out that I had spent seven summer holidays running at the same resort, and must therefore know it better than he did. Annoyed by my contradicting him, however, my patient soon produced the name. The inn was called the Hochwartner. I had to admit that I was wrong, and indeed confess that during my seven summers at the resort I had stayed very close indeed to that same inn, although I had denied its existence. Why should I have forgotten both that fact and its name? I think it was because the name was uncomfortably like that of a Viennese colleague of mine, in this case touching on a ‘professional’ complex in me.

2）另一位病人提到附近有个度假胜地，说那里不仅有两家著名的旅馆，还有第三家，他因为某种原因对这家旅馆印象特别深刻；他说，稍等片刻，他就能告诉我旅馆的名字。我质疑这第三家旅馆的存在，指出我曾在同一个度假胜地度过了七个暑假，因此肯定比他更了解。然而，我的病人被我反驳得有些恼火，很快就说出了旅馆的名字。那家旅馆叫霍赫瓦特纳旅馆（Hochwartner）。我不得不承认自己错了，而且坦白说，在我待在那个度假胜地的七个夏天里，我确实就住在那家旅馆附近，尽管我一直否认它的存在。我为什么会忘记这件事和它的名字呢？我想是因为这个名字和我一位维也纳同事的名字太像了，这让我感到很不舒服，也触动了我内心深处的“职业情结”。

3) Another time, just as I was about to buy a train ticket at Reichenhall station, I could not remember the name of the next large railway station, although I had passed it very often, and it was usually perfectly familiar to me. I actually had to look for it on the timetable. It was Rosenheim , and then I immediately knew the association that had made me forget it. An hour earlier, I had been to see my sister who lives quite close to Reichenhall. My sister’s name is Rosa, so I had been visiting a ‘Rose Home’. The ‘family complex’ had removed the name of the place from my mind.

3）还有一次，我正准备在赖兴哈尔火车站买票，却突然想不起下一个大火车站的名字。虽然我经常路过那里，通常都非常熟悉。我不得不查时刻表才找到。原来是罗森海姆，我立刻明白了是什么让我忘记了它。一个小时前，我去看望了住在赖兴哈尔附近的姐姐。姐姐名叫罗莎，所以我去的是一个“玫瑰之家”。这个“家庭式养老院”让我完全忘记了它的名字。

4) I can trace the positively predatory effects of the ‘family complex’ through a whole series of examples. One day a young man visited my consulting rooms. He was the younger brother of a woman patient of mine, I had met him on countless occasions, and I was used to referring to him by his first name. I was about to mention his visit when I discovered that I had forgotten that first name, not at all an unusual one, and there was no way I could call it to mind. I went out into the street to read the signboards over business premises, and recognized the name as soon as I encountered it. Analysis told me that I had seen a parallel between my visitor and my own brother which was trying to lead me to the repressed question of whether my brother would have acted in a similar way or an entirely different one in the same case. The external connection between the ideas of his family and my own was established by the coincidence that both our mothers had the same first name: Amalia. In retrospect, I was then able to understand the substitute names, Daniel and Franz, which had come into my mind without throwing any light on my difficulty. Like Amalia, they are names of characters in Schiller’s play Die Räuber [ The Robbers ], and in his essays on ‘Walks in Vienna’, the Viennese journalist Daniel Spitzer makes a humorous reference to these names.

4）我可以通过一系列例子来追溯“家庭情结”的积极影响。有一天，一位年轻男子来我的诊室就诊。他是我一位女病人的弟弟，我见过他无数次，习惯直呼其名。我正要提起他的来访，却发现自己忘记了他的名字——一个并不罕见的名字——而且怎么也想不起来。我走到街上，查看商铺的招牌，一眼就认出了这个名字。分析告诉我，我当时看到了这位来访者和我自己的弟弟之间的相似之处，这试图引导我思考一个被压抑的问题：如果换作是我弟弟，他会采取类似的行动，还是会采取完全不同的行动？我们之间家庭观念的外部联系，源于一个巧合：我们的母亲都叫阿玛莉亚（Amalia）。现在回想起来，我才明白之前脑海中浮现的丹尼尔和弗朗茨这两个替代名字的含义，它们并没有解答我的疑惑。和阿玛莉亚一样，它们也是席勒戏剧《强盗》中的人物名字。维也纳记者丹尼尔·施皮策在其关于“维也纳漫步”的文章中，曾幽默地提及这两个名字。

5) On another occasion I could not remember a patient’s name because of certain associations dating back to my youth. My analysis took a long and circuitous path around the subject before coming up with the name I wanted. My patient had expressed a fear of going blind, which reminded me of a young man who had in fact been blinded by a shotgun; this memory was associated with the thought of another young man who had shot himself and whose surname was the same as the first patient’s, although they were not related. However, I hit upon the name only after realizing that I had transferred a sense of anxious expectation from these two cases involving young people to a member of my own family.

5）还有一次，我因为一些可以追溯到我年轻时的联想而记不起一位病人的名字。我的分析围绕着这个话题绕了很久，才最终想起我想要的名字。我的病人曾表达过对失明的恐惧，这让我想起一个被猎枪击中致盲的年轻人；这段记忆又让我想到另一个开枪自杀的年轻人，他的姓氏与第一位病人相同，尽管他们之间并无亲缘关系。然而，直到我意识到自己把这两个年轻人身上的焦虑和担忧转移到了我自己的一个家人身上时，我才恍然大悟，想起了这个名字。

There is thus a constant stream of ‘self-referentiality’ going through my mind. I am not usually aware of it, but it betrays itself when I forget names in this way. It is as if I were obliged to relate everything I hear about other people to myself: as if my personal complexes were aroused by my perception of others. This cannot possibly be a quality peculiar to myself alone; instead, it must contain some indication of the way in which we perceive ‘otherness’. I have reason to suppose that exactly the same thing happens in other people’s minds as in mine.

因此，我的脑海中始终萦绕着一股“自我指涉”的思绪。我通常对此浑然不觉，但当我因此忘记人名时，它便会显露出来。仿佛我必须将听到的关于他人的一切与自身联系起来：仿佛我对他人的感知会唤起我的个人情结。这绝非我独有的特质；相反，它必然包含着我们感知“他者”方式的某种暗示。我有理由推测，在他人心中，也同样存在着类似的现象。

My best example of this kind was told me, as an experience of his own, by one Herr Lederer. On his honeymoon in Venice, he met a gentleman whom he knew slightly and whom he therefore felt he should introduce to his young wife. But as he had forgotten the stranger’s name, he got over the difficulty on this first occasion by murmuring something indistinct. When he met the man again, as he was bound to do in Venice, he took him aside and asked him to remind him of his surname, which he, Herr Lederer, was sorry to say he had forgotten. The stranger’s answer showed great understanding of human nature: ‘I can easily believe that you didn’t remember my name. It’s Lederer , like yours!’ One cannot help feeling slightly uncomfortable on discovering that a stranger has the same name, as I realized very clearly not long ago, when a Herr S. Freud called during my consulting hours. (However, I must mention here the assurance of one of my critics that his reaction to such an eventuality is the opposite of mine.)

我听过一个关于这类事情的最佳例子，是一位名叫莱德勒的先生讲述的亲身经历。他在威尼斯度蜜月时，遇到一位略有交情的绅士，便觉得应该介绍给年轻的妻子。但由于他忘记了这位陌生人的名字，第一次见面时，他含糊不清地嘟囔了几句，勉强应付过去。后来，在威尼斯他又一次遇到了这位男士，于是他把对方拉到一边，请他提醒自己姓氏，因为莱德勒先生很遗憾地承认自己已经忘记了。这位陌生人的回答展现了他对人性的深刻理解：“我完全相信你记不起我的名字。我的姓是莱德勒，和你的一样！” 发现陌生人与自己同名，难免会感到有些不自在，这一点我不久前就深有体会，当时一位名叫S·弗洛伊德的先生在我咨询时间打电话来。（不过，我必须在此提及一位批评家，他向我保证，他对这种情况的反应与我截然相反。）

6) The effectiveness of self-referentiality is also evident in the following example, cited by Jung: 3

6) 荣格引用的以下例子也体现了自我参照的有效性： 3

‘A certain Herr Y. fell in love with a lady who did not return his affection, and soon afterwards married another man, Herr X. Although Herr Y. had known Herr X. for some time and even had business dealings with him, he was constantly forgetting the man’s name, and on several occasions when he wanted to correspond with Herr X. he had to ask other people what it was.’

“有一位名叫Y的先生爱上了一位不爱他的女士，不久之后便嫁给了另一位男士，X先生。虽然Y先生认识X先生已经有一段时间了，甚至还和他有过生意往来，但他总是忘记X先生的名字，有好几次他想和X先生通信时，不得不向别人询问他的名字。”

In this case the motivation for his forgetting the name is clearer than in the previous one, which was governed by self-referentiality. Here the forgetfulness seemed to derive directly from Herr Y.’s dislike of his more successful rival; he did not want to know anything about him; ‘let him be expunged from memory [ Nicht gedacht soll seiner werden : a line from the poet Heine]’.

在这种情况下，他忘记对方名字的动机比前一个由自我指涉所驱动的例子要清晰得多。这次的遗忘似乎直接源于Y先生对这位更成功的竞争对手的厌恶；他不想了解他的任何事；“让他从记忆中抹去吧[Nicht gedacht soll seiner werden: a line from the poet Heine]”。

7) There can also be a subtler motive for forgetting a name, something that might be called ‘sublimated’ resentment of its bearer. For instance, a lady called Fräulein I. von K. writes, from Budapest:

7）忘记名字也可能存在更微妙的动机，可以称之为对名字持有者的“潜移默化”的怨恨。例如，一位名叫Fräulein I. von K.的女士从布达佩斯写道：

‘I have a little theory. I have noticed that people with a talent for painting do not generally have any feeling for music, and vice versa. Not long ago I was talking to someone about my theory, and said, “So far I have found that my observation always holds good, with just a single exception.” But when I tried to remember the name of that one exceptional person it was lost from my mind without trace, although I knew that the man concerned was one of my closest acquaintances. When I heard someone mention him by chance a few days later, of course I realized at once that this was the name of the man who invalidated my theory. My unconscious resentment of him was expressed in my forgetting his name, which I usually knew perfectly well.’

我有个小理论。我注意到，有绘画天赋的人通常对音乐没什么感觉，反之亦然。不久前，我和人谈起我的理论，我说：“到目前为止，我的观察一直都成立，只有一个例外。” 但当我试图回忆起那个例外的人的名字时，却怎么也想不起来，尽管我知道这个人是我最亲近的人之一。几天后，我偶然听到有人提起他，当然，我立刻意识到，这就是那个推翻我理论的人。我潜意识里对他的怨恨，体现在我忘记了他的名字上，而我通常对他的名字都记得很清楚。

8) Self-referentiality led to a name’s being forgotten in a rather different way in the following case, recorded by Ferenczi. Its analysis is particularly useful because of the light it casts on substitute ideas (as in my substitution of Botticelli-Boltraffio for Signorelli).

8）在费伦齐记录的以下案例中，自指性导致一个名字以一种截然不同的方式被遗忘。对它的分析特别有用，因为它揭示了替代概念（例如我用波提切利-博尔特拉菲奥代替西尼奥雷利）。

‘A lady who had heard something about psychoanalysis could not remember the name of the psychiatrist Jung.

一位女士听说过精神分析，但却记不起精神分析学家荣格的名字。

‘Instead, she came up with the following ideas: “Kl. (a name) -Wilde — Nietzsche — Hauptmann.”

相反，她想出了以下几个主意：“Kl.（一个名字）-王尔德—尼采—豪普特曼。”

‘I did not tell her Jung’s name, but asked her to try free association on each of the ideas that had occurred to her.

“我没有告诉她荣格的名字，而是让她对她想到的每一个想法进行自由联想。

‘Taking Kl., she immediately thought of Frau Kl. , saying she was an affected lady but good-looking for her age. “She never seems to grow old. ” She mentioned “ mental illness ” as something in common to both Wilde and Nietzsche , and said ironically: “You Freudians will go on looking for the causes of mental illnesses until you fall mentally ill yourselves.” Then she added: “I can’t bear Wilde and Nietzsche. I just don’t understand them. I’ve heard they were both homosexual, and Wilde went around with young men.” (She had actually given the correct name in this sentence, Jung, although admittedly in Hungarian, but she still could not remember it.)

“提到Kl，她立刻想到了Kl夫人，说她是个矫揉造作的女人，但年纪虽小却容貌姣好。“她好像永远不会老。”她提到“精神疾病”是王尔德和尼采的共同点，并讽刺地说：“你们这些弗洛伊德主义者会一直寻找精神疾病的病因，直到你们自己也患上精神疾病为止。”然后她又补充道：“我受不了王尔德和尼采。我就是理解不了他们。我听说他们都是同性恋，王尔德还和年轻男子厮混。”（其实她在这句话里已经说出了正确的名字——荣格，虽然是用匈牙利语说的，但她还是记不起来了。）

‘When she came to Hauptmann she thought first of Halbe , and then of Jugend [Hauptmann and Halbe are the names of dramatists; Jugend — ‘youth’ — was the title of a play by Halbe]. Only now, when I drew her attention to the word “youth”, did she realize that the name she was trying to remember was Jung [young].

“当她来到豪普特曼面前时，她首先想到的是哈尔贝，然后是《青年》（豪普特曼和哈尔贝是两位剧作家的名字；《青年》是哈尔贝的一部戏剧的标题）。直到现在，当我提醒她注意‘青年’这个词时，她才意识到她努力记住的名字是荣格（年轻）。

‘In fact this lady, who had lost her husband when she was thirty-nine and was unlikely to marry again, had sufficient reasons to avoid thinking of anything that would call youth and age to her mind. The striking factor is that her substitute ideas were associated with the name she was looking for purely in terms of their content, and there were no associations of sound.’

事实上，这位女士在39岁时失去了丈夫，而且不太可能再婚，她有充分的理由避免去想任何会让她联想到青春和衰老的事情。令人惊讶的是，她想到的替代名字与她正在寻找的名字之间的联系完全是基于内容上的，而与发音上没有任何关联。

9) Another and very subtly motivated example of the forgetting of a name was explained by the person concerned himself.

9) 另一个因非常微妙的原因而忘记名字的例子是由当事人自己解释的。

‘When I was taking an examination in philosophy as a subsidiary subject, the examiner asked me about the doctrines of Epicurus , and then inquired whether I knew who had taken up his doctrines again in later centuries. I gave the name of Pierre Gassendi , whom I had heard mentioned in a café only a couple of days before as a disciple of Epicurus. When the examiner asked, in surprise, how I came to know that name, I boldly told him that I had long taken an interest in Gassendi. As a result I passed the examination magna cum laude , but later, I am sorry to say, I had a persistent tendency to forget Gassendi’s name. I suspect I should blame my guilty conscience for my failure to keep that name in my mind now, however hard I try — I ought not really to have known it at the time.’

“我参加哲学辅修考试时，考官问了我关于伊壁鸠鲁学说的问题，然后又问我是否知道后世有哪些人继承了他的学说。我回答说是皮埃尔·伽桑狄，几天前我在一家咖啡馆里听到有人提起他是伊壁鸠鲁的弟子。考官惊讶地问我怎么会知道这个名字，我大胆地告诉他，我一直对伽桑狄很感兴趣。结果我以优异的成绩通过了考试，但遗憾的是，后来我总是会忘记伽桑狄的名字。我想，无论我多么努力，现在都记不住这个名字，我应该怪自己良心不安——当时我的确不应该知道他的名字。”

To appreciate the intensity of this informant’s distaste for remembering that episode during his examination, one needs to know how highly he values his doctorate, which has to compensate for a great deal else in his life.

要体会这位线人在考试期间对回忆起那件事的厌恶程度，就需要了解他有多么看重自己的博士学位，因为博士学位弥补了他生活中很多其他方面的不足。

10) Here is another example of the name of a town being forgotten, perhaps not such a simple case as those cited above, although it will seem both convincing and valuable to anyone familiar with such investigations. The name of an Italian city could not be recalled because of its close similarity of sound to a woman’s first name, which the subject associated with a number of deeply felt memories, not all of them, probably, exhaustively covered in the following account. S. Ferenczi of Budapest, who observed this case of forgetfulness in himself, treated it much as one might analyse a dream or a neurotic idea, and that was certainly the right approach.

10）这里是另一个城镇名称被遗忘的例子，或许不像前面提到的那些案例那样简单，但对于熟悉此类研究的人来说，它既令人信服又颇具价值。一个人想不起一个意大利城市的名字，因为它的发音与一位女士的名字非常相似，而这个名字唤起了他许多刻骨铭心的回忆，这些回忆或许无法在下文中一一详述。布达佩斯的S. Ferenczi观察到自己也出现了这种遗忘现象，他像分析梦境或神经质的想法一样处理了这个问题，这无疑是正确的方法。

‘Today, when I was visiting a family with whom I am friendly, our conversation turned to certain cities in northern Italy. Someone said that they still betray traces of Austrian influence. The names of some of these cities were cited, and there was one that I wanted to mention myself, but I could not think of its name, although I do know that I passed two very pleasant days there, a fact which does not bear out Freud’s theory of forgetfulness. Instead of the name of the city I was looking for the following ideas came into my mind: Capua — Brescia — the Lion of Brescia.

今天，我去拜访一位朋友，我们聊起了意大利北部的一些城市。有人说这些城市至今仍保留着奥地利的影响。他们提到了一些城市的名字，其中有一个我也很想提，但我却怎么也想不起来了。虽然我知道我在那里度过了非常愉快的两天，但这似乎并不符合弗洛伊德的遗忘理论。我脑海中浮现的不是我想找的那个城市的名字，而是以下几个词：卡普阿——布雷西亚——布雷西亚雄狮。

‘I saw this “lion” vividly before me, as if it were really there in the shape of a marble statue , but I immediately noticed that it looked less like the Hon on the monument to liberty in Brescia (which I have seen only in a picture) than another marble lion which I saw in Lucerne on the monument to the Swiss Guards who fell at the Tuileries. I have a miniature reproduction of it standing on my bookshelves. Then, at last, I remembered the name I was looking for: Verona.

“我眼前清晰地浮现出这尊‘狮子’，仿佛它真的就在那里，是一尊大理石雕像。但我立刻注意到，它看起来不像布雷西亚自由纪念碑上的狮子（我只在照片上见过），而更像我在卢塞恩杜伊勒里宫瑞士卫队纪念碑上看到的另一尊大理石狮子。我的书架上就摆着它的微缩复制品。最后，我终于想起了我一直在寻找的名字：维罗纳。”

‘I also know at once whom to blame for this amnesia — none other than a woman who had once been employed by the family I was visiting at that moment. Her name was Veronika , or in Hungarian Verona , and I used to dislike her very much because of her unattractive face, her hoarse, raucous voice and her insufferably overbearing manner (which she felt was justified by her long period of service). Nor could I stand the tyrannical way in which she treated the children of the house. And now I knew the significance of my substitute ideas.

“我也立刻知道该怪谁让我失忆——正是我当时拜访的那户人家曾经雇佣过的一个女人。她叫维罗妮卡，或者用匈牙利语叫维罗娜。我以前非常讨厌她，因为她长相丑陋，嗓音沙哑刺耳，而且为人傲慢无礼（她觉得这是因为她工作时间长，所以理所当然）。她对待那户人家孩子的方式也让我无法忍受。现在我终于明白我那些替代想法的意义了。”

‘I had immediately associated Capua with the phrase caput mortuum , and I had often compared Veronika’s face to a death’s head. The Hungarian word kapzsi (avaricious) must also have played a part in the displacement of my ideas. Of course I also hit upon the much more direct associations linking Capua and Verona, as geographical terms and as Italian words with the same rhythm.

“我立刻将卡普阿与‘死人头’（caput mortuum）这个短语联系起来，而且我经常把维罗妮卡的脸比作骷髅头。匈牙利语单词‘kapzsi’（贪婪的）肯定也影响了我的联想。当然，我也想到了卡普阿和维罗纳之间更直接的联系，无论是作为地理名称，还是作为发音相同的意大利语单词。”

‘The same may be said of Brescia, but once again tortuous byways were involved in the association of ideas.

“布雷西亚的情况也类似，但在此之前，各种想法的联系也经历了曲折的过程。”

‘My dislike of Veronika in the past had been so great that I found her actually nauseating, and expressed amazement, on several occasions, at the idea that she had a love life at all, or could ever be loved. “Surely,” I said, “kissing her would make you feel sick [ Brechreiz , ‘nausea’ in German, echoing the sound of Brescia ”.] And yet I had obviously associated her, long ago, with ideas of the dead Swiss Guards.

“我过去对维罗妮卡的厌恶之情如此强烈，以至于我觉得她令人作呕，我曾多次对她居然有爱情生活，或者说她竟然会被人爱感到震惊。“你肯定，”我说，“吻她会让你感到恶心[Brechreiz，德语意为‘恶心’，发音与布雷西亚相似]。然而，很显然，很久以前，我就把她和死去的瑞士卫队联系起来了。”

’ Brescia is often mentioned, here in Hungary at least, in connection not with the lion but with another wild beast. The most hated name in this country and in northern Italy alike is that of General Haynau, known here simply as the Hyena of Brescia. So one train of thought led from the detested tyrant Haynau by way of Brescia to the city of Verona, and another led from that grave-digging, raucous creature the hyena (an idea connected in my mind with that of a funerary monument) to the death’s head and the grating voice of Veronika, whom my unconscious mind had accused so harshly of being almost as tyrannical in this house in the past as the Austrian general was after the Hungarian and Italian freedom-fighting.

至少在匈牙利，人们提起布雷西亚，往往不是因为狮子，而是因为另一种野兽。在这个国家和意大利北部，最令人憎恶的名字莫过于海瑙将军，他在这里被人们亲切地称为“布雷西亚的鬣狗”。于是，我的思绪从令人憎恶的暴君海瑙，经由布雷西亚，延伸到了维罗纳；而另一条线索则从那只掘墓喧闹的鬣狗（在我脑海中，它与一座墓碑联系在一起）引向了骷髅头和维罗妮卡那刺耳的声音。我的潜意识曾严厉地指责她，说她过去在这个家里的暴政几乎和那位奥地利将军在匈牙利和意大利的自由斗争后一样。

‘And Lucerne was associated with thoughts of the summer spent by Veronika with her employers beside the Lake of Lucerne near that city; then again, the Swiss Guard reminded me of the way she used to tyrannize over not only the children but even the adult members of the family, since she liked to think of herself in the role of Garde-Dame or chaperone.

“卢塞恩让我想起维罗妮卡和她的雇主在卢塞恩湖畔度过的那个夏天；而瑞士卫队又让我想起她过去是如何专横跋扈的，她不仅管束孩子，甚至还管束家里的成年人，因为她喜欢把自己想象成女卫士或监护人的角色。

‘I hasten to add that I long ago overcame this antipathy of mine towards V. — at least consciously. She has now changed very much for the better in both her outward appearance and her behaviour, and I can feel genuinely friendly to her when I meet her (not that I often do so). But as usual, my unconscious mind clings more tenaciously to old impressions, and is unforgiving in retrospect.

我赶紧补充一句，我很久以前就克服了对V的这种反感——至少在意识层面上是这样。她现在无论外表还是行为都发生了很大的变化，而且是朝着好的方向发展，我见到她时也能真心实意地对她友好（虽然我并不经常见到她）。但和往常一样，我的潜意识更顽固地坚持着过去的印象，而且事后回想起来总是难以释怀。

‘The Tuileries referred to another person, an elderly French lady who really did act as a chaperone guarding the ladies of the family on many occasions, and who was respected — and probably to some extent feared — by one and all. For a time I was her élève for French conversation. And the word élève reminded me that when I was visiting my present host’s brother-in-law in northern Bohemia, I couldn’t help laughing at the way in which the local rustic people called the élèves [students] at the College of Forestry there Löwen [‘lions’, because of a similarity of sound between the French and German words]. This amusing memory may also have played a part in the displacement of my ideas from hyena to lion.’

“杜伊勒里宫指的是另一个人，一位年长的法国女士，她确实多次担任杜伊勒里宫女眷的监护人，受人尊敬——或许在某种程度上也令人畏惧。有一段时间，我曾是她的法语口语学生。说到‘学生’这个词，我想起之前去波西米亚北部拜访我现在的房东的姐夫时，当地乡下人称呼林学院的学生为‘狮子’（因为法语和德语发音相似），我忍不住笑了起来。这段有趣的记忆或许也促使我把脑海中的意象从鬣狗转移到了狮子。”

11) The following example 4 is another that shows how a personal complex affecting someone at a certain time can induce him to forget a name very remote from it:

11) 以下示例 4 说明了个人情结在特定时期如何影响一个人，导致他忘记一个与此情结非常遥远的名字：

‘Two men, one older and one younger, who had visited Sicily together six months earlier, were exchanging reminiscences of their pleasant and eventful holiday. “Now, what was the name of that place where we spent the night before going on our expedition to Selinunt?” asked the younger. “I think it was Calatafimi, wasn’t it?” The elder man contradicted him. “No, I’m sure it wasn’t, but I’ve forgotten the name too, although I remember every detail of our visit to the place very clearly. I only have to find that someone has forgotten a name in order to forget it myself. Let’s try to remember the name — although the only thing that comes to my mind is Caltanisetta, and I’m sure that’s not right.” “No,” agreed the younger man, “the name begins with a w , or there’s a w in it somewhere.” “There’s no letter w in Italian,” the elder man reminded him. “Well, I meant v. I only said w because that’s what I’m used to in my native German,” But the older man would have none of the v. “In fact,” he said, “I think I’ve forgotten quite a number of those Sicilian names; it’s about time I tried remembering them. For instance, what’s the name of that place at high altitude which the ancients called Enna? Oh, now I remember: Castrogiovanni” Next moment the younger man remembered the name he had forgotten too. “ Castelvetrano ” he cried, pleased to find that the name did in fact contain the v he had claimed for it. For some time the older man still did not feel that the name was familiar, but once he had accepted it he had to try explaining why it had eluded him. “Obviously because the second half of the name, vetrano , sounds like veteran,” he said. “I know I don’t like to think of growing old, and I react oddly when I’m reminded of the subject. For instance, not long ago I told a friend whom I esteem highly, in rather a strange phrase, that he was “well past his youthful years”, because once he himself, although making various flattering remarks about me, had said that I was not a young man any more. The fact that the first sound in the name Castelvetrano also occurs in my substitute name Caltanisetta shows that it was the second half of the place name I didn’t like.” “What about the name Caltanisetta itself?” asked the younger man. “It has always sounded to me like a pet name for a young woman,” the elder man admitted.

六个月前结伴游览西西里岛的两位男士，一老一少，正在回忆那段愉快而又精彩的假期。“对了，我们去塞利农探险前一晚住的那个地方叫什么名字来着？”年轻人问道。“我想应该是卡拉塔菲米，对吧？”年长的男士反驳道：“不对，我确定不是，不过我也忘了名字，虽然我对那里的每一个细节都记得清清楚楚。我只要发现有人忘了名字，自己也会跟着忘。咱们想想看——虽然我唯一能想到的就是卡尔塔尼塞塔，但我肯定不对。”“不对，”年轻人同意道，“这个名字以w开头，或者里面肯定有w。”“意大利语里没有字母w，”年长的男士提醒他。 “嗯，我指的是v。我说w只是因为我的母语是德语，习惯用w。” 但老人不接受v这个说法。“事实上，”他说，“我想我已经忘记了不少西西里岛的地名；是时候努力记住它们了。比如说，古人称之为恩纳（Enna）的那个高海拔地方叫什么名字来着？哦，我想起来了：卡斯特罗乔瓦尼（Castrogiovanni）。” 话音刚落，年轻人也想起了自己忘记的那个地名。“卡斯特尔韦特拉诺（Castelvetrano）！”他喊道，很高兴地发现这个名字确实包含他之前认为的v。过了一会儿，老人仍然觉得这个名字很陌生，但一旦接受了这个名字，他就不得不解释为什么自己之前一直想不起来。“很明显，因为名字的后半部分，vetrano，听起来像vetér（老兵）。”他说。 “我知道我不喜欢想到变老，而且每当有人提起这个话题，我的反应都会很奇怪。比如，不久前，我用一种很奇怪的措辞告诉一位我非常尊敬的朋友，他已经‘过了青春年华’了，因为他自己曾经虽然对我赞不绝口，但也说过我不再年轻了。卡斯特尔韦特拉诺（Castelvetrano）这个名字的第一个音也出现在我的别名卡尔塔尼塞塔（Caltanisetta）中，这说明我不喜欢的是地名的后半部分。” “那卡尔塔尼塞塔这个名字本身呢？”年轻人问道。“我一直觉得它听起来像是对年轻女性的昵称，”年长者承认道。

‘And a little later he added: “The name I gave Enna was a substitute name too, and now I realize that the name Castrogiovanni , which rationalized its way into my mind, suggests giovane — young — just as the name I could not remember, Castelvetrano , suggested the word veteran — old.”

“过了一会儿，他又补充道：‘我给恩娜取的名字也是一个替代名字，现在我意识到，卡斯特罗乔瓦尼这个名字，在我脑海中逐渐浮现出来，它让人联想到“giovane”（年轻的），就像我记不起的名字卡斯特尔韦特拉诺一样，它让人联想到“veteran”（老的）这个词。’”

‘The elder man thought he had accounted for his forgetting the name in this way, but they did not stop to wonder why the younger man had forgotten it too.’

“年长者认为他已经用这种方式解释了自己忘记名字的原因，但他们并没有停下来思考为什么年轻人也忘记了。”

The mechanism of the phenomenon whereby names are forgotten deserves our interest, as well as the motives for forgetting them. In a great many cases a name is forgotten not because it evokes such motives in itself, but because some similarity of sound suggests another name which we do have good reason to forget. It will be obvious that this broader application of the factors causing the phenomenon helps it to occur very much more easily, as the following examples will show:

名字被遗忘的机制及其背后的动机都值得我们关注。很多时候，名字被遗忘并非因为其本身具有某种动机，而是因为发音上的相似之处让我们联想到另一个我们有充分理由遗忘的名字。显而易见，这种对导致名字遗忘的因素的更广泛应用，使得遗忘现象更容易发生，以下例子将对此进行说明：

12) From Dr E. Hitschmann: ‘Herr N. wanted to give someone the name of the booksellers Gilhofer & Ranschburg, but however hard he racked his brains he could remember only the name of Ranschburg, although he was very familiar with the firm. Coming home with a sense of slight dissatisfaction, he felt the matter was important enough for him to ask his brother, who seemed to have fallen asleep, for the first half of the firm’s name. The brother supplied it at once. Thereupon Herr N. immediately associated the name “Gallhof” with “Gilhofer”. A few months earlier, he had taken a walk which he remembered with pleasure to the Gallhof in the company of an attractive girl, who gave him a souvenir inscribed with the words: “In memory of our delightful hours at the Gallhof” [ Gallhofer Stunden ]. A day or so before he forgot the name of Gilhofer, this item, which it seems was rather fragile, was damaged when N. closed a drawer too rapidly and, being familiar with the significance of symptomatic actions, he registered the fact with a certain feeling of guilt. His attitude to the lady was rather ambivalent at the time; he loved her, but he hesitated to fall in with her wish to get married’ ( Internationale Zeitschrift für Psychoanalyse I, 1913).

12）摘自E. Hitschmann博士的记载：‘N先生想告诉别人吉尔霍夫和兰施堡书店的名字，但他绞尽脑汁也只记得兰施堡这个名字，尽管他对这家书店非常熟悉。他带着些许懊恼回到家，觉得这件事很重要，于是向似乎睡着的哥哥询问书店名字的前半部分。哥哥立刻告诉了他。N先生这才把“Gallhof”和“Gilhofer”联系起来。几个月前，他曾和一位漂亮的姑娘一起散步，去了Gallhof，他至今仍记得那次愉快的经历。姑娘送给他一个纪念品，上面写着：“纪念我们在Gallhof的美好时光”[Gallhofer Stunden]。大约在忘记吉尔霍弗名字的前一天，这件似乎相当易碎的物品被N.用力关抽屉时损坏了。由于他熟悉症状行为的意义，他带着某种内疚感意识到了这件事。当时他对那位女士的态度相当矛盾；他爱她，但他犹豫是否要答应她结婚的愿望。（《国际精神分析杂志》I，1913）

13) From Dr Hanns Sachs: ‘While he was talking about Genoa and its immediate surroundings, a young man wanted to mention a place called Pegli , but he had to think hard before he could remember the name. On the way home he thought about the embarrassing way in which this usually familiar name had eluded him, and his mind led him to the word Peli , which sounds very like Pegli. He knew that there was a South Sea island of that name, and that its inhabitants have retained some curious customs, of which he had recently read in an ethnological work. At the time, he decided to use the information for a hypothesis of his own. Then it struck him that Peli was also the setting of a novel that he had read with interest and pleasure, Laurids Bruun’s Van Zantens glücklichste Zeit [ The Happiest Time of Van Zantens Life ]. The ideas that had occupied him almost all that day were connected with a letter which he had received that morning from a lady who was very dear to him, and which made him fear that a rendezvous they had arranged would fall through. Having spent the whole day in a very bad temper, he had set out in the evening intending to shake off his distressing thoughts and enjoy the party he was going to as whole-heartedly as possible, for he had been looking forward to it a great deal. Obviously the word Pegli was a severe threat to this good resolution, since it sounds so much like Peli , while Peli , which had associated itself with his own ego because of its ethnological interest for him, stood for not only the “happiest time” of Van Zanten’s life but also of his own, and consequently for the fears and anxieties he had felt all day. It is typical of the phenomenon that he could make this simple interpretation only after a second letter had transformed his doubts into the happy certainty of seeing the lady again soon.’

13）汉斯·萨克斯博士写道：“当他谈论热那亚及其周边地区时，一位年轻人想提及一个叫佩格利（Pegli）的地方，但他费了好大劲才想起来。回家的路上，他想到自己竟然想不起这个通常很熟悉的名字，感到很尴尬，于是想到了佩利（Peli）这个词，它的发音与佩格利（Pegli）非常相似。他知道南海有一个同名岛屿，岛上的居民保留着一些奇特的习俗，他最近在一本民族学著作中读到过。当时，他决定利用这些信息提出自己的假设。然后他突然意识到，佩利也是他曾饶有兴致地读过的一部小说——劳里兹·布鲁恩的《范赞滕斯最幸福的时光》（Van Zantens glücklichste Zeit）——的背景地。”他几乎一整天都在想着早上收到的一封信，这封信来自一位他非常珍视的女士，信中他担心两人约好的约会会泡汤。他一整天都心情糟糕，晚上出门时，他打算摆脱这些烦心事，尽情享受即将参加的聚会，因为他一直非常期待。显然，“Pegli”这个词严重威胁着他的好心情，因为它听起来很像“Peli”。而“Peli”这个词，由于其民族学意义，与他的自我意识紧密相连，它不仅代表着范赞滕一生中最快乐的时光，也代表着他自己的，因此也代表着他一整天感受到的恐惧和焦虑。这种现象很典型：直到第二封信到来，他的疑虑才被即将再次见到那位女士的喜悦和确定所取代，他才能够做出如此简单的解释。

If, in thinking of this example, we remember that other and very similar case in which it proved impossible for me to recollect the place name Nervi (example 1), we shall see how the double meaning of a single word can be replaced by assonance between two words.

如果在思考这个例子时，我们想起另一个非常相似的例子，即我不可能记住地名 Nervi（例 1），我们就会明白一个词的双重含义是如何被两个词之间的谐音所取代的。

14) When war with Italy broke out in 1915, I found from my self-observations that a considerable number of Italian place names which I usually knew perfectly well had suddenly vanished from my memory. Like so many others of German origin, I had fallen into the habit of spending part of my holidays on Italian soil, and I could not doubt that my forgetting these names en masse expressed the understandable sense of hostility to Italy which had replaced my old liking for the country. This directly motivated forgetfulness of names, however, went together with an indirect version of the phenomenon that could be traced back to the same influence. I was also inclined to forget non-Italian place names, and in studying these cases I found that some distant similarity of sound connected those words with the enemy place names which I now felt were taboo. For instance, I was racking my brains one day to remember the name of the Moravian town of Bisenz. When it finally came into my mind I knew at once that I could blame my forgetting it on the Palazzo Bisenzi in Orvieto, in which the Hotel Belle Arti, where I had stayed on all my visits to Orvieto, is situated. Naturally, my fondest memories were those that had suffered most damage from my change of emotional attitude.

14）1915年意大利战争爆发后，我通过自我观察发现，许多我通常耳熟能详的意大利地名突然从我的记忆中消失了。像许多其他德裔人士一样，我习惯于在假期去意大利度假，毫无疑问，我集体遗忘这些地名，反映了我对意大利的敌意，这种敌意取代了我以往对这个国家的喜爱。然而，这种直接导致我忘记地名的现象，还伴随着一种间接的、同样源于此的现象。我也倾向于忘记非意大利地名，在研究这些案例时，我发现这些词语与我如今视为禁忌的敌对地名之间存在某种遥远的发音相似性。例如，有一天，我绞尽脑汁也想不起摩拉维亚小镇比森茨（Bisenz）的名字。当我终于想起这件事时，我立刻意识到，我之所以忘记它，要归咎于奥尔维耶托的比森齐宫，我每次去奥尔维耶托都住的贝莱阿蒂酒店就坐落于此。当然，我最美好的回忆，也正是那些因我情绪变化而受损最深的回忆。

It will also be useful to cite some examples reminding us of the various different purposes that can be served by the slip of the mind which makes us forget names.

举一些例子来提醒我们，一时疏忽导致我们忘记名字，这种疏忽可以起到各种不同的作用，这也很有意义。

15) A. J. Storfer (‘Forgetting Names to Ensure that an Idea is Forgotten’): ‘A lady living in Basel was told one morning that Selma X. from Berlin, a friend of her youth now on honeymoon, was passing through that city. This friend from Berlin would be in Basel for only a single day, so the lady who lived there made haste to her hotel. When the two friends parted they arranged to meet again that afternoon, intending to spend the rest of the time until the lady from Berlin had to leave together. That afternoon the lady living in Basel forgot to keep the appointment. I do not know just why she forgot, but in this kind of situation (a meeting with a friend of her youth who was just married) there are several typical sets of circumstances that might have set up resistance against the second meeting. But the really interesting aspect of this case is another slip unconsciously reinforcing the first. At the time when she should have been with her friend from Berlin again, the lady living in Basel was in company elsewhere. The conversation turned to the recent marriage of the Viennese opera singer Kurz. The lady from Basel expressed some criticism (!) of this marriage, but when she was about to mention the singer’s full name she found, much to her embarrassment, that she could not remember her first name. (As we all know, when someone’s surname is monosyllabic we tend to mention that person by his or her first name too.) The lady living in Basel was particularly annoyed by her poor memory because she had often heard Kurz sing, and she usually knew her full name perfectly well. Before anyone else could mention the elusive first name, the conversation took another turn. On the evening of the same day, however, our resident of Basel happened to be in company with some of the people who had also been with her that afternoon. By chance, the conversation again turned to the marriage of the Viennese singer, and the lady gave her full name of “ Selma Kurz ” without any difficulty, exclaiming immediately afterwards: “Oh dear, I’ve just remembered that I quite forgot I had an appointment with my friend Selma this afternoon.” But a glance at the time showed that her friend from Berlin would have left by now’ ( Internationale Zeitschrift für Psychoanalyse II, 1914).

15）A. J. Storfer（《忘记名字以确保一个想法被遗忘》）：一位住在巴塞尔的女士一天早上得知，她年轻时的朋友，来自柏林的塞尔玛·X，正在度蜜月，途经巴塞尔。这位柏林朋友只在巴塞尔待一天，于是这位女士赶紧赶回酒店。两位朋友告别时，约定下午再见面，打算一起度过余下的时光，直到柏林朋友不得不离开。然而，那天下午，这位巴塞尔女士却忘记了赴约。我不知道她究竟为什么会忘记，但在这种情况下（与一位刚刚结婚的年轻朋友见面），通常存在一些典型的因素，可能会使人对第二次见面产生抵触情绪。但这个案例真正有趣的地方在于，另一个无意识的疏忽强化了第一个疏忽。在她本该与柏林朋友再次见面的时候，这位巴塞尔女士却在别处与人相聚。谈话转到了维也纳歌剧演唱家库尔茨最近的婚事上。这位来自巴塞尔的女士对这桩婚事颇有微词（！），但当她正要说出这位歌唱家的全名时，却尴尬地发现自己竟然想不起她的名字。（我们都知道，如果一个人的姓氏是单音节的，我们通常也会用他的名字来称呼他。）这位住在巴塞尔的女士对自己的记忆力不佳感到格外恼火，因为她经常听库尔茨唱歌，而且通常都能清楚地记住她的全名。还没等其他人说出那个难以捉摸的名字，谈话就转向了另一个话题。然而，就在同一天晚上，这位巴塞尔居民恰巧和当天下午与她在一起的一些人聚在了一起。碰巧，谈话又回到了那位维也纳歌手的婚事上，这位女士毫不费力地报出了自己的全名“塞尔玛·库尔茨”，随后立刻惊呼道：“哦，天哪，我刚刚想起来，我完全忘记了今天下午和我的朋友塞尔玛有个约会。”但瞥了一眼时间，就知道她那位来自柏林的朋友现在应该已经离开了。（《国际精神分析杂志》第二卷，1914年）

We may not yet be prepared to do justice to every aspect of this interesting example. The following case is simpler, although it concerns not a forgotten name, but a foreign word forgotten for a motive arising from the situation. (It will be observed that the procedure is the same whether it relates to proper names, first names, foreign words or sequences of words.) In this example a young man forgot the English word for Gold , which in fact is identical with the word in German, to give himself a reason for something he wanted to do.

我们或许还无法全面详尽地分析这个有趣的例子。下面的例子则更为简单，虽然它并非涉及遗忘的名字，而是出于某种情境原因而遗忘的外语单词。（需要注意的是，无论是专有名词、名字、外语单词还是词组，处理方法都相同。）在这个例子中，一位年轻人忘记了英语中“金”这个词，而这个词实际上与德语中的“金”是同一个词，以此为自己想做的事情找个借口。

16) From Dr Hanns Sachs: ‘A young man staying in a mixed boarding house met an Englishwoman and was attracted to her. On the evening of their first meeting he was talking to her in her native language, having a reasonably good command of it, and he wanted to use the English word for “gold” but could not remember it, however hard he tried. Instead, substitute words come into his mind — French or, Latin aureum , Greek chrysos — so persistently that he had difficulty in rejecting them, although he knew perfectly well that they were not related at all to the word he wanted. Finally, the only way he could make himself understood was to touch a gold ring which the lady was wearing on her finger; he was abashed to discover from her that the word for “gold” he had been seeking for so long is exactly the same in English as in German. The significance of the physical contact motivated by his forgetfulness lies not merely in the inoffensive satisfaction of his wish to hold or touch her, a satisfaction that can be fully exploited by lovers on various other occasions, but rather in the light it cast on the prospects for his courtship. The lady’s unconscious mind, particularly when it was well disposed to her interlocutor, would have guessed at the erotic purpose concealed behind the harmless disguise of a forgotten word; her acceptance of the touch and the motive behind it could thus be a means of coming to an understanding on the prospects of this new flirtation — a very significant one even when neither party was conscious of it.

16）汉斯·萨克斯博士讲述道：“一位住在男女混住公寓的年轻男子邂逅了一位英国女子，并被她深深吸引。初次见面当晚，他用她的母语与她交谈，他的德语还算流利。他想用英语中表示‘黄金’的词，却怎么也想不起来。相反，一些替代词不断涌入他的脑海——法语、拉丁语的aureum、希腊语的chrysos——这些词如此挥之不去，以至于他难以摆脱，尽管他非常清楚这些词与他想要的词毫无关联。最终，他唯一能让对方明白他意思的办法是触摸那位女士手指上的一枚金戒指；他尴尬地发现，他苦苦寻找的‘黄金’一词，在英语和德语中竟然是同一个词。”他因遗忘而产生的身体接触，其意义不仅在于满足了他想要拥抱或触摸她的愿望——这种满足感在其他各种场合也同样适用——更在于它为这段恋情的未来走向提供了新的视角。女士的潜意识，尤其是在她对交谈者抱有好感的情况下，会察觉到这看似无害的遗忘之词背后隐藏的情欲意图；她接受这种触碰及其背后的动机，或许正是双方对这段新恋情前景达成共识的一种方式——即便双方当时并未意识到这一点，这种共识也意义非凡。

17) I will also add, from J. Stärcke, an interesting observation of the forgetting and subsequent recollection of a proper name, notable for the fact that the forgetting of the name is linked, as it was in the example of ‘The Bride of Corinth’, with the distortion of a sequence of words from a poem.

17) 我还要补充 J. Stärcke 的一个有趣的观察，即对专有名词的遗忘和随后的回忆，值得注意的是，名字的遗忘与诗歌中一系列词语的扭曲有关，就像“科林斯的新娘”的例子一样。

‘An old lawyer and linguistic scholar, Z., said in company that when he was studying in Germany he knew a remarkably stupid student, claiming that he could tell many tales of this student’s lack of intelligence. However, he could not remember the student’s name; he said he thought it began with W, but then changed his mind. He did remember that the stupid student later became a wine merchant. Then he told another anecdote about the stupidity of this same student, marvelled once more at his inability to remember the name, and said: “He was such an ass that I can still hardly understand how, by dint of sheer repetition, I was able to get some Latin into his head.” A moment later he remembered that the name he was looking for ended in… man. We asked whether he could think of another name ending in the same way, to which he replied: “ Erdmann ” “So who was he?” “Oh, another student I knew at the time.” His daughter, however, pointed out that there was also a Professor Erdmann. On further inquiry, it turned out that this Professor Erdmann, as editor of a journal, had recently printed a paper submitted by Z., but only in abbreviated form, because he was not entirely in agreement with it, etc., and that Z. had taken this badly. (I also learned later that in the past Z. was probably a candidate for a professorial chair in the faculty where Professor E. was now lecturing, so the name may have touched him on the raw for that reason too.)

一位名叫Z的老律师兼语言学家在一次聚会上说，他在德国求学时认识一个极其愚笨的学生，声称自己能讲出很多关于这个学生智力低下的故事。然而，他却想不起这个学生的名字；他说他一开始以为是以W开头的，但后来又改变了主意。他只记得这个愚笨的学生后来成了一名酒商。接着，他又讲了一个关于这个学生愚笨的轶事，再次惊叹于自己竟然记不起名字，说道：“他真是个笨蛋，我至今都难以理解，我究竟是如何靠着一遍又一遍的重复，才让他记住一些拉丁语的。”过了一会儿，他突然想起他要找的名字是以……man结尾的。我们问他是否还能想到另一个以相同结尾的名字，他回答说：“Erdmann。”“那他是谁呢？”“哦，是我当时认识的另一个学生。”然而，他的女儿指出，还有一位名叫Erdmann的教授。进一步询问后得知，这位埃德曼教授作为期刊编辑，最近刊登了Z.提交的一篇论文，但只刊登了节选版，因为他并不完全认同论文内容等等，而Z.对此非常不满。（后来我还了解到，Z.过去很可能曾是埃德曼教授所在学院的教席候选人，所以这个名字可能也因此触怒了埃德曼教授。）

‘But now he suddenly remembered the name of the stupid student: Lindeman ! He had already remembered that the name ended in… man , but the element Linde was repressed for longer. When asked what ideas he associated with Linde [lime tree] he said at first, “None at all” But when I insisted that the word must convey some kind of idea to him, he said, looking up and airily waving a hand: “Well, the lime is a handsome tree.” However, nothing else occurred to him. The company fell silent, and we all went on with our reading or whatever else we had been doing until a few moments later, in an abstracted tone of voice, Z. quoted the following lines:

“但现在他突然想起了那个笨学生的名字：林德曼！他早就记得这个名字以……man结尾，但林德（Linde）这个词却被他压抑了更久。当被问及他对林德（菩提树）有什么联想时，他起初说：‘什么都没有。’但当我坚持认为这个词肯定能给他带来某种联想时，他抬起头，漫不经心地挥了挥手，说道：‘嗯，菩提树很漂亮。’然而，除此之外，他什么也想不起来了。大家顿时鸦雀无声，各自继续阅读或做着其他事情，直到片刻之后，Z.用一种心不在焉的语气引用了以下几行诗句：

Steht er mit festen

他是否坚持己见

Gefügigen Knochen

柔韧的骨骼

Auf der Erde.

在地球上。

So reicht er nicht auf,

所以这还不够，

Nur mit der Linde

只有菩提树

Oder der Rebe

或者说，是葡萄藤。

Sich zu vergleichen.

将自己与他人比较。

[Though he may stand with firm and compliant bones upon the earth , he cannot rise so far as to compare himself even to the lime tree or the vine. ]

[虽然他能以坚实柔韧的骨骼立于大地之上，但他却无法攀升到足以与菩提树或葡萄藤相提并论的高度。]

‘I uttered a cry of triumph. “There we are, there’s your Erdmann,” I said. “The man who “stands upon the earth” is the “earth man” or Erdmann , and cannot compare himself with the lime tree [ Linde ], Lindeman , or the Rebe [vine], the wine merchant. In other words: Lindeman, the stupid student who later became a wine merchant, was an ass, but Erdmann is a much worse ass and doesn’t even compare with this Lindeman.” For the unconscious to produce such an expression of contempt is very usual, and it seemed to me that we had now discovered the main reason why Z. had forgotten the name.

我得意地喊了一声。“瞧，这就是你们的埃尔德曼，”我说。“‘立足大地’的人就是‘大地之人’，也就是埃尔德曼，他根本无法与菩提树（林德）或酒商（雷贝）相提并论。换句话说：林德曼，那个后来成了酒商的愚蠢学生，是个蠢货，但埃尔德曼更蠢，根本无法与这个林德曼相提并论。” 潜意识里流露出这种轻蔑的情绪是很常见的，我觉得我们现在终于找到了Z.忘记这个名字的主要原因。

‘I then asked from what poem the lines came. Z. said they were from a poem by Goethe, and he thought it began:

我接着问他这些诗句出自哪首诗。Z说它们出自歌德的一首诗，他认为这首诗的开头是：

Edel sei der Mensch,

人应当高尚，

Hilfreich und gut!

很有帮助，很好！

[May mankind be noble, helpful and good!)

愿人类高尚、乐于助人、善良！

‘and went on a little later:

过了一会儿，他又继续说道：

Und hebt er sick aufwärts,

如果他把它向上举起，

So spielen mit ihm die Winde.

风在戏弄他。

[And if he rises upwards, the winds will play with him.]

如果他向上飞升，风就会与他嬉戏。

‘Next day I looked up this poem by Goethe, and the case turned out to be even more interesting (and more complicated) than it had seemed at first.

“第二天，我查阅了歌德的这首诗，结果发现这起案件比最初看起来更有趣（也更复杂）。

a) the first lines quoted (cf. above) really run:

a) 上面引用的前几行实际上是这样的：

Steht er mit festen

他是否坚持己见

Markigen Knochen …

强壮的骨骼……

[Though he may stand with firm, powerful bones…]

[尽管他可能拥有坚实强壮的骨骼……]

“‘ Compliant bones” would have been rather an odd construction, but I will leave that aside.

“‘柔顺的骨骼’会是一个相当奇怪的结构，但我暂且不谈这个。”

b) The following lines of the verse (cf. above) run:

b) 以下几行诗句（参见上文）如下：

Auf der wohlbegründeten

基于充分的理由

Dauernden Erde,

永久地球

Reicht er nicht auf,

如果这还不够，

Nur mit der Eiche

只有橡树

Oder der Rebe

或者说，是葡萄藤。

Sich zu vergleichen.

将自己与他人比较。

[On the well-founded, enduring earth, he cannot rise so far as to compare himself even to the oak tree or the vine.]

在坚实而持久的土地上，他无法攀升到足以与橡树或葡萄藤相提并论的高度。

‘So there is no lime tree at all in the whole poem! The change of oak to lime was made (in Z.’s unconscious mind) purely to allow a play on words between “earth — lime — vine”.

“所以整首诗里根本没有菩提树！把橡树换成菩提树（在 Z. 的潜意识里）纯粹是为了玩弄‘泥土——菩提——藤蔓’的文字游戏。”

c) The poem is called ‘Grenzen der Menschheit’ [‘Limitations of Mankind’] and compares the omnipotence of the gods with the feeble powers of man. The poem, which actually does begin:

c) 这首诗名为《人类的局限》（Grenzen der Menschheit），将神的全能与人类的渺小力量进行对比。这首诗的开头是这样的：

Edel sei der Mensch,

人应当高尚，

Hilfreich und gut!

很有帮助，很好！

is another one and comes a few pages further on. It is called ‘Das Göttliche’ [‘The Divine’], and it too contains the poet’s ideas about gods and men. Since we did not go into the matter any further, I can only suspect that ideas about life and death, the temporal and eternal, man’s own weakness and the approach of death played a part in the background to this case.’ 5

还有一首，在后面几页。它名为《神圣》（Das Göttliche），也包含了诗人关于神与人的思想。由于我们没有进一步探讨此事，我只能推测，关于生死、暂时与永恒、人类自身的弱点以及死亡的临近等观念，在这件事的创作背景中发挥了作用。

In many of these examples all the subtleties of psychoanalytical technique have been employed to explain why a name was forgotten. I would suggest that anyone wishing to discover more about such work should read a paper by E. Jones of London which has been translated from the English. 6

在许多此类例子中，精神分析技术的各种微妙之处都被用来解释为什么会遗忘一个名字。我建议任何想要了解更多此类研究的人都应该阅读伦敦的 E. Jones 的一篇论文，该论文已从英文翻译而来。

18) Ferenczi has pointed out that forgetting names can also be a symptom of hysteria, when it operates by means of a mechanism very far from the inadvertent slip. I quote his own account to show the meaning of this distinction:

18）费伦齐指出，忘记名字也可能是癔症的症状，此时癔症的运作机制与无意的口误截然不同。我引用他自己的论述来说明这种区别的意义：

‘At the moment I am treating a patient, an elderly spinster lady, who cannot recall the most common proper names, even those she knows well, although in other respects she has a good memory. During analysis it turned out that this symptom was intended to illustrate her lack of schooling. Her demonstrative display of ignorance was really a reproach to her parents for denying her any higher education. Her painful compulsion to do housework (“housewife psychosis”) also derived in part from the same source. In effect, she was saying: you have made me into a domestic servant.’

“我目前正在治疗一位病人，一位年长的未婚女士，她记不住最常用的人名，即使是她很熟悉的人名也记不住，尽管她在其他方面的记忆力很好。分析结果显示，这种症状是为了表明她缺乏教育。她刻意表现出的无知实际上是在责备父母没有让她接受高等教育。她痛苦地强迫自己做家务（“家庭主妇精神病”）也部分源于此。实际上，她是在说：你们把我变成了一个家庭佣人。”

I could multiply such examples of forgetting names, and discuss them at much greater length, but at this point I would like to avoid mentioning many, indeed almost all, of the points to be considered under later headings. However, I will permit myself to sum up briefly the findings of the analyses described here:

我可以举出更多忘记名字的例子，并对此进行更详细的讨论，但在此我想避免提及许多（实际上是几乎所有）将在后续章节中讨论的要点。不过，我还是可以简要总结一下这里所描述的分析结果：

The mechanism of the forgetting of names (or, rather, the way they elude the mind in temporary forgetfulness) consists in the fact that an alien train of thought, which is not consciously perceived at the time, disturbs the intended reproduction of the name. Either there is an established connection between the name disturbed and the complex that disturbs it, or else such a connection has occurred through superficial (external) associations, often by what may seem a tortuous route.

遗忘名字的机制（或者更确切地说，名字在暂时遗忘中从脑海中溜走的方式）在于，一种当时未被意识察觉的外来思维干扰了对名字的预期回忆。这种干扰要么源于被干扰的名字与干扰它的思维情境之间既有的联系，要么源于表面上的（外部的）联想，而这种联想往往是通过看似曲折的路径产生的。

Among the complexes disturbing the memory those of a private nature (personal, family or professional) turn out to be the most influential.

在影响记忆的各种情结中，私人性质的情结（个人、家庭或职业方面的情结）影响最大。

A name belonging to several cycles of ideas (or complexes), as a result of some ambiguity of meaning, is often forgotten in connection with a certain train of thought because it belongs to another, stronger complex.

由于含义上的某些歧义，一个属于多个思想体系（或复合体）的名称，常常因为属于另一个更强大的复合体而被遗忘，从而与某种思路联系起来。

A wish to avoid arousing unpleasant feelings through the agency of memory is a very strong motive for such disturbances.

避免通过记忆唤起不愉快的情绪是造成这种干扰的一个非常强烈的动机。

In general we can distinguish between two main categories of cases in which names are forgotten: in one the name itself refers to something distressing, in the other it is linked with another that has a similar effect, and consequently the reproduction of names can be disrupted because of the names themselves or because of their immediate or more remote associations.

一般来说，我们可以区分两种主要类型的姓名被遗忘的情况：一种情况是姓名本身指代令人痛苦的事情，另一种情况是姓名与另一个具有类似效果的事物联系在一起，因此，由于姓名本身或由于其直接或更远的联想，姓名的再现可能会受到干扰。

A survey of these general remarks shows that temporarily forgetting names is one of the most frequently observed of all slips of the mind.

对这些普遍评论的调查显示，暂时忘记名字是所有记忆失误中最常见的一种。

19) However, we are a long way from having described all the features of this phenomenon. I will add that forgetting names is extremely infectious. In a conversation between two people, it is often enough for one of them to say he has forgotten some name or other for the other to forget it too. Where forgetfulness is thus induced, however, it is easier to recollect the forgotten name again. This ‘collective’ forgetfulness, strictly speaking a phenomenon of mass psychology, is a subject that has not yet been analytically studied. T. Reik provides a good explanation of this remarkable occurrence in a single but particularly good case. 7

19）然而，我们距离描述这种现象的所有特征还很远。我还要补充一点，忘记名字极易传染。在两个人的谈话中，通常只要其中一人说他忘记了某个名字，另一人也会跟着忘记。然而，一旦遗忘被这样诱发，就更容易再次想起被遗忘的名字。这种“集体性”遗忘，严格来说是一种群体心理学现象，目前尚未得到深入的分析研究。T. Reik 用一个特别出色的案例，对这种奇特的现象给出了很好的解释。

‘In a small social gathering of academics, which included two women students of philosophy, the conversation turned to the many questions posed in cultural history and theology by the origin of Christianity. One of the young ladies taking part in the discussion remembered finding an interesting picture of the many religious currents influencing the history of that period in an English novel she had recently read. She added that the novel described the whole life of Christ, from his birth to his death, but she could not remember the name of the work (although she had a very clear visual memory of the cover of the book and the typographical appearance of the title). Three of the men present said that they knew the same novel, and added that, oddly enough, they could not remember its title either…’

在一次小型学术聚会上，包括两位哲学系女学生在内的几位学者谈起了基督教起源在文化史和神学领域引发的诸多问题。一位参与讨论的年轻女士回忆起，她最近读过一本英国小说，书中描绘了当时影响历史的众多宗教思潮，颇为有趣。她补充说，这本小说讲述了基督从出生到死亡的一生，但她记不起书名（尽管她对书的封面和标题的字体印象非常深刻）。在场的三位男士表示他们也读过同一本小说，但奇怪的是，他们也记不起书名了……

Alone among the four of them, the young lady underwent analysis to find out why she had forgotten the title. It was Ben Hur , by Lewis Wallace. Her first substitute ideas had been: Ecce homo — homo sum — quo vadis ? The girl herself realized that she had forgotten the name ‘because it contains an expression that neither I nor any other young girl would wish to employ, particularly in front of young men’ [Ben Hur — Hure : ‘whore’ in German], an explanation which acquired a further dimension through this very interesting analysis. In the context on which she had touched, the translation of homo , ‘man’ in the sense of human being, can also have a risqué meaning. Reik concludes that the young lady treated the word as if, by simply mentioning the suspect title of the book in front of young men, she would have been admitting to desires that she rejected as both unseemly and out of tune with her character. In short, she unconsciously equated uttering the tide of Ben Hur out loud with offering sexual favours [‘Ich bin Hure’ — I am a whore’], and consequently her inability to remember it amounted to rejecting any unconscious temptation of that kind. There are reasons to suppose that the young men’s inability to remember it was caused by similar unconscious processes. Their unconscious minds picked up the real reason why the girl forgot the title and, as it were, interpreted it so that their own forgetting it shows deference to her attitude of repudiation. It is as if, through her sudden lapse of memory, their interlocutor had given them a clear signal, which they unconsciously understood very well.

四人之中，只有这位年轻女子接受了分析，以找出她忘记书名的原因。书名是刘易斯·华莱士的《宾虚》。她最初的替代想法是：“瞧，我是个男人——我该何去何从？”女孩自己意识到，她忘记书名是因为“它包含一个我和其他年轻女孩都不愿使用的表达，尤其是在年轻男子面前”。[宾虚——Hure：德语中意为“妓女”] 这项解释通过这项非常有趣的分析获得了更深层次的意义。在她所提及的语境中，“homo”（意为“男人”，指人类）也可以带有不雅的含义。赖克总结道，这位年轻女子对待这个词的态度，仿佛只要在年轻男子面前提及这个令人不安的书名，就等于承认了她所拒绝的欲望，而这些欲望既不雅，也与她的性格不符。简而言之，她无意识地将大声念出《宾虚》的标题等同于提供性服务（“Ich bin Hure”——我是个妓女），因此，她记不起标题就相当于无意识地拒绝了任何此类诱惑。有理由推测，年轻男子记不起标题也是由类似的无意识过程造成的。他们的潜意识捕捉到了女孩忘记标题的真正原因，并仿佛将其解读为对她拒绝态度的尊重。就好像女孩突然失忆，给了他们一个清晰的信号，而他们无意识地对此理解得非常透彻。

Names may also continue to be forgotten in such a way that whole series of them elude the memory. If a name escapes us, and we seek other and closely connected names in order to retrieve it, these other names, sought as points of reference, quite often escape us too. Forgetfulness thus moves on from one name to another, as if to demonstrate the existence of an obstacle that cannot easily be removed.

名字也可能被不断遗忘，以至于一连串的名字都无法记起。如果我们想不起某个名字，便去寻找其他密切相关的名字，而这些作为参照物的名字往往也同样会从我们脑海中消失。遗忘就这样从一个名字转移到另一个名字，仿佛在表明存在着难以逾越的障碍。

Notes

笔记

1 . My colleague in fact slightly changed both the wording and the application of this fine passage in the poem. The ghostly girl really tells her bridegroom:

1. 事实上，我的同事对诗中这段优美文字的措辞和运用都做了些许改动。诗中那个幽灵般的女孩实际上是对她的新郎说：

Meine Kette hub’ ich dir gegeben;

我把我的项链给了你；

而你只会以棕色的身影再次出现在那里。

# ↩

IV

第四

On Childhood Memories and Screen Memories

关于童年记忆和屏幕记忆

In a second article (published in 1899 in the Monatschrift für Psychiatrie und Neurologie ) I was able to demonstrate the tendentious nature of human memory in an unexpected area. I started out from the striking fact that a person’s earliest childhood memories frequently seem to be of trivial and unimportant matters, while often (although not always) no trace of major, impressive events with a strong emotional content remains in the adult memory. Since it is well known that the memory selects among the impressions it receives, one might think it likely that in childhood this selection functions according to principles quite different from those in operation at the age of intellectual maturity. Close investigation, however, shows that it is unnecessary to make such an assumption. The neutral memories of childhood owe their existence to a process of displacement; as reproduced, they are substitutes for other, genuinely significant impressions, the memory of which can be elicited by psychic analysis although resistance prevents their direct reproduction. Since they owe their retention in the mind not to their own content but to its associative connection with another, repressed subject, they have a good claim to be described, in the term I have adopted for them, as ‘screen memories’.

在第二篇文章（发表于1899年的《精神病学与神经病学月刊》）中，我得以在一个意想不到的领域论证人类记忆的倾向性。我从一个引人注目的事实出发：一个人最早的童年记忆往往似乎是一些琐碎无关紧要的事情，而成年后的记忆中却常常（尽管并非总是如此）找不到任何重大、令人印象深刻且具有强烈情感的事件的痕迹。众所周知，记忆会对其接收到的印象进行选择，因此人们可能会认为，童年时期的这种选择机制与智力成熟时期截然不同。然而，仔细的研究表明，这种假设是没有必要的。童年时期那些中性的记忆之所以存在，是因为它们被置换了；在被复述的过程中，它们是对其他真正重要的印象的替代，这些印象可以通过心理分析来唤起，尽管由于某种阻力，它们无法被直接复述。由于它们之所以能留在脑海中，不是因为它们自身的内容，而是因为它们与另一个被压抑的主题有关联，因此，用我为它们所采用的术语来说，它们完全可以被称为“屏幕记忆”。

I did not by any means give an exhaustive account of the full diversity of the associations between screen memories and their significance in the article mentioned above. In the example that I analysed there in detail, I laid particular emphasis on a special feature of the temporal relation between the screen memory and the subject it has screened out. The content of the screen memory in that example derived from a very early stage of childhood, while the thought processes represented by it in the subject’s memory, which had remained almost unconscious, occurred in his later years. I described this kind of displacement as retrospective or retrograde. It is perhaps even more frequent to come upon the opposite relationship, in which a neutral impression recently received establishes itself in the mind as a screen memory, owing that distinction only to its connection with an earlier experience which resists direct reproduction. These might be described as advanced or anticipatory screen memories. In such a case the essential matter on the subject’s mind occurred later in time than the screen memory. Finally, there is a third possibility: the screen memory may be linked with the impression it screens out not only in content but in temporal contiguity as well, and is thus a simultaneous or contingent screen memory.

在上述文章中，我并未详尽阐述屏幕记忆及其意义之间关联的全部多样性。在我详细分析的例子中，我特别强调了屏幕记忆与其所屏蔽的主体之间时间关系的一个特殊特征。该例子中的屏幕记忆内容源自童年早期，而主体记忆中呈现的思维过程（几乎处于无意识状态）则发生在其成年后。我将这种错位描述为回顾性或逆行性。或许更常见的情况是相反的关系：近期获得的某种中性印象在脑海中确立为屏幕记忆，其区别仅在于它与早期难以直接再现的经验相关联。这些可以被称为前瞻性或预期性屏幕记忆。在这种情况下，主体脑海中真正重要的内容发生的时间晚于屏幕记忆。最后，还有第三种可能性：屏幕记忆可能与它屏蔽掉的印象不仅在内容上，而且在时间上也具有关联性，因此是一种同时性的或偶然性的屏幕记忆。

In my article I did not go into the question of how much of our stock of memories belongs to the screen memory category, or of the part screen memories play in various neurotic thought processes, nor shall I study it here. My aim is simply to emphasize the similarity between the forgetting or faulty reproduction of proper names and the construction of screen memories.

我在文章中并未探讨我们记忆库中有多少属于屏幕记忆范畴，也未探讨屏幕记忆在各种神经质思维过程中扮演的角色，本文亦不作深入探讨。我的目的仅仅在于强调遗忘或错误回忆专有名词与构建屏幕记忆之间的相似性。

At first glance the differences between the two phenomena are much more striking than any potential similarities. In the first case proper names are forgotten, in the second complete impressions — experiences that either really took place or occurred in the mind; the first phenomenon concerns an obvious failure of the function of memory, the second an operation of the memory which seems disconcerting. The first is a brief slip of the mind — for the name that has just been forgotten may have been spoken correctly a hundred times before and will be correctly spoken again tomorrow — the second is a permanent and unremitting condition, since it seems that neutral childhood memories can accompany us through a great part of our lives. The riddle appears to be of a diametrically different nature in the two cases. In the first, scientific curiosity is aroused by what has been forgotten, in the second by what is remembered. Further study of the question, however, makes it clear that despite the differences in the psychic material and duration of the two phenomena, the similarities by far predominate. Both involve a failure of memory, which does not reproduce what it should correctly, but instead substitutes something else. When we forget names the memory is still at work, but forms substitute names. When we construct screen memories, we substitute them for other and more important impressions which have been forgotten. In both cases we feel a certain intellectual impression that memory has been disturbed, but in different ways. In forgetting names we know that the substitute names are incorrect; in reproducing screen memories we are surprised to find that we have them at all. While psychological analysis shows that the construction of substitutes has occurred in the same way in both cases, through displacement by way of some superficial association, it is the difference of material, duration and focal interest in the two phenomena which contributes to heightening our sense that we have come upon something important and generally valid. This general validity would imply that the failure and misdirection of the function of memory indicates, more frequently than we suppose, that a partisan factor has intervened, a tendency which favours one memory while it works against another.

乍看之下，这两种现象之间的差异远比任何潜在的相似之处更为显著。第一种情况是人名被遗忘，第二种情况是完整的印象——无论是真实发生过的体验还是在脑海中产生的体验；第一种现象显然是记忆功能的失效，第二种现象则是一种令人不安的记忆运作。前者只是短暂的记忆失误——因为刚刚被遗忘的名字可能之前已经被正确念出过一百次，明天也可能再次被正确念出——而后者则是一种持续不断的状态，因为看似中性的童年记忆似乎可以伴随我们一生的大部分时间。这两种情况下的谜题似乎截然不同。在前一种情况下，科学的好奇心源于被遗忘的内容，而在后一种情况下，则源于被记住的内容。然而，对这个问题的进一步研究表明，尽管这两种现象在心理物质和持续时间上存在差异，但它们的相似之处却远胜于其他方面。两者都涉及记忆的失效，即记忆无法正确再现原本应该再现的内容，而是用其他事物取而代之。当我们忘记名字时，记忆仍在运作，但会形成替代名称。当我们构建屏幕记忆时，我们会用它们来替代其他已被遗忘的、更重要的印象。在这两种情况下，我们都会感受到某种认知上的错觉，但错觉的方式不同。忘记名字时，我们知道替代名称是错误的；而再现屏幕记忆时，我们惊讶地发现自己竟然拥有这些记忆。虽然心理分析表明，在这两种情况下，替代物的构建方式相同，都是通过某种肤浅的联想进行转移，但正是两种现象在材料、持续时间和关注焦点上的差异，增强了我们意识到自己发现了某种重要且普遍有效信息的感觉。这种普遍有效性意味着，记忆功能的失效和误导，比我们想象的更频繁地表明，某种偏袒的因素介入其中，这种倾向有利于某些记忆，而不利于其他记忆。

The theme of childhood memories appears to me so significant and interesting that I would like to add a few more remarks, going further than the views I have put forward so far. How far back into childhood do memories go? I know of certain studies of this question, for instance by V. and C. Henri 1 and Potwin . 2 These show great individual differences between the subjects studied, some of whom dated their first memories back to the age of six months, while others could remember nothing before the end of their sixth or even eighth year of life. But what are these differences in the retention of childhood memories connected with, and what is their significance? Obviously, the simple accumulation of material relating to such questions is not enough; the information must be studied further with the help of the person who provided it.

童年记忆这个主题在我看来意义非凡且引人入胜，因此我想补充几点，进一步探讨我目前提出的观点。记忆究竟能追溯到童年的哪个阶段？我知道一些关于此问题的研究，例如V.和C. Henri以及Potwin的研究。这些研究表明，受试者之间存在显著的个体差异，有些人最早的记忆可以追溯到六个月大，而另一些人则在六岁甚至八岁之前都无法回忆起任何事情。但是，这些童年记忆保留方面的差异与哪些因素相关？它们的意义又是什么？显然，仅仅积累与此类问题相关的材料是不够的；我们必须在提供信息的人的帮助下，对这些信息进行更深入的研究。

I believe we are far too ready to accept the fact of infantile amnesia, the obliteration from our memory of the first few years of life, failing to notice a curiously puzzling factor. We forget the high intellectual achievement and complex emotions of which a child of about four is capable, whereas we should feel surprised that, as a rule, later memory has retained so few of these mental processes, all the more so since there is every reason to assume that those same forgotten childhood achievements have not, so to speak, been eliminated from someone’s development leaving no trace, but have exerted an influence that will affect the whole of the rest of his life. Yet in spite of this unprecedented degree of efficacy they have been forgotten! This fact indicates the very special way in which the memory (the conscious memory, that is) is conditioned, something which has so far eluded perception. It is perfectly possible that the forgetting of events in childhood can give us the key to understanding amnesia of the kind which, according to the latest findings, lies at the heart of the construction of all neurotic symptoms.

我认为我们太容易接受婴儿期失忆症这一事实，即我们对生命最初几年的记忆被抹去，却忽略了一个令人费解的奇特因素。我们忘记了一个四岁左右的孩子所拥有的极高的智力成就和复杂的情感，而令人惊讶的是，通常情况下，成年后的记忆中却只保留了极少的这些心理过程。尤其考虑到，我们完全有理由认为，这些被遗忘的童年成就并非彻底从一个人的发展历程中消失，而是对其一生都产生了深远的影响。然而，尽管它们的影响如此巨大，却仍然被遗忘了！这一事实揭示了记忆（即意识层面的记忆）形成的一种非常特殊的机制，而这种机制迄今为止一直未被我们察觉。完全有可能，对童年事件的遗忘能够为我们理解失忆症提供关键线索，而根据最新的研究发现，这种失忆症正是所有神经症症状的核心所在。

Of the childhood memories we do retain, some appear easy to understand, others strange or incomprehensible. It is not difficult to correct certain errors affecting both kinds. If a person’s retained memories are analytically investigated, one can easily see that there is no guarantee of their accuracy. Some remembered images are certainly falsified, incomplete, or temporally and spatially displaced. Statements by the subjects of such studies to the effect that, for instance, their first memory dates from the age of two, are obviously unreliable. It is also quite easy to find reasons accounting for the distortion and displacement of an experience, but also showing that such slips cannot be put down simply to faulty memory. Strong forces from later periods of a subject’s life have affected his ability to remember childhood experiences, probably the same forces that are responsible for the fact of our having removed ourselves, in general, so far from an understanding of our childhood years.

在我们保留下来的童年记忆中，有些似乎很容易理解，有些则显得怪异或难以理解。纠正影响这两类记忆的某些错误并不难。如果对一个人保留的记忆进行分析研究，很容易发现其准确性无法得到保证。一些记忆中的画面肯定是错误的、不完整的，或者在时间和空间上发生了错位。例如，研究对象声称他们的第一个记忆可以追溯到两岁，这种说法显然是不可靠的。我们也很容易找到导致记忆扭曲和错位的原因，但这同时也表明，这些错误不能简单地归咎于记忆缺陷。个体生命后期阶段的强大力量影响了他们回忆童年经历的能力，而这些力量可能正是导致我们普遍对童年时期缺乏理解的原因。

Adult memory is well known to operate on the basis of various kinds of psychic material. Some people remember in visual images and have good visual memories; others can hardly reproduce the faintest visual memory of something they have seen. In Charcot’s classification such people are called auditifs and moteurs , as distinct from the first category, the visuels. These differences disappear in dreams; we all dream mainly in visual images. But this development works in reverse on childhood memories; they are realistically visual even in those whose later memories lack the visual element. Visual memory thus preserves typical infant memory. My own earliest childhood memories are the only visual memories I have, and they are positively three-dimensional, scenes that I can compare only to a stage performance. Whether such childhood scenes turn out to be accurate or misremembered, we regularly see our own childish selves in them, complete with our clothing. This is surprising, for even adults with good visual memories do not visualize themselves in their memories of later events. 3 It runs counter to all we know to suppose that a child’s attention is directed to himself rather than entirely to the outside impressions he is receiving from his experiences, so for various reasons we must assume that our so-called earliest childhood memories preserve not the real trace of memory but a later revision of it, one which may have undergone the influence of many later psychic forces. ‘Childhood memories’ in general thus take on the significance of screen memories’, and in this are remarkably analogous to early racial or national memories as recorded in myths and legends.

众所周知，成人的记忆是基于各种心理素材运作的。有些人能通过视觉图像记忆，并且拥有良好的视觉记忆；而另一些人则几乎无法重现他们所见事物的任何模糊的视觉记忆。在夏科的分类中，这类人被称为听觉型（audifs）和运动型（moteurs），以区别于第一类——视觉型（visuels）。这些差异在梦境中消失；我们所有人的梦境主要都是视觉图像。但这种发展在童年记忆中却截然相反；即使在那些后来的记忆中缺乏视觉元素的人身上，童年记忆也具有逼真的视觉特征。因此，视觉记忆保留了典型的婴儿记忆。我自己最早的童年记忆是我唯一的视觉记忆，它们是立体的，场景之逼真，我只能将其比作舞台表演。无论这些童年场景最终被证实是准确的还是错误的记忆，我们经常会在其中看到自己孩童时期的模样，甚至连当时的穿着都清晰可见。这令人惊讶，因为即使是拥有良好视觉记忆的成年人，在回忆后来的事件时也不会将自己形象化。 3 认为儿童的注意力会集中在自身而非完全集中在从经验中获得的外部印象上，这与我们所知的一切都相悖。因此，出于各种原因，我们必须假设，我们所谓的早期童年记忆保存的并非记忆的真实痕迹，而是后来对其进行的修正，这种修正可能受到了许多后期心理因素的影响。“童年记忆”总体上因此具有了“屏幕记忆”的意义，在这方面，它们与神话传说中记载的早期种族或民族记忆有着惊人的相似之处。

Anyone who has studied a number of minds using psychoanalytical methods will have assembled a wealth of examples of screen memories during his work. Communicating these examples, however, is greatly complicated by the nature of the relationship of childhood memories to later life; if a childhood memory is to be identified as a screen memory, the subject’s whole life story would often have to be recounted first. It is rarely possible — as it is in the following fine example — to take a single childhood memory out of context and communicate it.

任何运用精神分析方法研究过众多心理的人，都会在研究过程中积累大量“屏幕记忆”的例子。然而，由于童年记忆与成年生活之间关系的复杂性，这些例子的传达变得极其困难；如果要将某个童年记忆认定为“屏幕记忆”，通常需要先回顾研究对象的整个人生经历。像下面这个绝佳的例子一样，将某个童年记忆从其背景中剥离出来进行阐述，几乎是不可能的。

A man of twenty-four had retained the following memory from his fifth year. He was sitting on a little chair in the garden of a holiday house, next to an aunt who was trying to teach him his alphabet. He had difficulty in distinguishing between m and n , and asked his aunt to show him how to tell them apart. The aunt pointed out that when compared with n, m has a whole extra part to it, a third stroke. There was no reason to query the accuracy of this childhood recollection, but it acquired its true significance only later, when it could stand symbolically for something else the boy wanted to know. Just as he had been anxious to be able to tell m and n apart in the past, later he was trying to discover the difference between boys and girls, and one senses that he would have been happy to get the information from the same aunt. And the differences, as he discovered, were of a similar nature: by comparison with a girl, a boy has a whole extra part to him. It was when he found out this that his memory of his childish thirst for knowledge revived.

一位二十四岁的男子保留着五岁时的一段记忆。他坐在度假屋花园里的一把小椅子上，旁边是一位正在教他字母的姑妈。他分不清m和n，便请姑妈教他。姑妈指出，与n相比，m多了一个部分，也就是第三笔画。这段童年记忆的准确性毋庸置疑，但它的真正意义直到后来才显现出来，因为它象征着男孩渴望了解的另一件事。正如他过去渴望区分m和n一样，后来他又试图弄明白男孩和女孩的区别，人们感觉他如果能从那位姑妈那里得到答案，一定会非常高兴。而他发现，两者的区别本质上是相似的：与女孩相比，男孩多了一个部分。正是当他发现这一点时，他孩提时代对知识的渴望被唤醒了。

Another example comes from later childhood: a man of over forty, who suffered from severe inhibitions in his sexual life, was the eldest of nine children. When the ninth and youngest was born he was fifteen, but he insisted that he had never noticed any of his mother’s pregnancies. Challenged by my disbelief, he did remember that once, when he was eleven or twelve, he had seen his mother rapidly undoing her skirt in front of the looking-glass. He now added, quite casually, that she had just come in from the street and unexpectedly found that she had gone into labour. Her undoing [German: Aufbinden ] of her skirt had become a screen memory for her delivery [German: Entbindung ]. We shall find such ‘verbal bridges’ used again in other cases.

另一个例子来自他的童年后期：一位四十多岁的男子，性生活极度压抑，他是九个孩子中的老大。第九个也是最小的孩子出生时，他十五岁，但他坚称自己从未注意到母亲怀孕。面对我的质疑，他这才想起，在他十一二岁的时候，曾看到母亲在镜子前迅速解开裙子。他漫不经心地补充道，母亲当时刚从街上回来，突然发现自己要生了。她解开裙子的动作成了她分娩时的“记忆屏障”。我们会在其他案例中再次发现这种“语言桥梁”的运用。
