# ↩

VI

六

Slips in Reading and Slips of the Pen

阅读失误和笔误

The same views and comments apply to mistakes in reading and writing as to slips of the tongue — not surprisingly, considering the close relationship between those functions. I shall confine myself here to an account of some carefully analysed examples, rather than making any attempt to describe these phenomena in their entirety.

对于阅读和写作错误以及口误，人们的看法和评论基本相同——考虑到这两种功能之间的密切联系，这并不奇怪。在此，我将仅限于对一些经过仔细分析的例子进行阐述，而不是试图全面描述这些现象。

A) Slips in reading

A) 阅读失误

1) I was looking through a copy of the Leipziger Illustrierte in the coffee house, holding it at an angle in front of me, when I read the caption under a picture spread right across the page as: ‘A Wedding in der Odyssee [in the Odyssey].’ It caught my attention, and in some surprise I straightened out the page and read, correctly: ‘A Wedding an der Ostsee [on the Baltic Sea].’ How did I make this nonsensical mistake in reading the caption? My thoughts went at once to a book by Ruths, his Experimentaluntersuchungen über Musikphantome 1 [ Experimental Studies of Musical Phantoms ], which had been occupying my mind a great deal recently because it touches on matters close to the psychological problems with which I myself am concerned. Its author had said that he would soon be publishing a work entitled Analyse und Grundgesetze der Traumphänomene [ Analysis and Fundamental Laws of the Phenomena of Dreaming ]. No wonder that, as I had just published my own Interpretation of Dreams , I looked forward with keen anticipation to reading this book. In Ruths’s previous work, on musical phantoms, I found an announcement, at the beginning of the contents list, of extensive inductive evidence for the fact that the ancient Greek myths and legends were principally rooted in the phantoms of sleep and music, in dream phenomena and in states of delirium. I immediately looked up the text to see if the author was also aware that the scene in which Odysseus appears before Nausicaä can be traced back to the widespread dream of being naked. A friend had drawn my attention to the fine passage in Gottfried Keller’s Der Grüne Heinrich that explains this episode in the Odyssey as an objective version of the dreams of a mariner wandering far from home, and I had added this reference to the account of exhibitionist dreams of nakedness in my book (8th edition, p. 170 [V.D]). But I found nothing on the subject in Ruths. In this case my mind was obviously occupied by ideas of priority.

1）我在咖啡馆里翻阅着一本《莱比锡画报》，斜着拿在面前，突然看到一幅横跨整页的图片下方的文字说明是：“奥德赛中的婚礼”。这引起了我的注意，我有些惊讶地把页面摆正，然后正确地读了出来：“波罗的海沿岸的婚礼”。我怎么会把文字说明读成这样呢？我立刻想到了鲁斯的一本书，他的《音乐幻影实验研究》（Experimentaluntersuchungen über Musikphantome），这本书最近一直萦绕在我的脑海中，因为它涉及一些与我自身关注的心理问题密切相关的内容。作者曾说过他即将出版一部名为《梦境现象的分析与基本规律》（Analyse und Grundgesetze der Traumphänomene）的著作。难怪我刚出版了自己的《梦的解析》，就对这本书充满了期待。在鲁思之前关于音乐幻影的著作中，我在目录开头发现，他列举了大量归纳证据，证明古希腊神话和传说主要源于睡眠和音乐的幻影、梦境现象以及谵妄状态。我立刻查阅了原文，想看看作者是否也意识到，奥德修斯出现在瑙西卡面前的场景可以追溯到广为流传的裸体梦境。一位朋友曾向我推荐戈特弗里德·凯勒的《绿海因里希》中一段精彩的文字，这段文字将《奥德赛》中的这一情节解释为一位远离家乡的水手梦境的客观版本。我已将这段文字添加到我书中关于裸露梦境的描述中（第八版，第170页[V.D]）。但我在鲁思的著作中却找不到任何相关内容。显然，当时我的注意力被优先性问题所占据。

2) How did I come to read in the paper one day: ‘ Im Fass [In a tub] through Europe’, instead of ‘ zu Fuss [on foot] through Europe’? It took me quite a long time to find the answer. My first ideas suggested that I must have been thinking of Diogenes’ tub, and I had recently been reading about art in the age of Alexander in a work of art history. It seemed obvious to think of Alexander’s famous remark: ‘If I were not Alexander I would wish to be Diogenes.’ I also had a vague memory of a man called Hermann Zeitung [ Zeitung , ‘newspaper’] who went travelling packed up in a crate, but I could make no further connection, nor could I find the page in the history of art with the remark that had struck me. Only months later did I suddenly think of the puzzle again. I had put it out of my mind, but now it came back complete with its solution. I remembered a comment in a newspaper on the curious means of transport [German: Beförderung ] some people now chose in order to go to the World Exhibition in Paris, and I believe the article also contained a facetious remark to the effect that some gentleman or other intended to get another man to roll him to Paris in a tub. Their sole motive, of course, was to attract attention through such silly pranks. Hermann Zeitung was indeed the name of the man who had first thought up this far-fetched method of transport. Next I remembered that I once treated a patient whose morbid fear of reading newspapers turned out to be a reaction against his morbid ambition to see himself mentioned in print as a celebrity. Alexander of Macedonia was certainly one of the most ambitious men who ever lived, and indeed he complained that he could find no Homer to celebrate his great deeds. But how could I not have remembered another Alexander, much closer to me? Alexander is my own younger brother’s name! I now immediately traced the unwelcome idea that I had wished to repress in relation to that Alexander, and the reason why it emerged now. My brother is an expert on tariffs and transport , and was to receive the tide of professor in his work as a teacher at a commercial college. Several years ago, I myself had been proposed for the same promotion [in German, also Beförderung ] to the title of professor at the university, but nothing came of it. At the time our mother expressed her surprise and dissatisfaction at the idea of her younger son’s becoming a professor before his older brother. This had been the state of affairs at the time when I could find no reason for my slip in reading. But then my brother encountered difficulties of his own, and his chances of becoming a professor were now even less than mine. Suddenly the significance of my slip in reading was obvious: the turn taken for the worse in my brother’s chances had removed an obstacle. It was as if I had been reading about his appointment in the newspaper and saying to myself: how strange to think a person can get into the papers (i.e., with the announcement of his appointment as professor) for something so stupid (as his profession). I then easily found the passage about Hellenistic art in the age of Alexander, and to my surprise realized that during my earlier search I had read the page on which it occurred several times, but as if I were under the influence of a negative hallucination I had skipped the relevant sentence on every occasion. In fact it contained nothing to enlighten me, nothing that I would have felt I would rather forget, and I think the symptom of my inability to find it in the book was designed merely to lead me astray. I was meant to continue with my train of thought where an obstacle had been placed in the path of my search, in some idea about Alexander of Macedonia, so that I would be better protected against thinking of my brother, that other Alexander. And the device had worked perfectly; I devoted all my efforts to looking for the lost passage in the history of art.

2）我怎么会有一天在报纸上看到“Im Fass [乘桶] 游历欧洲”，而不是“zu Fuss [徒步] 游历欧洲”呢？我花了很长时间才找到答案。我最初的想法是，我一定是想到了第欧根尼的桶，而且我最近刚读过一本关于亚历山大时代的艺术史著作。想到亚历山大那句名言“如果我不是亚历山大，我愿成为第欧根尼”似乎也合情合理。我还隐约记得有个叫赫尔曼·泽通（Hermann Zeitung，Zeitung意为“报纸”）的人，他把自己装在木箱里旅行，但我无法将两者联系起来，也找不到艺术史中那句让我印象深刻的话。几个月后，我突然又想起了这个谜题。我把它抛诸脑后，但现在它又回来了，而且答案也找到了。我记得报纸上曾刊登过一篇评论，说有些人为了去巴黎世博会，选择了一种奇特的交通方式（德语：Beförderung）。我记得那篇文章里还讽刺地提到，某位先生打算找个人把他放在桶里滚到巴黎去。当然，他们唯一的目的就是通过这种愚蠢的恶作剧来博取关注。赫尔曼·泽通（Hermann Zeitung）正是第一个想出这种异想天开的交通方式的人。接着我又想起，我曾经治疗过一位病人，他极度害怕读报纸，后来发现这是因为他内心深处渴望成为报纸上的名人。马其顿的亚历山大无疑是历史上最有野心的人之一，他甚至抱怨找不到荷马来歌颂他的丰功伟绩。但我怎么可能想不起另一个亚历山大呢？他离我更近！亚历山大正是我弟弟的名字！我立刻明白了之前一直想压抑的、与亚历山大有关的不愉快想法，以及它为何现在浮现的原因。我的哥哥是关税和运输方面的专家，在一家商业学院任教，即将晋升为教授。几年前，我也曾被提名晋升为大学教授，但最终未能如愿。当时，母亲对小儿子比哥哥先当教授感到惊讶和不满。那时，我还没弄明白自己为何会犯这样的错误。但后来，哥哥遇到了自己的困难，他成为教授的机会比我还要渺茫。我突然明白了自己犯错的意义：哥哥的处境恶化，反而扫清了我前进道路上的一个障碍。就好像我曾在报纸上读到他被任命的消息，然后自言自语道：一个人竟然能因为如此愚蠢的事情（比如他的职业）登上报纸（也就是宣布他被任命为教授），真是不可思议。之后，我轻而易举地找到了关于亚历山大时代希腊化艺术的那段文字，令我惊讶的是，我之前查找时曾多次翻阅过那一页，但仿佛受到了某种负面幻觉的影响，每次都跳过了相关的句子。事实上，那段文字并没有给我带来任何启发，也没有任何我宁愿忘记的内容，我认为我在书中找不到它，只是为了误导我。我的目的是让我继续沿着我的思路前进，在寻找过程中遇到的障碍——关于马其顿的亚历山大——这样我就不会再想起我的兄弟，那个亚历山大了。而这个计策果然奏效了；我将所有的精力都投入到寻找艺术史中那段遗失的文字上。

The double meaning of the German word Beförderung , in this case, was the associative bridge between the two complexes: the unimportant one evoked by the newspaper report, and the more interesting but unwelcome complex that emerged here in disrupting what I ought to have read. My example shows that it is not always easy to explain incidents such as this slip in reading, and finding the answer to the riddle sometimes has to be put off to a more favourable time. However, the more difficult it is to find that answer, the more certainly one may expect that the disruptive idea, once it is finally discovered, will be condemned by the conscious mind as strange and conflicting.

在这种情况下，德语单词“Beförderung”的双重含义成为了连接两个复杂情境的桥梁：一个是报纸报道引发的无关紧要的情境，另一个则是更有趣却又令人不快的情境，它打断了我本应阅读的内容。我的例子表明，解释诸如此类的阅读失误并非易事，有时我们不得不将解谜的时机推迟到更合适的时候。然而，答案越难找到，我们就越可以肯定，一旦最终发现这个令人困惑的想法，它就会被意识视为怪异且矛盾的。

3) One day I received a letter from a place near Vienna containing bad news. I called for my wife at once, and asked her to sympathize with the fact that poor Wilhelm M. — whom I called, using the feminine article, die arme Wilhelm M. — was so ill that the doctors held out no hope for him. Something about the words in which I expressed my regret must have sounded wrong, for my wife seemed suspicious, asked to see the letter, and said she thought it couldn’t say what I had claimed, since no one calls a wife by her husband’s first name, and anyway our correspondent knew the first name of Wilhelm M.’s wife very well. I defended myself doggedly, mentioning the usual custom of visiting cards where a woman calls herself by her husband’s first name — ‘Frau Wilhelm M.’ At last I had to bring out the letter again, and sure enough we read der arme Wilhelm M. , with the correct masculine article. In fact it even said, and this I had entirely overlooked, der arme Dr W. M. My misreading was therefore an almost convulsive reaction attempting to shift the sad news from husband to wife. The title of Dr between the article, the adjective and the name did not fit my insistence that the letter-writer must have meant the wife, and so I had simply overlooked it in reading the phrase. The reason for this slip in reading was not, however, because I liked the wife any less than the husband, but because the poor man’s fate had aroused my anxieties about someone else who was very close to me, and who had what I knew was one of the medical symptoms also present in the case of Dr W. M.

3）有一天，我收到一封来自维也纳附近地方的信，信里说了件坏事。我立刻叫来妻子，请她体谅可怜的威廉·M——我用阴性冠词称呼他为“可怜的威廉·M”——他病得很重，医生们都束手无策了。我表达遗憾的措辞可能有些不对劲，因为妻子似乎起了疑心，要看信，说信里不可能写着我说的那些话，因为没人会直呼妻子的丈夫的名字，而且我们的来信人对威廉·M妻子的名字也了如指掌。我坚持己见，提到名片上通常女士会用丈夫的名字称呼自己——“威廉·M夫人”。最后，我不得不再次拿出那封信，果然，我们看到的是正确的阳性冠词“可怜的威廉·M”。事实上，信中甚至还写着——这一点我完全忽略了——“der arme Dr W. M.”，而我却完全忽略了。因此，我的误读几乎是一种本能反应，试图将这则噩耗从丈夫转移到妻子身上。冠词、形容词和名字之间的“Dr.”头衔与我坚持认为写信人指的一定是妻子这一观点相悖，所以我在阅读这句话时完全忽略了它。然而，我之所以会读错，并非因为我不喜欢妻子胜过喜欢丈夫，而是因为这位可怜男人的遭遇让我对另一位与我关系非常亲近的人感到担忧，而我知道他身上也出现了与W. M.医生相同的某种医学症状。

4) A slip in reading that I perpetrate very often when I am on holiday and walking down the street in a foreign town is both annoying and ridiculous: I read every shop sign that suggests the word in any way at all as Antiques. This must be an expression of my interests as a collector.

4）我在度假时，走在异国小镇的街道上，经常会犯一个阅读错误，这既令人恼火又很可笑：我会把所有带有“古董”字样的商店招牌都读成“Antiques”（古董）。这大概是我作为收藏家的兴趣在作祟吧。

5) In his major work on Affektivität, Suggestibilität, Paranoia [ Affectivity, Suggestibility, Paranoia ] of 1906, p. 121, Bleuler writes: ‘Once, when I was reading, my mind told me that I had seen my own name two lines further down. To my surprise, all I found was the word Blutkörperchen [blood corpuscles]. This is the most striking instance I know among thousands of cases of slips in reading in both peripheral and central vision. On other occasions when I thought I saw my name, the word suggesting it was usually much more like the real thing, and generally all the letters in my name had to be somewhere near each other before I could make such a mistake. In this case, however, the misconnection and the illusion could be easily established: I had been reading the conclusion of some remarks on a certain kind of bad style found in scientific works, and I did not feel entirely blameless myself.’

5）布鲁勒在其1906年出版的《情感性、暗示性和妄想症》（Affektivität, Suggestibilität, Paranoia）一书第121页中写道：“有一次，我在阅读时，脑海中突然浮现出两行之后我看到自己名字的念头。令我惊讶的是，我看到的只是‘血细胞’（Blutkörperchen）这个词。这是我所知的成千上万次阅读时出现的错觉中最引人注目的一个，这些错觉既有周边视觉的，也有中心视觉的。在其他情况下，当我以为自己看到了自己的名字时，那个暗示它的词通常更接近真正的名字，而且通常情况下，我的名字的所有字母都必须彼此靠近，我才会犯这样的错误。然而，在这个例子中，这种错觉和错觉很容易解释：我当时正在阅读一篇关于科学著作中某种糟糕文风的评论的结论部分，我并不完全觉得自己没有责任。”

6) From H. Sachs: ‘In his formality [ Steifleinenheit , from Steifleinen , ‘stiff linen’, ‘buckram’] he passes over what strikes other people.’ The word Steifleinenheit caught my eye, and looking at it more closely I saw that it really said Stilfeinheit [stylistic subtlety]. This passage was in a piece by an author whom I admire, praising to the skies a historian whose work I do not like because it tends so much to stiff German academicism.’

6）H. Sachs 写道：“他过于拘泥形式（Steifleinenheit，源自 Steifleinen，意为‘硬麻布’或‘粗麻布’），忽略了那些引人注目之处。” Steifleinenheit 这个词吸引了我的注意，仔细一看，我发现它实际上是 Stilfeinheit（风格上的微妙之处）。这段话出自一位我非常欣赏的作家之手，这位作家对一位我并不喜欢的历史学家大加赞赏，因为我并不喜欢这位历史学家的作品，因为他的作品过于拘泥于德国学院派的僵硬风格。

7) In the Zentralblatt für Psychoanalyse I, 5/6, Dr Marcell Eibenschütz gives an account of a case of a slip in reading which he came upon in the course of his philological studies: ‘I was working on the tradition behind the Buch der Märtyrer [ Book of Martyrs ], a Middle High German collection of legends, which I was to edit for the series of German medieval texts published by the Prussian Academy of Sciences. Very little was known about this work, which had never before been printed, and there was only a single critical account of it, by J. Haupt, “Über das mittelhochdeutsche Buch der Märtyrer” [‘On the Middle High German Book of Martyrs’], Wiener Sitzungsberichte , 1867, vol. 70, pp. 101ff. Haupt’s essay was based not on an old manuscript but on a modern 19th-century copy of the main manuscript, Manuscript C (of Klosterneuburg), kept in the Hofbibliothek. The copy concludes with the following paragraph of attribution:

7) 在《精神分析中心学报》第一卷，5/6期中，马塞尔·艾本舒茨博士讲述了他在语言学研究过程中遇到的一个阅读失误：“我当时正在研究《殉道者之书》（Buch der Märtyrer）背后的传统，这是一部中古高地德语的传说集，我当时要为普鲁士科学院出版的德国中世纪文本系列编辑这部作品。这部作品此前从未印刷出版，人们对它知之甚少，只有一篇评论文章，即J. Haupt的《论中古高地德语殉道者之书》（Über das mittelhochdeutsche Buch der Märtyrer），发表于1867年维也纳会议记录第70卷，第101页及之后。豪普特的论文并非基于古老的手稿，而是基于一份19世纪的现代抄本，该抄本是主手稿C（克洛斯特新堡手稿）的副本，现藏于皇家图书馆。该抄本的结尾附有以下归属说明：

Anno Domini MDCCCL in vigilia exaltacionis sancte cruris ceptus est iste liber et in vigilia pasce anni subsequentis finitus cum adiutorio omnipotentis per me Hartmanum de Krasna tunc temporis ecclesie niwenburgensis custodem.

公元 1850 年，在圣腿升天节前夕，本书开始撰写；次年，在全能者的帮助下，通过我，克拉斯纳的哈特曼（当时是纽伦堡教堂的守护者），本书得以完成。

[I, Hartman of Krasna, began this book in the year MDCCCL [1850] on the eve of Holy Cross Day, and with the help of the Almighty finished it on Easter Eve in the next year, I being at that time sacrist of Klosterneuburg.]

[我，克拉斯纳的哈特曼，于公元1850年圣十字节前夕开始撰写此书，并在次年复活节前夕，在全能者的帮助下完成了此书。当时我担任克洛斯特新堡的圣器保管员。]

‘Haupt quotes this paragraph of attribution in his article, obviously believing that it was by the scribe who wrote Manuscript C itself, and suggests — consistently misreading the Roman numerals for the year 1850 — that C was written in 1350, although he had copied the paragraph of attribution down accurately and it is printed in his article perfectly correctly (with the Roman numerals MDCCCL).

“Haupt 在他的文章中引用了这段归属说明，显然认为这是手稿 C 本身的抄写员写的，并且——始终误读 1850 年的罗马数字——认为 C 写于 1350 年，尽管他准确地抄录了这段归属说明，并且在他的文章中也完全正确地印刷出来（带有罗马数字 MDCCCL）。

‘Haupt’s account was the source of some difficulty for me. First, I was a mere beginner in the academic world and bound to respect Haupt’s authority, and for a long time I too kept reading 1350 for 1850 in the accurate and correctly printed paragraph of attribution in front of me. But in the main Manuscript C, which I was using, there was no sign of any such paragraph, and moreover there turned out to have been no monk called Hartmann in Klosterneuburg throughout the whole of the 14th century. When light finally dawned on me I realized exactly what had happened, and further research confirmed my supposition: the much-quoted paragraph of attribution exists only in the copy used by Haupt and was by the copyist of the manuscript, Father Hartman Zeibig, born in Krasna in Moravia and choirmaster of Klosterneuburg, who also, as the monastery treasurer, copied Manuscript C in 1850, and mentions himself in the traditional way at the end of his copy. The medieval vocabulary and old orthography of the closing paragraph probably contributed to Haupt’s wish to be able to give as many details as possible about the work he was studying, and thus to be able to date Manuscript C , and that was the reason for his constant misreading of 1350 instead of 1850.’

“豪普特的记载让我感到困惑。首先，我当时只是学术界的初学者，不得不尊重豪普特的权威，很长一段时间里，我也一直把面前那段准确无误的归属段落中的1350年误读为1850年。但在我所使用的主要手稿C中，根本没有这样的段落，而且事实证明，在整个14世纪，克洛斯特新堡根本没有一个名叫哈特曼的僧侣。”当我终于恍然大悟时，我才明白究竟发生了什么，进一步的研究也证实了我的推测：那段被广泛引用的归属段落仅存在于豪普特使用的抄本中，其作者是手稿的抄写员哈特曼·泽比格神父，他出生于摩拉维亚的克拉斯纳，是克洛斯特新堡修道院的唱诗班指挥。泽比格神父同时也是修道院的司库，他在1850年抄写了C手稿，并在抄本末尾以传统的方式提及了自己。结尾段落中使用的中世纪词汇和古老的拼写方式，可能促使豪普特想要尽可能详细地描述他所研究的作品，从而确定C手稿的年代，而这正是他一直将1350年误读为1850年的原因。

8) Lichtenberg’s Witzíge und Satirische Einfälle [ Witty and Satirical Notions ] contains a remark that must derive from observation and sums up almost the entire theory behind slips in reading: ‘He had read Homer so often that he always read angenommen (assuming) as Agamemnon .’

8) 利希滕贝格的《机智与讽刺的观念》中包含一条评论，这条评论必然源于观察，并概括了阅读失误背后的几乎整个理论：“他读荷马史诗太多次了，以至于他总是把 angenommen（假设）读成 Agamemnon。”

In a majority of cases, the text is modified by the reader’s readiness to see something in it that he is prepared to see, some subject that is occupying his mind at the time. The text itself has only to assist the slip in reading by showing some similarity of verbal structure which the reader can alter in his mind. A brief glance, particularly with an inattentive eye, undoubtedly makes such an illusion more likely, but is by no means an essential condition.

大多数情况下，文本的解读会受到读者自身倾向的影响，即读者倾向于从中看到自己想要看到的内容，或者当时占据其思绪的主题。文本本身只需通过展现一些语言结构的相似性来促成这种解读偏差，而读者可以在脑海中将其改变即可。短暂的瞥视，尤其是在漫不经心的情况下，无疑会增加这种错觉发生的可能性，但这绝非必要条件。

9) I believe that the war, giving us all a number of powerful and long-lasting preoccupations, encouraged misreadings more than any other kind of slip. I have had a great many such observations, but unfortunately I have recorded only a few of them. One day I was looking at one of the midday or evening papers, and thought I saw, printed in large letters: Der Friede von Görz [The Peace of Gorizia]. But no — what it said was only: Die Feinde vor Görz [The Enemy Outside Gorizia]. A man with two sons fighting in that theatre of war could easily misread such a headline. Someone else found mention in a certain context of an alte Brotkarte [old bread ration card], which on closer reading he had to reject in favour of alte Brokate [old brocades]. However, it is worth pointing out that he used to ingratiate himself with the lady of a house where he was often a welcome guest by bringing presents of bread ration cards. An engineer whose equipment never proved successful for long in preventing a tunnel under construction from becoming damp was surprised to see an advertisement apparently offering for sale items made of Schundleder [poor-quality leather]. But tradesmen are seldom so honest; the advertisement was really for goods made of Seehundleder [sealskin].

9）我认为，战争给我们所有人带来了许多强烈而持久的忧虑，这比任何其他类型的失误都更容易导致误读。我观察到很多这样的情况，但遗憾的是，我只记录了其中的一小部分。有一天，我在看一份午报或晚报时，似乎看到用大字印着“Der Friede von Görz”（戈里齐亚和平）。但实际上并非如此——上面只写着“Die Feinde vor Görz”（戈里齐亚外的敌人）。一个有两个儿子在那个战区作战的人很容易把这样的标题看错。另一个人在一个特定的语境中看到了“alte Brotkarte”（旧面包配给卡）这个词，但仔细阅读后，他发现应该是“alte Brokate”（旧锦缎）。不过，值得一提的是，他经常去拜访的那户人家做客，为了讨好女主人，他会带面包配给卡作为礼物。一位工程师的设备总是无法长期有效地防止在建隧道受潮，他惊讶地看到一则广告，上面似乎在出售用劣质皮革（Schundleder）制成的商品。但商贩很少如此诚实；这则广告实际上是在出售用海豹皮（Seehundleder）制成的商品。

The reader’s profession or present situation can also influence his slip in reading. A philologist who was at odds with his professional colleagues over his latest (and very fine) works read Sprachstrategie [linguistic strategy] for Schachstrategie [chess strategy]. A man walking in a strange city at around the time when, because of a course of medical treatment, he needed to open his bowels read the word Klosetthaus [lavatory] on a large sign over the first floor of a tall department store, although his pleasure at seeing it was mingled with some surprise at the unusual situation of this convenient place. Next moment he was less pleased to see that the signboard really read: Korsetthaus [corset-makers].

读者的职业或当前处境也会影响其阅读错误。一位语言学家因其最新（且非常出色）的著作与同行意见相左，便将“国际象棋策略”（Schachstrategie）误读为“语言策略”（Sprachstrategie）。一位男子在陌生的城市漫步，正值因治疗需要排便之际，他看到一家高大百货商店一楼上方的大型招牌上写着“Klosetthaus”（厕所），虽然看到这个词让他感到高兴，但也对这个便利场所的出现感到有些惊讶。然而，下一刻，当他发现招牌上写的其实是“Korsetthaus”（束身衣制造商）时，他的高兴之情便荡然无存。

10) In another group of cases the part played by the text itself in a slip in reading is considerably greater. It contains something that the reader rejects, some information or supposition that is painful to him, and his slip therefore corrects it to bring it into line with his own rejection or with wish-fulfilment. Of course we have to assume that the text was initially correctly read and rejected before being altered, even though the conscious mind does not remain aware of that first reading. Example 3 above is of this kind: another very topical one I give as it is reported by Dr M. Eitingon, who was then in the field hospital in Igló ( Internationale Zeitschrift für Psychoanalyse II, 1915):

10）在另一类情况下，文本本身在阅读错误中所起的作用要大得多。文本中包含着读者所排斥的内容，一些令读者感到痛苦的信息或假设，因此，读者的阅读错误会对其进行修正，使其与自身的排斥或愿望的实现相一致。当然，我们必须假设文本最初在被篡改之前已被正确阅读并排斥，即使意识层面不再记得最初的阅读过程。上文的例3就属于这种情况：以下是另一个非常具有现实意义的例子，由当时在伊格洛野战医院的M. Eitingon博士记录（《国际精神分析杂志》第二卷，1915年）：

‘Lieutenant X., who was in our hospital with traumatic war neurosis, one day, and with obvious emotion, read aloud the last line of the last verse of a poem by Wilhelm Heymann, 2 who fell so young, as follows:

“X 中尉，当时因战争创伤后应激障碍在我们医院接受治疗，有一天，他情绪激动地朗读了威廉·海曼（Wilhelm Heymann）的一首诗的最后一节的最后一行，这位英年早逝的诗人，诗的内容如下：

Wo aber steht’s geschrieben, frag’ ich, dass von allen

但我问，哪里写着这一切呢？

Ich übrig bleiben soll, ein andrer für mich fallen?

我该继续站着，还是让别人代替我倒下？

Wer immer von euch fällt, der stirbt gewiss für mich;

你们中间凡跌倒的，必为我而死；

Und ich soll übrig bleiben? warum denn nicht?

难道我应该是最后一个留下的？为什么不呢？

[Where is it written then that of you all I should be left, another for me fall? Whoever falls dies certainly for me. Am I to live unscathed? But why not me?]

经上哪里写着，你们众人之中，我必被留下，有人替我倒下？凡倒下的人，必是替我而死。难道我能毫发无损地活着吗？为什么不能是我？

‘Alerted by my surprise, he then, rather shamefacedly, read it correctly:

“他被我的惊讶所吸引，然后颇为羞愧地正确地读了出来：”

Und ich soll übrig bleiben? warum denn ich?

难道我就是最后一个留下的？为什么是我？

[Am I to live unscathed? How can that be?]

我能毫发无损地活下来吗？这怎么可能？

‘I owe several analytical insights into the psychic material of such “traumatic war neuroses” to the case of X., and although conditions in a field hospital with many patients and few doctors are not very favourable to our working methods, I could see more in the “causes” of these cases than the terrifying sound of shells exploding.

“我从 X 的案例中获得了许多关于此类‘创伤性战争神经症’心理物质的分析见解，尽管野战医院里病人多医生少，这样的条件对我们的工作方法不太有利，但我从这些病例的‘原因’中看到的，比炮弹爆炸的可怕声音要多得多。”

‘The same patient displayed the symptoms that at first glance lend a striking similarity to all bad cases of war neurosis: severe tremors, fearfulness, lachrymosity, an inclination to fits of fury accompanied by convulsive, infantile motor expressions, and a tendency to vomit (“for the slightest reason”).

“这位病人表现出的症状乍一看与所有严重的战争神经症病例惊人地相似：严重的震颤、恐惧、流泪、易怒，伴有抽搐的、婴儿般的运动表现，以及呕吐的倾向（‘哪怕是最轻微的原因’）。

‘The psychogenic nature of the last symptom in particular, more especially its ability to derive some secondary profit from illness, was bound to strike everyone: the mere appearance in the ward of the hospital commandant, who came in from time to time to visit the convalescents, a friend’s casual remark in the street — “You’re looking well, you must be better now” — were all quite enough to set off a prompt attack of vomiting. “Cured…that means going back to the front…why should I?”’

“最后一个症状的心理性，尤其是它能从疾病中获得某种次要好处的能力，必然会让每个人都感到震惊：医院指挥官偶尔会来病房探望康复者，他只要出现在病房里，朋友在街上随口说一句——‘你看上去气色不错，肯定好多了’——就足以引发一阵剧烈的呕吐。“痊愈了……那就意味着要重返前线……我为什么要回去？”

11) Dr Hanns Sachs gives an account of some other cases of slips in reading induced by wartime experience:

11）汉斯·萨克斯博士讲述了一些因战争经历而导致阅读能力下降的其他案例：

‘A close acquaintance had repeatedly told me that when his turn came he would not make any use of his expert training, for which he had gained a diploma, no, he was not going to take advantage of the chance to which it entitled him of employment behind the lines — he would enlist for active service. Shortly before that time actually came he told me one day very briefly, giving no further reason, that he had sent off corroboration of his expert qualifications to the appropriate quarter, and as a result he would soon be working in industry. Next day we met in a local office. I was standing at a desk writing; he came in, looked over my shoulder for a while, and then said, “Oh, I see the word at the top there is really Druckbogen [printed sheet]; I’d read it as Drückeberger [skiver]”’ ( Internationale Zeitschrift für Psychoanalyse IV, 1916/17).

“一位熟人曾多次告诉我，等他轮到自己时，他不会利用自己获得的专业技能证书，也不会去争取证书赋予他的后方工作机会——他会应征入伍。就在他真正入伍前不久，有一天他简短地告诉我，他已经把自己的专业资格证明寄给了相关部门，因此他很快就能在工厂工作了，也没有给出其他理由。第二天，我们在当地一家办公室见面。我当时正站在办公桌前写作；他走了进来，在我身后看了看，然后说：‘哦，我看到顶部的那个词实际上是Druckbogen（印刷纸）；我把它读成了Drückeberger（裁纸机）’”（《国际精神分析杂志》第四卷，1916/17年）。

12) ‘Sitting in the tram, I was thinking that many of the friends of my youth, who had always been considered delicate and frail, now seemed able to stand up to the harshest of conditions which would certainly have a shattering effect on me. In the middle of this unwelcome train of thought, as we were passing a firm’s signboard, I was only half aware of registering, as we passed, a word in big black letters saying Eisenkonstitution [iron constitution]. A moment later it struck me that this was not really right for a business sign, and turning back quickly I caught another glimpse of the inscription, and saw that it really read Eisenkonstruktion [Iron Construction]’ (op. cit).

12) “坐在电车上，我想着我年轻时的许多朋友，他们一直被认为体弱多病，现在似乎能够承受最恶劣的环境，而这肯定会对我造成毁灭性的打击。正当我沉浸在这种不愉快的思绪中时，我们经过一家公司的招牌，我隐约注意到上面用黑色大字写着‘Eisenkonstitution’（钢铁结构）。片刻之后，我突然意识到这不太像商业招牌上的字，于是我迅速回头又瞥了一眼，发现上面写的是‘Eisenkonstruktion’（钢铁结构）。”（同上）

13) ‘The evening papers printed a dispatch from Reuter’s, which later proved unfounded, reporting that Hughes had been elected President of the United States. This announcement was followed by a brief biography of the alleged President elect, informing me that Hughes had studied at Bonn University. I thought it odd that this circumstance had never been mentioned in the weeks of press debate leading up to election day. A second glance showed that in fact the report said Brown University. This striking case, where considerable violence had to be done to the real words for me to make my slip, is explained not just by the cursory nature of my glance at the newspaper report, but chiefly by the fact that I thought it would be excellent if, as the basis for future good relations, the new President’s sympathy for the central European powers derived from personal as well as political causes’ (loc. cit.).

13）“晚报刊登了路透社的一篇报道，后来证实该报道不实，报道称休斯当选美国总统。随后刊登了一篇关于这位所谓当选总统的简短传记，其中提到休斯曾在波恩大学就读。我感到奇怪的是，在选举日前的几周新闻讨论中，竟然从未提及此事。仔细一看，才发现报道中实际上写的是布朗大学。这起令人震惊的事件，需要对原文进行相当大的改动才能让我犯错，其原因不仅在于我对报纸报道的粗略浏览，更主要的原因是，我认为如果新总统对中欧列强的同情既源于政治原因，也源于个人原因，那么这将为未来建立良好的关系奠定基础，而这本身就是一件好事”（同上）。

B) Slips of the pen

B) 笔误

1) I was surprised to find a slip of the pen on a sheet of paper containing brief day-to-day notes, most of them relating to business: among several entries correctly dated to the month of September, 1 had written ‘Thursday, 20 October’. It was not difficult to account for this anticipation as expressing a wish. A few days earlier I had come back from a holiday, feeling refreshed and ready to tackle a considerable medical caseload, but I still did not have very many prospective patients. On arriving home, I found a letter from a woman patient proposing to visit me on 20 October. When I wrote down the same date of the month, but for September instead, I was probably thinking: I wish X. were here now; what a pity she can’t come for another month! And in so thinking, I anticipated the date. The disruptive idea can hardly be called an unwelcome one in this case, and indeed that was why I understood the reason for my slip of the pen as soon as I noticed it. I perpetrated an analogous and similarly motivated slip of the pen in the autumn of the following year. E. Jones has studied similar slips of the pen in recording dates and in most cases has easily recognized them as well motivated.

1）我惊讶地发现一张纸上笔迹潦草，上面记录着一些日常琐事，大部分都与工作有关：在几条日期都正确标注为九月份的记录中，有一条写成了“10月20日，星期四”。不难理解，这或许是出于某种愿望。几天前我刚度假回来，感觉精神焕发，准备迎接大量的医疗工作，但当时我还没有多少潜在的病人。到家后，我收到一位女病人的来信，她计划在10月20日来看我。当我把同样的日期写成九月份的日期时，我可能在想：真希望X女士现在就来；可惜她还要一个月才能来！就这样，我提前写下了这个日期。在这种情况下，这种突如其来的想法很难称得上是令人不快的，事实上，正因如此，我一注意到笔迹潦草就明白了其中的原因。第二年秋天，我又犯了一次类似的、出于同样动机的笔误。E. Jones 研究过类似的日期记录笔误，并且在大多数情况下都能轻易地识别出这些笔误都是有正当理由的。

2) I received the uncorrected proofs of my contribution to the Jahresbericht für Neurologie und Psychiatrie , and of course I had to check the names of the authors I had mentioned with particular care, since names of various nationalities commonly cause the typesetter a good deal of difficulty. Sure enough, I did find several foreign-sounding names in need of correction, but there was one that, remarkably enough, the typesetter had changed from the version in my manuscript, and moreover he was perfectly right to do so. I had written Buckrhard , which the typesetter had guessed should be Burckhard. In this passage I myself had described an obstetrician’s account of the influence of childbirth on cases of infantile paralysis as very good, and I had nothing to say against the Burckhard who was its author, but he bore the same name as a Viennese writer who had upset me by writing an ill-informed review of my Interpretation of Dreams. It was as if in writing the name of Burckhard to refer to the obstetrician I had been thinking something unpleasant about the other man, the author of the review, since spelling a name incorrectly is very often insulting, as I mentioned above in the section on slips of the tongue. 3

2）我收到了我为《神经病学和精神病学年鉴》（Jahresbericht für Neurologie und Psychiatrie）撰写的文章的未校对稿，当然，我必须格外仔细地核对文中提及的作者姓名，因为不同国籍的姓名常常会给排版员带来不少麻烦。果然，我发现了一些听起来像外国名字需要修改的地方，但令人惊讶的是，排版员竟然把我手稿中的版本改成了别的名字，而且他改得完全正确。我写的是Buckrhard，排版员猜应该是Burckhard。在那段文字中，我曾评价一位产科医生对分娩对小儿麻痹症病例影响的描述非常精彩，我并没有什么意见反对这位名叫Burckhard的作者，但他的名字和一位维也纳作家同名，这位作家曾写过一篇对我的《梦的解析》（Interpretation of Dreams）的评论，内容缺乏依据，让我很不高兴。就好像我在写“Burckhard”这个名字来指代那位妇产科医生时，心里对另一位男士——也就是那篇评论的作者——有什么不愉快的想法似的。因为拼错名字往往是一种侮辱，正如我在前面关于口误的部分提到的那样。

3) There is good support for this statement in a self-observation of A. J. Storfer’s where the author, with laudable frankness, sets out the reasons that made him remember the name of a supposed rival incorrectly and then misspell it when he wrote it down:

3）A. J. Storfer 的自我观察很好地支持了这一说法，作者以值得称赞的坦率，阐述了他记错一个假想竞争对手的名字，然后在写下来时又拼错的原因：

‘In December 1910 I saw the new book (as it then was) by Dr Eduard Hitschmann on the Freudian theory of neurosis in a bookseller’s window in Zurich. At the time I happened to be working on the manuscript of a lecture I was soon to deliver to an academic society on the fundamental principles of Freudian psychology. In the introduction to the lecture, which I had already written, I had mentioned the historical development of Freudian psychology from studies in an applied field of medicine, and the resulting difficulty of giving a comprehensive account of those fundamental principles, adding that so far there was no general account. When I saw the book (by an author previously unknown to me) in the shop window I did not at first intend to buy it. However, a few days later I decided that I would, but by then the book was not in the window. I told the bookseller the tide of this recently published work, giving the author’s name as “Dr Eduard Hartmann ”. The bookseller corrected me — “I expect you mean Hitschmann ” — and brought me the book.

1910年12月，我在苏黎世一家书店的橱窗里看到了爱德华·希奇曼博士关于弗洛伊德神经症理论的新书（当时还未出版）。那时我正巧在准备一份即将向学术团体发表的关于弗洛伊德心理学基本原理的演讲稿。在我已经写好的演讲稿引言中，我提到了弗洛伊德心理学从应用医学领域的研究发展而来，以及由此产生的难以对这些基本原理进行全面阐述的问题，并补充说，当时还没有人对这些原理进行过系统性的阐述。当我看到这本书（作者我之前并不认识）时，起初我并没有打算买。然而，几天后我决定要买，但那时这本书已经不在橱窗里了。我告诉书商这本新书的情况，并把作者的名字说成了“爱德华·哈特曼博士”。书商纠正我说：“我想您说的是希奇曼吧？”然后把书拿给了我。

‘The unconscious motive for my slip was obvious. I had been congratulating myself, so to speak, on writing a survey of the fundamental principles of psychoanalytical theory, and my attitude to Hitschmann’s book was obviously one of envy and annoyance because it might detract from my own merits. I told myself that, according to the Psychopathology of Everyday Life [in an earlier edition], my alteration to the name was an act of unconscious hostility, and for the time being I was satisfied with that explanation.

“我无意中犯错的动机显而易见。可以说，我一直在为自己完成了精神分析理论基本原理的综述而沾沾自喜，我对希奇曼的书显然是出于嫉妒和恼怒，因为它可能会削弱我自身的成就。我告诉自己，根据《日常生活心理病理学》（早期版本）的说法，我更改书名是一种无意识的敌意行为，而且我暂时对这个解释感到满意。”

‘A few weeks later I noted down this slip of mine. On that occasion I wondered exactly why I had changed Eduard Hitschmann to Eduard Hartmann. Was it just because of the similarity of Hitschmann’s name to that of the well-known philosopher Hartmann? My first association was with the memory of something I once heard said by Professor Hugo von Metzl, the authority on Schopenhauer, more or less to the effect that: “Eduard von Hartmann is a failed Schopenhauer — a Schopenhauer turned inside out.” The emotional tendency leading to the substituted structure of the forgotten name was thus: “Well, there won’t be much in this Hitschmann and his survey of the subject; he probably bears the same relation to Freud as Hartmann does to Schopenhauer.”

几周后，我记下了这张手写稿。当时我一直在想，我究竟为什么要把爱德华·希奇曼（Eduard Hitschmann）改成爱德华·哈特曼（Eduard Hartmann）。仅仅是因为希奇曼的名字和著名哲学家哈特曼的名字很像吗？我首先想到的是，我曾经听叔本华研究权威雨果·冯·梅茨尔教授说过的一句话，大意是：“爱德华·冯·哈特曼是一个失败的叔本华——一个颠倒过来的叔本华。” 导致我用这个被遗忘的名字替换原有结构的心理倾向是：“嗯，希奇曼和他对这个主题的研究不会有什么成果；他和弗洛伊德的关系，大概就像哈特曼和叔本华的关系一样。”

‘I had now recorded this case of predetermined forgetfulness accompanied by a substitute idea. Six months later I came upon the piece of paper on which I had written this note, and I saw that instead of Hitschmann I had twice written Hintschmann ’ ( Internationale Zeitschrift für Psychoanalyse II, 1914).

“我当时记录了这起预先发生的遗忘事件，并伴有替代想法。六个月后，我偶然发现了写下这条笔记的那张纸，我发现我两次把 Hitschmann 写成了 Hintschmann”（《国际精神分析杂志》第二卷，1914 年）。

4) Next is an apparently more serious case of a slip of the pen, which I might perhaps equally well place under the heading of ‘inadvertent actions’: I wanted to draw the sum of 300 crowns out of the post office savings bank, and was going to send the money to an absent relative to be used for medical treatment. As I did so I noticed that my account contained 4,380 crowns, and decided to bring it down to the round figure of 4,000 crowns, leaving that sum untouched for the time being. When I had made out my cheque in the usual way, which involved cutting the relevant figures from the sheet with my statement of account, I suddenly noticed that I had withdrawn not the 380 crowns I intended to take out but 438, and was quite alarmed by my own unreliability. I soon realized that there was no call for my alarm; after all, I was no poorer than before. None the less, it took me quite a long time to work out exactly what, without giving any notice to my conscious mind, had made me depart from my original intention. I set out along the wrong lines at first, and tried subtracting 380 from 438, but I could make nothing of the result. Finally, a sudden idea showed me the real connection. 438 was 10 per cent of the entire account, which contained 4,380 crowns! You get a 10 per cent discount from a bookseller. I remembered that a few days earlier I had sorted out a number of medical works that were of no further interest to me, and offered them to a bookseller for exactly 300 crowns. He thought the price too high, and said he would let me know his final answer within the next few days. If he accepted my offer, then he would be replacing the exact sum that I was going to give my sick relative. It cannot be denied that I regretted handing over that sum. My emotion in perceiving my mistake can be better understood as anxiety that I might impoverish myself by making such payments. But both my regret at parting with the money and the fear of indigence linked to it were entirely outside my conscious mind; I felt no regret when I agreed to pay my relative that sum, and I would have regarded such a motivation as ridiculous. It is likely that I would not have thought myself capable of an emotion of that nature had I not become reasonably familiar with repression in the life of the mind through my practical experience of psychoanalysis with my patients, and had I not had a dream some days earlier which required a similar explanation. 4

4）接下来要讲的是一个看似更严重的笔误，或许也可以归为“无意之举”：我想从邮局储蓄账户里取出300克朗，寄给一位不在身边的亲戚看病。取出时，我注意到账户里有4380克朗，于是决定取个整数4000克朗，暂时不动用这笔钱。我像往常一样填写支票，也就是从账户对账单上剪下相应的数字后，突然发现我取出的不是原本打算取出的380克朗，而是438克朗，这让我对自己的疏忽大意感到非常震惊。不过，我很快意识到自己不必惊慌；毕竟，我的钱并没有比之前少。然而，我花了很长时间才弄明白究竟是什么让我在不知不觉中偏离了最初的计划。起初我走错了方向，尝试用438减去380，但结果却毫无头绪。最后，一个灵光乍现的念头让我恍然大悟。438是账户总额的10%，而账户里正好有4380克朗！书商会给你10%的折扣。我突然想起几天前，我整理了一些不再需要的医学书籍，并以300克朗的价格卖给了书商。他觉得价格太高，说会在几天内给我最终答复。如果他接受我的报价，那么他就会把原本打算给生病亲戚的钱补回来。我不得不承认，我后悔把那笔钱给了他。我意识到自己犯错时的情绪，可以更好地理解为担心支付这些款项会让我陷入贫困。但是，无论是后悔把钱交给亲戚，还是害怕因此而变得贫穷，都完全不在我的意识之内；当我同意支付亲戚那笔钱时，我并没有感到后悔，而且我会觉得这种动机很荒谬。如果不是因为我通过与病人进行精神分析的实践经验，对心理压抑有了相当的了解，如果不是因为几天前我做了一个需要类似解释的梦，我可能根本不会认为自己会有这种情绪。

5) I quote the following case from W. Stekel, and can vouch for its authenticity myself: ‘An extraordinary instance of the misreading of a slip of the pen happened when a widely distributed weekly journal was being edited. The management of the journal had been publicly accused of venality, so an article of refutation had to be written in defence. And written it was — with much warmth and strong emotion. The editor-in-chief of the journal read the article, the author of course read it several times in manuscript and then in galley proof, and everyone was well satisfied. Suddenly the proofreader spoke up, pointing out a small mistake that had escaped everyone’s attention. The wording said, clearly: “Our readers will be well aware that we have always promoted the common good in the most self-interested [ eigennützig ] manner.” Of course it should have read uneigennützig [disinterested]. But the real thinking behind the emotional article broke through with elemental force.’

5）我引用W. Stekel的以下案例，并可亲自证实其真实性：“在一家发行量很大的周刊编辑过程中，发生了一起因笔误而导致的罕见误读事件。该刊管理层被公开指责贪污腐败，因此必须撰写一篇反驳文章进行辩护。文章写得热情洋溢，饱含深情。期刊主编阅读了这篇文章，作者当然也反复阅读了手稿和校样，大家都非常满意。突然，校对员指出了一个所有人都忽略的小错误。原文是：“我们的读者应该很清楚，我们一直以最自私（eigennützig）的方式促进公共利益。” 当然，它应该写成“uneigennützig”（无私的）。但这篇文章背后饱含情感的真实想法却以一种原始的力量显露出来。”

6) A reader of the daily Pester Lloyd newspaper, Frau Kata Levy of Budapest, recently noticed a similarly unintentional instance of honesty in a report that the journal received from Vienna by telegraph on 11 October 1918:

6）布达佩斯的《佩斯特·劳埃德日报》读者卡塔·莱维女士最近注意到，该报于 1918 年 10 月 11 日通过电报从维也纳收到的一份报告中，也出现了类似的无意诚实的例子：

‘On the grounds of the relationship of absolute trust that prevailed throughout the war between us and our German allies, it may be assumed, beyond all doubt, that the two powers will reach unanimous agreement in all cases. There is no need for any explicit mention of the fact that there is still lively and incomplete [ lückenhaft ] co-operation between the allied diplomats.’

“基于我们与德国盟国在整个战争期间所秉持的绝对信任关系，可以毫无疑问地认为，两国在所有问题上都将达成一致意见。无需赘述盟国外交官之间仍然存在活跃但并不完全的合作这一事实。”

Just a few weeks later people could express themselves more freely about this ‘relationship of trust’, without needing to resort to slips of the pen or misprints.

仅仅几周后，人们就可以更自由地表达自己对这种“信任关系”的看法，而无需诉诸笔误或印刷错误。

7) An American staying in Europe, who had parted with his wife on bad terms, thought perhaps they could now make the quarrel up and asked her to cross the Atlantic and meet him on a certain date. ‘It would be a good idea if you sailed on the Mauretania ,’ he wrote. However, he did not venture to send the sheet of paper on which he had written this sentence, preferring to rewrite the whole letter in case she noticed the correction he had been obliged to make to the name of the ship. He had originally written Lusitania.

7）一位旅居欧洲的美国人，与妻子不欢而散，心想或许现在他们可以和好如初，于是邀请妻子横渡大西洋，在某个日期与他见面。“如果你乘坐‘毛里塔尼亚号’就更好了，”他写道。然而，他不敢寄出写着这句话的那张纸，而是选择重写整封信，以免妻子发现他不得不修改船名。他最初写的是“卢西塔尼亚号”。

This slip of the pen needs no elucidation and can be easily interpreted. By a lucky coincidence, however, more can be added to this instance: his wife had visited Europe for the first time before the war, after her only sister’s death, and, if I am not mistaken, the Mauretania is the surviving sister ship of the Lusitania , which was sunk during the war.

这笔误无需赘述，很容易理解。然而，巧合的是，这件事还有更多值得注意的地方：他的妻子在战前，在她唯一的姐姐去世后，第一次访问了欧洲；而且，如果我没记错的话，“毛里塔尼亚号”是“卢西塔尼亚号”的姊妹船，后者在战争中被击沉。

8) A doctor examined a child, and was writing out a prescription containing alcohol. While he did so, the child’s mother kept bothering him with silly and unnecessary questions. He told himself he was not going to lose his temper, and stuck to this resolution, but his irritation caused a slip of the pen. His prescription contained the word not alcohol but achol. 5

8) 一位医生给一个孩子看病，正在开一张含有酒精的处方。期间，孩子的母亲不停地问他一些愚蠢又没必要的问题。医生告诉自己不要发脾气，并且坚持了这个决心，但他的烦躁导致笔误。处方上的“酒精”一词写成了“achol”，而不是“alcohol”。

9) Since the subjects are related, I will add here a story that E. Jones tells of A. A. Brill. Although Brill never drank at all in the usual way, a friend persuaded him to take a little wine. Next morning a violent headache made him regret agreeing. When he had to write down the name of a woman patient called Ethel, he wrote Ethyl instead. 6 Another factor in this case may have been that the lady herself drank rather more than was good for her. Since a doctor’s slip of the pen in writing out a prescription can have far greater practical consequences than ordinary slips, I will take this opportunity of giving a full account of the only analysis of such a medical slip yet published:

9）鉴于主题相关，我在此补充E. Jones讲述的A. A. Brill的故事。Brill虽然平时滴酒不沾，但一位朋友劝他喝了一点葡萄酒。第二天早上，剧烈的头痛让他后悔不已。当他需要写下一位名叫Ethel的女病人的名字时，他却写成了Ethyl。 6 另一个因素可能是，这位女士本人饮酒过量。由于医生在填写处方时笔误造成的实际后果可能远比普通的笔误严重得多，我将借此机会详细介绍迄今为止唯一一篇已发表的关于此类医疗笔误的分析文章：

10) Dr E. Hitschmann, writing on a repeated case of slips of the pen in a prescription: ‘A colleague told me that over the years he had several times made mistakes in prescribing a certain medication for women patients of advanced years. He twice prescribed ten times the correct dose, and when he suddenly realized what he had done, he had to make haste to cancel the prescription, in great alarm lest he had harmed the patient, which would put him in a very unpleasant situation himself. This curious symptomatic action deserves further elucidation by a more detailed account of the individual cases and by analysis.

10）E. Hitschmann 博士在论述一起反复出现的处方笔误案例时写道：“一位同事告诉我，多年来，他曾多次在给老年女性患者开某种药物时出错。他有两次开出的剂量是正确剂量的十倍，当他突然意识到自己犯了错时，他不得不赶紧取消处方，因为他非常担心自己会伤害到患者，而这也会让他自己陷入非常尴尬的境地。这种奇特的症状反应值得通过对个案的更详细描述和分析来进一步阐明。”

‘In the first case, the doctor prescribed a poor woman on the verge of great old age some belladonna suppositories ten times too strong for her spastic constipation. He then left the outpatients’ department of the hospital, and about an hour later, as he was reading the newspaper over lunch, his mistake suddenly struck him. In great alarm, he first hurried back to the outpatients’ department to ask for the patient’s address and then went straight to her home, which was some way off. He found that the old lady had not yet had her prescription made up, and left feeling greatly relieved, his mind at rest. By way of excuse, and not without some justification, he told himself that the loquacious head of the outpatients’ department had been looking over his shoulder as he wrote the prescription and had disturbed his concentration.

“第一个案例中，医生给一位年迈体弱的老妇人开了颠茄栓剂，剂量比她痉挛性便秘所需的剂量高出十倍。之后他离开了医院门诊部，大约一个小时后，当他一边吃午饭一边看报纸时，突然意识到自己犯了错。他惊慌失措，先是匆匆赶回门诊部询问病人的地址，然后直接去了她家，她家离医院还有一段距离。他发现老妇人的处方还没配好，这才松了一口气，心安理得地离开了。他为自己辩解说，门诊部那位喋喋不休的主任在他写处方的时候一直在旁边看着，打断了他的思路，这并非毫无道理。”

‘In the second case the doctor had to tear himself away from a flirtatious and good-looking woman patient and leave his consulting rooms in order to examine an elderly spinster lady. He went by car, since he did not have much time for this visit, and he was to have a secret meeting with a young girl of whom he was enamoured near her home at a certain hour. The same medical trouble as in the first case suggested that belladonna was indicated, and yet again he prescribed a dose ten times too high by mistake. The patient said something that, although interesting, was not relevant to her case at present, and although he overtly denied it the doctor showed his impatience and left her in good time to keep his appointment. Some twelve hours later, around seven in the morning, the doctor woke up; the realization that he had committed a slip of the pen came into his conscious mind, almost immediately accompanied by great alarm, and he made haste to send his patient a message, hoping the prescription had not been fetched from the pharmacy yet and asking her to return it so that he could alter it. However, he found that the prescription had already been made up, and went off with a certain stoical resignation — but also with the optimism of experience — to the pharmacy, where the pharmacist calmed his fears by saying that of course (unless it was a mistake of his own?) he had made up a weaker dose than the prescription specified.

“第二个病例中，医生不得不从一位风情万种、容貌姣好的女病人身边抽身，离开诊室去给一位年迈的未婚女士看病。由于时间紧迫，他开车前往，因为他还要在某个时间与一位他心仪的年轻女孩在她家附近秘密会面。与第一个病例相同的病症表明，颠茄可能有效，然而他又一次错误地开出了十倍剂量的处方。病人说了一些话，虽然有趣，但与她目前的病情无关。尽管医生表面上否认，但他还是显得很不耐烦，及时离开了，以便赴约。大约十二个小时后，早上七点左右，医生醒了过来；他意识到自己犯了笔误，几乎立刻感到极度恐慌，于是赶紧给病人捎了个信，希望药房还没取回处方，请她把处方送回来以便他修改。”然而，他发现处方药已经配好了，于是带着某种坚忍的无奈——但也带着经验带来的乐观——去了药房。药剂师打消了他的疑虑，说当然（除非是他自己的错误？），他配的药剂量比处方规定的要少。

‘In the third case, the doctor was going to write his old aunt, his mother’s sister, a prescription for a harmless dose of a mixture of Tinct. belladonnae and Tinct. opii. The maidservant took the prescription straight to the pharmacy. Quite soon afterwards it struck the doctor that he had written extractum instead of tinctura , and the next moment the pharmacist telephoned to query his mistake. The doctor untruthfully excused himself by saying that he was not to blame: he had not finished writing out the prescription before it was snatched up from the desk where he was sitting with unexpected speed.

“第三个例子是，医生打算给他的老姑妈，也就是他母亲的妹妹，开一张处方，让她服用无害剂量的颠茄酊和鸦片酊的混合物。女佣直接把处方送到了药房。没过多久，医生就意识到自己把酊剂写成了提取物（extractum），药剂师立刻打电话来询问他的错误。医生谎称自己没有错：他还没写完处方，就被人以惊人的速度从他坐着的桌子上抢走了。”

‘The salient points in common between these three cases of slips of the pen are that so far the doctor had perpetrated them only in relation to this one drug, that in all three the patient was female and advanced in age, and that the dose was always too strong. A brief analysis showed that the doctor’s relationship to his mother must be of crucial importance here. It struck him that he had once — and very probably before his symptomatic action — written his also elderly mother the same prescription in a dose of 0.03, hoping to bring her radical relief, although he would normally have prescribed the usual dose of 0.02. His mother, whose constitution was delicate, reacted to the drug with congestion in the head and an unpleasantly dry mouth. She complained half jokingly of the dangers of consulting a son on medical matters. And there had been other occasions when his mother, herself a doctor’s daughter, had shown a disinclination to take the medicaments recommended by her doctor son, referring in jest to being poisoned.

这三起笔误的共同点在于：迄今为止，这位医生只就这一种药物犯过错；三例患者均为年迈的女性；且剂量均过高。简要分析表明，医生与其母亲的关系在此至关重要。他突然想起，自己曾给同样年迈的母亲开过同样的处方——很可能是在他出现症状之前——剂量为0.03克，希望能够彻底缓解她的症状，尽管他通常会开0.02克的常用剂量。他的母亲体弱多病，服用后出现了头痛和口干舌燥的症状。她半开玩笑地抱怨说，向儿子咨询医疗问题有多么危险。此外，他的母亲本人也是一位医生的女儿，她也曾多次拒绝服用儿子推荐的药物，并开玩笑说自己中毒了。

‘So far as the writer can judge the relationship of this son to his mother, he had a natural love for her, but no personal respect or any great opinion of her intellectual qualities. Sharing a household with her and his brother, who was a year younger, he had felt for years that his erotic liberty was inhibited, although as psychoanalytical experience tells us, such reasons are often misused to cover up family ties of too intimate a nature. The doctor accepted this analysis, reasonably satisfied with the explanation, and said, smiling, that the word belladonna , “beautiful woman”, could also indicate an erotic connection. Earlier, he had sometimes taken the same medication himself’ ( Internationale Zeitschrift für Psychoanalyse I, 1913).

“就作者对这位儿子与其母亲关系的判断而言，他对母亲怀有自然的爱，但对她并无个人敬意，也未对其才智给予任何高度评价。他与母亲和比他小一岁的弟弟共同生活，多年来一直感到自己的性自由受到压抑。然而，正如精神分析经验告诉我们的，这种理由常常被滥用，用来掩盖过于亲密的家庭关系。医生接受了这一分析，对解释相当满意，并笑着说，颠茄（belladonna）一词，意为“美丽的女人”，也可能暗示着某种性方面的联系。此前，他自己有时也服用过同样的药物。”（《国际精神分析杂志》第一卷，1913年）

In my view such serious slips occur in exactly the same way as the harmless variety that we usually investigate.

在我看来，这种严重的失误与我们通常调查的无害失误的发生方式完全相同。

11) The following case of a slip of the pen described by S. Ferenczi will seem particularly innocuous. It may be regarded as a case of compression resulting from impatience (cf. my slip of the tongue in saying der Apfe , p. 60 ), and such a view could have been defended had not close analysis of the incident shown a stronger disruptive factor at work:

11）S. Ferenczi 描述的以下笔误案例似乎特别无害。这或许可以被视为因急躁而导致的笔误（参见我第 60 页说“der Apfe”时的口误），如果不是对该事件进行仔细分析后发现存在更强烈的干扰因素，这种观点或许还能成立：

‘I once wrote in my notebook: “This may be illustrated by the Anektode ” — meaning of course Anekdote [‘anecdote’, but echoing Tod , ‘death’], and referring to the tale of a gypsy condemned to death — zu Tode — who asked, as a favour, to make his own choice of tree from which he was to be hung himself. (Of course, despite zealous searching, he failed to find any suitable tree.)’

我曾在笔记本上写道：“这可以用《轶事》（Anektode）来说明”——这里指的当然是“轶事”（Anekdote，与“死亡”（Tod）谐音），指的是一个被判处死刑的吉普赛人——祖·托德（zu Tode）——的故事。他请求别人帮他一个忙，让他自己挑选绞刑的树。（当然，尽管他竭尽全力寻找，但最终也没找到合适的树。）

12) On other occasions, in contrast, the most insignificant slip of the pen can express a dangerous secret meaning. An anonymous correspondent writes:

12）相反，在其他情况下，最微不足道的笔误也可能表达出危险的秘密含义。一位匿名来信者写道：

‘I concluded a letter by sending “Very best wishes to your wife and ihren [her] son.” Just before putting the letter in the envelope I noticed the mistake in the initial [which should have been a capital I: Ihren — “your” — son], and corrected it. On the way home from my last visit to this married couple, my woman companion had commented that the son looked strikingly like a family friend of theirs and must surely be his child.’

“我在信的结尾写道：‘向您的妻子和她的儿子致以最美好的祝愿。’就在把信放进信封之前，我注意到首字母写错了（应该是大写字母 I：Ihren——‘您的’——儿子），于是改正了。上次拜访这对夫妇回家的路上，我的女伴说，他们的儿子长得特别像他们的一位朋友，肯定是他的孩子。”

13) A lady sent her sister a few lines of good wishes when she moved into a spacious new apartment. A woman friend present noticed that the writer had put the wrong address on the letter: not the sister’s last address, but that of her first home after she was just married, a place from which she had moved long ago. She pointed the mistake out to the letter-writer. ‘You’re right,’ the lady had to admit. ‘How on earth did I come to do that, and why?’ Her friend said: ‘I expect you don’t like to think of the beautiful big apartment she will have while you feel you’re short of space yourself, so you wish her back in her first home where she would be no better off than you.’ ‘Well, of course I’m not really glad she has her nice new apartment.’ the other woman honestly admitted, adding: ‘What a pity one always has such horrid feelings over these things!’

13）一位女士在妹妹搬进宽敞的新公寓时，给她写了一封简短的祝福信。在场的一位女性朋友发现，写信人把地址写错了：不是妹妹之前的住址，而是她刚结婚后的第一个家的地址，而她很久以前就搬走了。朋友指出了这个错误。“你说得对，”女士不得不承认，“我怎么会犯这种错误呢？为什么会这样？”她的朋友说：“我猜你是不愿看到她住进这么漂亮的大公寓，而你自己却觉得空间不够用，所以才希望她搬回原来的家，在那里她的生活也不会比你好多少。”“嗯，我当然不真的为她搬进这么漂亮的新公寓感到高兴。”另一位女士坦诚地承认道，并补充说：“真可惜，人们总是会对这些事情产生如此糟糕的情绪！”

14) E. Jones reports the following example of a slip of the pen [in English], given him by A. A. Brill: ‘A patient wrote to Dr Brill suggesting that his nervous state should be ascribed to his business anxieties during a crisis in the cotton trade. He claimed, in this letter: “My trouble is all due to that damned frigid wave; there isn’t even any seed.” Of course he meant to write “wave”, meaning a current on the money market, but in fact he wrote wife. Fundamentally, he was accusing his wife of frigidity and childlessness, and he was not very far from recognizing that his lack of sexual relations were to a considerable extent the cause of his trouble.’

14）E. Jones 报告了 A. A. Brill 给他的以下笔误示例（英文）：一位病人写信给 Brill 医生，认为他的神经衰弱是由于棉花贸易危机期间的商业焦虑造成的。他在信中写道：“我的麻烦全都是那该死的寒流造成的；连种子都没有。”他当然想写的是“wave”（浪潮），指的是金融市场的波动，但实际上他写的是“wife”（妻子）。从根本上说，他是在指责妻子性冷淡且不育，而且他离意识到自己性生活不和谐在很大程度上是造成他困境的原因也并不遥远。

15) Dr R. Wagner writes of himself, in the Zentralblatt für Psychoanalyse I, 12:

15) R. Wagner 博士在 Zentralblatt für Psychoanalysis I, 12 中这样描述自己：

‘On reading through an old college notebook I found that I had made a small slip because of the speed with which I wrote. Instead of Epithel [epithelium] I had written down Edithel , a word which, if the first syllable bears the stress, becomes the diminutive of a girl’s name [Edith, with the Austrian diminutive l ]. In retrospect, analysis is simple enough. At the time I made this slip of the pen my acquaintance with the girl who bore that name was still entirely superficial, and our friendship did not become intimate until much later. My slip of the pen is thus a neat proof of the emergence of an unconscious fondness for her at a time when I myself really had no notion of it yet, and at the same time my choice of the diminutive illustrates the feelings connected with my slip.’

“翻阅大学时期的一本旧笔记本时，我发现自己因为书写速度太快而犯了一个小错误。我把Epithel（上皮）写成了Edithel，而Edithel这个词，如果重音在第一个音节上，就成了女孩名字的昵称（Edith，奥地利语昵称l）。现在回想起来，分析起来很简单。当时我和那个叫Edithel的女孩还只是泛泛之交，我们的友谊直到很久以后才变得亲密。因此，我的这个笔误恰恰证明了，在我完全没有意识到的时候，我已经对她产生了一种无意识的好感；同时，我选择使用昵称也反映了我当时的感受。”

16) Frau D. von Hug-Hellmuth writes: ‘A doctor prescribed Leviticowasser [Levitical water] instead of Levicowasser [mineral water from Levico] for his woman patient. This mistake, which gave the pharmacist a welcome opportunity to make sarcastic remarks, can easily be given a milder interpretation if we look for possible motives in the unconscious mind and do not deny them some degree of probability out of hand, even if these are only subjective assumptions on the part of someone who is not close to the doctor concerned. Although he used to accuse his patients, in no uncertain terms, of preferring a poor diet, and it could be said that he read them die Leviten [‘read them a stern lecture’, a colloquial German idiom], he was very popular, and his waiting room was full both before and during surgery hours, a good enough reason for him to wish that once he had finished a consultation his patients would get dressed as quickly as possible — vite, vite. As I thought I remembered, and I was correct, his wife was a Frenchwoman by birth, which to some extent supports what may seem my rather bold supposition that he spoke French in urging them to make haste. In fact many people are in the habit of expressing such wishes in a foreign language; my own father used to encourage us children to go faster when we were out on a walk by crying Avanti gioventù or Marchez au pas , and I remember that a doctor getting on in years, who treated me for a disorder of the throat when I was a young girl, tried to control my movements when they were too quick for his liking with a soothing Piano, piano. So it seems to me perfectly possible that this doctor was in the same habit, and thus, in error [thinking of the word vite ], wrote Levitico Water instead of Levico Water’ ( Zentralblatt für Psychoanalyse II, 5).

16）D. von Hug-Hellmuth 女士写道：“一位医生给他的女病人开了 Leviticowasser（利未水），而不是 Levicowasser（利未矿泉水）。这个错误让药剂师有机会冷嘲热讽，但如果我们去探寻潜意识中可能的动机，并且不轻易否定其可能性（即使这些只是与医生关系不密切的人的主观臆断），那么这个错误就很容易被赋予一个更温和的解释。尽管这位医生总是毫不含糊地指责他的病人饮食不健康，甚至可以说他给他们上了‘die Leviten’（德语俗语，意为‘严厉训诫’），但他非常受欢迎，诊室在诊前和诊疗期间总是挤满了人，这足以让他希望病人在结束诊疗后尽快穿好衣服——快点，快点。”我记得没错，他的妻子是法国人，这在某种程度上印证了我之前那个或许有些大胆的推测：他催促他们快点时用的是法语。事实上，很多人都习惯用外语表达这种愿望；我父亲以前带我们出去散步时，会喊着“Avanti gioventù”（前进吧，年轻人）或“Marchez au pas”（走开），以此鼓励我们走快点。我还记得，我小时候，一位年纪较大的医生给我治疗喉咙痛，他有时会用舒缓的“Piano, piano”（钢琴，钢琴）来控制我的动作，因为我走得太快了。所以，我觉得这位医生很可能也有同样的习惯，因此，他可能误把“Levico Water”（利未记）写成了“Levico Water”（利未记）。（《精神分析中心学报》第二卷，第5页）

The writer mentions other examples from her own youthful memories ( frazösisch instead of französisch [French], and a slip in writing the name Karl).

作者还提到了她自己年轻时的记忆中的其他例子（比如把 französisch 写成 frazösisch [法语]，以及写 Karl 这个名字时出错）。

17) I owe this account of a slip of the pen, which coincides with a familiar bad joke although there was certainly no intention of joking, to Herr J. G., a contribution from whom I have already mentioned.

17) 我要感谢 J. G. 先生，感谢他提供的帮助，让我得以解释笔误，这与一个熟悉的糟糕笑话不谋而合，尽管我绝对没有开玩笑的意图。我已经提到过他的贡献。

‘As a patient in a tuberculosis sanatorium I found, to my great grief, that a close relation had been diagnosed with the same illness as the one that had sent me to hospital. I wrote to my relative urging him to see a specialist, a well-known professor who was treating me and of whose medical competence I was confident, although on the other hand I had every reason to complain of his incivility: only a little while earlier the professor in question had refused to write me a reference that meant a great deal to me. In replying to my letter, my relation pointed out a slip of the pen, which amused me a great deal, since I could see the reason for it at once. When I wrote to him, I had said: “…and anyway I advise you to in sult [German: insultieren ] Professor X. without delay.” Of course I had meant to write consult [ konsultieren ]. Perhaps I should point out that my knowledge of Latin and French excludes any possibility of my having made such a mistake out of ignorance.’

“我当时在一家肺结核疗养院接受治疗，却悲痛地发现一位近亲也被诊断出患有和我一样的疾病。我写信给这位亲人，敦促他去看一位专家，一位正在为我治疗的知名教授，我对他的医术深信不疑。尽管另一方面，我完全有理由抱怨他的无礼：就在不久前，这位教授拒绝为我写一封对我意义重大的推荐信。在回信中，我的亲人指出了我笔误的地方，这让我觉得十分有趣，因为我立刻明白了其中的原因。我写信给他时说的是：‘……无论如何，我建议你立刻去羞辱（德语：insultieren）X教授。’当然，我本想写的是咨询（德语：konsultieren）。或许我应该指出，我精通拉丁语和法语，因此绝不可能是因为无知而犯了这样的错误。”

18) Omissions in writing can of course be assessed in the same way as slips of the pen. In the Zentralblatt für Psychoanalyse I, 12, Dr B. Dattner, a doctor of law, reports a curious example of a ‘historical slip’. In one of the legal articles agreed in the settlement between Austria and Hungary in 1867 on the financial obligations of the two states, the word effective has been left out in the Hungarian translation, and Dattner considers it probable that the unconscious wish of the Hungarians who drew up the agreement to allow Austria as few advantages as possible had something to do with this omission.

18）当然，书面遗漏可以像笔误一样进行评估。在《精神分析中心期刊》（Zentralblatt für Psychoanalyse）第一卷第12期中，法学博士B. Dattner报告了一个有趣的“历史性疏漏”案例。在1867年奥匈两国就财政义务达成的协议中，其中一项法律条款的匈牙利语译文中遗漏了“生效”一词。Dattner认为，匈牙利人在起草协议时，很可能是出于无意识的意愿，希望尽可能减少奥地利的利益，才导致了这一遗漏。

There is also every reason to suppose that frequent repetitions of the same word in writing and copying — perseverations — are not without their significance either. If the writer repeats a word he has already written a second time, he is probably showing that he cannot shake it off so easily, that he could have said more on this point but has refrained, or something of that nature. Perseveration in copying seems to be a substitute for saying: ‘Hear, hear!’ I have seen long forensic reports with perseverations added by the copyist in particularly outstanding passages, and I could well have imagined, in interpreting them, that he was tiring of his impersonal role and adding a gloss: ‘My own case entirely’, or: ‘Yes, I feel just the same’.

我们完全有理由认为，在写作和抄写中频繁重复同一个词——即重复使用——也并非毫无意义。如果作者第二次重复使用一个已经写过的词，他很可能是在表明自己无法轻易摆脱它，表明他本可以就此多说一些，但却克制住了，或者诸如此类。抄写中的重复使用似乎是一种表达“说得好！”的替代方式。我见过一些篇幅很长的法庭报告，其中抄写员在一些特别精彩的段落中添加了重复使用，在解读这些重复使用时，我完全可以想象，他是厌倦了自己客观的角色，于是添加了一句注释：“完全是我自己的情况”，或者：“是的，我也有同感”。

19) Furthermore, there is nothing to prevent us from treating a misprint as a ‘slip of the pen’ on the part of the typesetter, and regarding it as having some considerable motivation. I have not made a systematic collection of misprints, although something along those lines could be very amusing and informative. Jones has devoted a special paragraph to the misprint in his work (mentioned here several times). The distorted words in telegrams can also sometimes be taken as ‘slips of the pen’ on the part of the telegraphist. In the summer holidays I received a telegram from my publisher, and could make nothing of it. The text ran:

19）此外，我们完全可以将印刷错误视为排字工的“笔误”，并认为其背后可能存在某种深意。我并没有系统地收集印刷错误，尽管这样做或许会非常有趣且富有启发性。琼斯在他的著作中专门用一个段落讨论了印刷错误（此处曾多次提及）。电报中的文字歪曲有时也可以被视为电报员的“笔误”。暑假期间，我收到出版商的一封电报，却完全摸不着头脑。电报内容如下：

’Vorräte [provisions] received, Einladung [invitation] to X. urgent.’ The solution to the puzzle comes from the name of the X. mentioned in the telegram. X. is an author for whose book I was to write an introduction [ Einleitung ]. The Einleitung had become an Einladung. Next I had to remind myself that a few days earlier I had sent the publisher a foreword [ Vorrede ] to another book, and the telegram was confirming its safe arrival. The correct text very probably read: Vorrede erhalten, Einleitung X. dringend [Foreword arrived, introduction to X. urgent]. We may assume that it fell victim to reworking by a hunger complex on the telegraphist’s part, making a closer connection between the two halves of the message than the sender of the telegram intended. This, incidentally, is a fine example of ‘secondary reworking’ of the kind evident in most dreams. 7

“Vorräte [物资] 已收到，Einladung [邀请] 紧急。” 谜题的答案就在于电报中提到的 X 的名字。X 是一位作家，我原本要为他的一本书写序 [Einleitung]。序变成了邀请。接下来，我不得不提醒自己，几天前我给出版社寄了另一本书的前言 [Vorrede]，而电报确认它已安全送达。正确的文本很可能是：Vorrede erhalten, Einleitung X. dringend [前言已收到，X 的引言紧急]。我们可以推测，这是电报员饥饿心理作祟，将信息的前后两部分联系得比电报发送者的本意更紧密了。顺便一提，这正是梦境中常见的“二次加工”的绝佳例子。

H. Silberer, in the Internationale Zeitschrift für Psychoanalyse VIII, 1922, mentions the possibility of ‘tendentious misprints’. And some misprints that it can hardly be denied are tendentious have been pointed out by other people, for instance by Storfer in the Zentralblatt für Psychoanalyse II, 1914: ‘The Political Misprinter’s Devil’, also in ibid. HI, 1915, a brief note which I reproduce here:

H. Silberer 在 1922 年出版的《国际精神分析杂志》第八卷中提到了“带有倾向性的印刷错误”的可能性。其他人也指出了一些几乎无法否认带有倾向性的印刷错误，例如 Storfer 在 1914 年出版的《精神分析中心杂志》第二卷中发表的《政治印刷错误的魔鬼》（也见于 1915 年的《国际精神分析杂志》第一卷），以下是一篇简短的评论，我在此摘录如下：

20) ‘There is a political misprint in the number of März for 25 April this year. A letter from Argyrokastron reported the remarks of Zographos, leader of the Epirote rebels in Albania, or if you prefer it President of the Independent Government of the Epirus. Among other things he is reported as saying: “Believe me, an autonomous Epirus would be very much in Prince Wied’s interests. He could stürzen [fall] on it…” Very likely the Prince of Albania was well aware that accepting the Stütze [support] offered by the Epirotes would mean his Stürz [fall], even without that ominous misprint.’

20）“今年4月25日的《März》杂志刊登了一则政治错误。阿尔吉罗卡斯特龙的一封信中报道了阿尔巴尼亚境内伊庇鲁斯叛军领袖佐格拉福斯（或称伊庇鲁斯独立政府总统）的言论。据报道，他曾说过：“相信我，一个自治的伊庇鲁斯对维德王子来说非常有利。他可能会因此而垮台……” 很可能，即使没有这则不祥的错误，这位阿尔巴尼亚王子也很清楚，接受伊庇鲁斯人的支持就意味着他的垮台。

21) I myself recently read in one of our Viennese daily papers an article on The Bukovina Region under Romanian Rule’, a headline that must be regarded as premature at the very least, since at the time the Romanians had not yet acknowledged their hostility to us. The content showed that the headline should have read not Romanian but Russian , but even the censor seems to have found the general idea so likely that he himself overlooked this misprint.

21）我最近在维也纳的一份日报上读到一篇题为“罗马尼亚统治下的布科维纳地区”的文章，这个标题至少可以说是不合时宜的，因为当时罗马尼亚人还没有公开承认他们对我们的敌意。文章内容表明，标题应该用俄语而不是罗马尼亚语，但就连审查员似乎也觉得文章的整体意思合情合理，以至于忽略了这个印刷错误。

It is difficult not to think of a ‘political’ misprint in reading the following spelling mistake in the circular issued by the famous printing works of Karl Prochaska in Teschen (formerly the Imperial and Royal Austro-Hungarian printers):

读到卡尔·普罗查斯卡在特申（Teschen）的著名印刷厂（前身为奥匈帝国皇家印刷厂）发布的通告中的以下拼写错误，很难不联想到“政治”方面的错误：

‘By order of the Entente, pleno titulo , it is declared that the River Olsa is the frontier, dividing not only Silesia but also Teschen into two, one half of which [ zuviel , ‘too much’, in error for zufiel , ‘fell to’] went to Poland, the other to Czechoslovakia.’

“根据协约国的命令，宣布奥尔萨河为边界，不仅将西里西亚一分为二，还将特申一分为二，其中一半归波兰，另一半归捷克斯洛伐克。”

Theodor Fontane once, and amusingly, had to defend himself against an only too meaningful misprint. On 29 March 1860 he wrote to the publisher Julius Springer: 8

西奥多·冯塔纳曾有一次颇为滑稽的经历，他不得不为自己辩护，因为一个印刷错误意义重大。1860年3月29日，他写信给出版商尤利乌斯·施普林格： 8

Dear Sir

尊敬的先生

It seems that my modest wishes are not to be granted. A glance at the proofs I enclose will show you what I mean. Moreover, I was sent only one set of proofs, although for the reasons I have given you I need two. And you have not yet sent back the first set for me to look through it again — for the sake of the English words and phrases. I am extremely anxious to do so. On page 27 , for instance, in a scene between John Knox and the Queen of Scots, the present proof has the phrase ‘ worauf Maria aasrief ’ [‘whereupon Mary cried ‘Carrion!’, in error for ausrief ‘cried out’]. In view of such brilliant notions one would like to be sure that the error really has been corrected. The unfortunate aas for aus is all the worse in that there is no doubt she (the Queen) really must have called him names of that nature in her mind. With kind regards.

看来我的小小愿望恐怕难以实现。您只需瞥一眼我随信附上的校样，便能明白我的意思。此外，我只收到了一份校样，但正如我之前所述，我需要两份。而且您至今仍未将第一份校样寄回给我，让我再仔细审阅一遍——尤其是为了校对其中的英文词汇和短语。我非常渴望这样做。例如，在第27页，约翰·诺克斯与苏格兰女王的对话场景中，这份校样中出现了“worauf Maria aasrief”（玛丽随即喊道“腐肉！”，误写为ausrief，意为“喊叫”）。鉴于如此精彩的构思，我们当然希望确认这个错误确实已被纠正。更糟糕的是，将aus误写成了aas，因为毫无疑问，女王当时肯定在心里真的骂过他。谨致问候。

Yours sincerely,

此致，

Theodor Fontane.

西奥多·冯塔纳。

Wundt gives an interesting reason for the readily confirmed fact that we find it easier to commit slips of the pen than slips of the tongue (op. cit, p. 374). ‘In normal speech the inhibitory function of the will is constantly operating to reconcile the workings of the imagination with the process of articulation. If the movement of expression following on from ideas is slowed by mechanical causes, as in writing […] such anticipations will be especially likely to occur.’

冯特对一个显而易见的现象给出了一个有趣的解释，即我们更容易出现笔误而非口误（同上，第374页）。“在正常的言语中，意志的抑制功能不断运作，以协调想象的运作与表达过程。如果由于机械原因（例如写作）导致表达过程减缓，那么这种预期就更容易发生。”

Observation of the conditions in which mistakes in reading are made suggests a doubt which I would not like to leave unmentioned, since I believe that it can be the point of departure for a fruitful investigation. Everyone knows how often, when someone is reading aloud, the reader’s attention wanders away from the text and turns to his own thoughts. Quite often, and because of this inattention, he cannot say anything about the content of the text if he is interrupted and asked what it was. He has been reading almost automatically, but nearly always correctly. I do not believe that mistakes in reading are noticeably greater in such conditions. We are used to assuming that a whole series of other functions is meticulously but automatically performed, and little conscious attention is paid to them. It would seem to follow that whether or not one’s attention is alerted must, in the case of slips of the tongue, reading and writing, be determined in some way other than Wundt’s idea of the cessation or neglect of attention. The examples subjected to analysis have not really allowed the assumption of a quantitative decrease in attention; what we found, and it may not be quite the same thing, was the disruption of attention by another thought that emerged and claimed it.

观察阅读错误发生的条件，会引出一个疑问，我不想对此视而不见，因为我相信这可以成为一个富有成效的研究的出发点。每个人都知道，当有人朗读时，读者的注意力常常会从文本上游离，转向自己的想法。很多时候，正是由于这种注意力不集中，如果有人打断他并问他文本的内容是什么，他却答不上来。他几乎是在自动地朗读，但几乎总是正确的。我不认为在这种情况下，阅读错误会明显增多。我们习惯于认为一系列其他功能都是一丝不苟地自动完成的，人们很少会对此有意识地关注。由此看来，在口误、阅读和写作中，一个人的注意力是否被调动，必然是由某种不同于冯特关于注意力停止或忽视的观点所决定的。所分析的例子实际上并没有支持注意力数量减少的假设；我们发现的（可能并不完全相同）是注意力被另一个出现并占据的想法所干扰。

Neglecting to add a signature should come somewhere between slips of the pen and ordinary forgetfulness. An unsigned cheque means a forgotten cheque. To illustrate the significance of such an omission I will cite a passage in a novel, which caught the attention of Dr H. Sachs:

漏签支票的情况介于笔误和普通遗忘之间。未签名的支票意味着被遗忘的支票。为了说明这种疏忽的严重性，我将引用一部小说中的一段话，这段话引起了H·萨克斯博士的注意：

‘There is a very clear and informative example of the creative writer’s sure touch in dealing with the psychoanalytic handling of slips and symptomatic actions in a novel by John Galsworthy, The Island Pharisees. The plot turns on the hesitation of a young man, a member of the rich bourgeoisie, between deep social sympathy and the conventions of his own class of society. Chapter XXVI describes his reaction to a letter from a young vagabond to whom he had given aid several times in the past, feeling drawn to his unconventional way of life. The young man’s letter does not contain any direct request for money, but describes a situation of great need which allows no other interpretation. At first its recipient rejects the idea of throwing money away on someone so incorrigible, rather than supporting charitable institutions.

约翰·高尔斯华绥的小说《岛上的法利赛人》中，有一个非常清晰且信息丰富的例子，展现了这位作家在处理精神分析中对口误和症状性行为的精准把握。故事围绕着一位富裕资产阶级青年展开，他内心深处既有对社会的同情，又受到自身阶级习俗的束缚。第二十六章描述了他收到一位年轻流浪汉的来信后的反应。这位流浪汉曾多次得到他的帮助，他被其特立独行的生活方式所吸引。年轻人的信中并没有直接索要钱财，而是描述了一种极度需要帮助的处境，让人无法做出其他解读。起初，收信人拒绝将钱财浪费在这样一个无可救药的人身上，而是选择支持慈善机构。

‘To give a helping hand, a bit of himself, a nod of fellowship to any fellow being irrespective of a claim, merely because he happened to be down, was sentimental nonsense! The line must be drawn! But in the muttering of this conclusion he experienced a twinge of honesty. “Humbug! You don’t want to part with your money, that’s all!”

“不顾一切地伸出援手，哪怕只是因为对方碰巧落魄，就给予帮助、付出一点心意、表示同情，这简直是多愁善感的胡闹！必须划清界限！” 但就在他喃喃自语得出这个结论的同时，他却感到一丝诚实。“胡说！你只是不想掏钱而已！”

‘Thereupon he wrote a friendly letter, ending with the words: “I enclose a cheque. Yours sincerely, Richard Shelton.”

于是他写了一封友好的信，结尾写道：“随信附上一张支票。此致，理查德·谢尔顿。”

‘Before he had written out the cheque, a moth fluttering round the candle distracted his attention, and by the time he had caught and put it out he had forgotten that the cheque was not enclosed.’

“在他写支票之前，一只飞蛾在蜡烛周围飞来飞去，分散了他的注意力，等他抓住飞蛾把它扑灭时，他已经忘记支票还没附上。”

And the letter is sent off just as it stands. Its writer’s forgetfulness, however, is more subtly motivated even than in the way in which his selfish wish to spare himself expense, although apparently overcome, finally wins the day.

信件就这样原封不动地寄了出去。然而，写信人的健忘背后，隐藏着比他自私地节省开支这一动机更为微妙的动机——尽管这种自私的动机表面上被克服了，但最终还是占了上风。

Staying at the country house of his future parents-in-law, with his fiancée, her family and their guests, Shelton feels lonely; his slip tells us that he misses his protégé, whose past history and attitude to life make him a complete contrast to Shelton’s present blameless company, all of them the products of one and the same convention. As it turns out, his correspondent, who cannot remain in his post any longer without support, arrives a few days later to find out why the cheque promised in the letter never arrived.’

谢尔顿和他的未婚妻、她的家人以及他们的客人一起住在未来岳父母的乡间别墅里，感到十分孤独；他的便条表明他想念他的门生，门生的过往经历和人生态度与谢尔顿现在身边这些无可指摘的人形成了鲜明的对比，而他们都是同一种习俗的产物。几天后，他的通信对象——因为没有资助而无法继续留任——前来询问信中承诺的支票为何迟迟未到。

笔记

# ↩

VII

第七章

Forgetting Impressions and Intentions

遗忘印象和意图

Should anyone feel inclined to overestimate the present state of our knowledge of the life of the mind, one need only mention the function of memory to induce a sense of humility. No psychological theory has yet succeeded in giving a full account of the basic phenomena of remembering and forgetting. Indeed, overall analysis of what can in fact be observed has hardly begun. Perhaps we find forgetfulness more of a riddle than memory today, now that the study of dreams and of pathological cases has shown that something we thought long forgotten can suddenly surface in the memory again.

如果有人倾向于高估我们目前对心灵生活的了解程度，只需提及记忆的功能，便足以令人感到谦卑。迄今为止，没有任何心理学理论能够对记忆和遗忘的基本现象做出全面的解释。事实上，对实际可观察现象的全面分析几乎还未开始。或许，如今我们发现遗忘比记忆更像一个谜，因为对梦境和病理案例的研究表明，我们以为早已遗忘的事物可能会突然再次浮现于记忆之中。

However, we are now in possession of a few insights which may be expected to be generally acknowledged. We assume that forgetting is a spontaneous process involving a certain lapse of time. We emphasize the fact that when something is forgotten, a kind of selection is made from among the available impressions, and that the same thing happens with the details of any impression or experience. We know some of the conditions for the tenacity of certain memories and for the possibility of retrieving a memory that would otherwise be forgotten. However, countless occasions in everyday life show how incomplete and unsatisfactory our knowledge of the subject is. One has only to listen to two people who have received external impressions together, for instance on a journey in each other’s company, and who are exchanging memories some time later. An incident that has lodged firmly in the mind of one of them has often been forgotten by the other as completely as if it had never been, even when there is no reason to claim that the impression was any more psychically significant for one than the other. A considerable number of the factors determining what the memory selects obviously still elude our understanding.

然而，我们现在掌握了一些可以预见会被普遍认可的见解。我们假设遗忘是一个自发的过程，需要一定的时间流逝。我们强调，当某件事被遗忘时，人们会从现有的印象中进行某种选择，任何印象或经历的细节都会经历同样的过程。我们了解某些记忆得以保留以及能够找回原本会被遗忘的记忆的一些条件。然而，日常生活中无数的例子表明，我们对这一主题的了解是多么的不完整和不足。只需听听两个曾经一起接受过外部印象的人（例如，在旅途中结伴而行）的对话，他们之后会交流彼此的记忆。其中一人牢牢记住的某件事，往往会被另一人彻底遗忘，仿佛从未发生过一样，即使没有任何理由表明该印象对其中一人比另一人具有更重要的心理意义。显然，决定记忆选择内容的许多因素仍然让我们难以理解。

With the intention of making a small contribution to our knowledge of the causes of forgetfulness, I am in the habit of subjecting my own instances of forgetting to psychological analysis. As a rule I study only a certain group of these cases, those in which I am surprised to find I have forgotten something because I would have expected to know it. I will just add that I am not inclined to forgetfulness in general (I mean to forgetting experiences, not to forgetting something I have learnt!), and I was capable of unusual feats of memory for a short time in my youth. When I was a schoolboy I thought it quite natural that when I had read a page of a book I could recite its contents by heart, and shortly before going to university I was able to write down popular lectures on scientific subjects almost word for word directly after hearing them. I must still have been using what remained of that ability during the stressful period before my last oral examination for my doctorate of medicine, since I almost automatically gave the examiners answers in some subjects faithfully echoing the text of a book that I had once leafed through in great haste.

为了对遗忘的原因略尽绵薄之力，我习惯于对自己的遗忘经历进行心理分析。通常，我只研究其中一部分案例，即那些我惊讶地发现自己忘记了某些本应记得的事情。需要补充的是，我并非天生健忘（我指的是遗忘经历，而非遗忘所学知识！），而且年轻时曾短暂地拥有过非凡的记忆力。学生时代，我读过一页书就能背诵其内容，这对我来说是再自然不过的事情了。在即将进入大学之前，我甚至能在听完科普讲座后几乎一字不差地将其记录下来。在医学博士最后一次口试前那段紧张的日子里，我大概还在运用着这种能力，因为在某些科目上，我几乎是下意识地向考官复述了一遍我曾经匆匆翻阅过的一本书的内容。

Since then my ability to gain access to what is stored in my memory has deteriorated, but until quite recently I have been able to convince myself that with the aid of a certain trick I can remember far more than I would otherwise have thought I could. For instance, if a patient in my consulting rooms mentions that I have seen him before, and I cannot remember when, or indeed recollect meeting him at all, I try guessing, that is to say, thinking quickly of a number of years running from the present backwards. Where written notes or the patient’s own certainty make it possible for me to check my ideas, it turns out that I am seldom wrong by more than six months within a period of over ten years. 1 It is much the same when I meet someone I do not know particularly well, and for the sake of politeness I ask how his small children are. If he tells me about their progress then I try to work out how old the child is now, check that age against what the father says, and I am wrong by a month at the most, or three months with older children, although I cannot say what points of reference I used for making my estimate. Recently I have felt bold enough to bring out my guess spontaneously, so as to run no risk of hurting the father’s feelings by revealing my ignorance of his offspring. In this way I extend my conscious recollections by calling on my unconscious memory, which in any case contains far more material.

从那时起，我提取记忆的能力就逐渐下降，但直到最近，我还能说服自己，借助某种技巧，我可以记住比我想象中多得多的事情。例如，如果诊室里的病人说我以前见过他，而我却想不起来是什么时候，甚至完全不记得见过他，我就会试着猜测，也就是从现在往前快速回忆几年。如果病人有书面记录或者他自己也确信无疑，我可以核实我的想法，结果发现，在十多年的时间跨度内，我的误差很少超过六个月。 1 遇到不太熟悉的人时，出于礼貌，我也会问他的孩子怎么样，情况也大致相同。如果他告诉我孩子的近况，我就会试着估算孩子现在的年龄，再和孩子父亲的说法核对，最多也就差一个月，大一点的孩子可能会差三个月，虽然我记不清当时是根据什么来估算的。最近，我胆子大了些，开始不经意地说出自己的猜测，这样就不会因为暴露自己对孩子的情况不了解而伤了孩子的心。这样一来，我便能通过调用潜意识记忆来拓展自己的认知，而潜意识记忆里本来就蕴藏着更丰富的信息。

I will therefore give an account of striking examples of forgetfulness, most of them observed in myself. I distinguish the forgetting of impressions and experiences, that is to say things I have seen or done, from the forgetting of intentions, that is to say, omitting to do something. I will begin by stating the uniform result of a whole series of observations: in all cases the motive for forgetting something proved to be based on aversion.

因此，我将列举一些令人震惊的健忘例子，其中大部分是我亲身经历的。我区分了对印象和经验的遗忘（即忘记我所见所闻或所做之事）与对意图的遗忘（即疏忽去做某事）。首先，我将阐述一系列观察得出的一致结论：在所有情况下，遗忘的动机都源于厌恶。

A) Forgetting impressions and knowledge

A) 遗忘印象和知识

1) One summer my wife made me very cross, although the reason was harmless in itself. We were sitting at the table d’hôte opposite a gentleman from Vienna whom I knew, and who obviously remembered me too. However, I had my own reasons for not reviving our acquaintance. My wife, who had heard only the well-known name of the man opposite, made it too obvious that she was listening to what he said to his neighbours at table, for she turned to me from time to time with questions referring to the theme of their conversation. I grew impatient and finally short-tempered. A few weeks later, I was complaining to a woman relative about my wife’s conduct, but I could not remember a single word the man had said. As I am usually rather inclined to bear a grudge, and do not forget any of the details of an incident that has annoyed me, my amnesia in this case was probably motivated by consideration for my wife. A similar thing happened to me only recently. I was going to invite a close friend to laugh at something my wife had said just a few hours earlier, but found that I could not put this intention into practice because, remarkably, I had completely forgotten what it was. I had to ask my wife herself to remind me.
