It is easy to see that this forgetfulness of mine should be regarded as analogous to the typical disruption of the powers of judgement we encounter in dealing with members of our immediate family.

1）有一年夏天，我妻子惹我生气，虽然事情本身并无恶意。我们坐在餐桌旁，对面是一位来自维也纳的绅士，我认识他，他显然也记得我。然而，我却有自己的理由不想重提旧谊。我妻子只听说过对面那位男士的名号，却表现得过于明显地在偷听他和邻桌的谈话，时不时地转向我，询问一些与他们谈话内容相关的问题。我渐渐变得不耐烦，最终发了脾气。几周后，我向一位女性亲戚抱怨妻子的行为，却发现自己完全记不起那位男士说过什么。我通常比较记仇，而且一旦惹恼了我，就很难忘记任何细节，所以这次我的失忆大概是出于对妻子的顾虑。不久前，我也遇到过类似的事情。我原本打算邀请一位好友一起嘲笑我妻子几个小时前说过的一句话，却发现自己根本无法实现这个计划，因为我竟然完全忘记了她说的是什么。我只好请妻子提醒我。不难看出，我的这种健忘症与我们在与家人相处时经常遇到的判断力下降的情况非常相似。

2) A lady who had just arrived in Vienna and did not know the city wanted a small iron safe in which she could keep documents and money, and I had said I would get her one. When I made this offer the unusually vivid image of a shop window in the inner city where I must have seen such safes came before my mind’s eye. I could not remember the name of the street, but I felt sure I would find the shop on a walk through Vienna, since my memory told me I had passed it countless times. To my annoyance, however, and although I combed the inner city, I could not find the shop with safes on display. There was nothing for it, I thought, but to get the names of manufacturers of safes from the addresses in a trade directory, and then go round the area again to identify the shop window I was looking for. However, there was no need for all that; among the addresses listed was one that I could instantly identify as the shop I had forgotten. It was true that I had passed the display window countless times — every time I visited the M. family, who had lived in the same building for years. But now that we were no longer close friends, and indeed were not on good terms at all, I was in the habit of avoiding both the area and the building without stopping to wonder why. On that walk of mine through the city in search of the display of safes I had gone down every other street in the area, avoiding only this single one as if it were forbidden. The aversion motivating my poor sense of direction in this case was palpably obvious. The mechanism whereby I forgot, however, was less simple than in the first example. My dislike was not, of course, for the safes manufacturer, but for someone else whom I did not want to think about, and it transferred itself from that other person to the present occasion, causing me to forget. In exactly the same way, as in the Burckhard case, my resentment of one person had caused a slip of the pen in the name of another. The effect of their identical names in that case, linking two essentially different trains of thought, had its parallel in spatial contiguity and indissoluble proximity in the example of the display window. In fact this latter case had a firmer factual basis; there was a second link, one of content, since money had played some part in the reasons for my estrangement from the family living in that building.

2）一位刚到维也纳、对这座城市不熟悉的女士想要一个小型铁制保险箱，用来存放文件和现金。我答应帮她找一个。当我提出这个提议时，脑海中突然浮现出一幅异常清晰的画面：在市中心，我肯定见过一家商店橱窗里摆放着类似的保险箱。我记不起那条街的名字，但我确信在维也纳漫步时一定能找到它，因为我的记忆告诉我，我曾无数次路过那里。然而，令我懊恼的是，尽管我把市中心都找遍了，却始终找不到那家展示保险箱的商店。我想，看来别无他法了，只能从商业名录上找到保险箱制造商的地址，然后再去附近转一圈，看看能不能找到我要找的那家店。然而，这一切都是多余的；在列出的地址中，我一眼就认出了那家我忘记的商店。的确，我曾无数次路过那个橱窗——每次我去拜访M一家时都会路过，他们已经在同一栋楼里住了好几年了。但现在我们不再是亲密的朋友，事实上关系非常糟糕，我养成了刻意避开那个区域和那栋建筑的习惯，却从未停下来思考过原因。那天我穿过城市寻找保险箱展示柜，几乎走过了附近所有的街道，唯独避开了这条街，仿佛它是一条禁区。在这种情况下，我方向感差的原因显而易见，那就是对它的厌恶。然而，我忘记这件事的机制却比第一个例子要复杂得多。当然，我厌恶的并非保险箱制造商，而是另一个我不想去想的人，这种厌恶感从那个人转移到了眼前的这件事上，导致我忘记了。就像在布克哈德的案例中一样，我对一个人的怨恨导致我记错了另一个人的名字。在那个案例中，他们的名字相同，将两种截然不同的思路联系起来，而在这个展示柜的例子中，空间上的相邻和不可分割的接近性也起到了类似的作用。事实上，后一种情况有更坚实的事实基础；还有第二个联系，即实质联系，因为金钱在我与住在那栋楼里的家庭疏远的原因中起到了一定的作用。

3) I was called in by the firm of B. & R. to give medical advice to one of its employees. On the way to his home I was preoccupied by the idea that I must have been in the building where the firm had its offices many times before. I felt that I had noticed the nameplate on a lower floor while I was visiting a patient on a floor higher in the same building, but I could remember neither what the building was nor whom I had been visiting there. Although the whole thing was trivial and unimportant, I could not get it out of my mind, and finally, trying to take my usual long and circuitous route around the subject by assembling my ideas on it, I worked out that the Pension Fischer, where I have frequently visited patients, is one floor above the offices of the firm of B. & R. I now knew which building accommodated both the firm’s offices and the boarding house, but I still could not think why I had forgotten. I could discover nothing repellent in my memory about the firm itself, or the Pension Fischer, or my patients who lodged there. I suspected that it could not be anything very unpleasant, or I would have been unable to recollect what I had forgotten simply by thinking round the subject without, as in the previous case, calling on other aids. It finally occurred to me that only just now, on my way to visit my new patient, a man had spoken to me in the street, and I had found it quite difficult to recognize him. Months before I had seen this man in what looked like a very serious condition, and had diagnosed progressive paralysis, but then I heard that he had recovered, so my diagnosis was wrong. Or perhaps he was in one of those remissions that do occur in dementia paralytica , in which case I would have been right after all! It was this encounter that had affected my memory of the neighbourhood of the offices of B. & R., and my interest in finding out what I had forgotten had been transferred from that case of a doubtful diagnosis. The link associating the two, although slight in terms of content — the man who had recovered contrary to my expectations was also an employee of a large firm which used to send me patients — was another instance of an identical name. The doctor who had been with me when I saw the possibly paralytic patient was called Fischer, like the forgotten name of the boarding house in the same building as the B. & R. offices.

3）B. & R.公司请我去给他们的一位员工提供医疗建议。去他家的路上，我一直想着我以前肯定去过这家公司所在的办公楼很多次。我感觉我曾经在同一栋楼的较高楼层探望病人时，注意到过较低楼层的门牌，但我既想不起来是哪栋楼，也想不起来当时是去探望谁。虽然这件事微不足道，但我却一直耿耿于怀。最后，我像往常一样绕了好大弯，试图理清思路，终于想起来我经常去探望病人的费舍尔疗养院就在B. & R.公司办公楼的楼上。现在我知道哪栋楼既是公司的办公室又是疗养院了，但我还是想不明白自己为什么会忘记。我努力回忆，却找不到任何关于这家公司、费舍尔养老院，或是住在那里的病人的令人反感之处。我怀疑这不可能是什么特别糟糕的事情，否则我不可能像上次那样，仅仅靠思考就能想起我遗忘的内容，而需要借助其他线索。最后我突然想起，就在刚才，我去探望新病人的路上，有个男人在街上跟我说话，我当时很难认出他。几个月前，我见过这个人，当时他的病情看起来非常严重，我诊断他患有进行性麻痹，但后来听说他已经康复了，所以我的诊断是错误的。或许他正处于麻痹性痴呆症的缓解期，如果是这样，那我的诊断就完全正确了！正是这次偶遇影响了我对B.&R.公司附近环境的记忆，而我对遗忘内容的兴趣也从那个疑点重重的病例转移到了这件事上。两人之间的联系虽然在内容上微弱——那位出乎我意料康复的病人也是一家大型公司的员工，而这家公司过去常常给我转诊病人——但却是另一个同名的例子。我当时陪同那位可能瘫痪的病人就叫费舍尔，和B&R公司办公室所在大楼里那家早已被人遗忘的寄宿公寓同名。

4) Mislaying something means simply forgetting where you have put it down, and like most people who have a great deal to do with written papers and books, I know what is where on my desk, and can lay my hands on anything I want. What looks like disorder to other people is, to me, order of what is eventually a historical nature. But why did I recently mislay so completely a catalogue of books which had been sent to me that it simply could not be found? I had intended to order a book advertised in it, Über die Sprache [ On Language ], because it was by an author whose lively, amusing style I like and whose knowledge of cultural history and psychological insights I admire. I believe that was the very reason why I mislaid the catalogue. In the usual way, I lend this author’s books to my acquaintances for their information, and a few days ago someone returning me a book said: ‘His style reminds me very much of yours, and he thinks in the same way too.’ The speaker did not know what an effect this remark would have on me. Years ago, when I was younger and needed to establish good contacts, an older colleague to whom I had praised the writings of a well-known medical author said much the same to me. ‘Yes, just your style, very much in your own line.’ I was encouraged by this to write to the medical author suggesting we might become acquainted, but was put in my place by a cool reply. And perhaps there were also other and even earlier deterrent experiences behind this one, for I never did find the mislaid catalogue, and was probably prevented by this ominous sign from ordering the advertised book, although the disappearance of the catalogue did not really put any difficulty in my way, since the name of the book and its author were lodged in my memory. 2

4）遗失某物仅仅意味着忘记把它放在哪里了。像大多数经常与书面文件和书籍打交道的人一样，我知道桌上每样东西放在哪里，也总能找到我需要的任何东西。在别人看来是杂乱无章的东西，在我看来却是井然有序的，最终具有历史意义。但是，为什么我最近会把别人寄给我的书籍目录弄得如此彻底，以至于怎么也找不到呢？我原本打算订购目录中推荐的一本书——《论语言》（Über die Sprache），因为我喜欢这位作者生动风趣的文风，也欣赏他对文化史和心理学的深刻见解。我相信，这正是我弄丢目录的原因。我像往常一样把这位作者的书借给熟人参考。几天前，有人还书时说：“他的文风让我想起了你，而且他的思路也和你很像。” 说话的人并不知道这句话会对我产生怎样的影响。多年前，我年轻的时候，为了拓展人脉，曾向一位年长的同事推荐过一位知名医学作家的作品，他也对我说了类似的话：“没错，就是你的风格，很有你自己的特点。” 这句话激励我给那位医学作家写信，提议我们或许可以认识一下，但却收到了一封冷冰冰的回信，让我顿时感到措手不及。或许在此之前还有其他更早的阻碍性经历，因为我始终没能找到那份遗失的目录，可能正是这个不祥的预兆阻止了我订购广告上的那本书。尽管目录的丢失并没有真正给我造成任何困难，因为书名和作者都深深地印在我的脑海里。

5) Another case of mislaying something deserves our attention because of the circumstances in which the mislaid item was found again. A young man told me: ‘A few years ago there were some misunderstandings in my marriage. I felt my wife was too cool, and although I was very ready to acknowledge her excellent qualities we lived together without any tenderness between us. One day she came home from a walk bringing me a book that she had bought, thinking it might interest me. I thanked her for this kind attention, promised to read the book, put it somewhere and couldn’t find it again. Months passed by, and now and then I thought of the missing book and tried in vain to find it. About six months later my beloved mother, who did not live with us, fell ill. My wife left our home to care for her mother-in-law. The invalid’s condition became serious, and gave my wife an opportunity of showing herself in her best light. One evening I came home, feeling great admiration and gratitude for what my wife had done. I went to my desk, opened a certain drawer in it without any particular intention, but with a sleepwalker’s unerring sense of direction, and at the top of the drawer I found the book that had been missing so long.’

5）另一个遗失物品的案例值得我们关注，因为失物被找回的情况比较特殊。一位年轻人告诉我：“几年前，我的婚姻出现了一些误会。我觉得妻子太冷淡，虽然我非常认可她的优点，但我们之间却缺乏温情。有一天，她散步回来，带回了一本她买的书，觉得我可能会感兴趣。我感谢她的这份心意，答应她会读这本书，然后把它放在某个地方，之后就再也找不到了。几个月过去了，我不时会想起那本书，也一直试图找到它，但都无果。大约六个月后，我亲爱的母亲（她不和我们住在一起）生病了。妻子离开家去照顾婆婆。婆婆的病情越来越严重，这给了妻子一个展现她最好一面的机会。一天晚上，我回到家，对妻子的付出充满了钦佩和感激。”我走到书桌前，漫不经心地打开了一个抽屉，却像梦游者一样拥有精准的方向感，在抽屉最上面，我找到了那本失踪已久的书。

J. Stärcke (op. cit.) gives an account of a case of a mislaid item that greatly resembles this one in its concluding feature: the curious certainty with which the lost item was found.

J. Stärcke（同上）讲述了一个物品丢失的案例，其结尾特征与此案非常相似：丢失的物品被找到的确定性令人匪夷所思。

6) ‘A young girl was going to make a collar, but she had spoiled the fabric in cutting the collar out. A dressmaker had to be called in to put her mistake right. When she had arrived, and the girl went to fetch the collar from the drawer where she thought she had put it away, she couldn’t find it. She turned the drawer right out, but it was nowhere to be found. Feeling annoyed with herself, and wondering why it had suddenly disappeared and whether perhaps the fact was that she didn’t want to find it, she realized that of course she was ashamed to let the dressmaker see that she had spoiled something as simple as a collar. Once that had occurred to her she stood up, went to another cupboard, and produced the cut-out collar at once.’

6) “一个年轻女孩想做个领子，结果裁剪的时候把布料弄坏了。只好请裁缝来帮忙补救。裁缝来了之后，女孩去她以为放领子的抽屉里拿，却怎么也找不到。她把抽屉翻了个底朝天，还是不见踪影。她懊恼不已，心想领子怎么突然不见了，是不是自己故意不想找？后来她才意识到，自己当然不好意思让裁缝看到她把这么简单的东西——领子——弄坏了。想到这里，她立刻站起来，走到另一个橱柜前，马上拿出了裁剪好的领子。”

7) The next example of ‘mislaying’ conforms to a type that is familiar to every psychoanalyst. I should say that the patient who mislaid something in this instance found the key to the puzzle himself:

7）下一个“遗失”的例子符合每位精神分析师都熟悉的类型。我应该说明，在这个例子中，遗失东西的病人自己找到了解开谜题的关键：

‘A patient in psychoanalysis whose treatment was to be interrupted by a summer holiday during a period of resistance, when he was not feeling well, put his key-ring down in the usual place, as he thought, on getting undressed in the evening. Then he remembered that he wanted to fetch a few items from his desk in readiness for his departure next day, which was also the last day of his course of treatment, when the fee for it would be due. He had put the money in the desk as well. But he found that his keys had disappeared. He began searching his small apartment systematically and with increasing agitation, but in vain. Since he recognized that “mislaying” the keys was a symptomatic action, and therefore something he had really done with intent, he woke his manservant so that he would have an impartial person’s help as he went on with his search. After another hour he gave up, fearing he really had lost the keys. Next morning he ordered new keys from the maker of the cashbox on his desk, and they were provided in great haste. Two acquaintances who went home in the cab with him thought they had heard something clink on the ground as he got out, and he felt sure that the keys had fallen out of his pocket. That evening his manservant triumphantly presented him with the original keys. They were tucked between a thick book and a thin pamphlet (a paper by one of my pupils), which he meant to take away to read on holiday, and were so skilfully concealed that no one would have suspected they were there. He found it impossible to replicate the concealment of the keys to make them equally invisible. The unconscious skill with which an item is mislaid as a result of secret but strong motivation is very reminiscent of the sleep-walker’s “unerring sense of direction”. Of course his motives were dislike of the idea of interrupting his treatment, and his secret annoyance at having to pay a high fee when he still felt so unwell.’

一位正在接受精神分析治疗的病人，正值抗拒治疗期间，由于暑假假期即将中断，他身体也不太舒服。晚上脱衣服时，他像往常一样把钥匙串放在他以为放的地方。然后他想起第二天要离开，而第二天也是他疗程的最后一天，也是支付治疗费用的日子，所以他需要从书桌上拿几样东西。他把钱也放在了书桌上。但他发现钥匙不见了。他开始有条不紊地在自己的小公寓里寻找，越来越焦躁不安，但一无所获。他意识到“弄丢”钥匙是一种症状行为，因此实际上是他有意为之，于是他叫醒了男仆，希望在寻找的过程中能得到一个公正的人的帮助。又过了一个小时，他放弃了，担心自己真的把钥匙弄丢了。第二天早上，他向书桌上钱箱的制造商订购了新钥匙，很快就收到了。和他一起乘出租车回家的两个熟人，在他下车时似乎听到地上有东西叮当作响，他确信是钥匙从口袋里掉了出来。那天晚上，他的男仆得意洋洋地把钥匙原件递给了他。钥匙夹在一本厚厚的书和一本薄薄的小册子（我一个学生写的）之间，他打算把小册子带去度假时阅读。钥匙藏得如此巧妙，以至于没人会想到它们的存在。他发现自己根本无法复制这种藏钥匙的方法，让它们同样隐蔽。这种由于某种隐秘而强烈的动机而无意识地丢失物品的技巧，与梦游者“精准的方向感”非常相似。当然，他的动机是不愿中断治疗，以及在身体仍然很不舒服的情况下还要支付高额费用而感到暗自恼火。

8) A man, writes A. A. Brill, was urged by his wife to attend a social occasion in which he took no interest. He finally gave way to her pleas and began taking his evening dress out of the chest where it was kept, but then interrupted himself and decided to shave first. When he had finished shaving he came back to the chest, but it was closed and locked, and the key could not be found. It was impossible to get hold of a locksmith, since it was a Sunday evening, so the couple had to excuse themselves from the party. When the chest was opened next morning, the key was found inside. Absent-mindedly, the man had dropped it into the chest and then closed the lid. He did assure me, says Brill, that he had done so unintentionally and entirely without his own knowledge, but I knew that he did not want to go to the party, so there were reasons for him to mislay the key.

8）A·A·布里尔写道，一位男士在妻子的劝说下，不得不参加一个他毫无兴趣的社交聚会。最终，他还是答应了妻子的请求，开始从存放晚礼服的箱子里取出礼服，但随即停了下来，决定先刮胡子。刮完胡子后，他回到箱子旁，却发现箱子已经关上并上了锁，钥匙也找不到了。由于是星期天晚上，根本联系不上锁匠，这对夫妇只好找借口离开了聚会。第二天早上，箱子被打开时，人们发现钥匙就在里面。原来，这位男士心不在焉地把钥匙丢进了箱子，然后又关上了盖子。布里尔说，他向我保证，这完全是无意的，他自己也毫不知情。但我知道他并不想去参加聚会，所以他弄丢钥匙也是情有可原的。

E. Jones noticed that he always used to mislay his pipe when he had been smoking too much and consequently felt unwell. The pipe would then turn up in all kinds of places where it had no business and where it was never usually kept.

E·琼斯注意到，每当他抽烟抽多了，感到身体不适时，他总是会把烟斗弄丢。然后，烟斗就会出现在各种各样不该出现的地方，那些地方他通常根本不会放烟斗。

9) An innocuous case in which the motivation was admitted has been recorded by Dora Müller:

9) 多拉·穆勒记录了一个动机被承认的无害案例：

Fräulein Erna A. said, two days before Christmas: ‘Guess what — yesterday evening I took out my packet of spiced biscuits and ate some. I thought that when Fräulein S. (her mother’s companion) came in to say good night to me I ought to offer her some, not that I really wanted to, but all the same I decided I would. Later, when she did come in and I put my hand out to my little table to pick up the packet, it wasn’t there. When I looked for it afterwards I found it in my wardrobe. I’d put the packet in there without knowing it.’ There was no need for any analysis; the narrator was clear about the connection herself She had just repressed a wish to keep all the biscuits for herself, but it made itself felt all the same, automatically, although in this case the phenomenon was reversed by her subsequent conscious action.

圣诞节前两天，艾尔娜·A小姐说道：“猜猜怎么着——昨天晚上我拿出那包香料饼干吃了些。我想着等S小姐（她母亲的伴侣）进来跟我道晚安的时候，应该分给她一些，虽然我并不想这么做，但我还是决定这么做。后来，当她进来的时候，我伸手去拿小桌子上的饼干包，却发现它不见了。之后我找了找，才发现它在衣柜里。我竟然不知不觉地把它放进去了。” 无需任何分析；叙述者自己很清楚其中的联系。她刚刚压抑住想要独吞所有饼干的欲望，但这种欲望却不由自主地涌上心头，尽管在这种情况下，她随后的有意识行为逆转了这种现象。

10) H. Sachs describes the way he once mislaid something to avoid having to work. ‘Last Sunday afternoon I was hesitating: should I work, or should I go out for a walk and pay a call? I struggled with myself for a while, but decided to work. After about an hour I noticed that I had run out of paper. I knew I had been keeping a stack of paper somewhere in a drawer for years, but I searched my desk and other places where I thought I might find it in vain, although I went to a great deal of trouble, rummaging everywhere and looking in between old books and pamphlets and so forth. So I felt I had no alternative but to stop work and go out after all. When I came home in the evening I sat down on the sofa, and half in thought, half absent-mindedly, looked at the bookcase opposite. A drawer in it caught my eye, and I remembered that it was a long time since I had examined its contents. I went over and opened it. On top was a leather folder full of blank paper, and only when I had taken it out and was just putting it in the drawer of my desk did I realize that this was the same paper I had been looking for in vain that afternoon. I should add that although I am not thrifty by nature I am very careful about paper, and keep every scrap that can still be used. It was obviously this habit, nurtured by an instinctive drive, that made me remedy my forgetfulness as soon as the present motive for it had gone.’

10）H·萨克斯描述了他为了逃避工作而故意弄丢东西的经历。“上周日下午，我犹豫不决：是该工作，还是该出去散步拜访朋友？我纠结了一会儿，最终决定工作。大约一个小时后，我发现纸用完了。我知道多年来我一直把一叠纸放在某个抽屉里，但我还是在书桌和其他我认为可能找到的地方翻遍了，尽管我费了很大劲，到处翻找，甚至在旧书、小册子等等之间寻找，却一无所获。所以我觉得自己别无选择，只能停下工作出去走走。晚上回家后，我坐在沙发上，半是沉思，半是心不在焉地看着对面的书柜。一个抽屉吸引了我的目光，我这才想起自己很久没看过里面的东西了。于是我走过去，打开了抽屉。”最上面放着一个皮质文件夹，里面装满了空白纸。直到我把它拿出来，正要放进书桌抽屉时，才意识到这正是我下午苦苦寻找却始终找不到的那张纸。我得补充一句，虽然我生性并不节俭，但我对纸张却非常爱惜，每一张还能用的纸片我都会留着。显然，正是这种出于本能的习惯，让我一旦忘记了这件事，就立刻着手弥补。

11) In the summer of 1901 I once told a friend with whom I used to have lively exchanges of scientific ideas at the time that neurotic problems can be solved only if we take it as read that individuals are originally bisexual. He replied: ‘But I told you that myself two and a half years ago in Br., when we were out for an evening walk, and you wouldn’t hear of it at the time.’ It is painful to be required to surrender one’s claim to originality in that way. I could remember no such conversation, nor what my friend had said. One of the two of us was obviously mistaken, and on the principle of who benefits — cui prodest? — it must be me. Over the next week I did in fact remember everything just as my friend had tried to remind me of it. I even remembered what I had replied at the time: ‘No, I can’t agree with you, and I don’t want to get drawn into that line of argument.’ But since then I have become more tolerant if I come upon one of the few ideas with which my name can be linked elsewhere in medical literature, and find that I have been given no credit for it.

11）1901年夏天，我曾对一位当时经常就科学观点进行热烈交流的朋友说，只有当我们默认人天生是双性恋时，神经症问题才能得到解决。他回答说：“但我两年半前在布列塔尼的时候就跟你说过这话，当时我们一起散步，你根本不听。” 被迫以这种方式放弃自己的原创性，真是令人痛苦。我完全不记得有过这样的对话，也不记得我的朋友说过什么。显然，我们俩之中有一个人犯了错，而根据“谁受益”的原则——cui prodest？——受益的肯定是我。接下来的一个星期，我竟然真的把所有事情都记起来了，就像我的朋友试图提醒我的那样。我甚至还记得当时我的回答：“不，我不能同意你的观点，我也不想卷入这场争论。”但从那以后，如果我在医学文献中发现少数几个与我的名字相关的想法之一，却发现我没有因此获得任何赞誉，我就会变得更加宽容。

Criticisms of one’s wife — friendship that has turned to its opposite — a mistake in medical diagnosis — rejection by people working along the same lines — borrowed ideas: it can hardly be coincidence that a number of examples collected at random like this require me to face such painful subjects in order to explain them. I suspect that anyone else trying to examine his own forgetfulness for its motives could draw up a similar sample card of unpleasant ideas. The tendency to forget unpleasantness seems to me general; the ability to do so is probably developed to a different degree in different people. Much of the refusal to acknowledge something that we encounter in the field of medicine may probably be put down to forgetfulness . 3 Our view of such forgetfulness, however, restricts the difference between these behavioural phenomena to purely psychological conditions, allowing us to see the same motive expressed in both ways of reacting. Of all the many examples of the refusal to entertain unpleasant memories that I have seen in relatives of the sick, one remains in my mind as particularly strange. A mother was telling me about the childhood of her nervous son, who was now going through puberty, and said that like his siblings he had wet the bed until quite a late age, something not without significance in a case history of neurosis. A few weeks later, when she wanted to know what stage his treatment had reached, I had occasion to mention the young man’s signs of a constitutional disposition to illness, and referred to the bed-wetting she had mentioned in her account of his medical history. To my surprise she denied that either he or her other children ever used to wet the bed, asked me what made me think I knew that, and I finally said that she herself had told me so quite recently, although now she had forgotten it. 4

对妻子的批评——友谊的反面——医疗诊断的失误——同行的排斥——借用他人的想法：像这样随机收集的例子，需要我面对如此痛苦的话题才能解释，这绝非巧合。我怀疑，任何试图探究自身健忘动机的人，都能列出类似的令人不快的想法清单。在我看来，遗忘不愉快经历的倾向似乎很普遍；不同的人可能在这种能力上发展程度不同。我们在医学领域遇到的许多拒绝承认某些事情的情况，或许都可以归因于健忘。然而，我们对这种健忘的看法，将这些行为现象之间的差异局限于纯粹的心理状态，使我们能够看到相同的动机在两种反应方式中得以体现。在我所见过的众多拒绝回忆不愉快记忆的例子中，有一个例子让我印象尤为奇怪。一位母亲向我讲述了她神经质的儿子的童年经历，他现在正处于青春期。她说，像他的兄弟姐妹一样，他尿床的习惯一直持续到很晚，这在神经症的病史中并非无关紧要。几周后，当她想了解儿子的治疗进展到什么阶段时，我提到了这个年轻人的体质易感疾病，并提到了她在病史中提到的尿床问题。令我惊讶的是，她否认她的儿子或她的其他孩子曾经尿床，并问我为什么会认为我知道这件事。最后，我告诉她，她自己不久前确实告诉过我，只是现在她忘记了。

Healthy people who are not neurotic also display many signs of resisting the memory of painful impressions and the recollection of unwelcome ideas. 5 The full significance of this phenomenon, however, can be assessed only with reference to the psychology of neurotics, when it becomes obvious that such an elementary resistance to ideas that can arouse unpleasant ideas — a resistance comparable only to the flight reflex in reaction to painful stimuli — is to a great degree responsible for the mechanism producing hysterical symptoms. One cannot protest against the acceptance of such a tendency of resistance by claiming that on the contrary, we often enough find it impossible to shake off the painful memories that pursue us and rid ourselves of such unpleasant emotions as remorse and the pangs of conscience. I am not saying that this tendency to resistance will come into effect everywhere, or that in the interplay of psychic forces it may not encounter factors which are working in the opposite direction for purposes of their own, and can defy it. A structure of multiple stratified agencies can be seen as the architectonic principle of the mental apparatus , and it is perfectly likely that the tendency to resistance belongs to a lower psychic agency which can be inhibited by a higher authority. However, it says much for the existence and forcefulness of that tendency when we can derive from it processes such as those in the above examples of forgetfulness. We can then see that a good deal is forgotten for its own sake, and where that is not possible the tendency to resistance shifts its aim and at least causes us to forget something else, something less important but associated with whatever it is that really upsets us.

即使是健康且不神经质的人，也表现出许多抵抗痛苦记忆和不愿想起不愉快想法的迹象。然而，只有结合神经质患者的心理学才能充分评估这一现象的意义。当人们意识到这种对可能引发不愉快想法的基本抵抗——这种抵抗堪比面对痛苦刺激时的逃避反射——在很大程度上是导致癔症症状的机制所在时，这种抵抗就显得尤为重要。我们不能以“恰恰相反，我们常常无法摆脱挥之不去的痛苦记忆，也无法摆脱诸如悔恨和良心谴责等不愉快情绪”为由，来反对接受这种抵抗倾向。我并非认为这种抵抗倾向会无处不在，也并非认为在各种心理力量的相互作用中，它不会遇到出于自身目的而朝着相反方向发展的因素，从而被这些因素所抵消。多层级机构的结构可以被视为心理机制的架构原则，而抵抗倾向很可能属于较低层次的心理机构，并可被较高层次的机构抑制。然而，当我们能够从中推导出诸如上述遗忘例子中的过程时，就足以说明这种倾向的存在及其强大力量。由此可见，很多事情的遗忘本身就是一种目的，而当无法做到这一点时，抵抗倾向就会转移目标，至少会让我们忘记其他一些事情——一些不那么重要，但却与真正困扰我们的事物相关的事情。

The view proposed here, that painful memories are particularly apt to be forgotten for good motives, deserves to be related to several areas in which it has so far received insufficient or no attention. For instance, it seems to me that we still do not look at the idea keenly enough in considering the credibility of evidence in a law-court, 6 where the oath a witness has taken is obviously far too easily credited with exerting a purifying influence on the interplay of psychic forces in his mind. It is generally accepted that one must consider such motives as they affect the rise of racial traditions and legends, eliminating incidents painful to national feeling from the memory. On closer examination the way in which national traditions and the individual’s childhood memories are formed might turn out to be entirely analogous. The great Darwin’s insight into the motive of aversion in causing forgetfulness has become a ‘golden rule’ for scientists. 7

本文提出的观点，即痛苦的记忆尤其容易出于善意而被遗忘，值得与几个迄今为止尚未得到充分或完全关注的领域联系起来。例如，在我看来，我们在法庭上考虑证据的可信度时，仍然没有足够重视这一观点，证人所作的宣誓显然很容易被认为对其内心心理力量的相互作用起到净化作用。人们普遍认为，必须考虑此类动机如何影响种族传统和传说的形成，从而将那些触及民族情感的痛苦事件从记忆中抹去。仔细研究后会发现，民族传统和个人童年记忆的形成方式可能完全相似。伟大的达尔文关于厌恶动机导致遗忘的洞见已成为科学家们的“黄金法则”。

False memories can occur when impressions are forgotten, just as they occur in the forgetting of names, and, in this case, when the person affected believes them, they are described as paramnesia. The phenomenon of false memory in pathological cases — and in paranoia, when it acts as a constituent factor in the patient’s illusions — has given rise to an extensive body of literature, but nowhere do I find any account of its motivation. Since this phenomenon is also part of the psychology of neuroses it is outside the scope of my subject here. Instead, let me describe a curious example of a false memory of my own, obviously motivated by unconsciously repressed material; the way in which the two were linked is also clear enough.

虚假记忆的产生与印象的遗忘类似，就像遗忘名字一样。在这种情况下，如果受影响的人相信这些虚假记忆，就被称为妄想性记忆障碍。病理情况下的虚假记忆现象——以及妄想症中作为患者错觉构成因素之一的虚假记忆现象——已经催生了大量的文献，但我却找不到任何关于其动机的解释。由于这种现象也属于神经症心理学的范畴，因此超出了本文的讨论范围。相反，我想描述一个我自己的奇特虚假记忆案例，它显然是由无意识压抑的内容所驱动的；两者之间的联系也十分清晰。

When I was writing the final sections of my book on the Interpretation of Dreams I was on my summer holiday and had no access to libraries and reference books. I was obliged to insert all references and quotations in my manuscript from memory, intending to check them later. In the section on daydreams I thought of the well-drawn character of the poor bookkeeper in Alphonse Daudet’s Le Nabab , through whom the author was probably describing his own daydreaming. 1 thought I clearly remembered one of the fantasies entertained by this man — I called him Monsieur Jocelyn — on his walks through the streets of Paris, and began describing it from memory. When M. Jocelyn boldly stands in the way of a bolting horse in the street and brings it to a halt, the door of the carriage opens, a distinguished personage gets out, presses M. Jocelyn’s hand, and says: ‘My saviour! I owe you my life. What can I do for you?’

当我撰写《梦的解析》一书的最后几章时，正值暑假，无法查阅图书馆和参考书。我只能凭记忆将所有参考文献和引文插入手稿，打算之后再核对。在论述白日梦的章节中，我想到了阿尔方斯·都德的小说《纳巴布》中那个刻画生动的贫穷簿记员的形象，作者很可能借此来描述自己的白日梦。我清晰地记得这个男人——我称他为乔斯林先生——在巴黎街头漫步时的一个幻想，于是开始凭记忆描述。乔斯林先生勇敢地挡在一匹狂奔的马前，让它停了下来。这时，马车门打开，一位显赫的人物走下车，握住乔斯林先生的手，说道：“我的救命恩人！我欠你一条命。我能为你做些什么？”

I told myself that I could easily correct any inaccuracies in my account of this fantasy at home, when I had the book to hand. But when I did leaf through Le Nabab to compare the passage in print with my manuscript, I was dismayed and abashed to find nothing about any such daydream by a M. Jocelyn, which was not even the poor bookkeepers name; he was called M. Joyeuse. This second mistake soon provided the key to the first, my false memory. Joyeux (the man’s surname being the feminine form of the adjective) is the way my own name Freud would translate into French. So where did the incorrectly remembered fantasy that I had attributed to Daudet come from? It could be only a product of my own mind, a daydream I had invented myself without being conscious of it, or perhaps I had once been conscious of it and had then entirely forgotten it. It was possible that I had it in Paris, where until Charcot took me into his circle I often enough walked the streets alone and full of longing, in great need of some friend and patron to help me. Subsequently I met the author of Le Nabab several times at Charcot’s home. 8

我告诉自己，回家后手边有书，就能轻松纠正我对这段幻想描述中的任何错误。但当我翻阅《纳巴布》将书中的文字与我的手稿进行比对时，却沮丧而尴尬地发现，书中根本没有提到过一位名叫乔斯林先生的白日梦——这甚至不是那位可怜的簿记员的名字；他的名字是乔尤斯先生。这第二个错误很快就为第一个错误——我的错误记忆——提供了线索。“乔尤斯”（Joyeux，这个男人的姓氏是形容词的阴性形式）正是我的名字弗洛伊德在法语中的写法。那么，我错误地将这段幻想归于都德的幻想究竟从何而来？它只能是我自己臆想出来的，是我无意识中虚构的白日梦，或者也许我曾经意识到过它，但后来完全忘记了。或许我是在巴黎得的病。在夏尔科把我带入他的圈子之前，我常常独自一人漫步街头，满怀渴望，迫切需要一位朋友和赞助人来帮助我。后来，我在夏尔科家中多次见到《纳巴布》的作者。

Another case of false memory that proved capable of satisfactory explanation is reminiscent of the phenomenon of fausse reconnaissance , which will be discussed later: I had told one of my patients, an ambitious and capable man, that a young student had recently introduced himself into my circle with an interesting paper on The Artist: An Attempt at a Sexual Psychology’. When this paper was printed a year and a quarter later, my patient said he could remember it perfectly well, since he had read the announcement of its forthcoming publication somewhere before I had first mentioned it (a month or half a year before), perhaps in a bookseller’s advertisement. This notice had come straight to his mind at the time, and he said, moreover, that the author had changed the title, since it was now called not an ‘essay or ‘attempt’ [ Versuch ] but ‘approaches’ [ Ansätze ] to a sexual psychology. However, careful questioning of the author and comparison of all the dates involved showed that my patient was claiming to remember something impossible. No advertisement for the work had appeared anywhere before its publication, certainly not a whole year and a quarter in advance. When I refrained from analysing this false memory, the same man came up with a similar but new variation. He thought that recently he had seen a work on Agoraphobia in the display window of a bookshop, and tried to get hold of it by consulting all the publishers’ catalogues. I was then able to explain why his efforts were bound to be unsuccessful: the work on agoraphobia existed only in his imagination as an unconscious intention, because he was planning to write such a book himself. His ambition to emulate the other man and become a member of my circle through producing a scientific work of that kind had led him to both the first and the second false memory. He then remembered that the bookseller’s advertisement which he had used as the basis for his first false memory referred to a work entitled Genesis, das Gesetz der Zeugung [ Genesis, the Law of Procreation ]. I was responsible, however, for the change of title that he mentioned, since it was I who had misquoted it myself as Versuch instead of Ansätze.

另一个可以得到合理解释的虚假记忆案例，让人联想到稍后将要讨论的虚假认知现象：我曾告诉一位雄心勃勃、能力出众的病人，一位年轻学生最近带着一篇题为《艺术家：性心理学的尝试》的有趣论文来认识我。一年零三个月后，这篇论文出版了，我的病人却说他记得清清楚楚，因为在我首次提及此事之前（大概一个月或半年前），他曾在某个地方看到过论文即将出版的预告，可能是在书商的广告上。当时他立刻就想到了这个预告，而且他还说作者改了标题，现在不再是“论文”或“尝试”（Versuch），而是“性心理学的途径”（Ansätze）。然而，仔细询问作者并核对所有相关日期后，我发现我的病人声称自己记得一件不可能的事情。这部作品出版前从未出现过任何广告，更别提提前整整一年零三个月了。当我没有分析这个虚假记忆时，同一个人又编造了一个类似但又不同的版本。他以为最近在一家书店的橱窗里看到了一本关于广场恐惧症的书，于是翻遍了所有出版社的目录，试图找到它。这时我才明白他为什么注定失败：那本关于广场恐惧症的书只存在于他的想象中，是一种无意识的意图，因为他自己也计划写一本这样的书。他渴望效仿他人，并通过撰写这类科学著作加入我的圈子，正是这种野心驱使他编造了第一个和第二个虚假记忆。然后他想起，他用来编造第一个虚假记忆的书商广告，指的是一本名为《创世记，生育法则》（Genesis, das Gesetz der Zeugung）的书。然而，他提到的标题更改是我的责任，因为是我自己把它错误地引用成了 Versuch 而不是 Ansätze。

B) Forgetting intentions

B) 忘记意图

No other group of phenomena is more suitable than the forgetting of intentions to prove the hypothesis that inattention is not enough to explain a slip in itself. An intention is an impulse to perform an action upon which one has already decided, while postponing its execution to some appropriate time. Now, in the interval of time thus created a change in motivation can occur, a change of such a nature that the intention is not carried out, but it has not been actually forgotten, merely revised and rejected. Forgetting intentions, as we are apt to do every day and in all kinds of situations, is not something we usually explain to ourselves by reassessing our motives. We generally leave it unexplained, or look for some psychological elucidation by assuming that around the time it was to have been carried out, the requisite attention to the subject was no longer present, although it would have been an essential condition for the forming of the original intention and must thus have been available at that time for putting it into practice. But observation of our normal attitude to intentions allows us to dismiss this attempt at explanation as arbitrary. If I form an intention in the morning, meaning to carry it out in the evening, I may be reminded of it several times before then, but it does not have to be consciously present in my mind during the day at all. When the time to carry it out approaches, I shall suddenly remember it, and it will impel me to make the preparations necessary for the intended action. If I go out for a walk taking a letter to the post, as a normal rather than a nervous individual I am not in the habit of clutching it in my hand the whole time, constantly looking out for a letterbox in which to post it; instead, I put it in my pocket, go for my walk, allowing my thoughts to wander as they will, and expect that one of the next letterboxes I see will remind me to put my hand in my pocket and take the letter out. Normal behaviour once an intention has been formed coincides exactly with the experimentally induced behaviour of people to whom ‘long-term post-hypnotic suggestion’ has been given under hypnosis. 9 This phenomenon is usually described as follows: the suggested intention lies dormant in the person concerned until the time to carry it out approaches. It is then aroused and impels the person into action.

没有比遗忘意图更适合用来证明“注意力不集中不足以解释失误”这一假设的例子了。意图是指一个人已经决定要采取的行动的冲动，同时将其执行推迟到某个合适的时间。在这段时间间隔内，动机可能会发生变化，这种变化会导致意图没有被执行，但实际上并没有被遗忘，只是被修正和放弃了。我们每天都会在各种情况下遗忘意图，而我们通常不会通过重新评估自己的动机来解释这种现象。我们通常对此不予解释，或者试图通过假设在原本应该执行意图的时候，对这件事的必要注意力已经不在了来寻求某种心理学上的解释，尽管这种注意力原本是形成最初意图的必要条件，因此在当时应该有足够的注意力来实现意图。但是，观察我们对待意图的通常态度，就能让我们驳斥这种解释，因为它纯属武断。如果我早上立下心愿，打算晚上执行，在此之前我可能会多次想起这件事，但它完全不必在我白天刻意地存在于我的脑海中。当执行的时间临近时，我会突然想起它，并促使我为计划的行动做好必要的准备。如果我出门散步时顺便寄一封信，作为一个正常人而非神经质的人，我不会一直把信攥在手里，不停地寻找可以投递的邮箱；相反，我会把它放进口袋，继续散步，任由思绪飘荡，期待着下一个看到的邮箱会提醒我把手伸进口袋，把信拿出来。一旦形成意图，正常行为便与接受过“长期催眠后暗示”的受试者在催眠状态下的实验诱导行为完全一致。这种现象通常描述如下：被暗示的意图在受试者心中处于休眠状态，直到执行时机临近。此时，意图被唤醒，并驱使受试者采取行动。

In two situations in life, even lay people realize that forgetting an intention cannot by any means be regarded as an elementary phenomenon incapable of being traced further back, and will conclude that tacit motives exist. The two situations I mean are love and military matters. A lover who misses his rendezvous will not find that an excuse to the effect that, unfortunately, he forgot goes down well with his inamorata. She will not hesitate to retort: ‘You wouldn’t have forgotten a year ago. You don’t love me any more.’ Even if he were to resort to the psychological explanation mentioned above and try excusing himself by pleading pressure of business, he would only make the lady — as perceptive by now as any psychoanalyst — reply: ‘How odd that business worries never used to trouble you!’ The lady will not, of course, deny that he may have forgotten; she will merely think, with some justification, that much the same conclusion — a certain cooling of his ardour — can be drawn from unintentional forgetting as from a conscious excuse.

在生活中，有两种情况即使是普通人也能意识到，忘记某个意图绝非一种无法追溯根源的基本现象，而是背后必然存在某种隐性动机。我指的是爱情和军事事务。一个错过约会的恋人，如果用“很遗憾，我忘记了”这样的借口来搪塞心上人，是行不通的。她会毫不犹豫地反驳道：“一年前你肯定不会忘记。你不再爱我了。” 即使他诉诸上述的心理学解释，试图以公务繁忙为由开脱，这位女士——此时的洞察力不亚于任何一位心理分析师——也只会回应道：“真奇怪，以前你从来都不为公事烦心！” 当然，这位女士不会否认他可能真的忘记了；她只是会理所当然地认为，无意的遗忘和有意识的借口一样，都会导致他热情的消退。

In the same way, any distinction between unintentional and intentional forgetting is ignored in the army on principle, and rightly so. The soldier must not forget what his military service requires of him. If he does forget, even though he knew what he had to do, the motives urging him to do his military duty are opposed by other motives running counter to them. For instance, the man doing a year’s military service who tries excusing himself on parade by saying he forgot to polish his buttons until they shone can be sure of punishment. But that punishment is as nothing compared to what he would risk if he told his superior officers the real reason for his omission: ‘I hate army service and all this wretched drill.’ It makes economic sense, so to speak, to use forgetting as an excuse or as a compromise solution to spare himself the punishment he would then incur.

同样，军队原则上忽略了无意遗忘和故意遗忘之间的区别，这样做是理所当然的。士兵绝不能忘记服兵役的要求。如果他忘记了，即使他知道自己该做什么，促使他履行兵役义务的动机也会被其他与之相反的动机所抵消。例如，一个服役一年的士兵，如果在阅兵式上以忘记擦亮纽扣为由为自己开脱，肯定会受到惩罚。但与他向上级军官坦白自己疏忽的真正原因——“我讨厌服兵役和所有这些糟糕的操练”——相比，这点惩罚简直微不足道。可以说，用遗忘作为借口或折衷方案来避免受到惩罚，在经济上是合理的。

Courtship and army service demand that eveiything to do with them must be impossible to forget, thus suggesting that it is permissible to forget unimportant things; to forget something important, however, shows that it is being treated as unimportant and is tantamount to denying that it matters at all. 10 The standpoint of psychic evaluation cannot be dismissed here. No one forgets to do something that seems to him important without being suspected of mental disturbance. Our study can therefore cover only the forgetting of more or less trivial intentions; but no intention can be considered entirely unimportant, for in that case it would certainly never be formed at all.

恋爱和服兵役要求与它们相关的一切都必须令人难以忘怀，这暗示着忘记无关紧要的事情是可以接受的；然而，忘记重要的事情则表明它被视为无关紧要，等同于否认它的重要性。 10 心理评估的视角在此不容忽视。没有人会忘记去做自己认为重要的事情而不被怀疑精神失常。因此，我们的研究只能涵盖或多或少无关紧要的意图的遗忘；但任何意图都不能被认为是完全无关紧要的，因为如果真是如此，它肯定根本不会形成。

As with the functional disturbances described above, I have collected cases observed in myself of neglecting to do something because I forgot, and have tried to cast light on them. I have found in general that they could be traced back to the intervention of unknown and unadmitted motives — or, one might say, to a counter-will implying negativity. In some of these cases I found myself in a situation similar to that of military service, under a compulsion which I had not entirely given up resisting, so that I was making my protest by forgetfulness. For instance, I am particularly apt to forget to send good wishes on birthdays, anniversaries, weddings and professional promotions. I always intend to send congratulations, and am increasingly convinced that I shall not succeed. I am now about to give up that intention and consciously allow the motives resisting it to have the upper hand. While I was in the transitional stage I told a friend in advance, when he had asked me to send a telegram of congratulations on his behalf as well as my own on a certain date, that I would forget both, and not surprisingly my prophecy came true. The reason why I feel unable to offer expressions of goodwill that are bound to sound excessive, since the appropriate phrases do not match the very minor amount of emotion I really feel, is to do with painful experiences in my own life. Ever since realizing that I have often taken other people’s words of goodwill at face value, I have felt a dislike for conventional expressions of sympathy, although I can see that they are socially useful. Condolences on someone’s death are an exception to my ambivalent attitude; when I have made up my mind to send them I do so at once. Nor is the expression of my feelings inhibited by forgetfulness when it has nothing to do with social duty.

与上文所述的功能障碍一样，我收集了自己因遗忘而疏忽某些事情的案例，并试图探究其根源。我发现，这些案例通常可以追溯到未知且未被承认的动机——或者说，源于一种消极的反抗意志。在某些情况下，我发现自己处于类似于服兵役的状态，受到某种我尚未完全放弃抵抗的强制力约束，因此我以遗忘来表达抗议。例如，我特别容易忘记在生日、周年纪念日、婚礼和职业晋升时送上祝福。我总是打算送上祝贺，但越来越确信自己无法做到。现在，我打算放弃这个念头，并有意识地让那些阻碍我这么做的动机占据上风。在我处于过渡期的时候，一位朋友请我帮忙在某个日期分别发一封祝贺电报，我事先告诉他，我肯定会忘记。不出所料，我的预言成真了。我之所以无法表达那些听起来过分的善意，因为合适的措辞无法表达我内心真正感受到的微弱情感，这与我自身痛苦的经历有关。自从意识到自己常常轻信他人的善意之言后，我便对传统的慰问表达方式感到反感，尽管我明白它们在社交场合中确实有用。对逝者的哀悼是我这种矛盾态度的例外；一旦决定要表达慰问，我就会立刻发出。而且，当与社交义务无关时，我表达情感也不会因为健忘而有所顾忌。

First Lieutenant T. gives an account, from his experience as a prisoner of war, of a case of forgetfulness in which an intention initially suppressed made itself felt as an act of ‘counter-will’ and led to an unfortunate situation: ‘The highest-ranking officer in a prisoner-of-war camp was insulted by one of his companions. To avoid further problems, he intended to make use of the one form of authority still available to him and have the other man moved to a different camp. Only on the advice of several friends did he decide, against his secret wishes, to refrain and take the conventionally honourable line of a challenge, which was bound to have a number of undesirable consequences. The same morning this commanding officer, under the supervision of the camp guard, had to take the roll-call of the officers. He had known his companions for a long time, and had never before made any mistake in reading out the list. Today, however, he omitted the name of the man who had insulted him, who therefore had to stay behind in the parade square after all his companions had left, until the mistake was cleared up. The forgotten name was in a perfectly obvious position in the middle of a sheet of paper. This incident was regarded by one of the parties concerned as an intentional insult, and by the other as an unfortunate and awkward accident which might well be misinterpreted. However, the protagonist in this drama later read Freud’s Psychopathology and drew the correct conclusions about what exactly had been going on.’

T中尉根据自己作为战俘的经历，讲述了一个因健忘而导致的不幸事件：原本压抑的意图最终以一种“反意志”的方式爆发出来，酿成了一场悲剧。“战俘营里级别最高的军官被一名同伴侮辱。为了避免事态进一步恶化，他打算利用自己仅存的权力，将那人调到另一个战俘营。然而，在几位朋友的劝说下，他最终违背了自己的内心意愿，决定采取按惯例的体面做法——挑战对方，但这必然会带来一系列不良后果。当天早上，这位指挥官在营地守卫的监督下，不得不点名。他与这些同伴相识已久，此前从未在点名时出错。”然而，今天他却漏掉了侮辱他的那个人的名字，结果那人不得不留在阅兵场上，等所有同伴都离开后，才把这个错误澄清。那个被遗忘的名字明明就在一张纸的正中央，位置非常显眼。其中一方认为这是故意侮辱，另一方则认为这是一场不幸而尴尬的意外，很可能被误解。不过，这出闹剧的主人公后来读了弗洛伊德的《精神病理学》，并对事情的真相得出了正确的结论。

There is a similar explanation for cases where people forget to carry out actions that they have promised to perform as a favour to someone else, because this conventional duty conflicts with their unadmitted personal opinion of it. In such cases it is usual for only the person who was supposed to do the favour to think that forgetting it is any excuse, while the person who asked him to do it undoubtedly gives himself the correct answer: he isn’t interested or he wouldn’t have forgotten. Some people are commonly described as forgetful, and are forgiven for it in much the same way as a short-sighted person is forgiven for failing to greet an acquaintance in the street. 11 These people forget all the minor promises they have made, and neglect all the tasks they are asked to perform, thus showing themselves unreliable in small things and suggesting that such minor offences in them should not be taken ill — that is to say, should not be explained by their characters but ascribed to something organic in them. 12 I am not one of them myself, and have had no opportunity of analysing the actions of such people in order to discover the motivation for their omissions by looking at what they choose to forget. However, I cannot help suspecting, by analogy, that unusually great if unadmitted contempt for another person is a motive employing that constitutional factor for its own ends. 13

对于有些人忘记履行答应帮别人的忙，也有类似的解释，因为这种约定俗成的义务与他们内心深处对此的看法相冲突。在这种情况下，通常只有被要求帮忙的人才会认为忘记是借口，而请求他帮忙的人无疑会给出正确的答案：他根本不在乎，否则就不会忘记了。有些人常被形容为健忘，人们也常常原谅他们，就像近视的人在街上没跟熟人打招呼一样。这些人会忘记自己做出的所有小承诺，也会忽略所有被要求完成的任务，从而在小事上显得不可靠，这也暗示着人们不应该对他们的这些小过错耿耿于怀——也就是说，不应该用他们的性格来解释，而应该归因于他们内在的某种特质。我本人并非如此，也没有机会分析这类人的行为，从而通过探究他们选择遗忘的内容来发现他们疏忽的动机。然而，我不禁怀疑，类比而言，对他人异常强烈却不承认的蔑视，或许正是利用这种内在因素来实现自身目的的动机。

In other cases the motives for forgetfulness are not so easy to find, and once discovered arouse more of a sense of surprised dissatisfaction. I noticed in the past that when I was paying a great many visits to sick patients, the only ones I ever forgot were those made to people I was treating free of charge or to colleagues. Feeling ashamed of this, I made it my habit to note down in the morning the visits I was going to make that day. I do not know if any other doctors have adopted this habit in the same way, but it does give some idea of what causes a so-called neurasthenic to write down the information he wants to give the doctor in his notorious ‘notes’. He seems to lack confidence in the ability of his memory to reproduce his symptoms. And he may well be right, but what happens is usually this: the patient has described his various complaints and put his questions in a very long-winded way. When he has finished, he pauses for a moment, then brings out his notes and says apologetically: ‘I wrote a few things down because I have such a bad memory.’ As a rule the notes contain nothing new. He goes over each point again, answering it himself: ‘Oh yes, I’ve already asked you that.’ His notes are probably just the demonstration of one of his symptoms: the frequency with which his intentions are disrupted by the intervention of unclear motives.

在其他情况下，遗忘的动机并不容易找到，一旦被发现，反而会引发一种惊讶和不满。我过去注意到，当我经常探访病人时，唯一会忘记的只有那些免费诊治的病人或同事的探访。为此感到羞愧，我养成了一个习惯，那就是每天早上记下当天要进行的探访。我不知道其他医生是否也养成了同样的习惯，但这确实能解释为什么所谓的神经衰弱患者会把想要告诉医生的信息写在他们臭名昭著的“笔记”里。他们似乎对自己记忆力重现症状的能力缺乏信心。他们或许是对的，但通常的情况是这样的：病人会非常冗长地描述自己的各种症状并提出问题。他说完后，停顿片刻，然后拿出笔记，歉意地说：“我记性不好，所以记了一些东西。” 通常，笔记里没什么新内容。他会把每一条都再重复一遍，自己回答：“哦，是的，我已经问过你了。” 他的笔记或许只是他症状之一的体现：他的意图经常被一些不明动机的干扰所打断。

I shall be mentioning something which afflicts the majority of healthy people I know when I admit that, especially in the past, I have found that I easily forget to return books I have borrowed, keeping them for a long time, and I was particularly inclined to put off paying bills by forgetting them. Not long ago I left the tobacconists where I had made my daily purchase of cigars one morning without paying. It was a perfectly innocent omission, since I am a regular customer there, and could therefore expect to be reminded of what I owed next day. But the small forgetfulness, the attempt to run up a debt, must certainly have been connected with the thoughts about my finances that had been occupying me all the previous day. It is easy to find traces of an ambivalent attitude even in most so-called well-conducted people when it comes to money and property. The baby’s primitive greed in trying to grab everything it can (and stuff it into its mouth) may prove to have been only incompletely overcome in general by culture and education. 14

我要说的是，我认识的大多数健康人都有这个问题：尤其是在过去，我发现自己很容易忘记归还借来的书，总是把书留很久。而且，我特别容易因为忘记还账而拖欠账单。不久前的一天早上，我去烟草店买雪茄，却忘了付钱。这完全是无意的疏忽，因为我是那里的常客，所以第二天店员应该会提醒我欠款。但这种小小的健忘，这种试图欠债的行为，肯定与我前一天一直在思考的财务问题有关。即使是那些所谓的“品行端正”的人，在金钱和财产问题上，也很容易发现他们内心的矛盾态度。婴儿那种想要抓住一切（并塞进嘴里）的原始贪婪，或许只是在文化和教育的熏陶下，才得以不完全地被克服。

I am afraid that all the examples above have been rather banal. However, I do not mind referring to matters known to everyone and, by the same token, understood by everyone, since my intention is solely to collect everyday examples and subject them to scientific study. I do not see why the insights that reflect our common experience of life should be denied admission to the category of scientific findings. The essential character of scientific study lies not in the disparity of its subjects, but in its strict approach to the establishment of its findings and in trying to make far-reaching connections.

恐怕以上所有例子都略显平庸。不过，我并不介意提及人人皆知、人人皆懂的事物，因为我的目的仅仅是收集日常实例并对其进行科学研究。我不明白为何反映我们共同生活经验的洞见就不能被纳入科学发现的范畴。科学研究的本质不在于其研究对象的差异，而在于其严谨的论证方法以及力求建立深远联系的努力。

Intentions of moderate importance are found, in general, to be forgotten when opposed by unclear motives. In even less important intentions, the transference to the intention of a negative counter-will from some other source, once an external association has been established between that other source and the content of the intention, constitutes a second mechanism for forgetting. The following example belongs in that category: I like to use good blotting paper, and on my afternoon walk into the inner city I meant to buy some. But on four successive days I forgot to do so, until I stopped to ask myself why. I found my forgetfulness easy to explain when I had recollected that I am in the habit of writing Löschpapier [blotting paper], but in speech I use the alternative term Fliesspapier. ‘Fliess’ is the name of a friend in Berlin who had caused me much anxious and painful reflection on the days concerned. I could not shake off such thoughts, but my tendency to resistance (cf. above, p. 139 ) was expressed by transference, through the similarity of the word, to my not very important and therefore not very resistant intention.

一般来说，当动机不明时，中等重要性的意图更容易被遗忘。对于更不重要的意图，一旦在其他来源与意图内容之间建立了外部联系，这种来自其他来源的负面反意志就会转移到该意图上，从而构成第二种遗忘机制。以下例子就属于这种情况：我喜欢用吸墨纸，那天下午我去市中心散步，打算买一些。但连续四天我都忘记了，直到我停下来问自己为什么。当我想起我习惯写“Löschpapier”（吸墨纸），但在口语中我用的是另一个词“Fliesspapier”（吸墨纸）时，我的健忘就很容易解释了。“Fliess”是我在柏林的一位朋友的名字，在那几天里，他让我感到非常焦虑和痛苦。我无法摆脱这些想法，但我的抵抗倾向（参见上文第 139 页）通过移情表达出来，通过词语的相似性，表达出来，指向我不太重要因此也不太抗拒的意图。

Direct counter-will and more distant motivation coincide in the following case: in the collection Grenzfragen des Nerven- und Seelenlebens [ Borderline Problems of Nervous and Mental Life ], I had written a short essay on dreaming, which summed up the content of my Interpretation of Dreams. The publisher, Bergmann of Wiesbaden, sent me a set of proofs and asked to have them back by return, because he wanted to bring the collection out before Christmas. I corrected the proofs that night and put them on my desk, ready to take them out with me next morning. In the morning I forgot, and remembered the proofs only that afternoon when I saw their wrapper on my desk. I continued forgetting to send off the proofs that afternoon, that evening and the next morning, until I pulled myself together and took them to a letterbox on the afternoon of the second day, wondering what the reason for my delay might be. Obviously there was some reason why I did not want to send them, but I could not think what it was. However, on the same walk I looked in on my Viennese publisher, the publisher of the book on dreams itself, ordered something from him, and then said, as if struck by a sudden idea: ‘I suppose you know I’ve rewritten my Dreams? ’ ‘Oh, no!’ he exclaimed. ‘No, don’t worry,’ I said, ‘it’s only a brief essay for the Löwenfeld-Kurella collection.’ But he was still upset; he feared that my contribution to the collection would harm sales of my own book. I assured him it wouldn’t, and finally said: ‘If I’d asked you in the first place, would you have forbidden me to publish the article?’ ‘No, of course not.’ I myself think I acted entirely within my rights, and did only what everyone usually does, but it seems to me certain now that I had some reservations about writing the article, along the same lines as the doubts expressed by my publisher, and those reservations had motivated my unwillingness to send off the proofs. They derived from an earlier occasion on which another publisher made a fuss when, unavoidably, I took several pages of text from an earlier work of mine on cerebral infantile paralysis published by another firm, and included them unaltered in my discussion of the same subject in Nothnagel’s Handbuch [ Manual ]. Once again, there was no good reason for anyone to blame me; on that occasion too I had duly told my first publisher (in fact the publisher of the Interpretation of Dreams ) what I intended to do. But if I look back yet further in this series of memories, it brings me to an even earlier occasion and a translation from the French, when I really did infringe the rights of intellectual property in a publication. I had added notes of my own to the translated text without asking the author’s permission, and a few years later I had reason to think that he was not happy with this unauthorized action of mine.

在以下案例中，直接的反抗意志和更深层次的动机同时出现：在我的文集《神经与精神生活的边缘问题》（Grenzfragen des Nerven- und Seelenlebens）中，我写了一篇关于梦的短文，概括了我《梦的解析》的内容。威斯巴登的出版商伯格曼（Bergmann）寄给我一套校样，并要求我尽快寄回，因为他想在圣诞节前出版这本文集。当晚我就修改了校样，并把它们放在桌子上，准备第二天早上带出去。第二天早上我却忘记了，直到下午看到桌上的校样包装纸才想起来。那天下午、晚上和第二天早上，我一直忘记寄出校样，直到第二天下午我才鼓起勇气把它们投递到邮箱，心里纳闷自己为什么会拖延。显然，我不想寄出校样是有原因的，但我却想不出是什么。然而，就在同一次散步中，我顺道拜访了我的维也纳出版商——也就是那本关于梦的书的出版商——向他订购了一些东西，然后仿佛突然想到什么似的说道：“我想您应该知道我重写了我的《梦》吧？”“哦，不！”他惊呼道。“别担心，”我说，“这只是为勒文菲尔德-库雷拉文集写的一篇短文。”但他仍然很不安；他担心我为文集撰写的文章会影响我自己的书的销量。我向他保证不会，最后说道：“如果我一开始就问您，您会阻止我发表这篇文章吗？”“当然不会。”我自己认为我的行为完全合乎我的权利，只是做了大家通常会做的事情，但现在我确信，我当时对写这篇文章确实有些顾虑，就像我的出版商表达的疑虑一样，而正是这些顾虑促使我迟迟不愿寄出校样。这些事源于早前的一次经历。当时，我无意中从另一家出版社借用了我之前出版的关于小儿麻痹症的著作中的几页文字，并将其原封不动地用在了我在《诺特纳格尔手册》（Nothnagel’s Handbuch）中对同一主题的讨论中。结果，另一家出版社对此大发雷霆。同样，当时也没有任何理由责怪我；我也事先告知了我的第一家出版社（实际上是《梦的解析》的出版社）我的意图。但如果我继续追溯这一系列记忆，就会发现更早的一次经历，那是一次法文翻译，在那次翻译中，我确实侵犯了他人的知识产权。我未经作者许可，就在译文中添加了自己的注释。几年后，我有理由相信，作者对我的这种未经授权的行为感到不满。

A proverb revealing the popular knowledge that intentions are not forgotten by chance runs: ‘What you forget to do once you will forget to do again.’

一句谚语揭示了人们普遍的认知：意图不会轻易被遗忘。谚语说：“忘记做一次的事，你还会忘记做第二次。”

Sometimes, in fact, it is difficult to avoid the impression that everything which can be said about forgetting and other slips is already known to humanity and accepted as perfectly natural. How odd, then, that one still has to point out such well-known facts to the conscious mind! Time and again I have heard someone say: Oh, don’t ask me to do that, I’m sure to forget! There can then surely be nothing mysterious about the accuracy of the prophecy. The person who made it was aware of intending not to carry out the task, and was merely unwilling to admit to it.

事实上，有时很难不让人产生这样的印象：关于遗忘和其他疏忽，所有能说的似乎都早已为人所知，并被视为理所当然。那么，为什么还要向人们的意识指出这些众所周知的事实呢？我一次又一次地听到有人说：“哦，别让我做那个，我肯定会忘记的！” 这样看来，预言的准确性自然也就无从谈起。做出预言的人其实很清楚自己并不打算执行这项任务，只是不愿承认罢了。

Light is also cast on the way in which we forget intentions by what could be called the forming of false intentions. I once promised a young author to write a review of his brief work, but I put it off because of some internal resistance, of which I was not unaware, until one day his urging induced me to promise that I would do it that very evening. And I seriously intended to do so, but I had forgotten that the same evening I was to write a report which could not be postponed. Once I had recognized my intention as a false one, I gave up the battle against my resistance and told the author that I would not write the review.

这也揭示了我们如何通过形成虚假意图来遗忘原本的意图。我曾答应一位年轻作家为他的短篇作品写一篇书评，但由于内心的某种抗拒（我并非对此一无所知），我一直拖延，直到有一天，在他的敦促下，我才答应当晚就写。我的确打算这么做，但我却忘记了当晚我还要写一份无法推迟的报告。一旦我意识到自己的意图是虚假的，我便放弃了与内心抗争，告诉那位作家我不会写书评了。

Notes

笔记

1 . During the consultation the details of the patient’s first visit on the earlier occasion then usually emerge into my conscious mind.

1. 在咨询过程中，患者第一次就诊的细节通常会浮现在我的脑海中。

2 . I would suggest similar explanations for many of the coincidental occurrences that have been ascribed, since T. Vischer wrote about them, to ‘the malice of objects’.

2. 对于许多自 T. Vischer 著述以来被归因于“物体的恶意”的巧合事件，我建议提出类似的解释。

3 . If you ask someone whether he suffered from a syphilitic infection ten or fifteen years ago, it is easy to forget that psychically he will think of this disease in quite different terms from, say, acute arthritis. In the accounts given by parents of their neurotic daughters’ medical history it is difficult to distinguish for certain between what they have forgotten and what they are concealing, since everything that might stand in the way of the girl’s subsequent marriage is automatically eliminated, that is to say, repressed by both parents. A man whose much-loved wife recently died of a lung infection told me the following case of misleading medical information, which can be ascribed only to such forgetfulness. ‘When my poor wife’s pleurisy was still no better after many weeks, Dr P. was called in as consultant. In taking down the history of her case, he asked the usual questions, among them whether anyone else in my wife’s family had suffered from pulmonary disorders. My wife said no, and I could not remember any either. When Dr P. left, the conversation turned by chance to excursions out of town, and my wife said, “Yes, and it’s a long way to Langersdorf where my poor brother is buried .” This brother had died some fifteen years earlier after suffering from tuberculosis for several years. My wife had loved him dearly, and often talked to me about him. Indeed, it occurred to me that she herself, when her pleurisy had been diagnosed, had been very anxious and had thought, sadly: My brother died of lung trouble too. But now she had repressed the memory to such an extent that even after what she had just said about expeditions to L., she could see no reason to correct what she had told the doctor about her family’s medical history. I myself had noticed her failure to remember at the very moment when she mentioned Langersdorf.’ E. Jones describes an analogous experience in his work, mentioned already several times above. A doctor whose wife was suffering from a disorder of the lower abdomen, which resisted diagnosis, said as if to comfort her: ‘It’s a good thing there are no cases of tuberculosis in your family.’ The wife, much surprised, replied: ‘Have you forgotten that my mother died of tuberculosis, and my sister did not recover from the disease until the doctors had given her up?’

3. 如果你问某人十年前或十五年前是否得过梅毒，人们很容易忘记，在心理层面上，他对这种疾病的理解与对急性关节炎之类的疾病截然不同。在父母讲述他们神经质女儿的病史时，很难确定他们究竟是遗忘了什么，还是故意隐瞒了什么，因为任何可能阻碍女儿未来婚姻的事情都会被父母自动排除，也就是说，被压抑了。一位丈夫告诉我，他深爱的妻子最近因肺部感染去世，他讲述了这样一个关于误导性医疗信息的案例，这只能归因于这种健忘。“我可怜的妻子胸膜炎好几周了，病情仍未好转，于是我们请来了P医生做会诊。在询问病史时，他问了一些常规问题，其中包括我妻子家族中是否有人患有肺部疾病。我妻子说没有，我也想不起来了。” P医生离开后，我们的话题偶然转到了郊游，我妻子说：“是啊，去朗格斯多夫可真够远的，我可怜的哥哥就葬在那里。”我哥哥大约十五年前去世，此前他患肺结核多年。我妻子非常爱他，也经常跟我提起他。事实上，我突然意识到，她自己确诊胸膜炎时，也曾非常焦虑，悲伤地想：我的哥哥也是死于肺病。但现在她已经把这段记忆压抑得如此之深，以至于即便刚才说了去朗格斯多夫的旅行，她也觉得没有必要纠正之前告诉医生的关于家族病史的说法。我注意到，就在她提到朗格斯多夫的那一刻，她突然想不起来了。E·琼斯在他的著作中也描述过类似的经历，前面已经多次提到过。一位医生的妻子患有下腹部疾病，一直无法确诊。医生为了安慰她，说道：“幸好你家没有肺结核病史。”妻子大吃一惊，回答说：“你忘了我母亲就是死于肺结核，我姐姐也是在医生束手无策的情况下才康复的吗？”

4 . At the time when I was writing these pages I suffered the following almost incredible instance of forgetfulness: on 1 January I was looking through my medical records so that I could send out the invoices for my fees, and in doing so came upon the name of M … for the month of June. I could not remember anyone with that name. My surprise grew as I noticed, looking forward through my records, that I had treated this case in a sanatorium, visiting daily for weeks. A doctor does not, a mere six months later, forget a patient whom he has treated in such circumstances. Had the patient been an uninteresting person, I wondered, a paralytic? At last, a note about having received my fee restored all the facts that were trying to elude my memory to my mind. M…had been a girl of fourteen, the most remarkable case I had treated the previous year and one that taught me something I am unlikely ever to forget. Its outcome was very painful to me. The child fell sick, unmistakably with hysteria, and swiftly and fundamentally improved under my treatment. But after this improvement the child’s parents withdrew her from my care. She was still complaining of abdominal pains, which had featured prominently as a symptom of her hysteria, and two months later she died of cancer of the abdominal glands. The hysteria to which the child was also predisposed had used the formation of the tumour as a cause provoking it, and I, with my mind on the obvious but harmless hysterical symptoms, had perhaps overlooked the first signs of her progressive and incurable illness.

4. 在我撰写这些文字的时候，我经历了一件几乎不可思议的健忘事：1月1日，我翻阅病历准备寄出收费发票，结果在六月份的记录中看到了M…这个名字。我完全想不起来有谁叫这个名字。当我继续翻阅病历时，发现我曾在疗养院治疗过这个病人，并且连续几周每天都去探望，这让我更加惊讶。一个医生不可能仅仅过了六个月就忘记自己在那种情况下治疗过的病人。我心想，难道这个病人是个无足轻重的人，或者是个瘫痪病人？最后，一张收到收费的通知才让我想起了所有试图从我记忆中溜走的事实。M…是个十四岁的女孩，是我去年治疗过的最特别的病例，也是我永远无法忘记的教训。她最终的结局让我非常痛苦。这个孩子生病了，毫无疑问是歇斯底里，但在我的治疗下，她的病情迅速而彻底地好转了。但病情好转后，孩子的父母便将她从我的照护中接走。她仍然抱怨腹痛，这曾是她癔症的主要症状之一。两个月后，她死于腹部淋巴结癌。孩子本身就容易患癔症，而肿瘤的形成似乎成了诱发因素。我当时只顾着关注那些显而易见但无害的癔症症状，或许忽略了她病情逐渐加重且无法治愈的早期征兆。

5 . A. Pick has recently gathered together papers by a series of authors (‘Zur Psychologie des Vergessens bei Geistes- und Nervenkranken’, Archiv für Kriminal-Anthropologie und Kriminalistik by H. Gross) on the influence on the memory of emotional factors, more or less clearly recognizing the contribution that resistance to unpleasant ideas makes to the memory. None of us, however, has described the phenomenon and its psychological basis as exhaustively and impressively as Nietzsche in one of his aphorisms ( Jenseits von Gut und Böse [ Beyond Good and Evil ], part II, 68): ‘I have done this, says my memory. I cannot have done that, says my pride, and insists upon it. At last it is the memory that gives way.’

5. A. Pick 近期汇编了一系列作者的论文（《精神和神经疾病患者的遗忘心理学》，H. Gross 著，发表于《犯罪人类学和犯罪学档案》），探讨了情绪因素对记忆的影响，并或多或少地明确指出了对不愉快想法的抵抗对记忆的贡献。然而，我们当中没有人能像尼采在其格言（《善恶的彼岸》，第二部分，第68段）中那样，对这种现象及其心理基础进行如此详尽而令人印象深刻的描述：“我的记忆说，我做了这件事。我的骄傲说，我不可能做那件事，并且坚持己见。最终，是记忆让步了。”

6 . Cf. Hans Gross, Kriminalpsychologie , 1898.

6.参见汉斯·格罗斯，《犯罪心理学》，1898年。

7 . Ernest Jones points to the following passage in Darwin’s autobiography, which tellingly reflects his scientific honesty and psychological acuteness: ‘I had, during many years, followed a golden rule, namely, that whenever a published fact, a new observation or thought came across me, which was opposed to my general results, to make a memorandum of it without fail and at once; for I had found by experience that such facts and thoughts were far more apt to escape from the memory than favourable ones.’

7. 欧内斯特·琼斯指出达尔文自传中的以下段落，这段话生动地反映了他的科学诚实和心理敏锐性：“多年来，我一直遵循一条黄金法则，那就是，每当我遇到与我的总体结论相悖的已发表事实、新观察或想法时，我都会毫不犹豫地立即将其记下来；因为我通过经验发现，与有利的事实和想法相比，这些事实和想法更容易被遗忘。”

8 . Some time ago, one of my readers sent me a little volume from F. Hoffmann’s series of books for young people, containing an extensive account of a scene involving a rescue, much like the one I had imagined in Paris. The coincidence even went so far as certain rather unusual expressions that appeared in both sources. The possibility of my having in fact read this book as a boy cannot be rejected. The library of my high school contained Hoffmann’s collection and was always ready to lend volumes to the schoolboys instead of other intellectual nourishment. The fantasy that I thought I remembered at the age of 45 as someone else’s, and then had to recognize as my own and dating from my 29th year, may therefore easily have been the faithful reproduction of an impression absorbed between the ages of 11 and 13. The rescue fantasy I ascribed to the unemployed bookkeeper in Le Nabab was only to pave the way for a fantasy of my own rescue, making my wish for a patron and protector tolerable to my pride. No student of the mind will be surprised to hear that even in my conscious life I have felt great resistance to the idea of being dependent on any protector, and have not borne the few real situations in which something similar has occurred with a very good grace. The deeper significance of fantasies involving such subjects, with an almost exhaustive explanation of their characteristics, has been shown by Abraham in a work entitled ‘Vaterrettung und Vatermord in den neurotischen Phantasiengebilden’ [‘Saving and Murdering the Father in Neurotic Fantasies’], 1922 ( Internationale Zeitschrift für Psychoanalyse VIII).

8. 不久前，一位读者寄给我一本F·霍夫曼青少年系列丛书中的小册子，里面详细描述了一个营救场景，与我在巴黎想象的场景颇为相似。巧合的是，两本书中甚至出现了一些相当独特的表达方式。我不能排除我小时候读过这本书的可能性。我高中的图书馆收藏了霍夫曼的系列丛书，而且总是乐于把书借给学生，而不是提供其他的书籍。因此，我45岁时以为是别人的幻想，后来才意识到那是我自己的，而且可以追溯到29岁，很可能是我11到13岁之间吸收的某种印象的忠实再现。我把在勒纳巴布发生的那个关于失业簿记员的营救幻想，归因于我自己的营救幻想，这只是为了让我能够容忍自己渴望得到庇护和保护的愿望，从而不至于让我的自尊心受到伤害。任何研究心灵的人都不会惊讶地听到，即使在我的意识层面，我也对依赖任何保护者的想法感到强烈的抵触，而且在少数几次类似的现实情境中，我也没有表现出极大的宽容。亚伯拉罕在其题为《神经症幻想中的拯救与谋杀父亲》（1922 年，《国际精神分析杂志》第八卷）的著作中，对涉及此类主题的幻想进行了深入的阐释，并几乎详尽地解释了它们的特征。

9 . Cf. Bernheim, Neue Studien über Hypnotismus, Suggestion und Psychotherapie [New Studies of Hypnotism, Suggestion and Psychology ], 1892.

9. 参见。伯恩海姆，Neue Studien über Hypnotismus, Suggestion und Psychotherapy [催眠、暗示和心理学的新研究]，1892。

10 . In Bernard Shaw’s play Caesar and Cleopatra , Caesar, about to leave Egypt, torments himself for some time with the idea that he intended to do something and has now forgotten what it was. At last it turns out that what Caesar had forgotten was to say goodbye to Cleopatra! This small incident is meant to illustrate — in complete contrast to the historical facts — how little Caesar thought of the Egyptian princess. (From E. Jones, op. cit, p. 488.)

10. 在萧伯纳的戏剧《凯撒与克莉奥佩特拉》中，凯撒即将离开埃及，他为此苦恼了许久，因为他觉得自己原本打算做某件事，但现在却忘记了。最终，他发现自己忘记的竟然是向克莉奥佩特拉道别！这个小插曲旨在说明——与历史事实截然相反——凯撒对这位埃及公主是多么的轻视。（引自E. Jones，《同上》，第488页。）

11 . Women, with their subtler understanding of the unconscious workings of the mind, are usually more inclined to be offended if someone fails to recognize and greet them in the street than to think of the obvious explanation: that their acquaintance is short-sighted, or so deep in thought that he or she has not seen them. They conclude that they would have been noticed if they were truly valued.

11. 女性对潜意识的运作机制有着更敏锐的理解，因此，如果有人在街上没有认出她们并打招呼，她们通常更容易感到被冒犯，而不是去思考显而易见的解释：对方可能目光短浅，或者过于专注地思考而没有注意到她们。她们会想，如果她们真的受到重视，就应该被注意到。

12 . S. Ferenczi says that he himself was ‘absent-minded’ and notorious among his acquaintances for the frequency and peculiarity of the slips he made. However, the signs of this ‘absence of mind’ have almost entirely disappeared since he began psychoanalytical treatment of his patients, and found himself obliged to turn his attention to his own ego as well. He thinks that slips are abandoned if one learns to extend one’s own responsibility, and therefore he contends, in my view correctly, that absence of mind is a condition which depends on unconscious complexes, and can be cured by psychoanalysis. One day, however, he was blaming himself for making a professional mistake in the psychoanalysis of a patient, and all his earlier symptoms of ‘absent-mindedness’ returned. He stumbled several times walking down the street (reflecting the faux pas he had made in treating his patient), left his wallet at home, offered a kreuzer too little for his tram fare, did not button up his clothing neatly, and so forth.

12. S. Ferenczi 说他自己以前“心不在焉”，而且由于经常犯一些奇怪的错误，在熟人中出了名。然而，自从他开始对病人进行精神分析治疗，并发现自己也必须关注自身的自我之后，这种“心不在焉”的迹象几乎完全消失了。他认为，如果一个人学会承担更多责任，就能避免犯错。因此，他认为（在我看来是正确的），心不在焉是一种取决于无意识情结的状态，可以通过精神分析治愈。然而有一天，他因为在给病人做精神分析时犯了一个专业错误而自责，他之前所有的“心不在焉”的症状都回来了。他走在街上时几次跌跌撞撞（反映了他之前在治疗病人时犯的失礼行为），把钱包忘在家里，给的克鲁泽硬币比电车票少了，衣服扣子也没扣好，等等。

13 . On this subject, E. Jones points out: ‘Often the resistance is of a general order. Thus a busy man forgets to post letters entrusted to him — to his slight annoyance — by his wife, just as he may “forget” to carry out her shopping orders.’

13. 关于这一点，E. Jones 指出：“这种抵触情绪往往是普遍性的。例如，一个忙碌的男人会忘记寄送妻子委托他寄的信件——这让他略感恼火——就像他可能会‘忘记’执行妻子的购物指令一样。”

14 . For the sake of thematic unity I will break into my scheme in this book here, and add to what I have said above by pointing out that human memory is especially selective in financial matters. False memories of having paid something already, as I myself know, are often very persistent. When the intention to make a profit is allowed free rein, over and beyond the major interests of life and thus, so to speak, for fun, for instance in a game of cards, the most honest of men are inclined to make mistakes, fail to remember or calculate properly, and find themselves involved in minor frauds without really knowing how. The psychically enjoyable nature of the game is based in part on such liberties. The proverb saying that a person’s real character is revealed in gaming may be admitted, so long as his manifest character is not meant. When head waiters make unintentional mistakes of calculation they are often to be regarded in the same way. Businessmen frequently show a certain hesitation to provide sums of money, pay bills, and so on, in a way that will bring them no profit but can be understood only psychologically, as an expression of the counter-will to get rid of money. Brill points out, with epigrammatic cogency: ‘We are more apt to mislay letters containing bills than checks.’ It is in connection with their most intimate and least clearly understood emotions that women in particular show especial aversion to paying a doctor. They have usually left their purses at home, and cannot pay in the consulting rooms; they then regularly forget to send the fee from home, and thus achieve the effect of having been treated free — for the sake of their charms. They pay, as it were, with their glance.

14. 为了保持本书主题的连贯性，我将在此打破常规，补充我之前的观点：人类的记忆在财务方面尤其具有选择性。正如我亲身经历的那样，关于已经支付过某笔款项的错误记忆往往非常顽固。当人们放任牟利的意图，凌驾于人生大事之上，甚至纯粹为了娱乐（例如在纸牌游戏中）时，即使是最诚实的人也容易犯错，记不住账或计算有误，并在不知不觉中卷入一些小的欺诈行为。这种游戏带来的心理愉悦感，部分就建立在这种“放纵”之上。俗话说“赌博能暴露人的真实性格”，这句话或许可以接受，但前提是它指的并非是人们显而易见的性格。当领班无意中计算出错时，我们通常也应该这样看待他们。商人常常对提供资金、支付账单等等表现出某种犹豫，这种犹豫并非出于自身利益，而只能从心理学角度理解，是他们想要摆脱金钱的一种心理表现。布里尔以精辟的格言指出：“我们更容易丢失装有账单的信件，而不是支票。” 尤其对于女性而言，她们对支付医生费用表现出特别的抵触情绪，这与她们最私密、最难以捉摸的情感密切相关。她们通常把钱包忘在家里，无法在诊室里支付；然后她们常常忘记从家里寄回诊费，从而营造出一种免费就诊的效果——这完全是出于她们的魅力。她们仿佛用眼神支付了费用。

# ↩

VIII

第八

Inadvertent Actions

无意之举

I take the following passage from the work by Meringer and Mayer, mentioned above ( p. 98 ):

我从上文提到的梅林格和梅耶的著作（第98页）中摘录了以下段落：

‘Slips of the tongue do not stand in isolation, but correspond to those slips that often occur during other kinds of human activities, and are ascribed, in a rather simple way, to forgetfulness.’

“口误并非孤立存在，而是与人类其他活动中经常发生的失误相对应，并且通常被简单地归因于遗忘。”

I am therefore by no means the first to have suspected that there is significance and intention behind the small functional disturbances in the daily life of healthy people. 1

因此，我绝非第一个怀疑健康人日常生活中那些细微的功能性障碍背后蕴含着某种意义和意图的人。

If slips of the tongue — and speaking is a motor function — allow of such an interpretation, it seems obvious that we may expect mistakes in our other motor functions to operate in the same way. I have drawn up two groups of cases here: those in which the essential factor seems to be the effect of failure itself — the departure from an intention — I have described as ‘inadvertent actions’, and those in which, by contrast, the entire action appears inappropriate I call ‘symptomatic and fortuitous actions’. However, no clear-cut distinction can be drawn; one has to acknowledge that all the categories mentioned in this work have only a descriptive significance, running counter to the general consistency we find in such phenomena as a whole.

如果口误——而说话是一种运动功能——允许这种解释，那么我们显然可以预期，其他运动功能中的错误也以同样的方式运作。我在此列出了两类情况：一类是关键因素似乎是失败本身的结果——即偏离意图——我称之为“无意行为”；另一类则相反，整个行为本身似乎都不恰当，我称之为“症状性及偶然性行为”。然而，两者之间并无明确的界限；我们必须承认，本文中提到的所有类别都仅具有描述性意义，这与我们在此类现象整体上发现的普遍一致性相悖。

The psychological understanding of ‘inadvertent actions’ obviously gets no notable encouragement if such actions are classified as instances of ataxia, more particularly cortical ataxia. Let me try instead to trace some individual examples back to the conditions in which they occurred. Again, I shall use self-observations, although instances of the phenomenon are not particularly frequent in me.

如果将“无意行为”归类为共济失调，尤其是皮质性共济失调，那么对这类行为的心理学理解显然不会得到显著提升。因此，我尝试追溯一些具体案例的发生背景。同样，我将以自我观察为例，尽管这种现象在我身上并不常见。

a) In the past, when I used to visit patients at home more frequently than I do now, I would often happen to reach the door where I was to knock or ring the bell, and then take my own front-door key out of my pocket — and put it back again, feeling rather abashed. When I work out which patients this happened with, I can only suppose that the inadvertent action — getting out my own key instead of ringing the bell — was a compliment to the place where I perpetrated this slip. It amounted to thinking: ‘I feel at home here.’ since it occurred only when I had come to like the patient. (And of course I never ring my own front-door bell.)

a) 过去，我比现在更频繁地上门探访病人时，常常走到门口准备敲门或按门铃时，会不自觉地从口袋里掏出自己的钥匙——然后又不好意思地放回去。我仔细回想了哪些病人有过这样的经历，只能推测，这种无意的举动——掏出自己的钥匙而不是按门铃——其实是对病人家的一种赞美。这相当于我在想：“我在这里感觉很自在。”因为这种情况只发生在我对病人产生好感的时候。（当然，我从来不会按自己家的门铃。）

The inadvertent action was therefore the symbolic representation of an idea determined by something which was not really a serious conscious assumption, for in reality, as a neurologist, I know perfectly well that patients will remain close to me only as long as they expect to benefit from the relationship, and the neurologist himself takes an unusually warm interest in his patients merely so that he can offer psychic help.

因此，这种无意的行为象征性地代表了一种想法，而这种想法并非出于严肃的意识假设。因为实际上，作为一名神经科医生，我非常清楚，病人只有在期望从这种关系中获益时才会与我保持密切联系，而神经科医生本人之所以对病人表现出异常的热情，仅仅是为了提供心理上的帮助。

It is clear from many self-observations by others that this significant manoeuvre with the key was not by any means peculiar to myself.

从其他人的自我观察中可以清楚地看出，这种使用钥匙的重大操作绝不是我独有的。

A. Maeder (‘Contrib. à la psychopathologie de la vie quotidienne’, Archives de Psychologie VI, 1906) describes a case almost identical with my own experiences: ‘Il est arrivé à chacun de sortir son trousseau, en arrivant à la porte d’un ami particulièrement cher, de se surprendre pour ainsi dire, en train d’ouvrir avec sa clé comme chez soi. C’est un retard, puisqu’il faut sonner malgré tout, mais c’est une preuve qu’on se sent — ou qu’on voudrait se sentir — comme chez soi, auprès de cet ami [Almost everyone has found himself getting out his keys on arriving at the door of a particularly close friend, has surprised himself, so to speak, in the act of opening the door as if it were his own. He is delaying himself, since he will have to ring the bell after all, but it is evidence that he feels — or would like to feel — very much at home with that friend].’

A. Maeder（《日常生活心理病理学研究》，《心理学档案》第六卷，1906年）描述了一个与我自身经历几乎完全相同的案例：“几乎每个人都曾在到达一位特别亲密的朋友家门口时，发现自己掏出钥匙，然后，可以说，自己也惊讶地发现自己竟然像打开自家门一样打开了门。这虽然有点迟疑，因为毕竟还要按门铃，但这表明，你感觉——或者想要感觉——与这位朋友相处非常自在。”

E. Jones (op. cit., p. 509): ‘The use of keys is a fertile source of occurrences of this kind, of which two examples may be given. If I am disturbed in the midst of some engrossing work at home by having to go to the hospital to carry out routine work, I am very apt to find myself trying to open the door of my laboratory there with the key of my desk at home, although the two keys are quite unlike each other. The mistake unconsciously demonstrates where I would rather be at the moment.

E. Jones（同上，第509页）：“钥匙的使用是此类事件的常见来源，这里可以举两个例子。如果我在家正全神贯注地工作，却被打断，不得不去医院处理一些例行事务，我很有可能会发现自己试图用家里书桌的钥匙去打开医院实验室的门，尽管这两把钥匙完全不同。这种错误无意识地表明了我此刻更想待在哪里。”

‘Some years ago I was acting in a subordinate position at a certain institution, the front door of which was kept locked, so that it was necessary to ring for admission. On several occasions I found myself making serious attempts to open the door with my house key. Each of the permanent visiting staff, of which I aspired to be a member, was provided with a key to avoid the trouble of having to wait at the door. My mistakes thus expressed my desire to be on a similar footing, and to be quite “at home” there.’

“几年前，我曾在某机构担任下属职务，该机构的大门总是锁着的，必须按门铃才能进入。有好几次，我都试图用家里的钥匙打开大门。我渴望成为其中一员，而所有常驻的访问工作人员都配有钥匙，免去了在门口等候的麻烦。我的这些失误，恰恰反映了我渴望拥有同样的地位，渴望在那里如鱼得水。”

Dr Hanns Sachs gives an account of a similar incident: ‘I always carry two keys with me, one of which opens the door of my office and the other my front door at home. They are not at all easy to mix up, since the key to the office is at least three times the size of my front-door key, and furthermore I carry the former in my trouser pocket and the latter in my waistcoat pocket. All the same, as I stood outside one of the doors I quite often noticed that I had taken out the wrong key as I climbed the stairs. I decided to make a statistical experiment: as I approached the two doors in more or less the same state of mind every day, my mixing up the two keys ought to show some regular tendency if there were some psychic determination of a different kind for it. My subsequent observations showed that I regularly produced my front-door key outside the door of my office, but I did the reverse only once, when I came home feeling tired but knew there was a guest waiting for me. I then tried to open the front door with the office key, which of course was much too large.’

汉斯·萨克斯博士讲述了一个类似的事件：“我总是随身携带两把钥匙，一把打开办公室的门，另一把打开家里的前门。这两把钥匙不容易混淆，因为办公室的钥匙至少是前门钥匙的三倍大，而且我把办公室的钥匙放在裤兜里，把前门钥匙放在马甲口袋里。尽管如此，当我站在其中一扇门外时，我经常发现自己在上楼时拿出了错误的钥匙。我决定做一个统计实验：既然我每天在大致相同的心境下走向这两扇门，那么如果存在某种不同的心理决定因素，我弄错两把钥匙的情况应该会呈现出某种规律性。我随后的观察表明，我经常在办公室门外拿出前门钥匙，但只有一次我把前门钥匙拿错了，那是在我回家感到疲惫但知道有客人等我的时候。”然后我试图用办公室钥匙打开前门，但那把钥匙当然太大了。

b) In a certain building I used to come to a door on the second floor twice a day at fixed times over a six-year period. On two occasions during this long period of time (with a short interval between them) I happened to climb a floor too high. I had thus climbed the wrong way [ verstiegen , past participle of versteigen , ‘to become lost when mountaineering’]. On the first occasion I was absorbed in a daydream of an ambitious nature in which I was ‘climbing onward and upward’. I even failed to hear the door in question opening as I started up the first of the steps leading to the third floor. The second time I once again climbed too far while lost in thought; when I noticed I turned back, and tried to pin down the fantasy occupying my mind. I found that I was feeling angry with imaginary criticism of my writings which accused me of always ‘going too far’, and in which I now had to insert the not very respectful expression of being verstiegen [literally, see above, ‘having climbed the wrong way’, but colloquially, ‘high-flown, eccentric’ in literary style].

b) 在某栋楼里，我过去六年间每天都会在固定的时间两次来到二楼的一扇门前。在这漫长的六年里，我曾两次（两次间隔很短）爬过楼层，结果走错了方向。第一次，我沉浸在一个雄心勃勃的白日梦中，梦见自己“一路向上攀登”。当我开始爬上通往三楼的第一级台阶时，甚至没有听到那扇门打开的声音。第二次，我又一次因为走神而爬过了头；当我意识到这一点时，我转身往下走，试图弄清楚我脑海中究竟在想些什么。我发现我对想象中对我作品的批评感到愤怒，这些批评指责我总是“做得太过分”，而现在我不得不插入一个不太尊重的表达方式，即verstiegen（字面意思是，见上文，“爬错了方向”，但口语中指文学风格中的“浮夸、古怪”）。

c) For many years a reflex hammer and a tuning fork lay side by side on my desk. One day I was hurrying off at the end of my consulting hours because I wanted to catch a certain local city train, and in full daylight I put the tuning fork instead of the hammer in my coat pocket. The weight of the object dragging down my pocket alerted me to my mistake. Someone unused to thinking much about such small incidents would undoubtedly explain and excuse it by the haste I was in. Instead, I asked myself just why I had picked up the tuning fork instead of the hammer, for my haste might equally well have been a good reason for me to perform the correct action, so that I need not lose any time putting things right.

c) 多年来，我的办公桌上一直并排放着一把反射锤和一把音叉。一天，我结束了咨询工作，急着赶去搭乘某趟市内火车，在光天化日之下，我竟然把音叉而不是反射锤放进了外套口袋。音叉沉甸甸地垂在口袋里，让我意识到自己犯了错。一个不常思考这类小事的人，肯定会用匆忙来解释和原谅我的错误。但我却反问自己，为什么我会拿起音叉而不是反射锤？或许正是因为匆忙，我才更应该选择正确的工具，这样就不用浪费时间去纠正错误了。
