The question that now came into my mind was: who last touched the tuning fork? The answer was that it had been an idiot child a few days ago, when I was checking his sensory impressions. He had been so fascinated by the tuning fork that I had difficulty getting him to let go of it. Did that mean I was an idiot too? It certainly seems so, because the next idea I associated with ‘hammer’ [German: Hammer ] was chamer (Hebrew: ‘donkey’).

我脑海中浮现出一个问题：最后是谁碰过音叉？答案是几天前，一个傻孩子碰过它，当时我正在检查他的感官体验。他对音叉着迷不已，我费了好大劲才让他松手。难道我也是个傻瓜吗？看来确实如此，因为我接下来联想到的“锤子”（德语：Hammer）竟然是“驴”（希伯来语：chamer）。

But why call myself an idiot? I now had to look at the situation itself. I was hurrying off to a consultation in a place on the Western Railway line, to visit a woman patient who, in her medical history as described to me in a letter, had fallen from her balcony months ago and had been unable to walk ever since. The doctor who had turned to me as a consultant wrote that he still was not sure whether this was a case of injury to the spinal cord or traumatic neurosis – hysteria. I had been called in to decide. Here I had to remind myself to be particularly careful in the delicate matter of differential diagnosis. My colleagues are very ready in any event to believe that diagnoses of hysteria are much too glibly made when in fact the trouble is more serious. That, however, did not account for my calling myself an idiot! But now I recollected that years ago I had seen a young man who could not walk properly, as the result of an emotional disturbance, in the same place for which I was about to catch a train to take me to its little railway station. I had diagnosed hysteria at the time and subsequently took the patient into psychiatric treatment, but it turned out that while my diagnosis was not actually incorrect, it did not cover everything. A considerable number of my patient’s symptoms had been hysterical, and sure enough they promptly disappeared in the course of treatment, but it was then possible to see remaining symptoms that were inaccessible to therapy, and could only indicate multiple sclerosis. Doctors who saw the patient after me easily enough identified his organic ailment. I could hardly have done other than I did, nor could I have reached a different conclusion, but an impression was left that I had made a serious mistake, and of course I could not, as I had promised, cure him. My mistake in picking up the tuning fork instead of the hammer could thus be put into words as follows: you fool, you donkey, come on, pull yourself together and make sure you don’t diagnose hysteria again where there is really an incurable illness present, as you did with that poor man at the same place years ago! And luckily for the sake of my little analysis, although it did nothing for my state of mind, that same man, my patient with severe spastic paralysis, had been in my consulting rooms only a few days before, the day after I had seen the idiot child.

但我为什么要自称笨蛋呢？现在我必须审视一下眼前的状况。我正匆匆赶往西部铁路沿线的一个地方，去见一位女病人。根据她在信中提供的病史，几个月前她从阳台上摔了下来，之后就一直无法行走。那位请我做会诊的医生在信中写道，他仍然无法确定这究竟是脊髓损伤还是创伤性神经症——癔症。我被请来做判断。这时我必须提醒自己，在鉴别诊断这个敏感的问题上要格外谨慎。我的同事们总是很容易认为，癔症的诊断过于草率，而实际上问题可能更严重。然而，这并不能解释我为什么自称笨蛋！但现在我突然想起，多年前，我曾在同一个地方——也就是我即将乘火车前往的那个小火车站——见过一位因情绪紊乱而无法正常行走的年轻人。当时我诊断他患有癔症，随后将他送入精神科接受治疗。但结果证明，虽然我的诊断并非完全错误，却也并非无所不包。我的病人确实有很多症状符合癔症的特征，而且这些症状在治疗过程中也确实迅速消失了。然而，之后出现的一些症状却无法通过治疗消除，只能表明他患有多发性硬化症。在我之后接诊的医生很容易就确诊了他的器质性疾病。我当时的做法无可厚非，也无法得出不同的结论，但人们却因此觉得我犯了一个严重的错误，当然，我也无法像我承诺的那样治好他。我当时犯的错误，就像拿起音叉而不是锤子一样，可以用这样的话来形容：你这个傻瓜，你这个蠢货，醒醒吧，以后别再像几年前那样，把癔症误诊成不治之症了！幸运的是，尽管这对我当时的心情没有任何帮助，但就我这小小的分析而言，那个患有严重痉挛性瘫痪的病人，就在几天前，也就是我见到那个白痴孩子的第二天，也来过我的诊室。

It will be noted that on this occasion the voice of self-criticism made itself heard through the inadvertent action, and such occurrences are particularly apt to be a means of self-reproach. The inadvertent action here represents a similar action perpetrated elsewhere.

值得注意的是，这次的自我批评是通过无意的行为表达出来的，而这类事件尤其容易成为自我谴责的一种方式。此处的无意行为与之前在其他地方发生的类似行为如出一辙。

d) An inadvertent action can also, of course, be serving a whole series of other obscure intentions. Here is one example: I do not often break things. I am not particularly good with my hands, but there is nothing the matter with the anatomical integrity of my nervous and muscular systems that would account for my making clumsy movements with unfortunate consequences, so I cannot remember ever breaking any household item. There is not much space in my study, where I have a small collection of antique pottery and stone objects, and when handling them I therefore often have to do so in very awkward positions. People watching me used to express a fear that I would knock something over and break it, but I never did. So why did I once drop the marble top of my plain inkwell to the floor and break it?

d) 当然，无意之举也可能另有隐情。举个例子：我很少打碎东西。我的手并不灵巧，但我的神经和肌肉系统在解剖结构上没有任何问题，足以解释我笨拙的动作和由此造成的不幸后果，所以我记不起自己曾经打碎过任何家用物品。我的书房空间不大，里面摆放着一些古董陶器和石器，因此我经常不得不以非常别扭的姿势来摆弄它们。以前人们看着我，总是担心我会碰倒什么东西摔碎，但我从未这样做过。那么，为什么我曾经不小心把那只素面墨水瓶的大理石瓶盖掉到地上摔碎了呢？

My inkstand was a slab of Untersberg marble hollowed out to take the glass inkwell, which had a lid made of the same stone and with a knob. There was a row of bronze statuettes and terracotta figurines arranged in a circle behind this inkstand. I sat down at my desk to write, made a curiously clumsy, sweeping movement with the hand holding my pen and knocked the lid of the inkwell, which was already lying on my desk, to the floor. It is not difficult to find the explanation. A few hours earlier my sister had been in the room to see some of my new acquisitions. She admired them, and then said: ‘Your desk looks really nice now, except for the inkstand, which doesn’t suit the rest. You ought to have a prettier one.’ I left the room with my sister and did not come back for some hours. But then, or that is how it seems, I carried out the sentence she had pronounced and executed the condemned inkstand. Did I perhaps conclude from my sister’s words that next time she had occasion to make me a present she was going to give me a better inkstand, and had I broken the plain, old one to make sure that she put the plan she had indicated into practice? If so, then my sweeping movement was only apparently clumsy, and in reality was both dextrous and purposeful, since I contrived to avoid all the more valuable objects standing close to the inkstand.

我的墨水台是一块翁特斯贝格大理石板，中间挖空，用来放置玻璃墨水瓶。墨水瓶的盖子也是用同样的石头做的，上面有个旋钮。墨水台后面摆放着一圈青铜小雕像和陶俑。我坐在书桌前准备写作，握笔的那只手笨拙地挥动了一下，碰掉了放在桌上的墨水瓶盖，掉到了地上。原因不难理解。几个小时前，我姐姐来过房间，看了看我的一些新玩意儿。她赞叹了一番，然后说：“你的书桌现在看起来真不错，就是墨水台有点不搭。你应该换个更漂亮的。”说完，我和姐姐一起离开了房间，几个小时都没回来。但后来，或者说，感觉上是这样，我执行了她判的死刑，把那个该死的墨水台“处决”了。我是否从姐姐的话中推断出，下次她送我礼物时会送我一个更好的墨水瓶？我是否为了确保她能兑现承诺，才故意打碎了那个简陋的旧墨水瓶？如果是这样，那么我那看似笨拙的动作，实际上却既灵巧又有目的，因为我巧妙地避开了墨水瓶附近所有更贵重的物品。

I really do think we must assume that a great number of clumsy movements which appear to be accidents can be explained in this way. It is true that there is something violent and jerky about them, as if they were spastic or ataxic movements, but they betray their intentional nature and fulfil their purpose with a certainty that cannot always be attributed to conscious and voluntary movements. They have two characteristics, violence and a sure aim, in common with the motor expressions of hysterical neurosis and to some extent with the motor phenomena of somnambulism, and in both cases these features indicate the same unconscious modification of the process of innervation.

我确实认为我们必须假设，许多看似偶然的笨拙动作都可以用这种方式解释。诚然，这些动作带有某种剧烈和生硬的成分，如同痉挛或共济失调的动作，但它们却暴露出其有意为之的本质，并以一种并非总是由有意识的自主运动所展现的确定性来实现其目的。它们具有两个共同特征：剧烈性和明确的目标性，这与癔症性神经症的运动表现以及某种程度上与梦游症的运动现象相似，在这两种情况下，这些特征都表明神经支配过程发生了相同的无意识改变。

A self-observation recounted to me by Frau Lou Andreas-Salomé convincingly shows how persistent ‘clumsiness’ can be very skilfully put to the service of unacknowledged intentions.

路·安德烈亚斯-萨洛梅女士向我讲述的一次自我观察，令人信服地表明，持续的“笨拙”可以非常巧妙地用于不为人知的意图。

‘Just when milk was in short supply and had become very expensive I found, to my frequent alarm and annoyance, that I kept letting it boil over. I tried in vain to get the better of this tendency, although I cannot accuse myself of being absent-minded or careless in other ways, and I would have been more and not less likely to have a reason for that after my much-loved white terrier died; he was called “Friend” (Russian: Drujok), a name he deserved as much as any human being. But as it happened, I never let so much as a drop of milk boil over again after his death. My first thought was: “What a good thing, because milk boiling over on the stove and dripping to the floor would be no use to anyone now!” And at the same time I saw my “Friend” in front of me, sitting watching me as I was cooking, with his head slightly to one side, already wagging the end of his tail hopefully — waiting confidently for my enjoyable accident to happen. That explained it all, and showed that I had been even fonder of him than I knew.’

“就在牛奶短缺且价格高昂的时候，我却发现自己总是让牛奶溢出来，这让我既惊恐又恼火。我徒劳地试图克服这个毛病，尽管我在其他方面并不粗心大意，而且在我心爱的白色梗犬去世后，我或许更有理由犯这样的错误；它叫“朋友”（俄语：Drujok），这个名字对它来说和对任何人来说一样珍贵。但巧合的是，自从它去世后，我再也没有让牛奶溢出过一滴。我的第一个念头是：‘这真是太好了，因为牛奶在炉子上溢出来滴到地板上对谁都没用！’与此同时，我仿佛看到了我的‘朋友’坐在我面前，看着我做饭，它的头微微歪向一边，尾巴尖充满希望地摇着——它自信地等待着我那令人愉悦的‘意外’发生。”这就解释了一切，也表明我比自己意识到的还要喜欢他。

In the last few years, since I began collecting such observations, I have happened to damage or break objects of some value on several occasions, and study of these incidents has convinced me that they were never the result of chance or my unintentional clumsiness. For instance, one morning as I was walking through a room in my dressing gown, wearing straw slippers, I obeyed a sudden impulse and kicked one slipper off my foot and against the wall, where it brought down a pretty little marble Venus from her bracket. As she smashed into pieces, I cheerfully quoted Wilhelm Busch’s verse:

近几年，自从我开始收集这类观察记录以来，我曾多次不小心损坏或打碎一些贵重物品。对这些事件的研究让我确信，它们绝非偶然或我无意的笨拙所致。例如，一天早晨，我穿着睡袍，脚蹬草鞋，在房间里走来走去，突然一时冲动，踢掉了一只草鞋，鞋尖撞到了墙上，结果把墙上一个精致的小大理石维纳斯雕像也撞了下来。雕像摔得粉碎时，我兴高采烈地引用了威廉·布施的诗句：

Ach! Die Venus ist perdü –

哦！金星迷失了——

Klickeradoms! — von Medici.

Klickeradoms！——美第奇著。

[Dear me — crash! The Medici Venus is broken!]

【我的天哪——砰！美第奇维纳斯雕像坏了！】

This wanton violence and my lack of concern at the damage can be explained by my situation at the time. A member of the family was seriously ill, and I already had private doubts of her recovery. But that morning I was told of a great improvement, and I know that I said to myself: She will live after all. My destructive outbreak served to express gratitude to fate and enabled me to make a ‘sacrifice’, as though I had vowed that if she recovered I would indeed sacrifice something! My choice of the Medici Venus as victim can only have been a gallant tribute to the convalescent. But I still find it extraordinary that yet again I could make up my mind so quickly, aim so well, and ensure that I did not hit any of the other items so close to the statuette.

这种肆意妄为的暴力行为以及我对造成的破坏漠不关心，可以用我当时的处境来解释。一位家人身患重病，我私下里已经对她的康复感到担忧。但那天早上我得知她的病情有了很大的好转，我知道我当时对自己说：她终究会活下来。我的破坏行为是对命运的感恩，也让我得以做出一种“牺牲”，仿佛我曾发誓，如果她康复，我一定会做出某种牺牲！我选择美第奇家族的维纳斯雕像作为我的“牺牲品”，这无疑是对这位正在康复的家人的一种英勇致敬。但我仍然觉得不可思议，我竟然能够如此迅速地做出决定，如此精准地瞄准目标，并且确保没有伤及雕像附近的任何其他物品。

Another breakage, also with the significance of a sacrifice, this time to avert evil, was made with a pen that slipped out of my hand. I had allowed myself to blame a good and loyal friend for something that depended on no more than my interpretation of certain signals made by his unconscious mind. He took it ill, and wrote me a letter asking me please not to subject my friends to psychoanalysis. I had to agree that he was right, and was writing him a conciliatory answer. As I wrote this letter my latest acquisition, a fine glazed Egyptian figurine, was standing in front of me. I broke it as I have just described, and knew at once that I had done the damage to avert a greater one. Luckily it proved possible to mend both the friendship and the figurine so well that no one would ever have noticed the cracks.

另一次破损，同样带有牺牲的意味，这次是为了化解邪恶，是用我手中的笔造成的。我竟然把一件仅仅源于我对一位忠诚好友潜意识信号的解读的事情，归咎于他。他为此非常生气，写信恳求我不要让我的朋友们接受精神分析。我不得不承认他是对的，于是给他回了一封和解信。就在我写这封信的时候，我最新收藏的一件精美的埃及釉面小雕像就摆在我面前。我像刚才描述的那样把它摔碎了，立刻意识到我这样做是为了避免更大的损失。幸运的是，友谊和雕像都得到了很好的修复，以至于没有人会注意到裂痕。

A third breakage happened in a less serious context: it was simply, to borrow a phrase used by T. Vischer in his Auch Einer [ Another One ], a camouflaged ‘execution’ of an object I no longer liked. For some time past I had been carrying a walking stick with a silver handle; when the thin silver plate of the handle was damaged, not by my own fault, it was poorly repaired. Soon after the stick came back from being mended, and when I was in a cheerful mood one day, I used the crook of the handle to angle for one of my children’s legs, and during this game of course it broke and I was rid of it.

第三次损坏发生在一个不太严重的情况下：借用T·维舍尔在《又一个》（Auch Einer）一书中的说法，这不过是我以一种伪装的方式“处理”了我不再喜欢的物品。一段时间以来，我一直带着一根银柄拐杖；后来，杖柄上那层薄薄的银片损坏了（并非我所为），但修补得并不好。拐杖修好后不久，有一天我心情愉快，便用杖柄的弯钩去挠我孩子的腿，结果在玩耍的过程中，杖柄断了，我也就把它扔掉了。

The indifference with which I regarded the damage in all these cases may be taken as proof that I had some unconscious intention to inflict it.

我对所有这些案件中的损害都表现得漠不关心，这可以被视为我无意识中有意造成损害的证据。

There are times when, in looking for the reasons behind so small a slip as breaking an object, one uncovers connections going deep into someone’s past history and still affecting his present situation. The following analysis by L. Jekels may serve as an example.

有时，在探究诸如打碎物品这样的小失误背后的原因时，人们会发现与某人过往经历息息相关的深层联系，而这些联系至今仍在影响着他的处境。L. Jekels 的以下分析或许可以作为例证。

‘A doctor owned a very pretty although not expensive earthenware flower vase. It had once been given to him by a patient, a married woman, along with a number of other objects, some of them valuable. When the woman’s psychosis became obvious he returned all the presents she had made him to her family — except for the comparatively cheap vase from which he felt unable to part, allegedly because it was so attractive. But withholding this item cost the doctor, who was usually very scrupulous, a certain internal struggle, for he was well aware of the impropriety of his conduct and could calm his guilty conscience only by making excuses: the vase was really of no material value, it would have been difficult to pack up, and so forth. A few months later, when he was about to instruct a solicitor to claim and recover the outstanding fees for this patient’s treatment, which were the subject of dispute, his self-reproach returned; fleetingly, he felt alarm in case the woman’s relatives discovered what might be termed his misappropriation of the vase and brought it up against him during legal proceedings. The first factor in particular, his self-reproach, was so strong for a time that he actually entertained the idea of giving up his demand for the fees owed — worth about a hundred times more than the vase — as a kind of compensation for the item he had failed to return. However, he immediately saw that this idea was absurd and rejected it.

一位医生拥有一只非常漂亮但并不昂贵的陶土花瓶。这只花瓶是一位已婚女病人送给他的，同时还送给他一些其他物品，其中一些价值不菲。当这位女病人的精神疾病症状显现后，医生将她送给他的所有礼物都退还给了她的家人——除了那只相对便宜的花瓶，他觉得舍不得扔掉，据说是因为它太漂亮了。但扣留这件花瓶让这位平时非常谨慎的医生内心备受煎熬，因为他很清楚自己行为的不妥，只能通过编造理由来减轻内心的愧疚：花瓶其实没什么实际价值，打包也很麻烦等等。几个月后，当他准备委托律师追讨这位病人拖欠的治疗费用（这笔费用存在争议）时，他的自责之情再次涌上心头；他一闪而过地感到担忧，害怕那女人的亲属发现他擅自拿走了花瓶，并在诉讼中以此为由指控他。尤其是第一个因素，他的自责之情，一度强烈到他甚至考虑放弃追讨欠款——这笔钱大约是花瓶价值的百倍——以此作为对他未能归还花瓶的一种补偿。然而，他很快意识到这个想法荒谬至极，便立刻否定了它。

‘While he was in this frame of mind, it happened that although in the normal way he very seldom broke anything, and had excellent control of his muscular system, he swept the vase off the table while he was refilling it with water, making a curiously clumsy movement which had no organic connection with what he was doing, so that it broke into five or six large pieces. This happened when the previous evening, and only after much hesitation, he had decided to fill this very vase with flowers and put it on the dining-room table in front of some guests he had invited. Just before he broke it he had thought of it, was taken aback to find that it was not in his living room as usual, and then fetched it back from the dining room himself! When, after his initial shock, he had picked up the pieces of the vase and found, by fitting them together, that it could still be mended to look almost as good as new, two or three of the larger fragments slipped out of his hands, smashed into a thousand pieces, and with them went all hope of a successful repair.

“他当时心不在焉，虽然平时他很少打碎东西，而且肌肉控制力也很好，但那天他给花瓶加水的时候，却不小心把花瓶从桌子上碰掉了。那是一个极其笨拙的动作，跟他当时的动作毫无关联，结果花瓶摔成了五六块大碎片。而这件事发生在前一天晚上，他犹豫了很久才决定用这个花瓶插上鲜花，放在餐桌上招待客人。就在他要打碎花瓶的时候，他突然想起了这件事，却惊讶地发现花瓶不在客厅里，于是他自己又从餐厅把它拿了回来！”最初的震惊过后，他捡起花瓶碎片，发现把它们拼在一起后，还能修复得几乎和新的一样好。然而，两三块较大的碎片却从他手中滑落，摔成了无数碎片，修复成功的希望也随之破灭。

‘Undoubtedly this slip had the effect of allowing the doctor to take his case to court by destroying the vase he had withheld, which to some extent was inhibiting him from demanding what, in turn, had been withheld from himself. But as well as this direct determination, any psychoanalyst can see a further, much deeper, more important and symbolic meaning behind his slip: a vase, after all, clearly symbolizes a woman.

毫无疑问，这一失误使得医生得以将案件诉诸法庭，他销毁了自己扣留的花瓶，这在某种程度上阻止了他要求得到自己原本被剥夺的东西。但除了这一直接的认定之外，任何精神分析学家都能从他的失误背后看到更深层次、更重要、更具象征意义的含义：毕竟，花瓶显然象征着女人。

‘The protagonist of this anecdote had suffered the tragic loss of his young, beautiful and dearly loved wife; he fell into a state of neurosis dominated by the idea that he himself was responsible for his misfortune (“he had broken his beautiful vase”). He could no longer relate to women, and felt a distaste for marriage or any long-term loving relationship, which his unconscious regarded as inconstancy to his dead wife, but which he rationalized in his conscious mind as meaning that he brought women bad luck, a woman might kill herself for his sake, and so forth. (Then, of course, he need not keep the vase permanently!)

这则轶事的主人公痛失了年轻貌美、深爱的妻子；他陷入了神经质的状态，坚信自己的不幸都是咎由自取（“他打碎了漂亮的花瓶”）。他再也无法与女性相处，对婚姻或任何长久的恋爱关系都感到厌恶。他的潜意识认为这是对亡妻的背叛，而他的意识则将其合理化为：他会给女性带来厄运，女人可能会为了他而自杀，等等。（这样一来，他当然就不必一直保留着那个花瓶了！）

‘As he had a strong libido, it is not at all surprising that he saw relationships with married women, fleeting of their very nature, as the most suitable kind for him (hence the significance of his withholding someone else’s vase).

“由于他性欲旺盛，所以他认为与已婚妇女的关系，这种关系本质上是短暂的，最适合他，这并不奇怪（因此他扣留别人的花瓶才具有重要意义）。

‘There is good confirmation of this symbolism in the following two factors: first, he underwent psychoanalytical treatment for his neurosis. Later in the session when he described breaking the earthenware vase, he reverted to the subject of his relationships with women, and said he was ridiculously demanding: he insisted, for instance, that women must be of “unearthly beauty”. This clearly emphasized the fact that he still loved his wife (who was dead, and therefore unearthly) and wanted no ordinary “earthly beauty”; hence the breaking of the earthenware (earthly) vase. And at the very time when, in the course of transference, he was constructing a fantasy of marrying his doctor’s daughter, he gave the doctor a present — of a vase, as if indicating the kind of present he would like to be given in return.

以下两点有力地证实了这种象征意义：首先，他接受了精神分析治疗以治疗他的神经症。在治疗过程中，当他描述自己打碎陶罐时，他又回到了他与女性的关系这个话题，并说他要求过高：例如，他坚持认为女性必须拥有“超凡脱俗的美貌”。这清楚地表明，他仍然爱着他的妻子（她已经去世，因此是超凡脱俗的），不想要普通的“世俗美貌”；因此他打碎了陶罐（世俗的）。而且，就在他处于移情状态，幻想自己娶医生的女儿时，他送给医生一份礼物——一个陶罐，仿佛在暗示他希望收到什么样的回礼。

‘It is likely that the symbolic meaning of his slip could be susceptible to many other variations, for instance not wishing to fill the vase, and so on. However, it strikes me as more interesting to surmise that the presence of several motives — two at least, probably operating separately in the preconscious and unconscious minds — is reflected in the duplication of the slip: knocking it over and then dropping the pieces a second time.’ 2

“他脱下的纸条的象征意义可能有很多种变化，例如不想把花瓶装满水等等。然而，我觉得更有意思的是，至少有两种动机——很可能分别在潜意识和无意识中发挥作用——体现在纸条的重复出现上：先是打翻纸条，然后再次掉落碎片。”

e) Dropping objects, knocking them over and breaking them often seems to be a way of expressing unconscious trains of thought, and while this can sometimes be proved by analysis it is more often evident from the superstitious or jocular ideas contained in popular sayings. Everyone knows what spilling salt is supposed to indicate, or knocking over a wine glass, dropping a knife so that it sticks in the floor point down, and so on. I shall return later to the claims such superstitions have on our attention; here I will merely point out that a clumsy action in isolation by no means has a fixed meaning, but offers itself as a method of representing some intention or another, depending on the circumstances.

e) 掉落、碰倒和摔碎物品似乎常常是表达无意识想法的一种方式，虽然有时可以通过分析来证明这一点，但更多时候是从民间谚语中迷信或玩笑的意味中体现出来的。每个人都知道撒盐、打翻酒杯、刀尖朝下插在地板上等等分别代表什么。我稍后会再谈到这些迷信对我们注意力的吸引力；在这里，我只想指出，一个笨拙的动作本身并没有固定的含义，而是根据具体情况，可以作为一种表达某种意图的方式。

Recently there was a time when unusual quantities of glass and china were broken in my household; I myself contributed by damaging several items. This violent little psychic epidemic could easily be explained; it happened in the days leading up to my eldest daughter’s wedding. On festive occasions such as a wedding it is common to break something on purpose, accompanying the breakage by wishes of good luck. This custom may both suggest a sacrifice and have the significance of yet another symbolic meaning.

最近，我家玻璃器皿和瓷器被打碎的数量异常之多；我自己也难逃厄运，弄坏了好几件。这种突如其来的“精神瘟疫”其实很容易解释：它发生在我大女儿婚礼前的几天。在婚礼这样的喜庆场合，人们常常会故意打碎一些东西，并伴随着祝福。这种习俗或许既象征着一种牺牲，也可能蕴含着其他象征意义。

When servants drop and break something fragile our minds do not immediately fly to some psychological explanation, but once again it is not unlikely that hidden motives are involved. Nothing is further from an uneducated person’s mind than an appreciation of art and works of art. Unspoken hostility towards artistic items prevails among the servant classes, particularly when the objects, whose value they do not understand, give them extra work to do. People of the same origin and educational attainments, on the other hand, often prove very skilful and reliable in handling delicate objects in scientific institutes once they have begun to identify with their employers and regard themselves as important members of staff.

当仆人不小心打碎易碎物品时，我们不会立刻想到某种心理学解释，但其中很可能隐藏着一些动机。对于缺乏教育的人来说，欣赏艺术和艺术品几乎是不可能的。仆人阶层普遍存在着对艺术品的隐性敌意，尤其当他们不理解这些物品的价值，反而因此需要额外工作时。另一方面，同样出身且受过良好教育的人，一旦开始认同雇主，并将自己视为重要成员，往往就能在科研机构中熟练可靠地处理易碎物品。

I will add here some remarks from a young technician which give us an insight into the mechanism whereby property can be wilfully damaged. ‘Some time ago I was working with several colleagues in the university laboratory on a set of complicated experiments on elasticity, a task for which we had volunteered, although it was beginning to take up more time than we had expected. One day, when I went into the laboratory with my colleague F., he said that today in particular he disliked losing so much time, for he had a great many other things to do at home; I could only agree with him, and said half jokingly, referring to something that had happened the week before: “Well, let’s hope the machinery goes wrong again so that we can stop work and go home early!” When our duties were allotted to us, it so happened that my colleague F. had to control the valve of the hydraulic press, which meant letting the liquid under pressure flow slowly out of the accumulator and into the cylinder by carefully opening the valve. The man in charge of the experiment was standing by the manometer and called out a loud “Stop!” when the right pressure was reached. At this command F. took the valve and turned it as hard as he could — to the left (all valves without exception are turned to the right to close them!). This made the full pressure of the accumulator suddenly felt in the press. The tubing was not adjusted to take it, and a connection burst — a perfectly harmless accident to the machinery, but enough to mean that we had to stop work for the day and go home. Characteristically, some time later, when we were talking about the incident, my friend F. said he could remember absolutely nothing about it, although I recalled it perfectly.’

我在此补充一位年轻技术员的一些评论，这些评论让我们得以了解财产被蓄意破坏的机制。“不久前，我和几位同事在大学实验室里做一系列关于弹性的复杂实验，这项任务是我们自愿承担的，尽管它比我们预想的要耗时得多。一天，我和同事F一起去实验室，他说他今天特别不喜欢浪费这么多时间，因为他家里还有很多其他事情要做；我只能表示同意，并半开玩笑地提到上周发生的一件事说：‘好吧，但愿机器再次出故障，这样我们就可以停止工作，早点回家了！’分配任务时，我的同事F碰巧要控制液压机的阀门，这意味着要小心地打开阀门，让加压液体缓慢地从蓄能器流入气缸。负责实验的人站在压力计旁边，大声喊道：停！”当压力达到设定值时，F. 听到指令后，一把抓住阀门，使劲向左拧（所有阀门无一例外都是向右拧才能关闭！）。这使得蓄压器内的全部压力瞬间传递到压力机上。由于管路没有做好承受压力的准备，连接处爆裂——虽然对机器来说只是个小事故，但足以让我们停工回家。后来，我们谈起这件事时，我的朋友 F. 说他完全不记得了，而我却记得清清楚楚。

Nor need falling over, stumbling and slipping always be interpreted as a purely accidental disturbance to one’s motor action. The double meaning of such an expression as faux pas in itself indicates the kind of concealed fantasies that can be betrayed when our physical equilibrium is lost in this way. I remember a number of mild nervous disorders in women and girls which manifested themselves after a harmless fall, and were regarded as traumatic hysteria resulting from the alarm they had felt at falling. Even then, I had the impression that this was not the real explanation, that the fall itself had been a result of neurosis, expressing those unconscious sexual fantasies which one might suspect to be the motive forces behind the symptoms. After all, there is a proverb that runs: ‘When a young lady falls, she falls on her back’, and which could be regarded in the same way.

跌倒、绊倒和滑倒并非总是被解读为纯粹的意外动作障碍。诸如“失礼”之类的表达本身就具有双重含义，暗示着当我们以这种方式失去身体平衡时，某些隐藏的幻想可能会暴露无遗。我记得一些女性和女孩在一次无害的跌倒后出现了轻微的神经紊乱，被认为是跌倒时惊恐引发的创伤性癔症。即使在当时，我也觉得这并非真正的解释，跌倒本身可能是神经症的结果，表达了那些潜意识中的性幻想，而这些幻想或许正是这些症状背后的驱动力。毕竟，有一句谚语说：“年轻女子跌倒时，总是仰面摔倒”，这也可以作同样的解读。

Cases in which we give a beggar a gold coin by mistake for a copper or small silver coin can also be described as inadvertent actions. It is easy enough to resolve the meaning of such slips; they are sacrifices intended to placate destiny, avert misfortune, and so forth. If a loving mother or aunt is heard expressing anxiety about a child’s health just before going for a walk, and on that walk she inadvertently gives generous alms in this way, there can be no doubt of the meaning of her apparent mistake. Such slips allow us to observe all those pious and superstitious customs that the conscious mind cannot now acknowledge, because our rational thinking rejects them with incredulity.

我们误将金币当作铜币或小银币施舍给乞丐的情况，也可以被描述为无意之举。这类失误的含义很容易理解：它们是为了祈求神灵庇佑、避免厄运等等而进行的施舍。如果一位慈爱的母亲或阿姨在出门散步前，正为孩子的健康忧心忡忡，而散步途中她无意间慷慨施舍，那么她这看似无心之失的含义便不言而喻。正是这类失误，让我们得以观察那些虔诚而迷信的习俗，而这些习俗如今却因我们理性思维的排斥而无法被意识所理解。

f) The fact that fortuitous actions are really intentional will be especially readily accepted in the field of sexual activity, where the borderline between chance and intention really does seem blurred. A few years ago I observed in myself a good example of the way in which an apparently clumsy movement can be subtly exploited for sexual ends. I was in a friend’s house, where I met a young girl who was also a guest and who aroused feelings in me that I had thought were long gone, thus putting me in a cheerful, talkative and forthcoming frame of mind. Even then I wondered why; a year before the same girl had left me cold. When her uncle, a very elderly gentleman, came into the room, we both jumped up to bring him a chair standing in a corner. She was nimbler than I, and probably closer to the armchair, so she got hold of it first and carried it over in front of her with the back towards her, both her hands on the sides of the chair. As I joined her, still claiming my own right to carry the chair, I was suddenly standing right behind her. I put both arms around her, so that my hands momentarily met in front of her lower belly. Of course I brought the situation to an end as quickly as it had arisen, and no one seemed to notice how skilfully I had exploited my unskilful movement.

f) 偶然行为实际上是有意为之这一事实，在性行为领域尤其容易被接受，因为在性行为领域，偶然与意图之间的界限确实模糊不清。几年前，我亲身经历了一个很好的例子，说明看似笨拙的动作是如何被巧妙地用于性目的的。当时我在朋友家，遇到了一位年轻女孩，她也是客人。她唤起了我以为早已消失的感情，让我心情愉悦，健谈且热情。即便如此，我当时仍然感到疑惑；就在一年前，同一个女孩还让我毫无感觉。当她的叔叔，一位非常年长的绅士走进房间时，我们俩都跳起来去帮他搬角落里的一把椅子。她比我更灵活，而且可能离扶手椅更近，所以她先拿到了椅子，椅背朝向自己，双手扶着椅子的两侧，把椅子搬到了身前。当我跟在她身后，仍然坚持自己也应该搬椅子时，我突然发现自己站在了她的身后。我双臂环住她，双手在她小腹前短暂地相触。当然，我很快就结束了这一切，似乎没有人注意到我是如何巧妙地利用了自己笨拙的动作。

I have also sometimes told myself that the annoying and clumsy attempt to avoid someone else in the street, when you step to one side or another for several seconds but always end up on the same side, until you are both left facing each other and ‘barring the way’, duplicates some earlier improper form of provocative conduct, pursuing sexual intentions in the guise of clumsiness. From my psychoanalysis of neurotics I know that what is regarded as naïveté in children and young people is often only a disguise of this kind, enabling them to express indecency directly and unimpeded by embarrassment.

我有时也会告诉自己，那种在街上笨拙地试图躲避他人，一会儿向左，一会儿向右，几秒钟后却总是回到同一侧，最后两人面对面，互相挡路的尴尬举动，其实是在重复某种早期的不当挑衅行为，以笨拙为幌子，实则怀有性目的。从我对神经症患者的心理分析中，我知道儿童和青少年身上所谓的“天真”往往只是这种伪装，使他们能够直接而毫无顾忌地表达不雅行为。

W. Stekel has made similar self-observations: ‘I entered someone’s home, and gave the lady of the house my right hand. Oddly enough, in the process I untied the bow holding her loose morning dress together. I was not aware of any dishonourable intentions, yet I had performed this unskilful movement with a conjuror’s sleight of hand.’

W·斯特克尔也曾有过类似的自我观察：“我走进别人家，向女主人伸出了右手。奇怪的是，在这个过程中，我解开了她宽松晨礼服上的蝴蝶结。我当时并没有任何不轨的意图，但我却用魔术师般的手法完成了这个笨拙的动作。”

I have repeatedly provided evidence that literary writers see various slips as being meaningful and motivated in the way I suggest here. It is not surprising, then, to find another example of a writer’s seeing significance in a clumsy movement and using it as an omen prefiguring later events.

我已多次提供证据，证明文学作家会将各种笔误视为有意义的，并赋予其我在此提出的理由。因此，我们也能找到另一个例子，证明作家会从笨拙的动作中发现意义，并将其作为预示后续事件的征兆。

In Theodor Fontane’s novel L’Adultera (vol. II, p. 64 of the Collected Works published by S. Fischer) we read: ‘[…] and Melanie jumped up and threw her husband one of the large balls, as if in greeting. But she had not aimed accurately, the ball flew to one side, and Rubehn caught it.’ On returning from the expedition that led up to this little incident, Melanie and Rubehn have a conversation which betrays the first signs of attraction between them. This attraction turns to passion, and Melanie finally leaves her husband to give herself entirely to the man she loves. (Contributed by H. Sachs.)

在西奥多·冯塔纳的小说《通奸者》（S. Fischer 出版的《冯塔纳全集》第二卷，第64页）中，我们读到：“……梅拉妮跳起来，把一个大球扔给她的丈夫，仿佛是在打招呼。但她没扔准，球飞到了一边，鲁本接住了。”在引发这件小事的探险结束后，梅拉妮和鲁本进行了一次谈话，谈话中流露出了他们之间最初的爱慕之情。这种爱慕之情逐渐转化为激情，梅拉妮最终离开了她的丈夫，全身心地投入到她所爱的男人身边。（H. Sachs 供稿）

g) The effects of inadvertent actions when perpetrated by normal people are usually of an extremely innocuous nature. For that very reason it is particularly interesting to see whether actions of this kind, which actually can have weighty and far-reaching consequences, for instance if perpetrated by a doctor or a pharmacist, come into these categories of ours in any way.

g) 普通人无意之举造成的后果通常微乎其微。正因如此，我们才格外关注那些可能造成重大而深远后果的行为，例如医生或药剂师的无意之举，它们是否也属于我们定义的范畴。

Since I very seldom practise as a physician, I can describe only one example of an inadvertent action in a medical context from personal experience. I had been visiting a very old lady twice a day for years, and my medical activity on my morning visit was confined to two procedures: I put a few eye-drops in one of her eyes and gave her a morphine injection. I had two little bottles regularly prepared and ready, a blue one for the collyrium and a white one for the morphine solution. During both procedures, my thoughts were usually elsewhere; I had carried them out so often that I did not need to give them my full attention. But one morning I noticed that in working automatically I had made a mistake: I had dipped the eye-dropper into the white bottle instead of the blue one and put morphine instead of collyrium in my patient’s eye. I was much alarmed, but then calmed myself by reflecting that a few drops of a 2 per cent morphine solution could do no harm even in the conjunctival sac. The reason for my sense of alarm was obviously to be sought elsewhere.

由于我很少行医，所以只能根据个人经历描述一个医疗事故的例子。多年来，我每天两次去看望一位老太太，每次早上我的诊疗工作都仅限于两项操作：给她一只眼睛滴几滴眼药水，然后注射吗啡。我事先准备好了两个小瓶子，一个蓝色的装眼药水，一个白色的装吗啡溶液。在进行这两项操作时，我的注意力通常都在别处；因为操作次数太多，我不需要全神贯注。但有一天早上，我突然意识到自己下意识地犯了个错误：我把滴管伸进了白色的瓶子里，而不是蓝色的瓶子里，结果把吗啡而不是眼药水滴进了病人的眼睛。我当时非常惊慌，但转念一想，即使滴进结膜囊里，几滴2%的吗啡溶液也不会有什么害处，便平静了下来。我的担忧显然另有原因。

In trying to analyse this little slip I thought first of the phrase sich an der Alten vergreifen [‘to assault the old woman’; vergreifen is also the verb for ‘performing inadvertent actions’, used here in German], which seemed the shortest way to the answer. I was still thinking of a dream told to me the previous evening by a young man, the content of which could only be interpreted as sexual intercourse with his own mother. 3 The curious fact that the classical legend does not seem to balk at Queen Jocasta’s age seems to me to bear out the idea that a sense of being in love with one’s own mother never relates to her person as she is now, but to her youthful image remembered from childhood. Such incongruities always appear when a fantasy oscillating between two periods comes into the conscious mind and becomes fixed on one of them. Deep in thoughts of this nature, I went to visit my patient, who was over ninety years old, and I must have been on my way to seeing the generally human character of the fable of Oedipus as corresponding to the destiny foretold by the oracles, for I did then ‘make the mistake’ of ‘committing an assault on’ the old lady [German: sich vergreifen , see above]. However, this slip was innocuous in itself: of the two possible mistakes, using the morphine solution as eye-drops or injecting the eye-drops into my patient, I had chosen by far the least harmful. But we still cannot say whether inadvertent actions that could in fact do severe damage can be traced back to an unconscious intention in a similar way to the one described above.

在试图分析这个小小的口误时，我首先想到了“sich an der Alten vergreifen”（意为“侵犯老妇人”；vergreifen 也是动词，意为“无意之举”，此处为德语），这似乎是找到答案的最直接途径。我当时还在想着前一天晚上一个年轻人跟我讲的一个梦，梦的内容只能被解读为与他自己的母亲发生性关系。 3 古典传说中似乎并没有对伊俄卡斯忒女王的年龄感到不安，这在我看来恰恰印证了这样一个观点：爱上自己的母亲，并非源于她现在的样子，而是源于童年记忆中她年轻时的形象。当一个在两个时期之间摇摆不定的幻想进入意识层面并最终定格在其中一个时期时，这种不协调之处总是会出现。我当时正沉浸在这样的思考中，于是去探望我的病人，她已经九十多岁了。我当时可能正逐渐意识到俄狄浦斯寓言中普遍存在的人性特征与神谕预言的命运相符，因为我当时确实犯了一个“错误”，那就是“冒犯”了这位老妇人（德语：sich vergreifen，见上文）。然而，这个失误本身并无大碍：在两种可能的错误中——把吗啡溶液当眼药水用，或者把眼药水注射到病人身上——我选择了危害最小的那一种。但是，我们仍然无法断定，那些实际上可能造成严重伤害的无意行为，是否也能像上述情况一样，追溯到某种无意识的意图。

For here, as might be expected, my own material lets me down, and I have to fall back on assumptions and conclusions. It is well known that self-injury is sometimes a symptom in severe cases of psychoneurosis, and that the ending of psychic conflict by suicide can never be excluded in such cases. I have known instances, well vouched for, of many apparently accidental injuries that are really self-inflicted, when a latent tendency to self-mortification, which is usually expressed in self-reproaches or contributes to the formation of symptoms, skilfully exploits an external situation that happens to offer itself, or gives it a little extra help to achieve the desired effect of injury. Such incidents are by no means rare even in cases of only moderate severity, and betray the part played by unconscious intentions through a series of particular features, for instance the notable composure with which the patients contemplate what they claim to have been accidents. 4

正如预料的那样，我自己的资料在这里并不充分，我不得不依赖假设和结论。众所周知，自残有时是严重精神神经症的症状，在这些病例中，以自杀结束精神冲突的可能性永远不能排除。我见过许多有据可查的案例，其中许多看似意外的伤害实际上是自残造成的。当潜在的自虐倾向（通常表现为自我责备或促成症状的形成）巧妙地利用偶然出现的外部环境，或为其提供一些额外的帮助以达到预期的伤害效果时，这种自虐倾向就会发生。即使在病情较轻的情况下，这类事件也绝非罕见，并且通过一系列特殊特征暴露出无意识意图的作用，例如，患者在思考他们声称是意外的事件时表现出的显著镇定。

I will give a detailed account of a single example from my medical experience, rather than citing several: a young woman broke one of her shinbones in a carriage accident, and was confined to her bed for weeks. A striking feature of her misfortune was the fact that she did not complain of the pain and bore it with equanimity. This accident led to her developing a severe neurotic disorder which lasted a long time, and of which she was finally cured by psychoanalysis. In treatment, I discovered the attendant circumstances of the accident, and certain incidents that had preceded it. The young woman and her husband, a very jealous man, were staying on her married sister’s estate in the company of her many other siblings and their spouses. One evening, in this close-knit family circle, she performed one of her party pieces, dancing a very good cancan to the plaudits of her relations but much to the displeasure of her husband, who whispered to her afterwards: ‘There you go again, behaving like a tart as usual!’ His accusations hit home; we will leave aside the question of whether he was referring only to her dancing. She slept poorly that night, and next morning said she would like to go for a drive. She chose the carriage-horses herself, rejecting one pair and demanding another. Her youngest sister wanted her baby and his nurse to go on the drive too, but she energetically opposed that idea. During the drive she acted nervously, warned the coachman that the horses were getting restive, and when the nervous animals really did create momentary trouble she jumped out of the carriage in alarm and broke her leg, while the others, who had stayed inside, got away unscathed. Once we know these details, can anyone doubt that this accident was really staged in advance? One has to admire the skill that caused the accident to make the punishment fit the crime so well, since the lady would not be able to dance a cancan for quite a long time to come.

我将详细讲述我行医经验中的一个案例，而不是列举多个：一位年轻女子在一次马车事故中胫骨骨折，卧床数周。她不幸遭遇的一个显著特点是，她没有抱怨疼痛，而是平静地忍受着。这次事故导致她患上了严重的神经症，持续了很长时间，最终通过精神分析治愈。在治疗过程中，我发现了事故发生的缘由，以及事故发生前的一些事件。这位年轻女子和她那极度嫉妒的丈夫，当时正和她的其他兄弟姐妹及配偶一起住在她已婚姐姐的庄园里。一天晚上，在这个亲密的家庭聚会上，她表演了她的拿手好戏——跳了一段精彩的康康舞，赢得了亲戚们的喝彩，却惹恼了她的丈夫。事后，他低声对她说：“你又来了，像往常一样像个荡妇！”他的指责让她如鲠在喉；我们暂且不讨论他是否仅仅是指她的舞姿。那天晚上她睡得很不好，第二天早上说想出去兜风。她亲自挑选马车的马匹，拒绝了一匹，又要求换一匹。她最小的妹妹想带上她的孩子和保姆一起去，但她极力反对。兜风途中，她表现得十分紧张，警告车夫说马匹开始躁动不安。当这些躁动的马匹真的制造了一些小麻烦时，她惊慌失措地跳下马车，摔断了腿，而留在车里的其他人却毫发无损。了解了这些细节之后，还有谁会怀疑这场意外是事先安排好的呢？不得不佩服制造这场意外的巧妙手法，使得惩罚与罪行如此相称，因为这位女士在很长一段时间内都无法跳康康舞了。

I cannot say that I have inflicted any injuries on myself at times when my mind is calm, but I find that they can happen under stress. If one of my family complains of having bitten his or her tongue, pinched a finger, or so on, I am inclined to ask: ‘What did you do that for?’ instead of offering the sympathy expected of me. I myself pinched my thumb very painfully after a young patient told me during his hour of treatment that he planned to many my eldest daughter (of course I did not take him seriously), while I knew that at that very moment she was lying in a sanatorium, in mortal danger of her life.

我不能说我在心境平静的时候会伤害自己，但我发现压力之下确实容易受伤。如果我的家人抱怨咬到舌头、夹到手指等等，我往往会问：“你为什么要这么做？”而不是像人们期望的那样表示同情。我自己也曾被一个年轻病人用一个小时的治疗时间狠狠地夹了一下拇指，当时他告诉我他打算杀了我的大女儿（当然我没当真），而我知道就在那一刻，她正躺在疗养院里，生命垂危。

One of my sons, whose lively temperament made it difficult for anyone to nurse him when he was unwell, fell into a temper one morning because he had been told to spend the morning in bed, and threatened to kill himself, an idea he had picked up from the newspaper. That evening he showed me a bump on his ribcage, caused when he ran into the door-handle. When I asked why he had done that, and what the idea of it was, my son, then aged eleven, said as if suddenly enlightened: ‘Oh, it was my suicide attempt, the one I threatened this morning.’ I do not think, incidentally, that my children knew anything about my views on self-inflicted injuries at the time.

我的一个儿子生性活泼好动，生病时很难照顾他。一天早上，因为被告知要卧床休息，他大发脾气，扬言要自杀——这个想法是他从报纸上看到的。那天晚上，他给我看他肋骨上的一个肿块，那是他撞到门把手造成的。我问他为什么要这么做，他的想法是什么，当时十一岁的儿子突然恍然大悟：“哦，那是我今天早上扬言要自杀的。”顺便说一句，我认为我的孩子们当时并不知道我对自残行为的看法。

Anyone who believes that semi-intentional self-inflicted injuries do happen — if I may be allowed that rather clumsy way of putting it — will be prepared to accept that besides conscious and intentional suicides there are also cases of semi-intentional suicide attempts, made for reasons unconsciously nurtured, ingeniously exploiting life-threatening situations and dismissing them as chance accidents. Such a thing is by no means uncommon. A suicide wish is present to some extent in many people who never actually try to kill themselves; self-inflicted injuries are generally a compromise between this drive and the forces countering it, and even when the suicide wish does prevail, a tendency in that direction has been present for a long time already, either to a lesser degree or as an unconscious, suppressed tendency.

任何相信半故意自残行为确实存在的人——如果我可以用这种略显笨拙的说法——都会接受这样一个事实：除了有意识的自杀之外，还存在一些半故意的自杀未遂案例，其动机源于潜意识中滋生的因素，巧妙地利用危及生命的处境，并将其归咎于偶然事故。这种情况并非罕见。许多从未真正尝试自杀的人，在某种程度上都存在自杀的念头；自残行为通常是这种冲动与阻碍它的力量之间的一种妥协，即便自杀的念头最终占据上风，这种倾向也早已存在，只是程度较轻，或者是一种无意识的、被压抑的倾向。

A conscious intention to commit suicide also picks its time, method and opportunity; it is entirely consistent with this for the unconscious intention to wait for an occasion that can act as the partial cause, freeing the intention from suppression by the subject’s powers of rejection by making other demands on them. 5 These ideas of mine are by no means put forward at random; I have heard of more than one case of what looked like a riding or carriage accident which, when more closely investigated, gave grounds for the suspicion that it was an unconscious suicide attempt. For instance, during a horse-race between some army officers, one officer fell and injured himself so badly that he died some days later. His behaviour when he returned to consciousness is striking in many respects, but even more remarkable was his conduct before the race. He was deeply depressed by the death of his mother, whom he had loved dearly, was overcome by fits of weeping in the company of his comrades, and told his close friends that he was tired of life, saying he planned to leave the army and go to fight in a war in Africa which had nothing to do with him. 6 Once a daring horseman, he now avoided riding whenever possible. Finally, he expressed gloomy forebodings before the race, although he could not back out, and, as I see it, it was not surprising that his presentiments came true. It may be objected that it was understandable for a man in a state of such nervous depression to be unable to control his mount as well as he would in full health. I agree entirely, but I would locate the mechanism of his motor inhibition by ‘nervousness’ in the intention of suicide which I have been describing here.

有意识的自杀意图也会选择时机、方法和机会；无意识的自杀意图也完全可以等待一个可以作为部分原因的契机，通过对主体提出其他要求，使其摆脱拒绝能力的压制。 5 我的这些想法绝非随意提出；我听说过不止一个案例，表面上看似骑马或马车事故，但经过更深入的调查后，却有理由怀疑这是一起无意识的自杀未遂事件。例如，在几位军官的赛马比赛中，一位军官摔倒并受了重伤，几天后去世。他恢复意识后的行为在很多方面都令人震惊，但更引人注目的是他在赛前的行为。他深爱的母亲去世，这让他悲痛欲绝。在战友面前，他常常嚎啕大哭，并告诉挚友自己厌倦了生活，打算离开军队，去非洲参加一场与他无关的战争。他曾经是一位英勇的骑手，如今却尽可能地避免骑马。最后，在比赛前，他表达了不祥的预感，尽管他已无退路。在我看来，他的预感成真并不令人意外。或许有人会反驳说，一个处于如此精神抑郁状态的人无法像健康时那样驾驭坐骑，这是可以理解的。我完全同意这种说法，但我认为他因“紧张”而导致的运动抑制机制，正是源于我在此描述的自杀意图。

S. Ferenczi of Budapest has let me see his analysis of a case of an apparently accidental shooting injury, which he interprets as an unconscious suicide attempt. I can only say that I agree with his interpretation:

布达佩斯的S. Ferenczi让我看了他对一起看似意外的枪伤案件的分析，他将其解读为无意识的自杀未遂。我只能说，我同意他的解读：

‘J. Ad., a journeyman cabinetmaker aged 22, came to see me on 18 January. He wanted me to tell him whether the bullet that had entered his left temple on 20 March 1907 could or should be removed by an operation. He felt perfectly well apart from occasional headaches, which were not too bad, and examination showed only the characteristic powder-blackened scar on his left temple caused by the entry of the bullet, so I advised against the operation. When I inquired into the circumstances of the case, he said he had shot himself by accident. He was playing with his brother’s revolver, thinking that it was not loaded , held it against his left temple with his left hand (he is not left-handed), put his finger on the hammer, and the gun went off. There were three cartridges in the revolver, which had six chambers. I asked him what induced him to pick up the revolver. He replied that he was about to be examined to see if he was physically fit to do his military service, and he had taken the gun to the tavern with him the evening before because he was afraid of a brawl. When the medical examination took place he was declared unfit for the army because of varicose veins, and felt deeply ashamed. He went home and fiddled about with the revolver, but without any intention of harming himself. Then the accident happened. When I made further inquiries, asking whether he was happy with his life in other respects, he sighed and told me that he was in love with a girl who returned his affection but had none the less left him; she had emigrated to America, just because she wanted to make some money. He would have liked to follow her, but his parents prevented him. His inamorata had left on 20 January 1907, two months before the incident, but despite all these suspect factors the patient insisted that the shot really had been an “accident”. I, however, am firmly convinced that his failure to look at the weapon to see if it was loaded before playing with it was psychically determined, and so was his self-inflicted injury. He was still under the depressing influence of his unhappy love affair, and obviously wanted to join the army in order to “forget”. It was when he was deprived of even this hope that the game with the gun occurred — or, rather, that he made his unconscious suicide attempt. The fact that he held the revolver in his left and not his right hand strongly supports the idea that he really was just “playing”, that is to say, he did not consciously mean to commit suicide.’

“22岁的木工学徒J. Ad.于1月18日来找我。他想问我，1907年3月20日射入他左侧太阳穴的子弹是否可以通过手术取出。除了偶尔头痛（程度并不严重）之外，他感觉身体一切正常。检查发现，他左侧太阳穴上只有子弹射入时留下的火药熏黑的疤痕，所以我建议他不要手术。当我询问他的情况时，他说他是意外走火。他当时在玩他哥哥的左轮手枪，以为枪里没有子弹，就用左手（他不是左撇子）把枪抵在左侧太阳穴上，手指碰到了击锤，结果枪走火了。那把左轮手枪有六个弹膛，里面有三发子弹。我问他当时为什么会拿起那把枪。”他回答说，他正准备接受体检，看看是否适合服兵役。前一天晚上，他因为害怕打架，所以把枪带到了酒馆。体检结果显示他患有静脉曲张，不适合参军，他为此感到非常羞愧。他回家后摆弄着那把左轮手枪，但并没有伤害自己的意图。然后，意外发生了。当我进一步询问他是否对生活的其他方面感到满意时，他叹了口气，告诉我他爱上了一个女孩，女孩也爱他，但最终还是离开了他；她移民去了美国，只是为了挣点钱。他很想追随她，但父母阻止了他。他的爱人在1907年1月20日离开了他，也就是事发两个月前。尽管有这么多疑点，病人仍然坚称那次枪击真的是“意外”。然而，我坚信，他玩弄枪支前没有查看是否上膛，是出于某种心理因素，他的自残行为也是如此。他仍然深受那段不幸恋情的折磨，显然想参军以“忘却”痛苦。当他连这点希望都破灭时，他才玩弄枪支——或者更确切地说，他无意识地试图自杀。他用左手而不是右手握枪这一事实，有力地佐证了他当时只是在“玩”，也就是说，他并非有意自杀。

Another analysis of an injury apparently self-inflicted by chance was given to me by an observer, and reminds one of the saying: ‘He who digs a pit for others may fall into it himself.’

一位观察者向我提供了另一份关于一起显然是偶然造成的自残伤情的分析，这让我想起一句谚语：“为别人挖坑的人，自己可能会掉进去。”

‘Frau X., of a good middle-class background, was married with three children. She was slightly neurotic but had never needed intensive treatment, since she was able to cope with life well enough. One day she disfigured her face temporarily, but for the time being rather obviously, as follows. She tripped over a pile of stones in a street where the road was being mended, and struck her face against the wall of a building. It was badly scratched, her eyelids were blue and bruised, and feeling afraid that her eyes themselves might be damaged she called me in as a physician. When I had set her mind at rest on that point I asked: “But what made you fall like that?” She said that just before she went out she had warned her husband, who for some months had suffered from a disorder of the joints which made him unsteady on his feet, to take good care if he was walking along that street, and she had often noticed that when she warned someone else against an accident, she suffered the very same accident herself.

X女士出身于不错的中产阶级家庭，已婚，育有三个孩子。她略微有些神经质，但从未接受过强化治疗，因为她基本能够应对生活。有一天，她的脸暂时毁容了，但当时伤势相当明显，事情经过如下：她在一条正在修路的街道上被一堆石头绊倒，脸撞到了一栋建筑物的墙上。她的脸被划伤得很厉害，眼睑青紫淤青，她担心自己的眼睛也会受伤，于是请我来给她看病。我让她放心后，问道：“那您为什么会摔倒呢？”她说，就在她出门前，她叮嘱过她的丈夫——他几个月来一直患有关节疾病，走路不稳——如果要在那条街上行走，一定要格外小心。她还注意到，每当她提醒别人注意安全时，自己往往也会遭遇同样的意外。

‘I was not satisfied with this explanation of her accident, and asked whether she could tell me anything else. Well, yes: just before the accident she had seen a pretty picture in a shop on the opposite side of the street, and all of a sudden she thought it would look nice hanging in her children’s room. She decided to buy it at once, went straight towards the shop, forgetting to look down at the road surface, stumbled over the pile of stones and fell against the wall of the building, without making the slightest attempt to protect herself with her hands. She immediately forgot about wanting to buy the picture, and went straight home. “But why didn’t you take more notice of the road surface?” I asked. “Well,” she said, “perhaps it was a punishment ! Because of that incident — the one I told you about in confidence.” “Does it still haunt your mind, then?” “Oh yes — afterwards I regretted it very much, I felt I was wicked, criminal and immoral, but I was quite beside myself with my poor nerves at the time.”

“我对她关于事故的解释并不满意，便问她是否还有其他补充。她说，就在事故发生前，她在街对面的一家商店里看到一幅漂亮的画，突然觉得挂在孩子们的房间里一定很好看。她立刻决定买下它，径直朝商店走去，却忘了看路面，结果被一堆石头绊倒，撞到了建筑物的墙上，连用手保护自己的动作都没有。她立刻就把买画的事忘了，直接回家了。“可是你为什么不注意路面呢？”我问。“嗯，”她说，“也许是惩罚吧！因为那件事——就是我私下跟你说的那件事。”“那件事现在还让你耿耿于怀吗？”“哦，是的——事后我非常后悔，觉得自己很坏，很像罪犯，很不道德，但我当时神经紧张，完全失去了理智。”

‘The incident of which we were speaking was an abortion that she had undergone with her husband’s consent, since their financial situation meant they did not want to be blessed with any more offspring. It had been induced by a back-street abortionist, but had to be concluded by a qualified specialist.

“我们谈论的这件事是她经丈夫同意堕胎，因为他们的经济状况不允许他们再要孩子。堕胎手术是由一名非法堕胎医生进行的，但最终必须由一名合格的专家来完成。”

“‘I often tell myself reproachfully: you had your baby killed, didn’t you? I was afraid something like that couldn’t go unpunished. Now that you’ve told me I shan’t have any trouble with my eyes, I feel much better: I’ve been punished enough as it is.”

“我常常责备自己：你害死了你的孩子，对吗？我害怕这种事不能逍遥法外。现在你告诉我我的眼睛不会有问题，我感觉好多了：我已经受够了惩罚。”

‘In one way, therefore, this accident was a punishment in penance for her sin, but in another it was self-inflicted to escape punishment of an unknown nature and perhaps much worse, something she had been constantly fearing for months. Just as she hurried towards the shop to buy the picture her memory of the whole incident, with all her fears, which had been working quite strongly in her unconscious as she warned her husband about the street, got the upper hand. Her thinking might perhaps be put into words along these lines: why would you need something pretty for your children’s room? You had your own child killed! You’re a murderess! Punishment is surely on its way!

因此，从某种意义上说，这场意外是她对罪孽的惩罚；但从另一个角度来看，这又是她自找的，为了逃避某种未知的、或许更可怕的惩罚——几个月来，她一直生活在恐惧之中。就在她匆匆走向商店准备买画的时候，她脑海中浮现出整个事件的记忆，以及所有恐惧——这些恐惧在她潜意识里一直强烈地涌现，就像她之前警告丈夫注意那条街一样。她的想法或许可以这样概括：你为什么要给孩子的房间买漂亮的东西？你自己的孩子被你害死了！你是个杀人犯！惩罚肯定快到了！

‘This thought did not reach her conscious mind, but instead she took the occasion at what might be called this psychological moment of punishing herself, making surreptitious use of the pile of stones, which seemed just the right means to her end; as a result she did not even put out her hands to save herself as she fell, nor did she feel too badly frightened. The second and probably less important factor in causing her accident was self-punishment for her unconscious wish to see her husband removed from the scene — for he, after all, had been a guilty party too. She had given away that wish in her warning to him to take great care in the street where the stones were lying about, which was quite unnecessary, since for the very reason that he was not good on his feet her husband took great care in walking.’ 7

“这个念头并未进入她的意识，相反，她借此机会，或许可以称之为自我惩罚的心理时刻，偷偷地利用了那堆石头，这似乎是达到目的的绝佳手段；结果，她摔倒时甚至没有伸出手来保护自己，也没有感到太过害怕。导致她发生意外的第二个因素，或许也是次要的因素，是她潜意识里希望丈夫离开现场的愿望——毕竟，他也是肇事者之一。她曾警告丈夫在满是石头的街道上要格外小心，这其实完全没有必要，因为正因为他腿脚不好，所以走路才格外小心。”

If we look at all the circumstances of the next case, we shall be inclined to agree with J. Stärcke (op. cit.) when he describes a burn apparently self-inflicted by chance as a ‘sacrificial action’:

如果我们审视下一个案例的所有情况，我们就会倾向于同意 J. Stärcke（同上）的观点，他将看似偶然造成的自残性烧伤描述为一种“献祭行为”：

‘A lady whose son-in-law had to go to do his military service in Germany scalded her foot in the following way. Her daughter was soon to have a baby, and the thought of the dangers of war naturally did nothing to cheer the family as a whole. The day before her son-in-law left she had asked him and her daughter to dinner. She cooked the meal herself in her own kitchen, but first, oddly enough, changed out of her high laced boots with their instep raisers, in which she could walk comfortably and which she usually wore at home, and put on a pair of her husband’s slippers. The slippers were too large for her and were open on top. As she was taking a large pan of boiling soup off the heat she dropped it, scalding one foot quite badly, including the back of it, which was not protected by the open slipper. Naturally everyone put this accident down to her understandably “nervous” state. For the first few days after making this “burnt offering” she was very careful with anything hot, which did not prevent her from scalding her wrist with hot broth a few days later.’ 8

一位女士的女婿要去德国服兵役，结果她烫伤了脚，事情经过是这样的。她的女儿即将临盆，想到战争的危险，全家人自然都忧心忡忡。女婿出发的前一天，她邀请他和女儿来家吃晚饭。她亲自在厨房做饭，但奇怪的是，她先脱掉了平时在家穿的、带鞋垫的高筒系带靴（这双靴子走路很舒服），换上了丈夫的拖鞋。这双拖鞋对她来说太大了，而且鞋面是敞开的。当她把一大锅滚烫的汤从火上拿下来时，锅掉在了地上，烫伤了一只脚，包括脚后跟，因为脚后跟没有被敞开的拖鞋保护。大家都把这起意外归咎于她紧张不安的状态。在献上这“燔祭”后的头几天，她对任何热的东西都非常小心，但这并没有阻止她在几天后被热肉汤烫伤手腕。

When anger like this directed against one’s own integrity and even one’s own life can be concealed by apparently chance clumsiness and motor inadequacy, it is not such a very great step further to believing it possible that the same concept is at work in slips which seriously endanger the life and health of others. The evidence I can produce for the validity of this idea comes from my experience with neurotics, and therefore does not entirely comply with my present requirements. I will describe a case of what was not exactly an inadvertent action, but rather what may be called a symptomatic or fortuitous action, and which put me on the right lines to enable me to resolve my patient’s conflict. I was once trying to improve the marriage of a very intelligent man who certainly had some genuine reasons for his quarrels with his young wife, who loved him dearly, but as he admitted himself those reasons did not fully explain the situation. He was constantly dwelling on ideas of divorce, which he then ruled out again because he loved his two small children so much. None the less, he kept coming back to the idea, and would try no means of making the marriage tolerable for himself. I saw this inability to deal with a conflict as evidence that unconscious and repressed motives had already reinforced the opposing conscious motives, and in such cases I try to resolve the conflict by psychic analysis. The man told me one day about a small incident that had alarmed him very much. He was romping about with his elder child, who was easily his favourite, swinging him up and down in the air, and once, from a certain place in the room, he swung the child up so high that the top of his head almost hit the heavy gas chandelier hanging from the ceiling. Almost, but not quite — or had it? No harm had come to the child, but he was quite dizzy with alarm. The father stood there, horrified, with the child in his arms, the mother became hysterical. The particular dexterity of this incautious movement and the parents’ extreme reactions suggested that the accident should be seen as a symptomatic action expressing ill-will towards a much-loved child. I could remove any contradiction between that action and the father’s present real love for his child if I transferred the impulse to harm him back to the period when this son was the only child, and still too small for his father to need to take an affectionate interest in him. Then I could easily suppose that at the time the husband, left unsatisfied by his wife, thought or projected something along these lines: I’m not at all fond of this little creature; if he died I should be free and could get a divorce from my wife. Unconsciously, therefore, he must still wish for the death of the child he now loved so much. It was easy to find my way from here to the manner in which the wish became an unconscious fixation. A powerful motive existed in my patient’s childhood memory of his own little brother’s death; their mother had blamed their father’s negligence for it, and as a result there were violent arguments between his parents, accompanied by threats of divorce. The successful effect of my therapy on the subsequent course of my patient’s marriage confirmed my deductions.

当这种针对自身尊严乃至生命的愤怒能够被看似偶然的笨拙和动作迟缓所掩盖时，我们很容易推断，同样的道理也可能体现在那些严重危及他人生命健康的失误之中。我所能提供的证据来自我与神经症患者的接触经验，因此并不完全符合我目前的要求。我将描述一个案例，这并非完全是无意的行为，而更像是一种症状性或偶然性的行为，正是它让我找到了正确的方向，从而能够解决患者的冲突。我曾经试图改善一位非常聪明的男士的婚姻。他与深爱他的年轻妻子争吵，这当然有他自己的理由，但他自己也承认，这些理由并不能完全解释目前的状况。他不断地想着离婚，但又因为深爱着两个年幼的孩子而放弃了这个念头。然而，他始终无法释怀，也不愿尝试任何方法来改善自己的婚姻状况。我认为他无法处理冲突，这表明潜意识中被压抑的动机已经强化了与之对立的意识动机。在这种情况下，我会尝试通过心理分析来解决冲突。有一天，他跟我讲了一件让他非常惊恐的小事。他正和自己最疼爱的大儿子玩耍，把孩子在空中荡来荡去。有一次，他从房间的某个位置把孩子甩得很高，孩子的头几乎撞到了天花板上沉重的煤气吊灯。几乎撞到了，但又没撞到——或者说，真的撞到了吗？孩子虽然没有受伤，但却惊恐万分，头晕目眩。父亲抱着孩子站在那里，惊恐万分，母亲则歇斯底里地哭喊起来。这种鲁莽动作的特殊技巧以及父母的极端反应表明，这起事故应被视为一种症状性行为，表达了对深爱孩子的恶意。如果我将伤害孩子的冲动追溯到儿子还是独生子、年幼到父亲无需对他倾注爱意的时期，就能消除这种行为与父亲如今对孩子真挚的爱之间的任何矛盾。这样，我就可以很容易地推断，当时丈夫因妻子的不满而心存不满，并可能这样想或投射：我一点也不喜欢这个小家伙；如果他死了，我就自由了，可以和妻子离婚。因此，在潜意识里，他一定仍然希望他现在如此深爱的孩子死去。由此很容易找到这种愿望如何演变成一种无意识的执念。我的病人童年时期弟弟去世的记忆中存在着一个强大的动机；他们的母亲将此事归咎于父亲的疏忽，结果导致父母之间爆发激烈争吵，甚至有人扬言要离婚。我的治疗对这位患者婚姻后续发展的成功效果证实了我的推断。

J. Stärcke (op. cit) gave an example of the way in which writers may have no scruples in substituting an inadvertent action for an intentional action, in such a way as to cause the most serious consequences:

J. Stärcke（同上）举例说明了作家们如何毫无顾忌地用无意的行为代替有意的行为，从而造成最严重的后果：

‘A sketch by Heyermans 9 contains an example of an inadvertent action, or more precisely a blunder, which the author takes as a dramatic subject.

“Heyermans 9 的一幅素描包含了无意之举的例子，或者更准确地说，是一个失误，作者将其作为戏剧主题。

‘The sketch is called “Tom and Teddie”, and the characters are a couple of divers performing in a variety theatre, with an act in which they stay under water for a long time and do tricks in an iron tank with glass sides. One of the couple, the wife, has been having an affair with another man, an animal trainer. The husband has just caught them together in the dressing room before the performance. They freeze, threatening glances are exchanged, and the male diver says: “Just wait till later!” The performance begins. The husband is about to do his most difficult trick, staying, as the sketch announces, “two and a half minutes under water in a hermetically sealed container”. It is a trick they have often done before, the container is closed, and “Teddie” — the wife — “shows the audience the key as they began checking the time on their watches.” She also drops the key into the tank a couple of times on purpose, and then dives quickly in after it so as to be on the spot when the tank is ready to be opened.

这段小品名为《汤姆和泰迪》，讲述的是一对在综艺剧院表演的潜水员夫妇的故事。他们的节目是在一个四面都是玻璃的铁罐里长时间待在水下，表演各种特技。其中一位夫妇，也就是妻子，与另一位驯兽师有染。演出前，丈夫在化妆间撞见了他们在一起。两人僵住不动，互相怒目而视，男潜水员说道：“等着瞧吧！”演出开始了。丈夫即将表演他最难的特技——正如小品介绍所说，要在“一个密封的容器里待上两分半钟”。这个特技他们以前经常表演，容器已经关闭，“泰迪”（妻子）“在观众开始看表的时候，向他们展示了钥匙”。她还故意把钥匙掉进罐子里几次，然后迅速潜入水中去捡，以便在罐子准备打开时能立刻抓住它。

‘On the evening of 31 January, Tom had been locked in, as usual, by his merry little wife’s nimble fingers. He was smiling behind the peep-hole — she was playing with the key, waiting for him to give the signal. Backstage stood the third party in the eternal triangle, the animal trainer in his immaculate frock-coat with his white tie and riding whip. He gave a brief whistle to attract her attention. She looked at him, smiled, and with the clumsiness of someone whose attention is distracted threw the key into the air so wildly that it fell beside the tank, after exactly two minutes twenty seconds of the show by a careful count, and landed on the bunting covering the trestles. No one had seen it. Indeed, no one could see it. The view from the auditorium produced an optical illusion: the audience all thought they had seen the key fall into the water — and none of the scene shifters noticed, because the bunting deadened the sound.

1月31日晚，汤姆像往常一样被他那快乐的小妻子用灵巧的手指锁在了里面。他透过窥视孔微笑着——她正摆弄着钥匙，等着他发出信号。后台站着永恒三角关系中的第三者，动物驯养员，身穿一丝不苟的礼服，系着白色领结，手持马鞭。他吹了一声短促的口哨，引起她的注意。她看了他一眼，笑了笑，然后像个心不在焉的人一样笨拙地把钥匙扔向空中，钥匙飞得如此之快，以至于在演出开始两分二十秒后，正好落在水箱旁边，落在了覆盖着支架的彩旗上。没有人看到。事实上，没有人能看到。从观众席上看，产生了一种视觉错觉：所有观众都以为自己看到钥匙掉进了水里——而没有一个换景人员注意到，因为彩旗隔绝了声音。

‘Smiling, without hesitation, Teddie climbed over the rim of the tank. Smiling — Tom was doing well — she climbed down the ladder. Smiling, she disappeared to look under the trestles, and on failing to find the key at once, she bowed, standing at the front of the bunting-covered trestles with a scene-stealing expression on her face as if saying, “Oh, what a bore this is!”

泰迪毫不犹豫地笑着爬过了水箱边缘。她笑着——汤姆做得很好——又顺着梯子爬了下来。她笑着消失在支架下面，一时没找到钥匙，便鞠了一躬，站在挂满彩旗的支架前，脸上带着一种抢尽风头的表情，仿佛在说：“哦，真是无聊透了！”

‘Meanwhile, Tom was making funny faces behind the peep-hole, as if he too were becoming uneasy. The spectators could see the white gleam of his false teeth, his lips working beneath his blond moustache, the comic bubble-blowing act he had done before when eating an apple. They could see his white knuckles as his hands clutched and contorted, and they roared with laughter as they had done before that evening.

与此同时，汤姆在窥视孔后面做着鬼脸，好像他也开始感到不安。旁观者能看到他假牙闪着白光，金色的胡子下嘴唇翕动，还有他之前吃苹果时吹泡泡的滑稽动作。他们能看到他紧握着、扭动着的双手，指节都泛白了，于是像那天晚上之前那样，他们哄堂大笑起来。

‘Two minutes fifty-eight seconds …

“两分五十八秒……”

‘Three minutes seven seconds … twelve seconds…

“三分七秒……十二秒……”

‘Bravo! Bravo! Bravo!

“好极了！好极了！好极了！”

‘But then there was dismay in the theatre, and feet began scraping on the floor as the scene shifters and the animal trainer began looking for the key too. The curtain fell before the tank was opened.

“但随后剧院里一片混乱，工作人员开始在地板上拖拽脚步声，舞台布景员和动物驯养员也开始寻找钥匙。水箱还没打开，幕布就落下了。”

‘Next on stage were six English dancing girls — then the man with the ponies, the dogs and the monkeys, and so on.

“接下来上台的是六位英国舞蹈女孩——然后是牵着小马、狗和猴子的男人，等等。”

‘Only next morning did the public learn that there had been an accident, and Teddie was now a widow…

“直到第二天早上，公众才得知发生了意外，泰迪成了寡妇……”

‘The sketch described above clearly shows how well its author must have understood the nature of a symptomatic action, enabling him to present so cogent an account of the underlying cause of the fatal act of clumsiness.’

“上面描述的草图清楚地表明，作者一定对症状性行为的性质理解得非常透彻，这使他能够对致命的笨拙行为的根本原因做出如此令人信服的解释。”

Notes

笔记

1 . A second publication by Meringer later showed me that I had misjudged this author in assuming that he had such an understanding of the subject.

1. 后来梅林格的第二篇出版物让我意识到，我之前误判了这位作者，以为他对该主题有如此深刻的理解。

2 . Internationale Zeitschrift für Psychoanalyse I, 1913.

2.国际精神分析杂志I，1913年。

3 . I call it ‘the Oedipal dream’ because it provides the key to understanding the legend of King Oedipus. In the play by Sophocles, the connection with such a dream is put into Jocasta’s own mouth. (Cf. The Interpretation of Dreams [V.D], p. 182. ( Gesammelte Werke , 8th edition.)

3. 我称之为“俄狄浦斯之梦”，因为它为理解俄狄浦斯王的传说提供了关键。在索福克勒斯的戏剧中，这种梦境的关联是通过伊俄卡斯忒的口述表达出来的。（参见《梦的解析》[V.D]，第182页。（索福克勒斯全集，第8版。）

4 . Self-injury falling short of suicide has no choice in our present civilized state but to conceal itself behind an appearance of accident, or make itself felt by simulating some ailment that has arisen spontaneously. In the past it was a customary sign of mourning, or could sometimes express piety and renunciation of the world.

4. 在当今文明社会，未达到自杀程度的自残行为别无选择，只能伪装成意外事故，或假装患有某种突发疾病。过去，自残是哀悼的习俗，有时也表达虔诚和遁世的愿望。

5 . In essence, this case is like that of a sexual attack on a woman in which all the woman’s muscular strength cannot prevail against the man’s violence because some part of the victim’s unconscious emotions is encouraging him. It is sometimes said that in such a situation the woman’s strength is paralysed ; we need only add the reasons for this paralysis. Here the amusing judgement passed by Sancho Panza in his capacity as governor of his island is psychologically inaccurate ( Don Quijote , part II, chapter XLV). A woman drags a man before the judge, claiming that he has robbed her of her honour by violence. Sancho provides her with compensation in the form of the full purse he takes from the accused man, and once she has left gives the man permission to run after her and snatch the purse away again. They both come back struggling, and the woman boasts that the wicked fellow had not been able to get hold of her purse. To which Sancho replies: ‘If you had defended your honour half as hard as that purse, the man could not have robbed you of it.’

5. 本质上，这起案件类似于女性遭受性侵犯，女性的所有力量都无法战胜男性的暴力，因为受害者潜意识中的某些情绪在纵容他。有时人们会说，在这种情况下，女性的力量被麻痹了；我们只需补充造成这种麻痹的原因即可。桑丘·潘萨作为岛屿总督所作出的滑稽判决，在心理学上是不准确的（《堂吉诃德》，第二部，第四十五章）。一位女子将一名男子拖到法官面前，声称他用暴力夺走了她的名誉。桑丘将他从被告男子那里拿走的全部钱袋作为补偿，并在女子离开后允许该男子追上去再次抢走钱袋。两人扭打着回来，女子得意洋洋地说，那个恶棍没能抢到她的钱袋。桑乔回答说：“如果你捍卫荣誉的决心有捍卫那只钱包一半的决心，那人就抢不到你的钱包了。”

6 . It is a plausible idea that the battlefield is a situation conducive to a conscious intention of committing suicide, which none the less shrinks from taking the direct way. Cf., in Wallenstein , the Swedish captain’s words on the death of Max Piccolomini: ‘They say he wished to die.’

6. 战场环境容易使人产生自杀的意识，但这种意识往往会避免直接自杀，这种观点不无道理。例如，瓦伦斯坦记载了瑞典上尉马克斯·皮科洛米尼之死，他说：“据说他想死。”

7 . Van Emden, ‘Selbstbestrafung für Abortus’ [‘Self-punishment for Abortion’], Zentralblatt für Psychoanalyse II/12. A correspondent writes, on the subject of ‘self-punishment by slips’: ‘Watching the way people behave in the street, one can see how often men who — as they commonly do — glance at women walking by suffer some small accident. A man may sprain his ankle, even on level ground, or bump into a lamp-post, or hurt himself in some other way.’

7. Van Emden，《堕胎的自我惩罚》，《精神分析中心杂志》II/12。一位通讯员就“因失误而自我惩罚”这一主题写道：“观察人们在街上的行为，你会发现，那些经常会瞥一眼路过女性的男人，往往会遭遇一些小意外。即使在平地上，男人也可能扭伤脚踝，或者撞到路灯柱，或者以其他方式受伤。”

8 . In a very great number of such cases of accidental injury or death the interpretation is doubtful. Those at a distance from the accident will see no reason to regard it as anything but chance, while someone close to and with intimate knowledge of the victim will have grounds to suspect the unconscious intention behind it. The following account by a young man whose fiancée was run down in the street is a good example of the kind of knowledge I mean, and the other circumstances involved:

8. 在很多此类意外伤亡案件中，其解释都令人怀疑。远离事故现场的人会认为这只是一场意外，而与受害者关系密切、了解其生平的人则会有理由怀疑背后存在某种无意识的意图。以下是一位年轻人的叙述，他的未婚妻在街上被车撞倒，这很好地体现了我所说的这种了解以及其他相关情况：

‘In September last year I met a Fräulein Z., aged 34. She lived in comfortable circumstances, and had been engaged before the war, but her fiancé, an officer on active service, fell in 1916. We came to know and love each other, at first without any idea of marriage, since the circumstances did not seem to either of us to admit it on account of the age difference — I myself was 27. Since we lived opposite each other in the same street, and saw one another every day, our friendship eventually became intimate. At this point the idea of getting married became more likely, and I finally thought it would be a good idea myself. We were going to get engaged at Easter of that year, but first Fräulein Z. intended to visit her relations in M. However, a railway workers’ strike resulting from the Kapp putsch prevented her from going. The dismal long-term prospects that the workers’ victory and its consequences held out were soon reflected in our own minds, more particularly by Fräulein Z., since she thought she saw new obstacles in our way. On Saturday 20 March, however, she was in an exceptionally cheerful frame of mind, a circumstance which quite surprised me, so that I too was swept away by it, and we thought we saw everything in the rosiest of hues. A few days earlier we had spoken of going to church together some time, without fixing on a definite date. Next morning, Sunday 21 March, around 9.15 a.m., she called me by telephone asking me to call for her and we would go to church at once, but I objected, since I could not have been ready in time, and anyway I had work to do. Fräulein Z. was very disappointed, set off by herself, met an acquaintance on the steps outside her house and went with him the short way through Tauentzienstrasse to Rankestrasse in a cheerful enough mood, without saying anything about our conversation. The gentleman said goodbye, making a joke as he did so. Fräulein Z. now had only to cross the Kurfürstendamm, which had been broadened just there, giving a good view — when she was run over close to the pavement by a horse-drawn cab (her liver suffered contusions and she died a few hours later). We had crossed the road here hundreds of times before; Fräulein Z. was very careful and had often kept me back when I made an incautious move, that morning there were almost no vehicles about, since the trams, omnibuses, etc., were on strike — there was almost absolute calm at the time, and the cab-driver must have heard her even if he couldn’t see her. Everyone thought it was an accident. My own first reaction was: impossible — how could anyone say she did it on purpose? But I looked for a psychological explanation, and after a while I thought I had found it in your Psychopathology of Everyday Life. In addition, Fräulein Z. had sometimes expressed certain suicidal tendencies, and had also tried to infect me with them. I had often enough talked her out of such thoughts. Two days earlier, for instance, on coming back from a walk, she had begun to speak for no reason at all of her death and of making a will, although she had not in fact done so — a sign that she was certainly not serious about what she said. If I may express my own humble opinion, I should say that I see this accident not as chance, and not as the effect of a clouding of the conscious mind, but as an intentional suicide carried out with unconscious intention, masquerading as an accident. I was supported in this opinion by what Fräulein Z. had said about her relations, both earlier, when she did not know me, and later, as also expressed to me up to those last days — all to be understood as arising from the loss of her first fiancé, whom nothing could replace in her eyes.’

去年九月，我遇到了34岁的Z小姐。她家境优渥，战前就已订婚，但她的未婚夫是一名现役军官，于1916年阵亡。我们相识相恋，起初并没有结婚的打算，因为年龄差距太大，我们都觉得结婚不太合适——我当时27岁。由于我们住在同一条街的对面，每天都能见面，我们的友谊逐渐发展成了亲密关系。这时，结婚的想法越来越强烈，我也最终觉得这是个好主意。我们原本打算在那年复活节订婚，但Z小姐想先去M探望亲戚。然而，卡普政变引发的铁路工人罢工使她无法成行。工人的胜利及其后果所带来的黯淡的长期前景很快也反映在我们自己心中，尤其是Z小姐，因为她觉得我们前进的道路上又出现了新的障碍。然而，3月20日星期六，她却异常高兴，这让我十分意外，我也被她的好心情感染，觉得一切都充满了希望。几天前，我们曾谈到要一起去教堂，但没有确定具体日期。第二天早上，3月21日星期日，大约9点15分，她打电话给我，让我去接她，我们马上就去教堂。但我拒绝了，因为我肯定来不及准备，而且我还有工作要做。 Z小姐非常失望，独自出发，在她家门外的台阶上遇到了一位熟人，两人心情愉快地沿着陶恩齐恩大街走到兰克大街，只字未提我们之前的谈话。那位先生道别时还开了个玩笑。Z小姐现在只需穿过库尔弗斯滕大街，这条街刚刚拓宽，视野开阔——就在这时，她被一辆马车撞倒在人行道附近（肝脏挫伤，几个小时后去世）。我们以前在这里过马路不下百次；Z小姐非常谨慎，我稍有不慎，她都会拦住我。那天早上路上几乎没有车辆，因为电车、公共汽车等等都在罢工——当时一片寂静，马车司机即使看不到她，也一定听到了她的声音。大家都以为这是一场意外。我的第一反应是：不可能——怎么会有人说她是故意的呢？但我还是试图从心理学的角度去解释，过了一段时间，我觉得在您的《日常生活心理病理学》一书中找到了答案。此外，Z小姐有时也表现出一些自杀倾向，甚至试图把这种倾向传染给我。我经常劝阻她放弃这些想法。比如，两天前，她散步回来后，突然毫无征兆地开始谈论自己的死亡和立遗嘱的事，尽管她实际上并没有立遗嘱——这表明她对她说的话显然并不认真。如果允许我发表一下我个人的看法，我认为这起事故并非偶然，也并非意识模糊所致，而是一场无意识的蓄意自杀，伪装成一场意外。 Z小姐曾向我讲述过她的人际关系，这更加坚定了我的这种看法。无论是在她还不认识我的时候，还是后来直到她生命的最后几天，她都曾这样告诉我——这一切都源于她失去了第一任未婚夫，在她眼中，没有人能够取代他。

9 . Hermann Heyermans, Schetsen van Samuel Falkland , 18th bundle, Amsterdam, H. J. W. Becht, 1914.

9. Hermann Heyermans，《塞缪尔·福克兰素描集》，第 18 卷，阿姆斯特丹，H. J. W. Becht，1914 年。
