5）我将再多花些时间分析与数字相关的想法，因为我尚未发现其他任何孤立的观察结果能如此有力地证明意识无法触及的极其复杂的思维过程的存在，也未发现其他任何分析案例能如此明确地排除医生（通过暗示）的影响——这种影响常常被怀疑——的可能性。因此，在征得他的同意后，我将讲述一位病人提出的数字想法的分析过程。关于他，我只需说明一下：他是家中最小的孩子，在他很小的时候就失去了他非常敬仰的父亲。在一次心情特别愉悦的状态下，他想到了数字426718，并问自己：“现在，我会把什么与这个数字联系起来呢？”首先，我听过一个笑话：“如果医生治疗你的感冒，它会持续42天；如果不治疗，它会持续6周。”这正好和这个数字的前几位数字吻合：42 = 6 × 7。当他提出这个想法后犹豫了一下时，我指出他选择的这个六位数包含了除3和5之外的所有数字，也就是8。他立刻继续解释道：“我们家有7个兄弟姐妹，我是最小的。按年龄排序，排行第三的是我的姐姐A，排行第五的是我的哥哥L——他们都是我的死对头。小时候，我每天晚上都会向上帝祈祷，求他把这两个折磨我的人从生活中带走。我想我当时已经实现了这个愿望：我跳过了3和5，也就是我讨厌的哥哥和姐姐。”“那么，如果这个数字指的是你的兄弟姐妹，那最后的18又是什么意思呢？” “你们家只有七个孩子。”“我常常想，如果我父亲活得更久，我就不会是最小的孩子了。如果再多一个‘1’，我们家就会有八个孩子了，作为老大，我就有个弟弟或妹妹可以管着了。”

So the number was accounted for, but we still had to find out the connection between the first part of the interpretation and the rest of it. That was explained very easily from the circumstances that had put the last two digits into the subject’s head, as he thought that ‘if his father had lived longer’ he would not have been the youngest. 42 = 6 × 7 expressed his low opinion of the doctors who had been unable to help his father, and thus a wish that he had not died. The whole number really reflected the granting of his two childish wishes about his family circle: he wanted the brother and sister he disliked to die, and he wanted another little sibling after him in the family: or to reduce the idea to its essence: if only those two had died instead of my dear father! 3

所以这个数字的由来可以解释，但我们仍然需要找出解释的第一部分与其余部分之间的联系。这一点很容易解释，因为受试者脑海中浮现出最后两位数字的情景，他认为“如果他父亲活得更久”，他就不会是家中最小的了。42 = 6 × 7 表达了他对那些未能救治他父亲的医生的不满，以及希望父亲没有去世的愿望。整个数字实际上反映了他关于家庭的两个幼稚愿望的实现：他希望他不喜欢的兄弟姐妹死去，并且希望在他之后再添一个弟弟或妹妹。或者更确切地说：如果死的是那两个人而不是我亲爱的父亲就好了！

6) Here is a little example from my correspondence. A telegraph director in L. wrote to tell me that his son, aged 18 1 ⁄ 2 , who wanted to study medicine, was at present interested in the psychopathology of everyday life and was trying to convince his parents that my views were correct. I reproduce one of the attempts the young man had made, without any comment on the discussion to which it gave rise.

6）以下是我信件中的一个小例子。伦敦的一位电报局局长来信告诉我，他18岁的儿子想学医，目前对日常生活中的心理病理学很感兴趣，并试图说服他的父母我的观点是正确的。我摘录了这位年轻人的一次尝试，不对此引发的讨论做任何评论。

‘My son was talking to my wife about what is usually called chance, and told her she could not really claim that any song or even any number came into her mind purely “by chance”. The conversation went on like this. Son: Give me a number — any number. Mother: Very well, 79. Son: What do you associate with it? Mother: It makes me think of the pretty hat I saw yesterday. Son: What did it cost? Mother: 158 marks. Son: There you are, then: 158 ÷ 2 = 79. The hat was too expensive, and I expect you were really thinking: “If it cost only half that, then I’d buy it.”

“我儿子跟我妻子聊起通常所说的“偶然性”，说她不能说任何一首歌，甚至任何数字，纯粹是“偶然”出现在她脑海里的。对话是这样的：儿子：给我一个数字——随便哪个数字。母亲：好的，79。儿子：你觉得它跟什么有关？母亲：它让我想起昨天看到的那顶漂亮的帽子。儿子：多少钱？母亲：158马克。儿子：瞧，158÷2=79。那顶帽子太贵了，我猜你当时心里想的是：‘如果只要一半的价格，我就买。’”

‘At first I objected to my son’s ideas, pointing out that ladies in general are not particularly good at arithmetic, and his mother had probably not worked out that 79 was half of 158, so his theory rested on the unlikely notion that the unconscious was better at arithmetic than the normal conscious mind. “Not at all,” he told me. “I’ll admit that Mother didn’t do the sum (158 ÷ 2 = 79), but she could well have seen the equation by chance; or indeed, she could have been thinking of the hat in her dreams and working out what it would cost at only half the price.”’

“起初我反对儿子的想法，指出女性的算术普遍不太好，他母亲很可能没算出79是158的一半，所以他的理论建立在一个不太可能的假设之上：潜意识比正常的意识更擅长算术。“完全不是，”他告诉我，“我承认母亲没有算出这道题（158÷2=79），但她很可能是偶然看到了这个等式；或者，她可能在梦里想着那顶帽子，算出了半价的价格是多少。”

7) I take the analysis of another number from Jones (op. cit., p. 478). A gentleman he knew thought of the number 986 and then challenged him to connect it with anything he could think of. ‘Using the free-association method he first recalled a memory, which had not previously been present in his mind, to the following effect: Six years ago, on the hottest day he could remember, he had seen a joke in an evening newspaper, which stated that the thermometer had stood at 986° F., evidently an exaggeration of 98.6° F. We were at the time seated in front of a very hot fire from which he had just drawn back, and he remarked, probably quite correctly, that the heat had aroused this dormant memory. However, I was curious to know why this memory had persisted with such vividness as to be so readily brought out, for with most people it surely would have been forgotten beyond recall, unless it had become associated with some other mental experience of more significance. He told me that in reading the joke he had laughed uproariously, and that on many subsequent occasions he had recalled it with great relish. As the joke was obviously a very tenuous one, this strengthened my expectation that more lay behind. His next thought was the general reflection that the conception of heat had always greatly impressed him; that heat was the most important thing in the universe, the source of all life, and so on. This remarkable attitude in quite a prosaic young man certainly needed some explanation, so I asked him to continue his free associations. The next thought was of a factory-stack that he could see from his bedroom window. He often stood of an evening watching the flame and smoke issuing out of it, and reflecting on the deplorable waste of energy. Heat, fire, the source of life, the waste of vital energy issuing from an upright, hollow tube — it was not hard to divine from such associations that the ideas of heat and fire were unconsciously linked in his mind with the idea of love, as is so frequent in symbolic thinking, and that there was a strong masturbation complex present, a conclusion which he presently confirmed.’

7）我引用琼斯（同上，第478页）对另一个数字的分析。他认识的一位先生想到了数字986，然后挑战他，让他把这个数字和任何他能想到的东西联系起来。“他运用自由联想法，首先回忆起一段之前从未出现在他脑海中的记忆，内容如下：六年前，在他记忆中最热的一天，他在晚报上看到一个笑话，说温度计显示温度为986华氏度，显然是夸大了98.6华氏度。当时我们正坐在一个很热的火炉前，他刚刚从火炉前退开，他说道（这或许说得没错），是高温唤醒了这段沉睡的记忆。然而，我很好奇为什么这段记忆如此鲜明，以至于如此容易被唤起，因为对大多数人来说，除非它与某种更重要的心理体验联系起来，否则它肯定会被彻底遗忘。”他告诉我，读到那个笑话时他捧腹大笑，之后很多次都津津有味地回忆起它。由于那个笑话显然非常牵强，这让我更加确信他还有更深层的含义。接下来，他想到了一些普遍的看法，比如他对“热”的概念一直印象深刻；他认为热是宇宙中最重要的东西，是所有生命的源泉等等。这样一个平凡的年轻人竟然有如此不同寻常的想法，这自然需要解释，所以我请他继续自由联想。他接下来想到的是从卧室窗户就能看到的工厂烟囱。他经常在傍晚站在那里，看着烟囱里冒出的火焰和浓烟，感叹能源的巨大浪费。热、火、生命之源、从直立的空心管中流出的生命能量的浪费——从这些联想中不难推断出，热和火的概念在他的潜意识里与爱的概念联系在一起，这在象征性思维中非常常见，而且他存在强烈的自慰情结，他随后证实了这一结论。

I would suggest that anyone wanting to get a good impression of the way in which unconscious thought works on numbers should read C. G. Jung’s article ‘Ein Beitrag zur Kenntniss des Zahlentraumes’ [‘A Contribution to the Understanding of the Numerical Dream’] ( Zentralblatt für Psychoanalyse I, 1911), and another by E. Jones (‘Unconscious Manipulations of Numbers’, ibid. II, 5, 1912).

我建议任何想要了解无意识思维如何作用于数字的人都应该阅读 C. G. Jung 的文章《对数字梦的理解的贡献》（《精神分析中心杂志》第一卷，1911 年），以及 E. Jones 的另一篇文章《对数字的无意识操纵》（同上，第二卷，第五期，1912 年）。

In my own self-analyses of this kind two things in particular have struck me: first, the almost somnambulistic certainty with which I make for my unknown aim, immersing myself in a train of thought that involves calculations and then suddenly arrives at the number I was seeking, not to mention the speed with which my mind performs the rest of the work; and second, the fact that the numbers are so readily available to my unconscious, although I am not good at arithmetic and have the greatest difficulty in consciously remembering dates, house numbers, and so forth. I actually find that this unconscious mental manipulation of numbers shows an inclination to superstition in me, although I had long found its origin a mystery. 4

在我进行这类自我分析的过程中，有两件事尤其令我印象深刻：第一，我几乎像梦游般笃定地朝着未知的目标前进，沉浸在一系列计算之中，然后突然间就得出了我想要的数字，更不用说我的大脑完成后续计算的速度了；第二，尽管我算术不好，而且很难有意识地记住日期、门牌号等等，但这些数字却如此轻易地出现在我的潜意识中。我发现，这种无意识地对数字进行心理操作，实际上表明我有一种迷信的倾向，尽管我一直觉得它的起源是个谜。

We shall not be surprised to find that not only numbers but also verbal ideas of a different land regularly prove to be well determined when they are subjected to analytical investigation.

我们不应感到惊讶，因为不仅数字，而且对另一个国家的语言观念，在进行分析调查时，通常都能得到很好的证实。

8) A good example of the derivation of an obsessive word, one that haunts the mind, is given by Jung ( Diagnostische Assoziationsstudien IV, p. 215). ‘A lady told me that for some days she had had the word “Taganrog” [a Russian place-name] always on the tip of her tongue, and she had no idea where it had come from. I asked the lady about any events of an emotional nature and any suppressed wishes of hers in the recent past. After some hesitation, she told me that she would have liked to have a Morgenrock [morning coat], but her husband did not show the interest she would have liked in it. “Morgenrock — Tag-an-rock [literally, ‘day-on-coat’]”; the partial relationship of the words in sense and sound is obvious. The determination of the Russian form of the word derives from the fact that at about the same time the lady had met someone who came from Taganrog.’

8) 荣格（《诊断学研究》第四卷，第215页）举了一个很好的例子，说明一个挥之不去的、令人难以忘怀的词语是如何产生的。“一位女士告诉我，她这几天一直念念不忘‘塔甘罗格’（一个俄罗斯地名），却不知道它从何而来。我问她最近有没有什么情绪波动，或者有什么被压抑的愿望。她犹豫了一会儿，告诉我她想要一件晨礼服，但她的丈夫对此并不感兴趣。“晨礼服——塔甘罗格（字面意思是‘日间礼服’）；这两个词在意义和发音上的部分关联显而易见。之所以确定这个词是俄语形式，是因为大约在同一时间，这位女士遇到了一位来自塔甘罗格的人。”

9) I owe Dr E. Hitschmann the explanation of another case where a couple of lines of verse kept obtruding themselves in a particular location, although their origin and the connections were not obvious.

9) 我欠 E. Hitschmann 博士一个解释，另一个案例中，几行诗句不断出现在某个特定位置，尽管它们的来源和联系并不明显。

‘Told to me by Dr E., a doctor of law: Six years ago I was travelling from Biarritz to San Sebastian. The railway line crosses the river Bidassoa, which is the boundary between France and Spain at this point. There is a splendid view from the bridge, with a broad valley and the Pyrenees on one side and the sea stretching away on the other. It was a fine, bright summer’s day, everything was flooded with bright sunlight, I was on holiday and looking forward to arriving in Spain — when these lines of verse came into my mind:

“一位法学博士E告诉我：六年前，我从比亚里茨前往圣塞巴斯蒂安。铁路线跨越比达索阿河，这条河在这里是法国和西班牙的边界。从桥上可以欣赏到壮丽的景色，一边是宽阔的山谷和比利牛斯山脉，另一边是绵延的大海。那是一个阳光明媚的夏日，万物沐浴在灿烂的阳光下，我正在度假，期待着抵达西班牙——这时，我脑海中浮现出这样几句诗：

Aber frei ist schon die Seele ,

但灵魂早已获得自由。

Schwebet in dem Meer von Licht.

漂浮在光之海洋中。

[Free as air the soul is flying, hovering in the sea of light.]

灵魂如空气般自由飞翔，盘旋在光之海洋中。

‘I remember that at the time I wondered where these lines came from, and could not remember; judging by their metrical form, they must be part of a poem, but it eluded my memory completely. I think I recollect that later, as the lines kept returning to my mind, I asked several people about them, but no one could place them.

“我记得当时我很好奇这些诗句出自哪里，却怎么也想不起来；从它们的韵律来看，它们肯定出自一首诗，但我完全想不起那首诗是什么。我想我后来记得，这些诗句不断在我脑海中浮现，我问过好几个人，但没有人能告诉我它们出自哪里。”

‘On my way back from a trip to Spain last year, I was travelling on the same stretch of railway line. It was night, pitch dark, and raining. I looked out of the window to see if we were coming to the frontier station yet, and noticed that we were on the Bidassoa bridge. The lines quoted above immediately came back into my mind, and yet again I could not remember where they came from.

“去年我从西班牙旅行回来时，也走的是同一段铁路线。当时是晚上，漆黑一片，还下着雨。我向窗外望去，想看看我们是否快到边境车站了，发现我们已经到了比达索阿桥上。上面引用的那些诗句立刻浮现在我的脑海中，但我却又一次想不起它们出自哪里。”

‘Several months later, I happened to pick up the poems of Uhland at home. I opened the volume, and my glance fell on the lines: “Free as air the soul is flying, hovering in the sea of light”, which form the conclusion of a poem entitled ‘Der Waller’ [The Pilgrim’]. I read the poem, and now remembered, very vaguely, that I did once know it, many years ago. It tells a story which is set in Spain, and this struck me as the only connection the quotation had with the part of the railway line that I have described. But I was not entirely satisfied with my discovery, and went on leafing automatically through the book. The lines “Free as air the soul is flying,” etc., were the last printed on a certain page. Turning it, I found a poem entitled ‘The Bidassoa Bridge’ on the next page.

几个月后，我在家偶然翻到了乌兰德的诗集。我打开诗集，目光落在了“灵魂如空气般自由飞翔，盘旋在光之海洋中”这几行诗上，这是诗作《朝圣者》（Der Waller）的结尾。我读了这首诗，隐约记得多年前我曾读过它。诗中的故事发生在西班牙，这让我觉得这句诗与我之前描述的那段铁路线之间只有一处联系。但我并不完全满足于此，于是继续漫不经心地翻阅着诗集。“灵魂如空气般自由飞翔”这几行诗出现在某一页的末尾。翻过这一页，我发现下一页是一首题为《比达索阿桥》（The Bidassoa Bridge）的诗。

‘I should add that the content of this second poem seemed to me even stranger than the subject of the first, and that its opening lines run:

我还要补充一点，这第二首诗的内容在我看来甚至比第一首诗的主题还要奇怪，它的开头几行是这样的：

Auf der Bidassoabrücke steht ein Heiliger altersgrau ,

在比达索阿桥上，矗立着一位圣人，他已年迈，头发花白。

Segnet rechts die span’schen Berge, segnet links den fränk’schen Gau.’

祝福右边的西班牙群山，祝福左边的弗兰肯山谷。

[On the Bidassoa bridge stands a saint both old and grey, blessing Spain to his right hand, blessing France the other way.]

[在比达索阿桥上，站着一位又老又白的圣人，他右手边祝福着西班牙，左手边祝福着法国。]

B) The light thus cast on the determination of names and numbers apparently chosen at random may perhaps help to clear up another problem. Many people, as we know, cite a special conviction of the existence of free will in order to reject the assumption of consistent psychic determinism. Their sense of conviction is real, and does not give way to a belief in determinism. It must, like all normal feelings, have something to justify it. However, so far as I can see, it does not express itself in major and important decisions, occasions on which we are more inclined to feel a sense of psychic compulsion, to which we readily appeal for support (‘Here stand I; I can do no other’). On the other hand, people like to think that in making trivial decisions of little importance they could just as well have decided differently, and that they acted from free will and not pre-motivation. Our analyses show that there is no need to dispute a person’s right to feel convinced of his free will. If we distinguish between conscious and unconscious motivations, this sense of conviction tells us that conscious motivation does not extend to all our motor decisions. Minima non curat praetor [The praetor does not concern himself with minor matters]. But what is left free by one side receives motivation from the other, from the unconscious, and so determination in the psychic area is duly carried out after all. 5

B) 由此对看似随机选择的姓名和数字的决定因素所揭示的真相，或许有助于澄清另一个问题。我们知道，许多人会援引他们对自由意志存在的坚定信念来否定前后一致的心理决定论假设。他们的这种信念是真实的，并且不会让位于对决定论的信仰。它必然像所有正常的感受一样，有其存在的理由。然而，就我所见，这种信念并不会体现在重大决策中，而正是在这些场合，我们更容易感受到一种心理上的强制感，并会轻易地寻求这种强制感的支持（“我只能如此，别无选择”）。另一方面，人们喜欢认为，在做一些无关紧要的琐碎决定时，他们完全可以做出不同的选择，而且他们的行为是出于自由意志而非预先动机。我们的分析表明，没有必要质疑一个人确信自己拥有自由意志的权利。如果我们区分有意识和无意识的动机，这种信念感告诉我们，有意识的动机并非延伸到我们所有的行动决定。Minima non curat praetor（执政官不关心琐事）。但是，一方留下的自由意志会从另一方，从无意识中获得动力，因此，心理领域的决定最终还是会得到恰当的执行。

C) Although in the nature of things an understanding of the motivation of the slips described above must elude the conscious mind, it would be good to find psychological evidence of its existence, and in fact it is probable, for reasons that emerge from closer study of the unconscious, that such evidence is indeed to be found somewhere. Phenomena which seem to correspond to an unconscious and therefore displaced understanding of that motivation can actually be shown to exist in two areas:

C) 虽然从本质上讲，上述失误的动机必然无法被意识所理解，但如果能找到其存在的心理学证据，那将是一件好事。事实上，基于对潜意识更深入研究后得出的原因，这种证据很可能确实存在。在以下两个领域，我们可以发现一些现象，它们似乎与潜意识中对该动机的理解存在偏差：

a) It is a conspicuous and generally observed feature of the conduct of paranoiacs that they attribute the utmost importance to certain small details of other people’s behaviour which the rest of us disregard; they interpret them in certain ways and draw wide-ranging conclusions from them. For instance, the last paranoiac I saw believed that all around him were in collusion because they waved one hand in a certain way when he was leaving the railway station. Another man carefully noted the way people walked down the street swinging their walking sticks, and so on. 6

a) 妄想症患者行为的一个显著且普遍的特征是，他们会过分重视他人行为中某些我们常忽略的细微之处；他们会以特定的方式解读这些细节，并从中得出广泛的结论。例如，我上次见到的妄想症患者认为，他周围的人都在串通，因为他离开火车站时，他们挥动一只手的方式很特别。另一个人则仔细观察人们在街上挥舞拐杖的方式，等等。

The category of fortuitous behaviour which does not need motivation, and which a normal person considers to form part of his own psychic operations and mental slips, is thus dismissed by the paranoiac where other people’s psychic expressions are concerned. Everything he notices about them is significant, everything can be interpreted. How does he come to see it in this way? Here, as in so many similar cases, he is probably projecting into the mental life of others factors that are unconsciously present in his own. In paranoia, moreover, all kinds of ideas which in normal people and neurotics cannot be traced as present in the unconscious except through psychoanalysis make their way, instead, into the conscious mind. 7 Here the paranoiac is partially correct; he recognizes something that eludes normal perception, and sees more keenly than someone with a normal mind, but his perceptions are invalidated by the displacement of what he recognizes in this way on to other people. I trust I shall not be expected to justify individual paranoiac interpretations. However, the modified amount of justification that we may allow to paranoia in this view of fortuitous actions will facilitate psychological understanding of the conviction which all these interpretations carry in the paranoiac’s mind. There is some truth in it ; our own errors of judgement, errors that need not be described as pathological, acquire their characteristic sense of conviction in just the same way. Such feelings are justified in relation to a certain part of a mistaken train of thought, or the source from which it comes, and we extend them to the rest of the context.

正常人认为无需动机的偶然行为是自身心理活动和思维失误的一部分，但妄想症患者却将这种行为排除在他人心理表达之外。在他看来，他人的一切行为都意义非凡，都可以被解读。他为何会这样看待他人？如同许多类似案例一样，他很可能将自身无意识中存在的因素投射到了他人的心理生活中。此外，在妄想症中，所有在正常人和神经症患者身上只能通过精神分析才能追溯到无意识中的观念，都会进入意识层面。妄想症患者的说法部分正确；他确实感知到了正常人难以察觉的事物，并且比正常人看得更敏锐，但他的感知却因将这种感知投射到他人身上而失效。我希望大家不会要求我去为个别妄想症患者的解读辩护。然而，在这种看待偶然事件的视角下，我们或许可以对妄想症给予一定程度的合理性解释，这将有助于我们从心理学的角度理解妄想症患者心中所有这些解读所蕴含的信念。这其中不乏真理；我们自身的判断失误——即便并非病态的错误——也同样会以类似的方式获得其特有的信念感。这种感觉在错误的思维脉络或其来源的某个特定部分看来是合理的，而我们却将其延伸到整个语境之中。

b) Another sign of our unconscious and displaced understanding of motivation in fortuitous actions and slips is conveyed by the phenomenon of superstition. Let me explain what I mean by discussing the little incident that was my point of departure for these reflections.

b) 迷信现象也体现了我们对偶然行为和失误背后的动机存在无意识的、错误的理解。让我通过讨论引发我这些思考的小事件来解释我的意思。

On returning from holiday I immediately thought about the patients with whom I was to be occupied in the new working year. My first call was paid to a very old lady for whom I had been carrying out the same medical tasks twice a day for years (see p. 169 above). Because of the monotony of my visits, unconscious ideas very frequently expressed themselves on my way to see her and while I was treating her. She was over ninety years old, so it was natural to wonder at the beginning of every year how much longer she had to live. On the day in question I was in a hurry, so I took a cab to her home. Every cab-driver on the rank outside the building where I live knows the old lady’s address, for they have all driven me there quite often. Today it so happened that the driver did not stop at her home, but outside the building of the same number in a nearby street running parallel, which in fact looked much the same. I pointed the driver’s mistake out to him, and he apologized. Was there any significance in the fact that I had been driven to a building where I would not find the old lady? Not to me, certainly, but had I been superstitious I would have seen an omen in this incident, a prophecy on the part of destiny that this year would be the last of the old lady’s life. A great many omens mentioned in historical records were based on symbolism just as flimsy as this, although I myself would explain this incident as chance, without any further significance.

假期结束后，我立刻开始思考新一年的工作安排。我首先拜访的是一位非常年迈的老太太，多年来，我每天都要为她做两次同样的诊疗工作（见上文第169页）。由于诊疗工作的单调乏味，在去她家的路上以及诊疗过程中，我常常会不自觉地冒出一些想法。她已经九十多岁了，所以每年年初，我都会忍不住去想她还能活多久。那天我比较赶时间，就打车去了她家。我住的楼外出租车站的每个司机都知道这位老太太的地址，因为他们都经常载我去那里。但今天，司机却没把车停在她家门口，而是停在了附近一条平行街道上门牌号相同的楼房门口，那条街看起来和她家很像。我指出了司机的错误，他向我道了歉。我被带到一栋根本找不到老太太的房子，这其中有什么寓意吗？对我来说，当然没有。但如果我迷信的话，或许会把这件事看作是一种预兆，一种命运的预言，预示着今年将是老太太生命的终点。历史记载中提到的许多预兆都基于这种牵强的象征意义，尽管我个人认为这纯属巧合，并无其他深意。

It would have been quite different if I had made my journey on foot, and then, ‘lost in thought’ and ‘absent-mindedly’ had gone to the building in the parallel street instead of the one where I was expected. I would explain that not as chance, but as an action performed with unconscious intent and calling for interpretation. I would probably have interpreted my mistake as suggesting that I did not expect to be visiting the old lady much longer.

如果我步行前往，然后“心不在焉”地走进了平行街道上的那栋楼，而不是我原本应该去的那栋，情况就完全不同了。我会把这解释为无意识的行为，而不是偶然，并赋予其某种含义。我可能会把我的失误解读为，我并不指望能再拜访那位老太太太太，我大概不会再去拜访她太久了。

I would distinguish myself from a superstitious man, therefore, as follows: I do not believe that an event not caused in any way by my own mental life can tell me any hidden facts about the future structure of reality, but I do believe that an unintentional expression of my own mental processes can reveal some hidden factor which itself belongs to my mental life alone. I may believe in outer (real) chance, but not in fortuitous inner (psychic) actions. A superstitious man will see it the other way around: he knows nothing of the motivation of his fortuitous actions and slips, he believes fortuitous psychic factors exist, and he is inclined to ascribe a significance to outside fortuitous events that will make itself felt in reality, and to see chance as a means of expression for something hidden that is outside him. There are two differences between me and the superstitious man: first, he projects a motivation on to something outside him, while I look for it within myself; and second, he interprets chance as some incident that has happened, while I derive it from an idea. However, what seems to him concealed corresponds to the unconscious in me, and we share an urge not to see chance as solely accidental but to place some kind of interpretation on it. 8

因此，我将自己与迷信者区分开来，理由如下：我不相信任何并非由我自身精神生活所引发的事件能够揭示未来现实结构的隐藏真相，但我相信，我自身精神过程的无意表达能够揭示某些仅属于我自身精神生活的隐藏因素。我或许相信外在（现实的）偶然性，但不相信内在（精神的）偶然行为。迷信者则恰恰相反：他对自身偶然行为和失误的动机一无所知，他相信偶然的精神因素存在，并且倾向于赋予外在的偶然事件以意义，认为这些意义会在现实中显现，并将偶然性视为某种外在隐藏之物的表达方式。我与迷信者之间有两点不同：首先，他将动机投射到外在事物上，而我则在自身内部寻找动机；其次，他将偶然性解释为已经发生的事件，而我则将其源于某种观念。然而，在他看来隐藏的事物，恰恰对应着我内心的无意识，我们都渴望不把偶然性仅仅视为意外，而是对其进行某种诠释。

I assume that this conscious ignorance and unconscious understanding of the motivation of psychic fortuitous events is one of the roots of superstition. Because a superstitious person is ignorant of the motivation of his own fortuitous actions, and because that motivation is clamouring to be recognized, he has to accommodate it in the world outside himself by displacement. If there is a connection of this kind it will scarcely be confined to this one case. In fact I believe that a large part of any mythological view of the world, extending a long way even into the most modern forms of religion, is nothing but psychology projected into the outside world. The vague recognition (it might be called endopsychic perception) of psychic factors and circumstances 9 in the unconscious is reflected — it is difficult to put it any other way, so here I must call on the analogy with paranoia — is reflected in the construction of a supernatural reality , which science will transform back into the psychology of the unconscious. The myths of Paradise and the Fall, of God, good and evil, immortality, and so on could be understood in this way, turning metaphysics into metapsychology. There is less of a gulf between paranoiac and superstitious displacement than may at first glance appear. When human beings first began thinking, as we know, they felt compelled to resolve the outer world, anthropomorphically, into a diversity of personalities in their own image; the chance events that they interpreted in superstitious terms were therefore the actions and expressions of persons. They were just like those paranoiacs who draw conclusions from the trivial signs they observe in other people, and like all those healthy people who, correctly, judge character by the fortuitous and unintentional actions of their fellow men. Superstition seems misplaced only in our modern, scientific but by no means complete view of the world; as the world appeared to pre-scientific ages and peoples, superstition was legitimate and logical.

我认为，这种对心理偶然事件动机的有意识的无知和无意识的理解，是迷信的根源之一。因为迷信的人不了解自身偶然行为的动机，而这种动机又迫切地想要被认可，所以他只能通过转移的方式将其纳入自身之外的世界中。如果这种联系确实存在，那么它绝非仅限于此个例。事实上，我认为，任何神话世界观的很大一部分，甚至延伸到最现代的宗教形式中，都不过是投射到外部世界的心理学。对无意识中心理因素和环境的模糊认知（或许可以称之为内心理感知）反映在——很难用其他方式来表达，所以在这里我必须借用妄想症的类比——超自然现实的构建中，而科学最终会将这种构建转化回无意识的心理学。天堂与堕落、上帝、善恶、永生等等神话都可以用这种方式来理解，从而将形而上学转化为元心理学。偏执狂和迷信之间的鸿沟远没有乍看之下那么大。我们知道，当人类开始思考时，他们感到有必要将外部世界拟人化地解读为各种各样符合自身形象的人格；因此，他们用迷信的语言解释的偶然事件，就成了人的行为和表达。他们就像那些从他人身上观察到的琐碎迹象中得出结论的偏执狂，也像所有那些能够正确地根据他人偶然和无意的行为来判断其品格的健康人一样。迷信似乎只有在我们现代的、科学的（但绝非完整的）世界观中才显得不合时宜；在科学出现之前的时代和民族眼中，迷信是合理且合乎逻辑的。

Relatively speaking, therefore, the Roman who abandoned some important enterprise if he saw birds flying in the wrong formation was right; he was acting logically in line with his assumptions. But if he abstained from the enterprise because he had stumbled on the threshold of his door ( un Romain retournerait [a Roman would turn back], as they say), he was definitely superior to us unbelievers, and a better psychologist than we are, despite our current efforts. His stumbling showed him that some doubt existed, something in him was working against his enterprise, and its power could impair his own ability to carry out his intention just as he was on the point of performing it. One can be sure of success only if all mental forces are united in making for the desired aim. As Schiller’s Wilhelm Tell, having hesitated for a long time before shooting the apple from his son’s head, says when asked by the governor why he had taken a second arrow too:

因此，相对而言，如果一个罗马人看到鸟群飞行队形错误而放弃一项重要的事业，那么他的做法是正确的；他的行动符合逻辑，与他的假设相符。但如果他因为在门槛上绊了一下而放弃这项事业（正如他们所说，“罗马人会回头”），那么他无疑比我们这些不信神的人更胜一筹，也比我们更懂心理学，尽管我们现在正努力钻研。他的绊倒表明他内心存在某种疑虑，某种东西在阻碍他的事业，这种力量甚至会在他即将实现目标时削弱他的能力。只有当所有精神力量都集中于实现目标时，才能确保成功。正如席勒笔下的威廉·泰尔，在射下儿子头上的苹果之前犹豫了很久，当总督问他为什么又射了第二支箭时，他这样说道：

Mit diesem zweiten Pfeil durchschoss ich — Euch ,

我用第二支箭射穿了你——你，

Wenn ich mein liebes Kind getroffen hätte ,

如果我曾见过我亲爱的孩子，

Und Euer — wahrlich, hätt’ ich nicht gefehlt.

至于你——说真的，我绝不会缺席。

[If I had killed my dear beloved child, the second arrow would have been for you. And that shot — truly — would have found its mark.]

[如果我杀了我亲爱的孩子，第二支箭就会射向你。而且那一箭——真的——一定会命中目标。]

D) Anyone who has had an opportunity of studying the hidden emotions of the human mind by psychoanalytic methods can also contribute some new ideas about the quality of the unconscious motives expressed in superstition. It is particularly easy to see how superstition arises from suppressed hostile and cruel feelings in neurotics, who are often very intelligent but afflicted with compulsive ideas and obsessions. Superstition is to a high degree an expectation of bad luck, and anyone who frequently ill-wishes other people, but has repressed such ideas because he has been brought up to wish them well instead, will be particularly likely to expect bad luck to descend upon him from outside as a punishment for his unconscious ill-will.

D) 任何有机会运用精神分析方法研究人类心灵深处隐藏情感的人，都可以对迷信中所体现的无意识动机的本质提出一些新的见解。尤其容易理解的是，迷信源于神经质患者被压抑的敌意和残酷情绪。神经质患者往往非常聪明，却饱受强迫性思维和执念的折磨。迷信在很大程度上是对厄运的预期，任何经常对他人怀有恶意，却因为从小被教育要善待他人而压抑了这种想法的人，都特别容易预期厄运会从外部降临到自己身上，作为对其无意识恶意的一种惩罚。

Admittedly I have by no means exhausted the psychology of superstition with these remarks, but I must at least touch on the other side of the question: can we dismiss the existence of any real roots for superstition entirely, and are we sure that presentiments, prophetic dreams, telepathic experiences, expressions of supernatural powers, and so forth have no basis in fact? I am far from wishing to dismiss out of hand phenomena that have been observed in circumstantial detail even by the intellectually outstanding; it would be better to take them as a subject for further investigation. One might even hope that some of those observations will be elucidated by our dawning knowledge of unconscious mental processes without obliging us to make drastic alterations to our present views. 10 Should other phenomena, such as those to which spiritualists lay claim, be capable of proof, then we would have to make the modifications demanded by this new discovery to our ‘laws’, without letting our belief in the consistency of terrestrial manifestations be shaken.

诚然，我这些论述远不足以穷尽迷信的心理学，但我至少必须触及问题的另一面：我们能否完全排除迷信存在任何真实根源？我们是否确信预感、预言梦、心灵感应、超自然力量的显现等等都毫无事实依据？我绝非想要断然否定那些即使是杰出的智者也曾细致观察过的现象；最好将它们作为进一步研究的对象。我们甚至可以期待，随着我们对无意识心理过程的认识不断加深，其中一些观察结果能够得到阐释，而无需我们对现有观点做出重大改变。如果其他现象，例如唯灵论者所声称的那些现象，能够得到证实，那么我们就必须根据这一新发现对我们的“法则”做出相应的修正，但同时又不能动摇我们对尘世现象一致性的信念。

In the context of these remarks, I can answer the questions that arise only subjectively, that is to say, from my own experience. Unfortunately I must confess that I am one of those unworthy individuals before whom ghosts desist from their haunting, and the supernatural eludes me, so I have never been in a position to experience anything that might persuade me to believe in signs and wonders. Like everyone else, I have had presentiments and I have known misfortune, but the two kept their distance from each other: nothing happened to justify the presentiments, and misfortune struck out of the blue. When I was a young man living alone in a foreign city, I often enough heard my name suddenly called by a beloved and unmistakable voice, and made a note of the exact moment in time when this aural hallucination occurred, thereafter asking my family anxiously what had been happening at home just then? The answer was nothing. Conversely, on a later occasion I was working with my patients, my mind at ease and without any presentiment of misfortune, at the very time when my child was in danger of bleeding to death. And I have never been able to acknowledge any of the presentiments reported to me by my patients as real phenomena. But I must admit that in recent years I have had several remarkable experiences that could have been explained easily enough if we assumed that telepathic thought-transference exists.

就这些话而言，我只能从主观角度，也就是从我自身的经历出发，来回答那些问题。遗憾的是，我必须承认，我属于那种不配与鬼魂纠缠、超自然现象无缘的人，所以我从未有机会体验到任何能让我相信神迹奇事的事情。和其他人一样，我也有过预感，也经历过不幸，但两者之间却始终保持着距离：预感总是毫无征兆地出现，而不幸却总是猝不及防地降临。年轻时，我独自一人生活在异国他乡，常常会听到一个熟悉而又清晰的声音突然呼唤我的名字，我会记下这种幻听出现的确切时间，然后焦急地询问家人刚才家里发生了什么事。得到的回答总是：什么也没发生。相反，后来有一次，我正在给病人看病，当时我心情平静，没有任何不祥的预感，而我的孩子却面临失血过多而死的危险。我始终无法承认病人向我描述的任何预感是真实存在的。但我必须承认，近年来我经历了一些非同寻常的事情，如果我们假设心灵感应确实存在，这些经历或许就能很容易地得到解释。

Many people believe in prophetic dreams, a belief resting on the fact that many future events really do turn out as our wishes have pre-constructed them in dreaming. 11 That is not surprising in itself, and as a rule extensive divergences that the credulous dreamer prefers to ignore exist between the dream and its fulfilment. A good example of a dream that can accurately be called prophetic was once offered to me for precise analysis by an intelligent and truthful patient. She told me she had once dreamed of meeting her former friend and family doctor outside a certain shop in a certain street, and when she went into the inner city next morning she really did meet him at the place specified in the dream. I may add that this remarkable coincidence did not prove significant in relation to any subsequent experience, so that there was nothing in the future to account for it.

许多人相信预知梦，这种信念基于这样一个事实：许多未来事件确实会按照我们在梦中预先设想的方式发生。这本身并不令人惊讶，而且通常情况下，梦境与现实之间存在着巨大的差异，而轻信的做梦者往往选择忽略这些差异。一位聪明诚实的病人曾向我提供了一个可以准确称之为预知梦的绝佳例子，让我进行精确分析。她告诉我，她梦见在某条街的某家商店外遇到了她以前的朋友兼家庭医生，第二天早上她去市中心时，真的在梦中指定的地点遇到了他。我还要补充一点，这个惊人的巧合与之后的任何经历都没有关联，因此未来没有任何事情可以解释它。

But careful questioning established the absence of any actual proof that the lady had remembered her dream as soon as she woke up in the morning, and before she went for a walk and met her friend. She could not object to a version of the facts that deprived the event of any element of the marvellous, leaving only an interesting psychological problem. She had gone down the street in question one morning, had met her former doctor outside a shop, and was convinced at the sight of him that she had dreamed of their meeting in that very place the night before. My analysis could then suggest, with a high degree of probability, just how she had come to feel so sure, for as a general rule conviction can claim a certain right to credibility. Meeting at a predetermined place when you have been expecting such a meeting is very much in the nature of a rendezvous. Her former doctor reminded her of old days in which meetings with a third person, also a friend of the doctor’s, had been significant to her. She was still involved with this other gentleman, and had been expecting to see him the day before her alleged dream, but he never turned up. If I felt it permissible to give a fuller account of the circumstances in this case, I could easily show that her illusion of having had a prophetic dream when she saw her friend from the past was equivalent to her saying something like: ‘Oh, doctor, you remind me so much of the past! I never had to wait in vain for N. when we had a rendezvous in those days.’

但仔细询问后发现，没有任何实际证据表明这位女士在清晨醒来后，在出门散步与朋友见面之前，就立刻记起了她的梦境。她无法反驳这样一种说法：这种说法使事件失去了任何奇幻色彩，只留下了一个有趣的心理问题。一天早上，她沿着那条街走去，在一家商店外遇到了她以前的医生，一见到他就确信自己昨晚梦见了他们在同一个地方相遇。我的分析可以颇具概率地解释她为何如此确信，因为通常来说，信念本身就具有一定的可信度。在预定的地点与你期待已久的会面相遇，这本身就带有约会的性质。她的前医生让她想起了过去与第三人（也是医生的朋友）的会面，这些会面对她来说意义非凡。她当时仍然和那位男士保持着联系，并且原本期待在她所谓的梦境发生的前一天见到他，但他却并未出现。如果我觉得可以更详细地描述一下此案的情况，我可以很容易地证明，她梦见老朋友时所表现出的预知梦，实际上等同于她说：“哦，医生，你让我想起了过去！那时候我们约好见面，我从来不用白等N。”

I myself have had a simple and easily interpreted experience of the famous ‘strange coincidence’ of meeting someone of whom one has just been thinking, and it may well be a good model for similar cases. A few days after I was granted the tide of professor, which confers much prestige in monarchical states, I was walking through the inner city when my thoughts were suddenly diverted into a childlike fantasy of revenge against a certain couple who had called me in to examine their little daughter a few months earlier. She had shown signs of an interesting symptom of obsession in connection with a dream. I was intrigued by her case, and thought I saw how her obsession had developed, but her parents declined to let me treat her, informing me that they were thinking of going to a foreign doctor who used hypnosis as a cure. I was now fantasizing that his efforts had failed completely, whereupon the parents begged me to begin treatment, saying they now had total confidence in me, and so forth. However, I replied: Oh, so now that I’m a professor myself you trust me, do you? My title makes no difference to my abilities; if you didn’t want me when I was a mere lecturer you can do without my services as a professor. At this point my fantasy was interrupted by a loud greeting of: ‘Good day, Professor!’ and I looked up to see, coming down the street, the same couple on whom I had just been revenging myself by refusing their request. My next idea did away with any notion of the marvellous. I had been walking along a straight, wide and almost empty thoroughfare, in the opposite direction from the girl’s parents, I had caught sight of their imposing figures as I briefly looked up when I was some twenty paces away from them, but rejected my sighting of them — as if it were a negative hallucination — for those emotional reasons that then expressed themselves in what had appeared to be the spontaneous emergence of a fantasy.

我本人就曾有过一次简单易懂的经历，符合著名的“奇特巧合”——遇到一个自己刚刚还在想着的人。这或许能为类似的案例提供一个很好的范例。几天前，我被授予教授头衔，这在君主制国家可是相当尊贵的。当时我正在城里散步，突然间，我的思绪飘到了一旁，幻想着要报复几个月前请我去给他们的小女儿看病的那对夫妇。她当时表现出一种与梦境相关的、有趣的强迫症症状。我对她的病情很感兴趣，自认为看透了她强迫症的成因，但她的父母拒绝让我给她看病，告诉我他们正考虑去找一位用催眠疗法治疗的外国医生。我幻想着那位医生的治疗彻底失败了，于是她的父母恳求我开始治疗，说他们现在完全信任我，等等。然而，我回答道：“哦，既然我现在自己也成了教授，你就信任我了，是吗？我的头衔并不能影响我的能力；如果你当初只是个讲师时就不想要我，那你也不需要我当教授的服务。” 这时，一声响亮的问候打断了我的幻想：“教授，您好！” 我抬头一看，只见那对夫妇正沿着街道走来，而我刚才拒绝了他们的请求，算是报复。接下来的想法彻底粉碎了我所有美好的幻想。我当时正沿着一条笔直、宽阔、几乎空无一人的大街走着，方向与那对女孩的父母相反。当我离他们大约二十步远时，我抬头瞥见了他们高大的身影，但我却否认了——仿佛那只是一场噩梦——这其中的情绪因素，最终以看似自发产生的幻想的形式呈现出来。

I take the following account of another ‘explanation of an apparent presentiment’ from Otto Rank:

我采纳了奥托·兰克对另一种“明显预感”的解释如下：

‘Some time ago I myself experienced a curious version of the “strange coincidence” of meeting a person when one has just been thinking about him. Just before Christmas I was on my way to the Austro-Hungarian Bank to exchange a note for ten new crowns in silver, which I planned to give as presents. Deep in grandiose fantasies connected with the contrast between my own small means and the money piled high in the bank, I turned into the narrow street where its building stands. I saw an automobile at the main entrance, and a great many people coming in and out. Well, I said to myself, I suppose the bank clerks will have time to deal with my few crowns, and anyway I shan’t keep them long; I shall just hand in the note I want changed and say: I’d like this changed into gold, please! I immediately noticed my mistake — it was silver I was going to ask for — and came down to earth from my daydreams. I was now only a few paces from the entrance, and saw a young man coming towards me who looked familiar, although as I am short-sighted I could not recognize him for certain. When he came closer I recognized him as a school friend of my brother’s , a man called Gold , and I had hoped for a good deal of support from this man’s own brother, a well-known writer, when I embarked on a literary career. However, it was not forthcoming, and nor as a consequence was the material success I had hoped for, a subject that had been occupying my imagination on my way to the bank. Deep in my fantasies, I must therefore have unconsciously seen Herr Gold coming towards me, and my conscious mind, dreaming of financial success, had transformed this incident into a form which made me think of asking the cashier for gold instead of the less valuable silver. On the other hand, the paradox of the fact that my unconscious could perceive something which my eye recognized only later seems partly explicable from what is called (by Bleuler) a “complexive readiness”, concentrating on financial matters and guiding me all along, contrary to what I really knew, to a place where in fact they deal only with transactions in gold and paper money’ ( Zentralblatt für Psychoanalyse II, 5).

“不久前，我亲身经历了一次奇特的‘巧合’：就在我刚刚想起某人的时候，竟然真的遇到了他。圣诞节前夕，我正要去奥匈帝国银行兑换一张纸币，想换成十枚新的银克朗，打算送人。我沉浸在自己微薄的收入和银行里堆积如山的金币之间的巨大反差带来的美好幻想中，拐进了银行所在的那条狭窄街道。我看到正门停着一辆汽车，还有很多人进进出出。我心想，银行职员应该有时间处理我这点克朗吧，反正我也不会留着它们太久；我只要把要兑换的纸币递过去，说：‘请把这个换成金币！’就行了！”我立刻意识到自己犯了个错误——我本来想换的是银币——这才从白日梦中回过神来。我离入口只有几步之遥，看到一个年轻人朝我走来，看起来很眼熟，但我近视，无法确定他是谁。他走近后，我认出他是哥哥的校友，名叫戈尔德。我曾希望他哥哥——一位知名作家——能在我投身文学事业时给予我大力支持。然而，事与愿违，我所期盼的物质成功也随之落空。在去银行的路上，我一直在想着这件事。或许，在我的幻想深处，我无意识地看到了戈尔德先生朝我走来，而我那渴望财富的意识，又将这一幕转化成了一种情境，让我想到应该向收银员要黄金而不是价值较低的白银。另一方面，我的无意识能够感知到我的眼睛后来才识别出的事物这一悖论，似乎部分可以用布鲁勒所说的“复杂准备”来解释，这种准备专注于金融事务，并一直引导我走向一个实际上只处理黄金和纸币交易的地方，这与我真正知道的相反（《精神分析中心学报》II，5）。

Also in the category of the amazing and uncanny is that curious sensation felt so often, and in so many situations, of having had an experience already, or having been in the same place before, although one can never succeed in remembering what seems to have been that earlier occasion. I know that I am simply adopting an imprecise verbal convention in calling what we feel at such moments a sensation: it is a process of judgement involving identification, but these cases have their own unique character, and one must not forget that it is never possible to locate the memory being sought. I do not know if this phenomenon of déjà vu has ever been cited in proof of an individual’s earlier psychic existence, but psychologists have turned their attention to it, trying to solve the riddle in all kinds of speculative ways. None of the attempts that have been made to explain it strikes me as satisfactory, because none of them takes anything into account but the concomitant features and conditions encouraging the phenomenon. Those psychic processes which, so my observations suggest, are solely responsible for elucidating the sense of déjà vu , that is to say, unconscious fantasies, are still generally ignored by psychologists today.

还有一种奇特的感觉也属于令人惊奇和匪夷所思的范畴，那就是经常在各种情况下感受到的那种似曾相识的体验，或者曾经到过同一个地方的感觉，尽管我们永远无法回忆起之前究竟发生了什么。我知道，我在这里用“感觉”来称呼我们此刻的感受，只是采用了一种不够精确的语言习惯：这是一种涉及识别的判断过程，但这些情况有其独特的性质，而且我们必须记住，我们永远无法找到所追寻的记忆。我不知道这种似曾相识的现象是否曾被用来证明一个人过去曾有过某种精神体验，但心理学家们已经对此展开了研究，试图用各种推测性的方法解开这个谜团。然而，所有这些解释在我看来都不尽如人意，因为它们都只考虑了促成这种现象发生的伴随特征和条件。根据我的观察，那些能够解释似曾相识感的心理过程，也就是无意识的幻想，至今仍被心理学家普遍忽视。

I think it is a mistake to describe the sensation of having had an experience already as an illusion. More probably, at such moments it touches on something one has indeed already experienced, but the experience was never conscious and so cannot be consciously recalled. The sensation of déjà vu , in short, is the memory of an unconscious fantasy — for unconscious fantasies (or daydreams) do exist, just like the conscious fantasies with which we are all familiar from personal experience.

我认为将似曾相识的感觉描述为一种错觉是错误的。更准确地说，在这种时刻，它触及了我们确实已经经历过的事情，但这种经历从未被意识觉察，因此无法被有意识地回忆起来。简而言之，似曾相识的感觉是对无意识幻想的记忆——因为无意识的幻想（或白日梦）确实存在，就像我们每个人都从个人经验中熟悉的有意识的幻想一样。

This subject, as I am aware, deserves extremely close study, but here I will cite only the analysis of a single case of déjà vu where the sensation was notable for its particular intensity and duration. A lady who is now 37 very clearly remembered her first visit to school friends in the country when she was 12 1 ⁄ 2 . When she went into the garden of their house she immediately felt that she had been there before; she had the same sensation when she went into the living rooms, and even seemed to know in advance which room adjoined which, what the view from it would be, and so on. However, as her parents confirmed, it was quite out of the question for her sense of familiarity to have arisen from some previous visit to the house and the garden, perhaps in very early childhood. The lady who told me this was not looking for any psychological explanation, but thought that her sensation foreshadowed the importance these friends of hers would assume in her emotional life later. Investigation of the circumstances in which the phenomenon occurred, however, pointed the way to a different concept. When she made her visit she knew that the daughters of the family, her friends, had an only brother who was seriously ill. She saw him during her visit, and thought that he looked very sick indeed and on the point of death. As it happened, her own only brother had been dangerously ill with diphtheria a few months before, and during his illness she had spent several weeks away from her parents’ house with a female relative. She thought that her brother had in fact been with her on this visit to her friends in the country, and even that it was his first expedition of any length after his illness, but her memory was curiously vague on these points, although she remembered all the other details very clearly, in particular the dress she had been wearing that day. It will not be difficult for anyone versed in such matters to conclude, from these indications, that expectation of her brother’s death loomed large in the girl’s mind at the time, but either it had never been consciously present or she had vigorously repressed it when, fortunately, he recovered. If he had not, she would have been in mourning and wearing a different dress. She found the same kind of situation at the home of her friends in the country, where their only brother was in danger of dying, and he did indeed die soon afterwards. She should have remembered consciously that she had been in the same situation herself a few months earlier, but instead she was prevented from recollecting it by repression, instead transferring her sense of something remembered to the house and garden of her friends’ home, and she fell victim to the fausse reconnaissance of having seen all those things before. We may conclude from what she repressed that her expectation of her brother’s death at the time was not so very far in nature from a wish-fulfilment fantasy: if he died she would be the only child in the family. She suffered from neurosis in later life, and was terrified by the fear of losing her parents. Analysis, as usual, revealed an unconscious wish to that effect behind her fear.

我深知，这个主题值得深入研究，但在此我仅引用一个似曾相识案例的分析，该案例中似曾相识的感觉以其特殊的强度和持续时间而著称。一位现年37岁的女士清晰地记得她12岁时第一次去乡下拜访老同学的情景。当她走进老同学家的花园时，立刻感到似曾相识；走进客厅时也有同样的感觉，她甚至似乎预先知道哪个房间与哪个房间相邻，从哪个房间望出去会看到什么景色等等。然而，正如她的父母所证实的那样，这种熟悉感绝不可能源于她幼年时曾到访过这所房子和花园。这位女士告诉我这件事时，并非寻求任何心理学解释，而是认为这种感觉预示着这些朋友日后会在她情感生活中扮演重要的角色。然而，对这一现象发生的具体情况进行调查后，却指向了另一种解释。她去拜访朋友时，知道朋友家的女儿们有一个独生子，而且病得很重。她在拜访期间见到了他，觉得他病得很重，似乎已经奄奄一息。巧合的是，几个月前，她自己的独生子也曾患过白喉，病情危重。在他生病期间，她曾和一位女性亲戚一起离开父母家，在外地住了几个星期。她觉得，这次去乡下拜访朋友时，她的弟弟其实也和她在一起，甚至觉得这是他生病后第一次长时间外出。但是，关于这些细节，她的记忆却异常模糊，尽管她对其他所有细节都记得清清楚楚，尤其是那天她穿的衣服。任何熟悉此类情况的人都不难从这些迹象中得出结论：当时，女孩心中始终萦绕着哥哥去世的阴影，但这种恐惧要么从未在她意识层面出现过，要么在她哥哥幸运康复后被她极力压抑。如果哥哥没有康复，她现在应该身着丧服，穿着不同的衣服。她在乡下朋友家也遇到了类似的情况，他们唯一的弟弟生命垂危，不久后便去世了。她本应清楚地记得几个月前自己也曾经历过同样的处境，但她却因为压抑而无法回忆起那段记忆，反而将某种似曾相识的感觉转移到了朋友家的房子和花园里，最终陷入了似曾相识的错觉之中。从她压抑的情感中我们可以推断，她当时对哥哥死亡的预期，本质上与一种愿望实现的幻想并无太大区别：如果哥哥死了，她将成为家中唯一的孩子。她晚年患有神经症，极度害怕失去父母。分析结果一如既往地揭示了她恐惧背后潜藏的无意识愿望。

I have been able to trace back my own fleeting experiences of déjà vu in a similar way to the emotional circumstances of the moment. ‘Here is another occasion to revive the fantasy (unconscious and unrecognized) that I formed at such and such a time in order to express my wish for the situation to improve.’ This explanation of déjà vu has so far been accepted by only one observer. Dr Ferenczi, to whom the third edition of this book owes so many valuable contributions, has written to me on the subject: ‘Both in myself and in others, I have become convinced that the inexplicable sense of familiarity can be derived from unconscious fantasies of which one is unconsciously reminded in an actual situation. The case of one of my patients appeared different, but in fact was quite similar. He had a sense of déjà vu very often, but it regularly proved to be the result of a forgotten (or suppressed) dream of the night before. It seems, then, that déjà vu can arise not only from daydreams but also from nocturnal dreaming.’

我发现自己曾有过几次转瞬即逝的似曾相识感，而这些感觉与当时的情绪状况有着相似的关联。“这又是一个机会，让我重拾在某个时刻形成的（无意识且未被察觉的）幻想，以此表达我希望情况好转的愿望。”迄今为止，只有一位观察者接受了这种似曾相识感的解释。费伦齐博士（本书第三版的诸多宝贵贡献都归功于他）曾就此主题给我写信说：“无论是我自己还是其他人，我都确信，这种难以解释的熟悉感可能源于无意识的幻想，而这些幻想会在现实情境中被无意识地唤起。我的一位病人的情况看似不同，但实际上却非常相似。他经常感到似曾相识，但最终都被证实是源于前一晚被遗忘（或压抑）的梦境。”由此看来，似曾相识的感觉不仅可能源于白日梦，也可能源于夜间的梦境。

I later learned that in 1904 Grasset explained the phenomenon in a manner very close to my own.

我后来得知，格拉塞在 1904 年对这种现象的解释与我的解释非常接近。

In 1913 I wrote a short paper 12 describing another phenomenon which is very similar to déjà vu. It is déjà raconté , the illusion of having already said something, and it is particularly interesting when it emerges during psychoanalytical treatment. The patient then claims, with every sign of subjective certainty, to have told the doctor about a certain memory long ago. However, the doctor is sure his patient never mentioned it, and can usually convince the patient that he is mistaken. The explanation of this interesting slip is probably that the patient did intend to describe the memory but omitted to do so, and is now substituting the memory of the previous intention for the later failure to put it into practice.

1913年，我写了一篇短文 12 ，描述了另一种与似曾相识（déjà vu）非常相似的现象，即似曾相识的叙述（déjà raconté），一种感觉自己已经说过某件事的错觉。这种现象在精神分析治疗中出现时尤其有趣。患者会非常肯定地声称，很久以前就告诉过医生某个记忆。然而，医生却确信患者从未提及此事，并且通常能够说服患者自己记错了。这种有趣的口误的解释可能是，患者原本打算描述这段记忆，但却忘记了，现在只是用之前想说却没说出口的记忆来代替后来未能付诸实践的事实。

Similar, and probably operating in the same way, are the ‘supposed slips’ mentioned by Ferenczi. 13 We think we have forgotten, mislaid or lost some object, but we can convince ourselves that nothing of the kind happened and everything is in order. For instance, a patient comes back to the doctor’s room for the umbrella she says she has left there, but the doctor sees that she actually has the umbrella in her hand. She therefore had an urge to make such a slip, and it was enough to act as the substitute for actually making it. Apart from this difference a supposed slip is just the same as a real one, but might be described as costing one less.

费伦齐提到的“假失言”与之类似，而且运作方式可能相同。 13 我们以为自己忘记、放错地方或丢失了某件东西，但我们却能说服自己根本没有发生过这种事，一切都井然有序。例如，一位病人回到诊室取她声称落在那里的雨伞，但医生却发现她手里拿着雨伞。因此，她当时有一种想要“失言”的冲动，而这种冲动足以代替实际的失言。除了这一点之外，“假失言”与“实际失言”并无二致，只是前者造成的损失要小一些。

E) Not long ago, when I was telling a colleague with a training in philosophy some instances of the forgetting of names, and their analysis, he immediately replied: ‘Yes, that’s all very well, but I don’t forget names in the same way at all.’ Obviously this is not an easy question; I don’t think that my colleague had ever before thought of analysing the forgetting of a name, so he could not say in just what way he did it differently. But his comment does touch on a problem which many people will be inclined to point out: is the account I have given here of slips and fortuitous actions generally or only occasionally valid, and, if it applies only in certain cases, then in what circumstances may it be cited to explain phenomena that could be caused in other ways? My experience fails me when it comes to answering this question. I can only warn against considering that connections of the kind I have explained here are unusual, for whenever I have put my theory to the test with myself and my patients it has proved accurate, as in the examples given above, or at least there have been good reasons for assuming it to be accurate. It is not surprising if one sometimes fails to find the hidden meaning of a symptomatic action, since the amount of inner resistance to that solution must be regarded as a crucial factor. Nor can one always interpret every single dream of one’s own or one’s patients, but to make a little further progress into its hidden meaning is enough to confirm the general validity of the theory. The dream that resists interpretation the next day can often be made to reveal its secret a week or a month later, when some real change in the conflicting strength of psychic factors has occurred. The same applies to the explanation of slips and symptomatic actions; the example of my misreading ‘in a tub through Europe’ (see pp. 104ff.) gave me a chance to show how a symptom that could not at first be understood may become susceptible of analysis when real interest in the suppressed idea has died down. 14 As long as there was a chance that my brother would get the coveted title of professor before me, the misreading I mentioned withstood repeated efforts at analysis; after it had turned out that he was unlikely to do so, I was suddenly able to see my way to solving it. It would therefore be wrong to say that all cases which resist analysis arise through some psychic mechanism other than the one set out here; negative evidence is not enough for such a supposition. And the readiness probably generally present in healthy people to believe in some other explanation of slips and symptomatic actions is devoid of any value as evidence; it naturally expresses the same mental forces as those that caused the mystery and are therefore working to maintain it and resist its explanation.

E）不久前，我向一位受过哲学训练的同事讲述了一些忘记名字的例子及其分析，他立刻回答说：“是的，这很好，但我忘记名字的方式完全不同。” 显然，这不是一个容易回答的问题；我想我的同事以前从未想过分析忘记名字这件事，所以他无法具体说明他忘记名字的方式有何不同。但他的评论确实触及了一个许多人都会指出的问题：我在这里对口误和偶然行为的解释是普遍有效还是只在特定情况下有效？如果它只适用于某些情况，那么在什么情况下可以引用它来解释那些可能由其他原因引起的现象？就我的经验而言，我无法回答这个问题。我只能提醒大家，不要认为我在此解释的这类关联是罕见的，因为每当我用自己的理论和病人的理论进行检验时，它都被证明是准确的，就像上面举的例子一样，或者至少有充分的理由认为它是准确的。有时无法找到症状行为的隐藏含义并不奇怪，因为内在对这种解释的阻力必须被视为一个关键因素。我们也不可能总是能解读自己或病人的每一个梦，但对梦的隐藏含义进行更深入的探究就足以证实该理论的总体有效性。第二天难以解释的梦，往往在一周或一个月后，当心理因素的冲突力量发生一些真正的变化时，就能揭示其秘密。这同样适用于对口误和症状行为的解释；我误读“乘浴缸游遍欧洲”（见第104页及之后）的例子，让我有机会展示，当人们对被压抑的想法真正失去兴趣时，一个起初无法理解的症状是如何变得可以分析的。只要我哥哥还有可能比我先获得梦寐以求的教授头衔，我提到的误读就经受住了反复的分析；在他不太可能获得这个头衔之后，我突然找到了解决之道。因此，认为所有难以分析的案例都是由此处未提及的某种心理机制造成的，是错误的；反面证据不足以支持这种假设。健康人普遍存在的、倾向于相信对口误和症状行为有其他解释的倾向，本身并不能作为证据；它自然而然地表达了与造成谜团的心理力量相同的心理力量，这些力量正在维持谜团并阻碍对其的解释。

On the other hand, we must not overlook the fact that repressed ideas and emotions do not of their own accord cause their expression in symptomatic actions and slips. The technical ability of innervations to make slips like this must operate independently; that ability is then gratefully exploited by the intention of something repressed to make itself consciously felt. In the case of verbal slips, extensive studies by philosophers and philologists have tried to establish the structural and functional relationships that make themselves available to carry out such an intention. If we distinguish the unconscious motive from the opposing physiological and psycho-physical factors conditioning the slip or symptomatic action, it is still an open question whether, within the range of normal behaviour, there are other factors which may produce slips and symptomatic actions in line with those relationships, resembling but acting as substitutes for the unconscious motive. It is not within the scope of this book to answer that question.

另一方面，我们不能忽视这样一个事实：被压抑的想法和情绪本身并不会主动导致它们以症状性行为和口误的形式表现出来。神经支配产生此类口误的技术能力必须独立运作；这种能力随后被某种被压抑的事物所利用，使其能够有意识地感受到自身。就口误而言，哲学家和语言学家进行了广泛的研究，试图确定促成这种意图的结构和功能关系。如果我们区分无意识动机与导致口误或症状性行为的生理和心理生理因素，那么在正常行为范围内，是否存在其他因素也会产生符合这些关系的口误和症状性行为，这些因素类似于无意识动机，但实际上只是替代了无意识动机，这仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。本书的范围不包括回答这个问题。

Nor is it my intention to exaggerate the differences between the psychoanalytic and the popular concept of slips, which are wide enough anyway. I would point, instead, to cases where those differences are a good deal less clear-cut. Highly complicated interpretations are not needed for the simplest and least striking examples of slips of the tongue and pen, for instance where words are compressed or words and letters omitted. From the psychoanalytic viewpoint, it must be said that in these cases some kind of disruption has indicated an intention, but there is no saying what caused the disruption or what its intention was. All it has done is to announce its presence. In cases like this conditions encouraging a slip, as I myself have never disputed, are encouraged by relationships of sound and obvious psychological associations. However, it is scientifically appropriate to ask for such rudimentary slips of the tongue or pen to be judged in relation to more conspicuous slips, those from which, when investigated, unambiguous conclusions can be drawn for the reasons behind slips as a whole.

我并非意在夸大精神分析和大众对口误概念之间的差异，毕竟这些差异本身就已相当显著。相反，我想指出的是，在某些情况下，这些差异远没有那么泾渭分明。例如，对于最简单、最不引人注目的口误或笔误，比如词语被压缩或漏字漏字，并不需要极其复杂的解释。从精神分析的角度来看，必须指出的是，在这些情况下，某种程度的干扰表明了一种意图，但我们无法确定干扰的原因或意图是什么。它所做的仅仅是表明了自身的存在。在这些情况下，正如我本人从未否认的那样，促成口误的条件是由合理且显而易见的心理联想所促成的。然而，从科学的角度来看，我们应该将这些基本的口误或笔误与更明显的口误进行比较，因为通过对更明显的口误进行研究，我们可以得出关于口误整体原因的明确结论。

F) Since my comments on slips of the tongue, I have contented myself with showing that there is a concealed motivation for slips of various kinds, and have been working towards an understanding of this motivation with the aid of psychoanalysis. So far I have left the general nature and peculiarities of the psychic factors expressed in such slips almost out of consideration, or at least I have not yet made any attempt to define them more closely and test them for regularity. Nor am I going to embark on a thorough study of the subject here, since the initial stages of any such study soon show that it is better approached from another direction. 15 But several questions may be asked at this point, and I will at least mention them and give a brief outline of their extent: 1) What is the content and origin of those ideas and emotions that indicate their presence through slips and fortuitous actions? 2) What are the conditions that induce an idea or emotion to use these incidents as a means of expression and enable them to do so? 3) Can constant and unambiguous connections be traced between the nature of a slip and the character of what it expresses?

F) 自从我评论口误以来，我一直致力于指出各种口误背后隐藏着某种动机，并借助精神分析来理解这种动机。到目前为止，我几乎没有考虑过这类口误所体现的心理因素的一般性质和特殊性，或者至少我还没有尝试更精确地定义它们并检验它们的规律性。我也不打算在此对这个主题进行深入研究，因为任何此类研究的初始阶段很快就会表明，从另一个角度切入会更好。 15 但在此可以提出几个问题，我至少会提及它们并简要概述其范围：1) 那些通过口误和偶然行为表明其存在的观念和情感的内容和来源是什么？2) 是什么条件促使某种观念或情感利用这些事件作为表达手段并使其能够这样做？ 3）能否在口误的性质和它所表达的内容的特征之间找到持续而明确的联系？

I will begin by assembling some material to help us answer the last question. In discussing examples of slips of the tongue, it was found necessary to go beyond the content of what the speaker intended to say, and search outside that intention for the cause of the speech disturbance. In a number of cases that cause was then evident, and was known to the speaker’s conscious mind. In the apparently simplest and most obvious examples it was another version of the idea concerned, which sounded equal in status but disrupted its expression, although one could not say why one idea was suppressed and the other made itself felt (Meringer and Mayer’s ‘contaminations’). In a second group of cases, the suppression of one concept was motivated by something which did not, however, prove strong enough to obliterate it entirely ( zum Vorschwein gekommen instead of zum Vorschein gekommen ). The suppressed concept was still obvious. The only thing that can be said without reservation of the third group is that in those cases the disruptive idea was different from the intended idea, and here we can make what looks like an essential distinction. The disruptive idea is either connected with the idea it disturbed by means of associated ideas (disturbance through inner resistance), or it is different in nature, and the word that has been disturbed is linked with the often unconscious idea disturbing it through a disconcerting outward association. In the examples I have cited from my psychoanalyses, the whole speech is influenced by ideas which have been simultaneously activated but are entirely unconscious, and which reveal themselves either through the disturbance itself ( Klapperschlange — Kleopatra ) or exert indirect influence, enabling various parts of the consciously intended speech to disturb each other ( Ase natmen , against the background of Hasenauerstrasse and reminiscences of French people who were known to the speaker). The withheld or unconscious ideas disrupting speech are of many different origins. My survey, then, does not reveal a general rule tending in any direction.

首先，我将收集一些资料来帮助我们回答最后一个问题。在讨论口误的例子时，我们发现有必要超越说话者原本想表达的内容，去探寻造成言语障碍的真正原因。在许多情况下，这个原因显而易见，说话者也意识到了。在看似最简单、最明显的例子中，是相关想法的另一个版本，这个版本听起来同样重要，但却干扰了原有想法的表达，尽管我们无法解释为什么一个想法被压抑而另一个想法却显露出来（梅林格和迈耶所说的“污染”）。在另一类例子中，某个概念的压抑是由某种因素引起的，但这种因素并不足以将其完全抹杀（例如，说成“zum Vorschwein gekommen”而不是“zum Vorschein gekommen”）。被压抑的概念仍然很明显。对于第三组案例，唯一可以毫不保留地说的是，在这些案例中，干扰性想法与预期想法不同，而在这里我们可以做出一个看似至关重要的区别。干扰性想法要么通过关联想法与被干扰的想法相连（通过内在阻力造成的干扰），要么本质上不同，被干扰的词语与通常无意识的干扰想法通过令人不安的外在联想而联系在一起。在我引用的精神分析案例中，整个言语都受到同时激活但完全无意识的想法的影响，这些想法要么通过干扰本身显现出来（例如“Klapperschlange”——克利奥帕特拉），要么发挥间接影响，使有意识意图的言语的各个部分相互干扰（例如“Ase natmen”，以哈森瑙尔大街为背景，并回忆起说话者认识的法国人）。干扰言语的被压抑或无意识的想法来源多种多样。因此，我的调查并未发现任何普遍规律。

Comparative study of examples of misreadings and slips of the pen leads to the same results. Individual cases, as in slips of the tongue, seem to owe their occurrence to compression without any other motivation (for instance, der Apfe ). However, it would be interesting to know whether special conditions must after all be met for such compressions to occur — compressions that regularly occur in dream work but appear wrong in our waking minds — and the examples themselves do not lead us anywhere. However, I would not draw the conclusion that no special conditions exist other than, for instance, failing to pay conscious attention, since I know from other sources that activities automatically performed are particularly notable for their correct and reliable nature. Instead I would emphasize that here, as so often in biology, normal or approximately normal subjects are less useful objects of research than their pathological counterparts. I expect to have light cast on what is still obscure in the explanation of these very mild disruptions by the elucidation of more severe disturbances.

对误读和笔误的比较研究得出了相同的结果。个别案例，就像口误一样，似乎仅仅由于压缩而产生，没有任何其他动机（例如，苹果）。然而，这类压缩的发生是否需要满足某些特殊条件，这很值得探究——这类压缩经常出现在梦境中，但在清醒状态下却显得错误——而这些例子本身并没有提供任何线索。不过，我不会就此得出结论，认为除了例如缺乏意识注意之外，不存在任何特殊条件，因为我从其他来源了解到，自动执行的活动往往以其正确性和可靠性而著称。相反，我想强调的是，正如生物学中经常出现的情况一样，正常或近似正常的受试者不如病理受试者更有研究价值。我希望通过阐明更严重的紊乱，能够揭示这些轻微紊乱的解释中仍然模糊不清的部分。

Nor is there any shortage of examples of misreadings and slips of the pen allowing us to recognize a more distant and complicated motivation. The misreading of ‘In a tub through Europe’ ( Im Fass for Am Fuss , on foot) can be explained by the influence of an idea remote and different from the real phrase, arising from repressed emotions of envy and ambition, and using the ‘bridge’ of the two meanings of the word Beförderung as a link with a neutral, innocuous theme. In the case of ‘Burckhard’ the name itself acted as a ‘bridge’.

误读和笔误的例子比比皆是，从中我们可以窥见更为深层和复杂的动机。例如，“乘着浴缸穿越欧洲”（Im Fass 误读为 Am Fuss，意为步行）的误读，可以用一个与原句截然不同的遥远想法来解释，这个想法源于压抑的嫉妒和野心，并利用“Beförderung”（帮助）一词的双重含义作为连接中性、无害主题的桥梁。在“Burckhard”这个例子中，名字本身就起到了“桥梁”的作用。

It is obvious that disturbances of the functions of speech arise more easily and make fewer demands on the disruptive forces than those of other psychic phenomena. We are on different ground when we come to study forgetfulness in the real sense, that is, forgetting past experiences (forgetting proper names and foreign words, as described in sections I and II, could be distinguished from this forgetfulness in the strict sense as ‘omission’). The basic conditions affecting the normal process of forgetting are not known. 16 We must also bear in mind that not everything thought to be forgotten actually is. My explanation here relates only to those cases in which we are surprised to find that we have forgotten something because our slip contravenes the rule that the memory forgets unimportant matters but retains what is really important. Analysis of examples of forgetfulness which seem to me to require special explanation always shows that the motive for forgetting was an aversion to remembering something which would arouse distressing sensations. One comes to suppose that this motive strives to express itself generally in psychic life, but is somehow prevented from making itself felt regularly by other forces working against it. The most careful psychological study of the extent and significance of an aversion to remembering painful impressions seems called for, and outside this wider context one cannot say what particular circumstances make this generally desirable form of forgetting possible in individual cases.

显然，言语功能障碍比其他心理现象更容易出现，对干扰因素的要求也更低。当我们真正研究遗忘，即遗忘过去的经历时，情况就有所不同了（如第一节和第二节所述，遗忘专有名词和外来词可以与严格意义上的遗忘区分开来，因为后者属于“遗漏”）。影响正常遗忘过程的基本条件尚不清楚。我们还必须记住，并非所有被认为遗忘的事情实际上都被遗忘了。我在此的解释仅涉及那些我们惊讶地发现自己遗忘了某些事情的情况，因为我们的疏忽违反了记忆会遗忘不重要的事情而保留真正重要的事情的规则。分析那些在我看来需要特殊解释的遗忘案例总是表明，遗忘的动机是对那些会引起痛苦感觉的事情的厌恶。人们逐渐认为，这种动机力图在心理生活中普遍表达出来，但却因其他力量的阻碍而无法经常显现。因此，似乎有必要对厌恶回忆痛苦印象的程度和意义进行最细致的心理学研究。脱离这一更广泛的背景，我们无法确定在个体案例中，究竟是哪些具体情况使得这种普遍可取的遗忘形式成为可能。

Another factor comes to the fore when we study the forgetting of intentions; here, the conflict that we only suspect to be involved in the repression of painful memories becomes tangible, and analysis of examples regularly reveals a negative force opposing but not eliminating the intention. As in slips discussed earlier, two types of psychic process can again be recognized; the negative counter-will either aims directly at the intention (when it is one of some importance), or in itself it is alien to the intention and creates a link with it through some outward association (in relatively unimportant intentions).

当我们研究意图遗忘时，另一个因素便凸显出来；在这里，我们原本只是怀疑与痛苦记忆压抑相关的冲突变得切实可感，对案例的分析也经常揭示出一种负面力量，它与意图对抗，但并未消除意图。正如前文讨论的口误一样，我们可以再次识别出两种心理过程：这种负面反意志要么直接针对意图（当意图较为重要时），要么本身与意图无关，而是通过某种外在联想与意图建立联系（在相对不重要的意图中）。

The same conflict dominates the phenomenon of inadvertent actions. The impulse expressed in the disruption of the action is often a counter-impulse, but more frequently still is a completely alien one, expressing itself by disturbing the execution of the action. The cases in which disturbance occurs through some internal contradiction are more significant and affect more important actions.

同样的冲突也主导着无意行为的现象。导致行为中断的冲动通常是一种反冲动，但更常见的是一种完全外来的冲动，它通过干扰行为的执行而表现出来。因某种内在矛盾而导致的干扰更为显著，并影响到更重要的行为。

Internal conflict is less and less important in fortuitous and symptomatic actions. The conscious mind thinks little of these motor expressions, or ignores them entirely. They serve to express many kinds of unconscious or suppressed emotions, and generally tend to be symbolic of fantasies or wishes.

在偶然行为和症状性行为中，内在冲突的重要性越来越低。意识层面很少关注这些肢体表达，甚至完全忽略它们。这些行为表达了许多无意识或被压抑的情绪，通常象征着幻想或愿望。

As for the first of my three questions, about the origin of those ideas and emotions which express themselves in slips, it may be said that in a good many cases the disruptive ideas can be shown to originate in suppressed emotions in mental life. In normal people selfish, jealous and hostile feelings and impulses, upon which the pressure of moral teaching weighs very heavily, quite often make use of slips in order to find some way of expressing their forces, forces that are undeniably present but are not recognized by the higher authorities in our minds. Permitting these slips and fortuitous actions to occur reflects, to a considerable extent, a useful toleration of amorality. Sexual currents of many kinds figure prominently among these suppressed emotions, and it is because of the chance nature of the material here that few of them are found among the ideas revealed by analysis in my examples. As the cases I have analysed are taken mainly from my own mental life, my choice of material was obviously partisan from the first and likely to exclude sexual matters. On other occasions, perfectly innocuous objections and considerations seem to be at the root of the disruptive ideas.

至于我的第一个问题，即那些在口误中流露出的想法和情绪的起源，可以说，在很多情况下，这些具有破坏性的想法源于被压抑的心理情绪。在普通人身上，自私、嫉妒和敌意等情绪和冲动，常常会受到道德教诲的沉重压迫，并借助口误来找到某种方式来表达它们的力量——这些力量无疑存在，但却不被我们头脑中更高层次的权威所认可。允许这些口误和偶然行为的发生，在很大程度上反映了一种对不道德行为的容忍。各种性冲动在这些被压抑的情绪中占据着显著地位，而正是由于这些素材的偶然性，在我的例子中，通过分析揭示的想法中很少发现性冲动。由于我分析的案例主要取材于我自身的心理生活，因此我选择这些素材从一开始就带有明显的个人倾向，并且很可能排除了性方面的内容。在其他情况下，一些完全无害的反对意见和考虑似乎是破坏性想法的根源。

We now face the second question, of the psychological conditions that account for an idea’s seeking expression not in full but in what might be called parasitical form, as the modification and disturbance of another idea. The most striking examples of slips suggest that these conditions should be sought in relation to their capacity to enter the conscious mind — in the more or less strongly marked character of their ‘repression’. However, following this idea through our series of examples dissolves that character into increasingly vague indications. An inclination to ignore something regarded as a waste of time — an assessment of an idea as not really relevant to a certain subject — would seem to motivate the suppression of an idea which then resorts to expressing itself by disrupting another idea, playing the same part as the moral condemnation of an unseemly emotion or derivation from entirely unconscious trains of thought. We can gain no insight into the general nature of the factors conditioning slips and fortuitous actions in this way. Such studies produce a single significant fact: the more innocuous the motivation of the slip, and therefore the less offensive and thus less inaccessible to the conscious mind is the idea expressed in the slip, the more easily is the phenomenon explained once attention is drawn to it; the simplest cases of slips of the tongue are immediately noticed and spontaneously corrected. Motivation by genuinely repressed ideas calls for solution by careful analysis, which may itself sometimes encounter difficulties or fail.

现在我们面临第二个问题：是什么心理条件导致一个想法并非以完整的形式表达，而是以一种可称之为寄生的方式——即对另一个想法的修改和干扰——来寻求表达？最引人注目的口误案例表明，这些条件应该与它们进入意识的能力——或多或少地体现在它们“压抑”的特征上——联系起来寻找。然而，沿着我们的一系列例子追溯这一观点，这种特征却逐渐消解为越来越模糊的迹象。一种倾向于忽略被认为是浪费时间的事情——认为某个想法与特定主题无关——似乎会促使人们压抑某个想法，而这个想法随后会通过干扰另一个想法来表达自身，其作用与对不雅情绪的道德谴责或完全无意识的思维过程类似。通过这种方式，我们无法深入了解影响口误和偶然行为的因素的普遍本质。这类研究得出了一个重要的结论：口误的动机越无害，口误中表达的想法就越不具冒犯性，也就越容易被意识所理解，一旦注意到这一现象，就越容易解释它；最简单的口误往往能立即被察觉并自发纠正。而真正由压抑的想法引发的口误则需要通过仔细分析来解决，而这种分析本身有时也会遇到困难甚至失败。

It is justifiable, then, to see the results of this last investigation as suggesting that a satisfactory explanation of the psychological conditions for the occurrence of slips and fortuitous actions is to be found by approaching the matter from another direction and along another path. The forbearing reader may therefore see in these remarks evidence of certain ragged edges where the subject was rather arbitrarily removed from a wider context.

因此，我们可以合理地认为，这项最新调查的结果表明，要对导致失误和偶然行为的心理条件做出令人满意的解释，需要从另一个角度、沿着另一条路径来探讨这个问题。因此，有耐心的读者或许会从这些论述中看出一些瑕疵，因为这些瑕疵表明，研究对象被相当武断地从更广泛的背景中剥离了出来。

G) I should end with a few words at least indicating the way to this wider context. In its essentials, the mechanism of slips and fortuitous actions, as we have seen through analysis, agrees with the mechanism of dream formation as I studied it in the section on ‘dream work’ in my book on the interpretation of dreams. Compressions and compromise formations (contaminations) occur in both phenomena; the situation is the same in that unconscious ideas express themselves in unusual ways, through external associations, as the modification of other ideas. The inconsistencies, absurdities and mistakes of the content of dreams, which have largely prevented them from being recognized as the product of psychic processes, arise in the same way, although admittedly with freer use of the means available, as do the common slips in our everyday life; in both, the appearance of an incorrect function is set off by the curious interference with each other of two or more operations functioning correctly. We may draw an important conclusion from this contingency: the curiously functioning operation, the results of which are most strikingly evident in the content of a dream, cannot be derived from the fact that the dreamer’s mental life is asleep at the time, if slips provide so much evidence that it works in waking life. The same context also prevents us from seeing the extensive disintegration of mental activity in a morbid state functioning as the condition for these psychic processes, abnormal and strange as they may seem to us. 17

G) 最后，我至少应该简要地指出通往更广阔背景的路径。正如我们通过分析所看到的，失误和偶然行为的机制，其本质与我在《梦的解析》一书中“梦的运作”一节中研究的梦的形成机制相一致。压缩和妥协的形成（污染）在这两种现象中都会发生；情况相同，即无意识的想法通过外部联想，以不寻常的方式表达出来，作为对其他想法的修改。梦的内容中的不一致、荒谬和错误，在很大程度上阻碍了人们认识到梦是心理过程的产物，它们的产生方式与我们日常生活中的常见失误相同，尽管梦境中对可用手段的运用更为自由；在这两种情况下，错误的出现都是由于两个或多个正常运作的操作之间奇特的相互干扰造成的。我们或许可以从这一偶然事件中得出重要结论：这种奇特的运作机制（其结果在梦境内容中最为显著）并非源于做梦者当时的精神状态处于睡眠状态，因为梦境中的失误足以证明它在清醒状态下也有效。同样的情况也使我们无法将病态状态下精神活动的广泛瓦解视为这些心理过程（尽管在我们看来异常怪异）的运作条件。

A correct assessment of the strange psychic activities which allow both slips and dreams to arise can be made only once we have recognized that psycho-neurotic symptoms, particularly psychic forms of hysteria and compulsive neurosis, also show all the major features of this method of functioning in their mechanism. Our investigations may continue from this point. I feel, however, that it is particularly interesting to look at slips, fortuitous and symptomatic actions in the light of this last analogy. If we equate them with the operations of psychoneuroses, that is to say, with neurotic symptoms, there is a good deal of sense in, and support for, the claims often made that the borderline between nervous normality and abnormality is a fluid one, and that we are all slightly neurotic. One does not need medical experience to call to mind various types of neuroticism that are merely indicated — neurotic formes frustes : cases where there are only a few symptoms, or they appear rarely or not violently, their diminution being expressed in the number, intensity and frequency of occurrence of the morbid phenomena. Perhaps, however, one would not guess which type seems to convey most frequently the transition between health and sickness. The type in question, expressing its signs of sickness in slips and symptomatic actions, is notable for the transference of its symptoms to the least important psychic procedures, while everything that can claim a higher psychic value remains undisturbed. The reverse accommodation of symptoms, when they appear in the functions most important to both individuals and society and disrupt eating and drinking, sexual intercourse, professional work and social life, is found in severe cases of neurosis, and is more characteristic of them than, for instance, the variety or vehemence of their signs of sickness.

只有当我们认识到，精神神经症症状，特别是癔症和强迫性神经症的精神表现形式，在其运作机制中也展现出这种运作方式的所有主要特征时，才能对那些导致口误和梦境产生的奇异心理活动做出正确的评估。我们的研究可以从这一点继续展开。然而，我认为，从最后一个类比的角度来审视口误、偶然行为和症状性行为尤其有趣。如果我们将它们等同于精神神经症的运作，也就是说，等同于神经症症状，那么关于神经正常与异常之间的界限是流动的，以及我们每个人都略带神经质的观点，就具有相当的道理和依据。无需医学经验，也能想到各种类型的神经质——例如，神经质的“不典型”形式：这类患者症状较少，或症状出现频率低、程度轻，其症状的减轻体现在病态现象的数量、强度和发生频率上。然而，或许人们难以猜到哪种类型最常体现健康与疾病之间的转换。这种类型以失误和症状性行为来表达疾病迹象，其显著特点是将症状转移到最不重要的心理活动中，而所有具有更高心理价值的活动则不受影响。相反，当症状出现在对个人和社会都至关重要的功能中，并扰乱饮食、性生活、职业工作和社交生活时，这种症状的转移则见于严重的神经质病例，并且比疾病迹象的种类或严重程度更具特征性。

However, the common characteristic of both the mildest and most severe cases, a characteristic also shown by slips and fortuitous actions, lies in the fact that the phenomena can be traced back to incompletely suppressed psychic material which, although displaced from the conscious mind, is not, however, deprived of all ability to express itself

然而，无论是最轻微的还是最严重的案例，其共同特征（这种特征也体现在失误和偶然事件中）在于，这些现象可以追溯到未被完全压抑的心理素材。这些素材虽然脱离了意识层面，但并未完全丧失表达自身的能力。

4 . Herr Rudolf Schneider, in Munich, has raised an interesting objection to the evidential force of such analyses of numbers (‘Zu Freud’s analytischer Untersuchung des Zahleinfalles’ [‘On Freud’s Analytical Study of Numerical Ideas’], Zeitschrift für Psychoanalyse I, 1920). He chose certain numbers, for instance one that first met his eye in a historical work when he opened it, or he faced someone else with the number he had chosen and waited to see if the apparently determining ideas that had emerged in connection with that number occurred to that other person too. This was in fact the case; in one example concerning himself which he gives, the ideas produced as rich and evocative a line of determination as we found in our analyses of spontaneously occurring numbers, while the number in Schneider’s experiment, coming from outside, did not need determination. In a second experiment with someone else, he obviously made the task too easy for himself by giving his subject the number 2, with which everyone is bound to connect some determining factor or other. R. Schneider draws two conclusions from his work: first, ‘the psychic is as easily able to associate with numbers as with words’, and second, the emergence of determining ideas connected with spontaneously produced numbers proves nothing about the origin of those numbers from the ideas found in their ‘analysis’. The first conclusion is undoubtedly correct. One can just as easily associate some suitable idea with a given number as with a word that is called out, perhaps even more easily, since the few digits available to us can give rise to a particularly wide range of possible associations. We are then simply in the situation of what has been called the association experiment, which has been studied in its many manifestations by the Bleuler-Jung school. In this situation the idea (or reaction) is determined by the given word (or stimulus). But such reactions may be of various different kinds, and Jung’s experiments have shown that even the wider distinction is not left to ‘chance’ but that unconscious ‘complexes’ play a part in its determination if they are affected by the stimulus. Schneider’s second conclusion goes too far. The fact that suitable ideas emerge in connection with given numbers (or words) says nothing about the derivation of spontaneously emerging numbers (or words) which could not have been taken into consideration before the knowledge of that fact. These ideas (verbal or numerical) could be indeterminate, or determined by the ideas that emerge in analysis, or by other ideas that do not surface in analysis, in which case the analysis has misled us. One must reject any impression that the problems with numbers and verbal ideas are different from each other. A critical study of the problem, and thus a justification of the psychoanalytical technique of ideas, is outside the scope of this book. In analytical practice, one sets out from the presumption that the second proposition is correct, and can be used in the majority of cases. Studies carried out by an experimental psychologist have shown that it is far the most likely (Poppelreuter). (And cf. in this connection Bleuler’s valuable comments in his book Das autistisch-undisziplinerte Denken …[ Autistic and Undisciplined Thinking …], 1919, part 9: ‘On the probabilities of psychological perception’.

4. 慕尼黑的鲁道夫·施耐德先生对这类数字分析的证据效力提出了一个有趣的质疑（《论弗洛伊德对数字观念的分析研究》，《精神分析杂志》第一卷，1920年）。他选择了一些特定的数字，例如，当他翻开一本历史著作时，首先映入眼帘的某个数字；或者，他让别人看到他选择的数字，然后观察与该数字相关的、看似具有决定性意义的观念是否也出现在对方的脑海中。事实的确如此；在他举的一个关于他自己的例子中，这些观念产生的决定性线索与我们在分析自发出现的数字时所发现的一样丰富且引人深思，而施耐德实验中的数字来自外部，无需任何决定。在与另一位受试者进行的第二次实验中，他显然为了方便自己，给受试者选择了数字2，因为每个人都必然会将某些决定性因素与这个数字联系起来。R·施耐德从他的研究中得出两个结论：第一，“心灵感应者与数字的联想能力与与词语的联想能力一样强”；第二，与自发产生的数字相关的决定性观念的出现，并不能证明这些数字源自于对其“分析”中发现的观念。第一个结论无疑是正确的。人们可以像将某个词语与一个给定的数字联系起来一样容易地将其与某个合适的观念联系起来，甚至可能更容易，因为我们可用的少数几个数字就能产生极其广泛的联想。这时，我们就处于所谓的联想实验状态，布鲁勒-荣格学派对其多种表现形式进行了研究。在这种情况下，观念（或反应）是由给定的词语（或刺激）决定的。但此类反应可能多种多样，荣格的实验表明，即使是更广泛的区分也并非偶然，而是无意识的“情结”在决定其是否受到刺激时发挥了作用。施耐德的第二个结论过于极端。与特定数字（或词语）相关的恰当观念的出现，并不能说明自发产生的数字（或词语）的来源，因为在了解这一事实之前，这些数字（或词语）是不可能被考虑的。这些观念（无论是语言上的还是数字上的）可能是不确定的，也可能是由分析中出现的观念决定的，或者是由分析中未出现的观念决定的，在这种情况下，分析误导了我们。我们必须摒弃任何认为数字观念和语言观念的问题彼此不同的印象。对这一问题进行批判性研究，从而为精神分析观念技术辩护，超出了本书的范围。在分析实践中，我们首先假定第二个命题是正确的，并且可以在大多数情况下使用。一位实验心理学家进行的研究表明，这才是最有可能的（Poppelreuter）。（另请参阅Bleuler在其1919年出版的《自闭且无纪律的思维……》一书第9部分“论心理感知的概率”中对此的宝贵评论。）

5 . These views on the strict determination of apparently arbitrary psychic actions have already borne much fruit for psychology — and perhaps for the administration of justice. In this sense, Bleuler and Jung have made it possible to understand reaction in what is known as the association experiment, in which the person being studied responds to a word which is uttered with whatever idea occurs to him (in reaction to the stimulus word), and the time he takes to do so is calculated (reaction time). In his Diagnostische Assoziationsstudien (1906) Jung has shown what a subtle test of psychic conditions the association experiment can be when it is interpreted in this way. Wertheimer and Klein, who have studied with H. Gross, the Prague lecturer in criminal law, have developed a technique for ‘diagnosing of the facts of a case’, which is being tested by psychologists and lawyers.
